findings.title: /api/draft-capital returns 200 with real pick dollar values to an unauthenticated caller, and takes 13.2s doing it
findings.claimUnderTest: Private valuation data is behind auth; only /api/public/* is anonymous.
findings.observed: An anonymous GET returns HTTP 200 with a 15,989-byte board of per-pick dollar values in 13,188 ms. Every other value-bearing route (/api/data, /api/movers, /api/terminal, /api/valuation/league-adjusted) correctly 401s anonymously.

reproduction.command: curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'status=%{http_code} bytes=%{size_download} time=%{time_total}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/draft-capital
reproduction.expected: 401 unauthorized, consistent with every other value-bearing route

numericProof.formula: observed HTTP status and wall time

findings.userImpact: Pick valuations that the rest of the platform treats as private are readable by anyone who can reach the API host, and the 13 s response makes the route a cheap way to consume backend capacity.

priorFinding.note: Measured directly in this audit's unauthenticated route sweep.

findings.whatWorks: The rest of the auth boundary is consistent — 47 of 66 probed GET routes correctly 401 anonymously.
findings.rootCause: The route is not wrapped by the auth dependency the other value routes use; the latency comes from a blocking Sleeper call for team-name mapping that fails and is retried inline (backend log: 'Sleeper API failed for draft capital team-name mapping').
findings.requiredRepair: Apply the same auth gate as /api/data, and make the Sleeper team-name lookup non-blocking with a bounded timeout.

findings.title: GET /api/bdvm/roster takes 48 seconds to return 310 bytes
findings.claimUnderTest: BDVM endpoints self-suppress cheaply when no projection snapshot exists (CLAUDE.md: the /rankings gap column 'gates on status == ok so it self-suppresses').
findings.observed: With data/bdvm/ absent, the endpoint still spends 47,994 ms before returning a 310-byte payload. Suppression is happening, but only after the full computation path has been walked.

reproduction.command: time curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{size_download}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/bdvm/roster
reproduction.expected: a fast negative — the precondition (no snapshot) is knowable up front
reproduction.actual: HTTP 200, 310 bytes, 47.994 s

numericProof.formula: wall time of a single authenticated GET

findings.userImpact: The /bdvm page blocks for ~48 s before rendering an empty state. On a shared backend this also occupies a worker for the whole window.

priorFinding.note: Latency measured in this audit; the prior audit noted BDVM had never run in production but not this cost.

findings.rootCause: To be confirmed by W13/W26 profiling — the snapshot-absent check appears to run after the roster/board assembly rather than before it.
findings.requiredRepair: Check for the projection snapshot before doing any per-player work, and return the documented unpriced/no-snapshot payload immediately.
findings.dependencies: W13 (BDVM) and W26 (performance) hold the call-path profile.

findings.title: /api/data is 11.95 MB, not the ~4 MB CLAUDE.md documents, and view=compact is larger than view=app
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'view=full (default, backward-compat): returns the full canonical contract (~4 MB uncompressed)'.
findings.observed: Measured 11,953,535 bytes uncompressed (1,176,182 gzipped) — about 3x the documented figure. Separately, ?view=compact returns 7,363,760 bytes while ?view=app returns 5,818,304, so the view named 'compact' is 27% LARGER than the app view.

reproduction.command: for v in '' '?view=app' '?view=compact'; do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -o /dev/null -w "$v %{size_download}\n" "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data$v"; done
reproduction.expected: ~4 MB full per the documentation; compact <= app

numericProof.formula: content-length of one authenticated GET

findings.userImpact: A reader sizing work off CLAUDE.md underestimates the payload threefold, and anyone reaching for 'compact' to reduce bytes gets more of them.

priorFinding.note: Measured in this audit.

findings.whatWorks: GZipMiddleware is effective — 11.95 MB compresses to 1.18 MB on the wire.
findings.rootCause: Documentation was written against an older contract; the compact view's field set has grown past the app view's.
findings.requiredRepair: Correct the documented figures and either rename or re-scope view=compact so its name matches its size.

findings.title: server.py says the consensus_edge flag defaults ON; feature_flags.py sets it False, and the live routes 503
findings.claimUnderTest: server.py's comment at the router registration states the consensus_edge flag has defaulted ON since 2026-08-04.
findings.observed: src/api/feature_flags.py:260 sets "consensus_edge": False with an ADR-023 rationale for the rollback, and every /api/consensus-edge/* route returns 503 {"error":"feature_disabled","flag":"consensus_edge"} on the running server. The code comment is the stale one — and it sits at the registration site a reader hits first.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/consensus-edge/health; sed -n '2688,2694p' server.py; sed -n '260p' src/api/feature_flags.py
reproduction.expected: comment and default agree
reproduction.actual: comment says ON; default is False; routes 503

numericProof.formula: observed HTTP status against the documented flag default

findings.userImpact: A maintainer reading server.py concludes the feature is live and will not look for the flag when the page renders nothing.

priorFinding.note: Found by diffing the comment against the registry and the live 503.

findings.rootCause: ADR-023 flipped the flag back off without updating the comment written when it was turned on.
findings.requiredRepair: Delete or correct the server.py comment; it duplicates state that feature_flags.py owns.

findings.title: /api/health registers a duplicate OpenAPI operation ID, which pytest warns about on every run
findings.claimUnderTest: Routes are registered once each.
findings.observed: FastAPI emits 'UserWarning: Duplicate Operation ID get_health_api_health_get for function get_health' during schema generation; it appears in the pytest run output and in /openapi.json generation. The live schema carries 100 operations across 97 unique paths.

reproduction.command: grep -n 'Duplicate Operation ID' docs/master-site-audit/evidence/pytest-full.txt
reproduction.expected: no duplicate-operation warnings
reproduction.actual: UserWarning raised for get_health_api_health_get

numericProof.formula: count of operations minus count of unique paths

findings.userImpact: Generated clients and API docs get a colliding operation name; the warning also trains readers to ignore warnings in the test output.

priorFinding.note: Observed in this audit's own test run.

findings.requiredRepair: Give the api_route registration an explicit distinct operation_id.

findings.title: Four value fields coexist on every contract row and diverge by up to 35.6%, with _finalAdjusted still read by a legacy branch of the arbitrage finder
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Both engines now read the same internal value' — finder.py reads the canonical board via board_values_from_contract.
findings.observed: Every row carries rankDerivedValue AND _finalAdjusted AND _composite AND _rawComposite AND (for offense) _offenseOnlyFinalAdjusted. Measured divergence of _finalAdjusted from the served rankDerivedValue: Carson Schwesinger +35.6%, Aidan Hutchinson +30.6%, Brock Bowers +6.8%, Travis Etienne -9.5%. finder.py's PRIMARY path does read the board — the _finalAdjusted reads at :498 sit in an explicit `else:` legacy branch taken only when no contract is supplied, and :1006 uses it deliberately on the composite scale to count unpriced assets. So the CLAUDE.md claim is upheld for the live path; what remains open is whether any caller can reach the legacy branch.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/tools/trace_asset.py 'Carson Schwesinger' 'Aidan Hutchinson' 'Travis Etienne'
reproduction.expected: one value concept per row, or clearly-scoped variants
reproduction.actual: four coexisting fields; _finalAdjusted differs from the served value by up to 35.6%

numericProof.formula: (rankDerivedValue - _finalAdjusted) / _finalAdjusted * 100

findings.userImpact: Any consumer that reaches the legacy branch prices IDP assets ~30% below the board the user sees.

priorFinding.note: The headline 'the finder arbitrages an invisible board' does NOT reproduce at HEAD — the primary path reads board values. Recorded as refuted for the live path; the residual risk is the ungated legacy branch.

findings.whatWorks: finder.py's primary path reads board_values_from_contract, and the scale reasoning at :478-497 is documented and correct.
findings.rootCause: The migration to the canonical board left the legacy composite path in place as a fallback rather than removing it.
findings.requiredRepair: Establish whether any live caller passes contract=None; if not, delete the legacy branch rather than leaving two scales reachable.

findings.title: Confidence reads High on two-source pick rows while fourteen-source player rows read Medium
findings.claimUnderTest: Confidence communicates how much evidence stands behind a number.
findings.observed: 2027 Early 1st (sourceCount 2) is labelled 'High — picks agree within 15%'. 2028 Late 1st (sourceCount 2) likewise. Travis Etienne (sourceCount 14) and George Kittle (sourceCount 14) are labelled 'Medium — multi-source, moderate spread'. The rule is agreement-based, which is defensible, but the rendered word inverts the evidence ordering: two sources agreeing outranks fourteen sources disagreeing slightly.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/tools/trace_asset.py '2027 Early 1st' 'George Kittle' | grep -E 'sourceCount|confidenceLabel'
reproduction.expected: a two-source row cannot outrank a fourteen-source row on displayed confidence
reproduction.actual: 2 sources -> High; 14 sources -> Medium

numericProof.formula: compare displayed confidence bucket against surviving source count

findings.userImpact: A user reads High confidence on a future pick whose value rests on two correlated pick markets and discounts a player value backed by fourteen sources.

priorFinding.note: The prior audit claims a 33.3% confidence misclassification rate; W03 is measuring that independently. This is a distinct, directly-observable presentation defect.

findings.rootCause: Agreement and evidence-volume are collapsed into one displayed word.
findings.requiredRepair: Show source count alongside the bucket, or floor the bucket by count so a two-source row cannot render High.
findings.dependencies: W03 owns the full confidence-calibration measurement.

findings.title: A current-year pick's provenance fields name two different sources
findings.claimUnderTest: Every visible number can identify its source (audit brief section 6).
findings.observed: On 2026 Pick 1.01: sourceRanks = {'idpTradeCalc': 12} while sourceOriginalRanks = {'dlfRookieSf': 1.0}. The two provenance stamps on the same row name different sources, and only idpTradeCalc appears in the committed CSVs for that asset. Separately, 2027 Early 1st reports sourceCount 2 with sourceOriginalRanks = {} (empty).

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/tools/trace_asset.py '2026 Pick 1.01' '2027 Early 1st'
reproduction.expected: provenance stamps agree on which sources produced the row
reproduction.actual: sourceRanks names idpTradeCalc; sourceOriginalRanks names dlfRookieSf

numericProof.formula: set intersection of the two provenance maps

findings.userImpact: Provenance cannot be trusted to answer 'where did this number come from' for pick rows, which is precisely where values are thinnest.

priorFinding.note: Observed directly in the pick traces.

findings.rootCause: Pick tethering overwrites the value from the merged rookie pool while the original-rank stamp survives from the pre-tether row.
findings.requiredRepair: Stamp the tethering source on tethered rows so both maps describe the same provenance.

findings.title: Measured through the production topology the frontend is clean: 41/41 pages load, 38 render an h1, median DOM-ready 83 ms, and the only client errors are correct auth and flag responses
findings.claimUnderTest: The site's pages render and are usable.
findings.observed: Every one of the 41 Next pages returns 200 authenticated. 38 render an <h1>. Median DOM-ready (navMs) is 83 ms, max 695 ms. Of 55 console errors, the only non-artifact ones are: 401 on / (one unauthenticated call from the home page), 403 on /admin (correct — the audit's test user is deliberately not in the admin allowlist) and 503 on /consensus-edge (correct — the flag is off per ADR-023). All 149 failed requests resolve to two harmless causes: ERR_ABORTED from the probe navigating away mid-flight, and sleepercdn.com avatar images, which this container cannot reach. Three redirects are by design: /finder -> /rankings, /intel -> /league/insider-trading, /rankings/qb -> /rankings?pos=QB.

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python <scratchpad>/probe_pages.py  # loads all 41 pages anon+auth with nginx-equivalent /api/* interception
reproduction.expected: pages render without client errors
reproduction.actual: 41/41 render; 0 genuine client-side failures

numericProof.formula: count of pages returning 200 with a rendered h1

findings.userImpact: None — this is a clean bill of health for the page layer, recorded because the audit's own first two measurements wrongly suggested otherwise.

priorFinding.note: Supersedes this audit's own invalid captures: page-probe-direct-next-INVALID.json (222 console errors) and page-probe-via-proxy-INVALID.json (dead shells). See evidence/INTEGRITY.md.

findings.whatWorks: The page layer. Bundles are all under the build's own budget, and DOM-ready is under 100 ms at the median.
findings.rootCause: n/a

findings.title: Three public league sub-pages render no heading and under 180 characters of text — franchise, rivalry and article-preview are effectively blank
findings.claimUnderTest: Franchise pages, rivalry pages and article previews are working public surfaces.
findings.observed: With real values substituted into the dynamic segments (owner=jasonleetucker, pair=jasonleetucker-vs-blaine, season=2025 week=1 matchup=1 mode=preview), all three return HTTP 200 but render NO <h1> and 143, 156 and 176 characters of body text respectively — anonymously and authenticated alike. For comparison /league/player/4046 renders 1,610 characters with an h1 of 'Patrick Mahomes', and /league/week/2025/1 renders 3,982 characters. The three are reachable, linked, and empty.

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/league/franchise/jasonleetucker | wc -c  # then compare rendered innerText via the page probe
reproduction.expected: a franchise page renders franchise content
reproduction.actual: 200 with no h1 and 143 characters of text

numericProof.formula: rendered document.body.innerText length

findings.userImpact: A visitor following a franchise or rivalry link from the league hub lands on a blank page with no explanation — the worst of the three states (content, honest empty state, blank).

priorFinding.note: Whether the cause is a missing data join or a wrong URL-parameter format is W19's to determine — the owner slug and pair format used here were inferred.

findings.rootCause: Unconfirmed: either the dynamic-segment format differs from what the page expects, or the backing data (week-level roster ownership / head-to-head history) is absent and the page renders nothing rather than saying so.

findings.title: Next bridges cover 36 of 99 backend operations and next.config.mjs declares no rewrites, so `npm run dev` serves a product where 40 client-called API routes 404
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md describes `frontend/app/api/` as '28 backend bridge routes' and Next as 'the sole production frontend'; the dynasty-data bridge's own comment says the bridges 'handle the dev flow (no nginx in front)'. The implication is that dev and production serve the same product.
findings.observed: There are 36 bridge route.js files against 99 unique backend method+path operations (openapi.json reports 100 because /api/health also carries an auto-generated HEAD). All 36 bridges do have a backend counterpart, so no bridge is orphaned — but 63 backend operations have no bridge, and 40 of those are fetched directly by client code. next.config.mjs declares distDir, turbopack.root and exactly one redirects() entry; it declares no rewrites(). `npm run dev` is `next dev -p 3000` with nothing in front. Measured against the running stack with a valid session: /api/health, /api/leagues, /api/user/state, /api/terminal, /api/movers, /api/data/rank-history, /api/ros/player-values, /api/custom-alerts and /api/data all return 404 on :3000 while returning 200 through the edge proxy on :3001 and directly on :8000. Only the bridged alias /api/dynasty-data returns 200 on :3000. This is not hypothetical: the audit harness had to stand up a separate nginx-equivalent proxy on :3001 because the first browser capture against :3000 was full of /api/* 404s plus a 'buildRows received a payload with zero backend rank stamps' console error that production never produces.

reproduction.command: for r in /api/health /api/leagues /api/user/state /api/terminal /api/movers /api/data /api/dynasty-data; do printf '%-26s %s %s %s\n' $r $(curl -s -m 25 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Cookie: jason_session=$SID" http://127.0.0.1:3000$r) $(curl -s -m 60 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Cookie: jason_session=$SID" http://127.0.0.1:3001$r) $(curl -s -m 60 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000$r); done
reproduction.expected: Same status from :3000 (Next) and :3001 (production topology) for every route the client calls.
reproduction.actual: /api/health 404/200/200 · /api/leagues 404/200/200 · /api/user/state 404/200/200 · /api/terminal 404/200/200 · /api/movers 404/200/200 · /api/data 404/200/200 · /api/dynasty-data 200/200/200

numericProof.formula: unbridgedButClientCalled = |{routes with a fetch() call site in frontend/ outside app/api/}| - |{routes with a matching frontend/app/api/**/route.js}|

findings.userImpact: A developer running the documented dev command sees a materially different, broken application: no terminal, no team switcher, no user state, no ROS panel, no movers, no rank history. Bugs get chased in dev that do not exist in prod, and prod bugs cannot be reproduced in dev. It also means the resilience code in the 264-line dynasty-data bridge (disk-snapshot fallback, per-chunk idle abort) is exercised only where it does not matter.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding named three ops pages and counted 30 route.js files. At HEAD e96c06ef there are 36 bridges and the gap is 63 unbridged operations, 40 of them client-called — an order of magnitude larger than reported, and the root cause (no rewrites() in next.config.mjs) was not named.

findings.whatWorks: Production is correct: nginx routes every /api/ to FastAPI, so the bridge gap is invisible to users. All 36 bridges do point at a real backend route — there are no orphan bridges. The e2e suite sidesteps the issue by keeping playwright baseURL on :8000.
findings.rootCause: Bridges were added one at a time as individual pages needed them, instead of one catch-all `rewrites()` entry mapping /api/:path* to BACKEND_API_URL. There is no test that asserts dev/prod route parity.
findings.requiredRepair: Add `async rewrites() { return [{ source: '/api/:path*', destination: `${process.env.BACKEND_API_URL || 'http://127.0.0.1:8000'}/api/:path*` }] }` to next.config.mjs (Next applies rewrites only after no route.js matches, so the 36 existing bridges keep winning), then delete the bridges that add nothing over a proxy. Pin with a test that every /api/ path referenced by frontend/ resolves under `next dev`.
findings.dependencies: Interacts with PRIOR-A06-F10 (bridges forward cookies inconsistently) — a single rewrite removes that class of divergence too.

findings.title: GET /api/gameplan exposes the entire src/roster_intel roster-intelligence engine and no page, component or script calls it
findings.claimUnderTest: server.py's docstring calls /api/gameplan 'The API surface over src/roster_intel/ — analyze_roster, the per-position profiles, the five-state competitive window, both target engines, the partner model, and (on request) the Trade Package Generator's Pareto frontier.' A route described as the API surface for a subsystem implies a consumer.
findings.observed: grep across every .js/.jsx under frontend/ (excluding node_modules and .next) returns exactly one hit for 'gameplan': a comment on line 32 of frontend/app/api/valuation/league-adjusted/route.js explaining that the overlay reuses gameplan's cached league bundle internally. There is no frontend/app/api/gameplan bridge directory. No script, workflow, systemd unit or nginx config references the path. The only callers are tests/api/test_gameplan_endpoint.py, tests/api/test_private_auth.py and tests/api/test_league_adjusted_endpoint.py. A bare authenticated GET returns 400 because `team` cannot be resolved for the e2e user, so even the smoke path is untested by any live client. The engine's code is not dead — /api/valuation/league-adjusted reaches parts of it — but the ROUTE, and the needs/window/targets/partners/Pareto-frontier outputs it alone exposes, reach no user.

reproduction.command: grep -rn 'gameplan' /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/frontend --include='*.js' --include='*.jsx' | grep -v node_modules | grep -v '\.next' ; ls /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/frontend/app/api/gameplan 2>&1 ; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/gameplan
reproduction.expected: At least one page or component fetching /api/gameplan.
reproduction.actual: 1 hit, and it is a comment. `ls: cannot access .../frontend/app/api/gameplan: No such file or directory`. Route returns 400.

numericProof.formula: reachability = frontendFetchCallSites + bridgeRoutes + opsCallers

findings.userImpact: Every answer this engine computes — positional needs, the five-state competitive window, buy/sell targets, ranked trade partners, the Pareto package frontier — is unavailable to any user. Users instead get the /phases contention label, which PRIOR-A18-F00 measured as giving the SAME team the opposite verdict, with no way to see the second opinion.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced exactly at HEAD e96c06ef: one grep hit, a comment, and no bridge directory. Adds the runtime observation that a bare authenticated GET 400s.

findings.whatWorks: The route is registered, auth-gated, league-scoped and test-covered; src/api/gameplan.py's cached league bundle is genuinely reused by /api/valuation/league-adjusted, so the underlying package is not dead code.
findings.rootCause: The backend engine shipped ahead of its UI and the UI was never built. Nothing fails when a route has no consumer, so nothing surfaced it.
findings.requiredRepair: Either build the consumer (the natural home is /rosters or a per-team page — see W01-F007) or retire the route and keep the internal helpers that /api/valuation/league-adjusted uses.
findings.dependencies: W01-F007 (no private team page) — gameplan is per-team and has nowhere to live until one exists.

findings.title: Sixteen backend routes have no caller outside the test suite, including six /api/scaffold/* introspection routes and POST /api/test-alert which nothing references at all
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md's API table advertises /api/scaffold/status, /api/scaffold/raw and /api/scaffold/identity as first-class endpoints ('Pipeline status', 'Raw source snapshots', 'Identity mappings'), implying they are part of the working product.
findings.observed: 16 of 99 backend operations (16.2%) have zero callers in frontend code, zero bridge consumers, zero references in .github/workflows, deploy/ or scripts/, and are referenced only by tests — or, for four of them, by nothing at all. The complete list is in the artifact. POST /api/test-alert has literally zero references anywhere in the repository including tests. GET /api/metrics is public and has no in-repo consumer (no dashboard, no workflow, no timer) — it is plausibly scraped by an external monitor, so it is classified ops rather than dead. Four of the sixteen have a Next bridge route built for them, so dev plumbing was written for endpoints nobody calls: /api/angle/find, /api/consensus-edge/health, /api/rankings/sources, /api/sharp/roster-percentage/audit.

reproduction.command: cat /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W01/dead-routes.txt ; grep -rn 'test-alert' /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket --include='*.py' --include='*.js' --include='*.jsx' --include='*.yml' --include='*.sh' | grep -v node_modules | grep -v master-site-audit
reproduction.expected: Every advertised route has at least one production consumer.
reproduction.actual: 16 routes with only test callers; `grep test-alert` returns only its own definition at server.py:9779.

findings.userImpact: No direct user impact — these routes are invisible. The cost is to maintainers and to this audit: CLAUDE.md's API table lists scaffold endpoints as product surface, so a reader budgets attention for a pipeline-introspection feature that has no UI and, per PRIOR-A23-F15, no producer either.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding established that /api/scaffold/* has no producer. This adds the other half — it has no consumer either — and extends the census to 16 routes across five subsystems.

findings.whatWorks: The census itself: openapi.json from the live app is an accurate authoritative route list, and every route that IS wired resolves to a real page or component (72 of 99).
findings.rootCause: Routes outlive their consumers. There is no CI check that a registered route is referenced by something other than a test.
findings.requiredRepair: Delete POST /api/test-alert. Decide per-route for the rest: retire, or wire. Add a test that walks the OpenAPI schema and asserts every path is referenced by frontend code, a workflow, a systemd unit, or an explicit OPS_ONLY allowlist — the same shape as tests/api/test_feature_flag_reachability.py, which already does this successfully for flags.
findings.dependencies: W01-F002 (gameplan), W01-F010 (scaffold/status is also a public info leak), W01-F011 (rankings/sources), W01-F012 (public-league CSV export).

findings.title: Two of four navigation surfaces ignore the adminOnly flag: /more and the command palette render Admin, Source Health, ROS Data Health and Trade Coverage to a session with isAdmin false
findings.claimUnderTest: nav-model.js states the rule outright: 'Ops surfaces are ADMIN-ONLY in the nav. ... the menu showed all four to every signed-in user — so a guest-pass holder saw a "Admin" entry, clicked it, and got a wall. Offering a door that is always locked is worse than not showing the door.' systemItemsFor({isAdmin}) exists to enforce it.
findings.observed: Only frontend/components/shell/TopBar.jsx:58 and frontend/components/shell/MobileChrome.jsx:106 call systemItemsFor({isAdmin}). frontend/app/more/page.jsx builds `[...NAV_MODEL, SYSTEM_MODEL]` and maps `group.items` directly, unfiltered — it imports SYSTEM_MODEL but not systemItemsFor. frontend/components/shell/CommandPalette.jsx:42 calls paletteTargets(), which spreads all of SYSTEM_MODEL.items with no isAdmin argument available to it. Fetched live with the e2e-test-user session (/api/auth/status returns isAdmin:false), the /more HTML contains 'Source Health', 'ROS Data Health', 'Trade Coverage' and '>Admin<' with their hrefs. This is not a hydration flash — no code path in either component ever filters.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/auth/status; curl -s -H "Cookie: jason_session=$SID" http://127.0.0.1:3001/more | grep -o 'Source Health\|ROS Data Health\|Trade Coverage\|>Admin<' | sort -u; grep -rn 'systemItemsFor' /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/frontend/app /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/frontend/components
reproduction.expected: Zero admin entries in /more for a session with isAdmin:false; systemItemsFor called by all four navigation surfaces.
reproduction.actual: auth_status isAdmin:false, yet /more renders all four Ops entries. systemItemsFor is called from exactly 2 files (TopBar.jsx, MobileChrome.jsx) out of 4 navigation surfaces.

numericProof.formula: leakedSurfaces = navigationSurfaces - surfacesCallingSystemItemsFor

findings.userImpact: A guest-pass holder or any non-admin signed-in user still sees four Ops destinations — on /more and in the command palette, which is the fastest navigation path in the app. Clicking Admin yields a 200 shell that then renders 'This page requires an admin session'. That is exactly the locked door the code comment says it removed, and it also discloses the operator tool inventory.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced at HEAD e96c06ef with a live non-admin session. Still open on both surfaces named by the prior finding.

findings.whatWorks: The desktop top bar and the mobile drawer both filter correctly. The server side is sound: every /api/admin/* route 403s a non-admin, and /admin degrades to an explicit 'requires an admin session' card rather than a blank or a fake dashboard. /admin's feature-flag panel is read-only and even renders gateStatus with an honest tooltip.
findings.rootCause: systemItemsFor is an opt-in helper rather than a property of the model. Three consumers had to remember to call it; two did.

findings.title: feature_flags._GATE_STATUS's claim that 7 of 15 flags cannot change a response is true — verified by booting a second backend with all seven forced ON and diffing 1,092 contract rows
findings.claimUnderTest: _GATE_STATUS classifies 7 of 15 registered flags as SCRIPT_ONLY, UNREACHABLE or NO_GATE — i.e. flipping them cannot change any response byte — and the remaining 8 as LIVE.
findings.observed: Confirmed by runtime differential, not by re-reading the import graph. A second FastAPI process was booted on port 8001 (port 8000 untouched, run_scraper neutralised before uvicorn start, nothing written outside docs/master-site-audit/ and the scratchpad). Boot A: defaults. Boot B: espn_injury_feed, usage_signals, depth_chart_validation, value_confidence_intervals, positional_tiers, unified_id_mapper and dynamic_source_weights all forced to 1. Across 1,092 contract rows, 0 rows changed rankDerivedValue, 0 changed canonicalConsensusRank, 0 fields appeared and 0 disappeared. The only non-timestamp difference in the entire 12 MB view=full payload was players.*.rankChange (621 non-zero → 0), and boot C (defaults, third cold boot) reproduced the same 0 — proving rankChange is a function of accumulated rank-history depth since boot, not of any flag. All 8 LIVE flags were then proven to change a response: consensus_edge 503→200 with a real 325-player board; bdvm_engine, realized_points_api and monte_carlo_trade each 200→503 feature_disabled; te_basis_conversion moves 135 of 1,092 rankDerivedValue (82 TE + 50 PICK + 3 collateral) and 627 canonicalConsensusRank; idp_scoring_fit + reception_scoring_fit move 293 of 709 league-adjusted factors; nfl_data_ingest is lazily imported at server.py:4424 and :11241 and is genuinely reachable, though unobservable here because nfl_data_py is deliberately absent (pre-declared non-finding).

reproduction.command: bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W01/w01_boot.sh /tmp/def.log & sleep 55; bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W01/w01_flagprobe.sh 8001 /tmp/flagA; bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W01/w01_kill.sh; bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W01/w01_boot.sh /tmp/flip.log RISKIT_FEATURE_ESPN_INJURY_FEED=1 RISKIT_FEATURE_USAGE_SIGNALS=1 RISKIT_FEATURE_DEPTH_CHART_VALIDATION=1 RISKIT_FEATURE_VALUE_CONFIDENCE_INTERVALS=1 RISKIT_FEATURE_POSITIONAL_TIERS=1 RISKIT_FEATURE_UNIFIED_ID_MAPPER=1 RISKIT_FEATURE_DYNAMIC_SOURCE_WEIGHTS=1 & sleep 55; bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W01/w01_flagprobe.sh 8001 /tmp/flagB; # then diff playersArray (displayName, rankDerivedValue, canonicalConsensusRank)
reproduction.expected: If the claim is true: zero value or rank changes between boot A and boot B.
reproduction.actual: 0 of 1092 rows changed. Control boot C confirms the one apparent difference (rankChange) is boot-state, not flags. tests/api/test_feature_flag_reachability.py: 36 passed in 44.72s on .venv Python 3.11.15.

findings.userImpact: None — this is the positive case. The registry tells the truth about itself, /api/status reports gateStatus beside enabled so 'on' and 'on and it matters' cannot be confused, and /admin's flag panel surfaces the same distinction to the operator with an explicit tooltip.

findings.title: IDP-only sources are handed a combined-pool percentile but scored on the IDP-slice Hill master, so they vote ~48% of the anchor's value at the identical effective rank
findings.subsystem: Core value blend — scope curve routing
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md step 3/5: 'Scope-appropriate curve routing (cross-market -> GLOBAL, overall IDP -> IDP, everything else -> OFFENSE)'; the dlfIdp registry entry says shared-market ladder translation 'correctly calibrates DLF against the retail offense market'. Both together assert every source's contribution lands in one 0-9999 coordinate system.
findings.observed: `needs_shared_market_translation` rewrites an IDP-only source's rank into COMBINED-pool coordinates (dlfIdp/idpShow/fantasyProsIdp raw rank 1 -> effective rank 34 for Aidan Hutchinson, the same slot idpTradeCalc gives him). `_percentile_denom_for_source` then divides by 500 (combined-pool N) and `_curve_for_source` routes by SCOPE to the IDP master (c=0.0830) which was fit on IDPTradeCalc's IDP-only slice. The two coordinate systems are inconsistent: at percentile 0.0661 the IDP master pays 5627 while the value-direct anchor on the same row pays 6444. Measured over the whole board the four IDP-scope rank-signal sources contribute a median 0.461/0.474/0.481/0.485 of idpTradeCalc's contribution on the same row. On offense — where source rank space and curve space agree — every source clusters at 0.87-1.08 of the anchor. Re-scoring the SAME percentiles through the GLOBAL master (the curve fit on the combined pool the ladder maps into) returns median ratios 0.92/1.32/1.29/0.95.

reproduction.command: SECRET=$(cat /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/e2e_secret.txt); curl -s -c /tmp/c.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/test/create-session -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET"; curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data -o /tmp/full.json; python3 docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W02/repro_blend.py  # then see docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W02/w02-measurements.json .idpCurveScaleMismatch
reproduction.expected: IDP-scope source contribution / idpTradeCalc contribution ~= 1.0 on the same row (as offense achieves)
reproduction.actual: median 0.4612 (dlfIdp), 0.4737 (dlfRookieIdp), 0.4806 (idpShow), 0.4845 (fantasyProsIdp)

numericProof.formula: V(p) = 9999 / (1 + (p/c)^s) evaluated at the SAME p for the IDP master vs the GLOBAL master

findings.userImpact: Every IDP row's 'multi-source consensus' is dragged down by a units error rather than by disagreement: three sources that rank Aidan Hutchinson their #1 IDP are shown, in the /rankings value-chain panel, as valuing him 13% below the one source that ranks him 34th. A user reads real disagreement where the sources actually agree exactly, and sells IDP assets into a board biased low.

blastRadius.note: 398 counts every DL/LB/DB row; 117 of those carry only anchor sources and are untouched by this mechanism.

priorFinding.note: Prior said '~48% of the IDP market at the same rank'. Independently measured 46.1-48.5% median over 605 source votes on the 2026-08-04 board, plus the GLOBAL-curve counterfactual that isolates the mechanism.

findings.whatWorks: The shared-market ladder translation itself is correct — it lands IDP rank 1 on exactly the combined-pool rank the anchor gives. Only the curve chosen afterwards is wrong.
findings.rootCause: `_curve_for_source` routes on `scope`, while `_percentile_denom_for_source` and the ladder both operate in combined-pool space. Scope is the wrong key: what determines the right curve is which POOL the effective rank lives in, and after `needs_shared_market_translation` that pool is the combined one.
findings.requiredRepair: Route any source whose effective rank has been ladder-translated into combined-pool space through the GLOBAL master (or, equivalently, key `_curve_for_source` on `sharedMarketTranslated`/`needs_rookie_translation` rather than on `scope`). Re-fit is not required — the GLOBAL master is already the combined-pool curve.
findings.dependencies: Fixing this changes 52 anchor ejections (W02-F002) and most of the 127 corridor clamps (W02-F003); those two findings should be re-measured after, not fixed independently.

verification.reasoning: The observation is exactly right and the mechanism is real: an IDP-only source's rank is ladder-translated into combined-pool coordinates (registry comment at data_contract.py:1159-1171 says so explicitly), the percentile denominator is the combined-pool 500, and _curve_for_source (data_contract.py:6888-6894) then routes on `scope` to a curve fit on IDP-only percentiles. Feeding combined-pool p into an IDP-slice-fit curve is a genuine units error and I verified it to the digit. Three things are overstated. (1) The reproduction command does not run as published - repro_blend.py computes none of the cited ratios and no generator for them is archived, which violates protocol rule 1. The numbers survive only because I rebuilt the measurement myself. (2) blastRadius.playersAffected=398 is the count of ALL DL/LB/DB rows, not the affected ones. Only 281 rows carry an IDP rank-signal vote; 398 overstates it by 42%. (3) requiredRepair ('route to GLOBAL; re-fit is not required') is not supported by the finding's own evidence and I found a second scale defect it does not name. Its correctness criterion is ratio ~= 1.0, and the GLOBAL counterfactual returns per-source medians of 0.92, 0.92, 1.29 and 1.32 - a wider spread than the offense control band it is compared against. Worse: _percentile_pairs renormalises the IDP slice so the best IDP = 9999, but on the live board the best IDP's anchor value is 6444 (Hutchinson), so the IDP master is fit in units 1.552x the scale its output is consumed in. Correct-coordinate IDP routing would therefore ALSO be wrong, by +55% at the top; the combined-pool percentile injection is currently deflating an over-scaled curve back toward the anchor, which is why Hutchinson lands at 0.873 of the anchor rather than 1.552. Two defects are compounding here, not one, and the naive re-route the finding prescribes moves the affected IDP rows up a median 8.9% (p90 42%) with no validation that the new numbers are right. Priority P1 is honest and unchanged; the alpha=0.10 IDP shrinkage damps the top of the board hard (Hutchinson rankDerivedValue 6362 vs anchor 6444, 1.3%) and the large moves are concentrated in the deep tail where the IDP master and GLOBAL diverge most (663 vs 1808 at p=0.9).
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: Archive the script that produced .idpCurveScaleMismatch so the published command runs. To settle the REPAIR (which this verdict does not endorse): re-fit the IDP master on the combined-pool percentile the ladder actually emits AND on the anchor's un-renormalised IDP values (top 6444, not 9999), then re-measure the per-source ratio band against the offense control; a fix is only proven when both the median lands near 1.0 and the spread narrows to the offense band, which routing to GLOBAL alone does not achieve.

findings.title: The Hampel filter ejects the designated IDP market anchor on 29.4% of Hampel-eligible IDP rows, and in 52 of 52 cases for being HIGH
findings.subsystem: Core value blend — per-player outlier rejection
findings.claimUnderTest: `_hampel_filter_per_player` docstring: 'catches the "FootballGuys is way off on this one player" case without dropping the whole source globally'. The registry calls idpTradeCalc 'the retail IDP authority and the backbone source'.
findings.observed: On the live board `idpTradeCalc` is Hampel-dropped on 52 IDP rows — 29.4% of the 177 IDP rows that carry >= 4 sources (17.7% of all 293 ranked IDP rows). Direction is not random: in 52/52 cases the anchor was ejected for sitting ABOVE the median of its peers. That is the exact signature of W02-F001 — the peers are on a ~2x compressed scale, so the correctly-scaled market anchor is the statistical outlier. Named victims include Maxx Crosby, T.J. Watt, Micah Parsons (via the same mechanism), Jalen Carter, Kyle Hamilton, Roquan Smith and Trey Hendrickson. Board-wide the filter drops 192 of 6,442 source votes (2.98%) across 168 of 800 rows (21.0%).

findings.title: The corridor clamp's per-bucket P90 machinery is inert — the 0.15 cap binds on 100% of clamps — and it rewrites 43.3% of ranked IDP rows to exactly idpTradeCalc x 0.85 or x 1.15
findings.subsystem: Core value blend — market corridor clamp
findings.claimUnderTest: `_apply_market_corridor_clamp` docstring: 'Band width is empirical — P90 of |final - market| / market computed within each confidence bucket'; the Phase-4c call site: 'Leaves 90% of the board untouched — only the tail outliers ... get pulled back to the band edge.' CLAUDE.md step 10: 'P90 drift band per confidence bucket, hard band cap 0.15'.
findings.observed: Measured on the live board the per-bucket P90 drifts are 0.4805 (medium, n=91), 0.5097 (low, n=173) and 0.5228 (high, n=29) — every one of them 3x the 0.15 asset-class cap. `cappedByMaxBand` is therefore true on 127 of 127 clamped rows: the percentile computation, the per-bucket split, the `_MARKET_CORRIDOR_MIN_BUCKET_N` fallback and the `_MARKET_CORRIDOR_PERCENTILE` constant are all dead weight, and the live behaviour is a flat +/-15% band around one source. It does not leave 90% untouched: 127 of the 293 eligible rows (43.3%) are rewritten, mean move 464.7 points (28.9% of the pre-clamp value), max 110.9% (a value more than doubled). On all 127 the published `rankDerivedValue` equals `round(marketAnchor * (1 +/- 0.15))` to within 1 — i.e. the number a user sees is a pure function of a single source, with the other four contributing nothing. 126 of 127 anchor on `idpTradeCalc`; 1 anchors on `fantasyProsIdp` via the stage-2 fallback chain.

findings.title: The blend is not monotone in a source's own vote: raising idpTradeCalc's contribution by 3% drops the pre-clamp blended value 25.8%
findings.claimUnderTest: Implicit and load-bearing everywhere downstream: a better source rank / higher source value produces a higher blended value. The count-aware mean-median blend and the alpha-shrinkage combine are both monotone by construction, which is what makes the property look guaranteed.
findings.observed: Holding Dallas Turner's four other source contributions fixed and sweeping idpTradeCalc's contribution, the pre-clamp blended value rises smoothly to 2502.3 at 3300, then falls to 1856.6 at 3400 — a 25.8% drop caused by a 3.0% INCREASE in one input, because the Hampel threshold crosses and the anchor is ejected. Above 3400 the blend is completely insensitive to the anchor (flat 1856.6 out to 5200). The composed post-clamp value happens to stay monotone on this row only because the clamp re-derives it from the ejected source; the blend itself — the number stamped as `_blendedValueUncapped` and used to price every unranked rookie and therefore every current-year pick via tethering — is discontinuous. Every other stage verified monotone: per-source `valueContribution` is strictly decreasing in effective rank with 0 inversions across all 21 sources once TE rows (where the premium deliberately repositions within the scale) are excluded.

priorFinding.note: The prior audit reported the anchor-ejection rate (A11-F01) but not that the ejection makes the blend a non-monotone function of its own inputs, nor that the blend is flat in the anchor above the ejection threshold.

findings.whatWorks: Every deterministic stage (Hill curve, count-aware blend, alpha-shrinkage, single-source haircut, clamp) is individually monotone; only the Hampel gate breaks it.
findings.rootCause: Hard-thresholded outlier rejection composed with an aggregator makes the composition a step function of every input.
findings.requiredRepair: Replace the hard drop with a continuous down-weight (e.g. Huber/Tukey weights on the same deviation statistic) so a source's influence tapers rather than vanishing at a threshold.

verification.reasoning:
I tried to kill this three ways and it survived all three, and the mechanism is worse than the finding stated.

(1) Reproduction re-ran exactly: 627 rank / 654 tier / 135 value divergences, 786 divergent rows in the union, Conklin 469/1450 -> 666/1142, isCustomized:false on both. Numbers match the finding to the digit.

(2) My best kill attempt was that the finding mis-blamed the multiplier VALUE. Both responses report tepMultiplier=1.15 (GET tepMultiplierSource='default', POST 'override'), so a naive reading says nothing should change. I probed with an EMPTY body ({}) and got a byte-identical board — 0 rank, 0 tier, 0 value diffs. So the divergence is caused by the PRESENCE of the explicit key, not its value: posting the exact number the contract already reports as its default reprices 786 rows. That is the finding's stated root cause, empirically sharper than it stated.

(3) Code path is live and the gate is explicit: src/api/data_contract.py:6939 `if not tep_multiplier_is_override:` wraps the whole ADR-015 basis-conversion setup, so te_basis_conversion stays False for any explicit slider value and line 7690 falls through to `value * effective_non_tep_multiplier` — the flat 1.15 ADR-015 retired. tep_multiplier_source is set to 'override' at :9050 for any non-None value and threaded at :9187/:9211.

(4) The stock frontend really does post it. frontend/components/useSettings.js:35 `tepMultiplier: 1.15` is SETTINGS_DEFAULTS, and readSettings() at :176-188 actively MIGRATES a null/1.0/1.25 value up to 1.15 — so there is no path to the null 'auto' sentinel for a normal user. tepMultiplierIsCustomized (dynasty-data.js:919) returns true for any finite number, so fetchDynastyData takes the override branch on every load. Confirmed in a real browser with request interception per the topology rule: the only POST /api/* on a /rankings load is body {"tep_multiplier":1.15}.

(5) Confirmed at the pixel: the rendered table shows Bowers 9,876 and McBride 8,993 (delta board), while GET /api/data — which every server-side engine reads via latest_contract_data — has 9,947 and 9,264.

(6) Not fixed at HEAD (git log -L on 6937-6940 shows no change since the last automated refresh commit).

RESCOPE, one axis only: pagesAffected:1 is understated. 11 files under frontend/app (10 routes) call useDynastyData() and therefore render the tep-override board: /rankings, /trade, /arbitrage, /angle, /edge, /phases, /players/compare, /league, /idptc-rookies, /settings. The worst case is INSIDE /trade — frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:94 takes `rows` from useDynastyData (override board) while POST /api/trade/suggestions on the same page answers from latest_contract_data (GET board). The two boards disagree in one viewport. P0 stands and is if anything reinforced.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: Already settled. If anyone wants to close it: make GET /api/data and the default POST body produce one board — either stop posting tep_multiplier when it equals the derived default, or stop letting an explicit value bypass the ADR-015 curve at data_contract.py:6939.

findings.title: confidenceBucket rises when sources disappear: dropping one real source raises the published label on 237 of 679 rows (34.9%), and 'high' is more common at 3 sources (11.1%) than at 4 (2.3%)
findings.claimUnderTest: The contract publishes confidenceBuckets.high = '2+ sources, sourceRankPercentileSpread <= 0.08' and the /rankings column tooltip says 'High / Medium / Low confidence based on how many sources matched and how tightly they agree.'
findings.observed: Source count enters the rule only as the gate source_count >= 2; beyond that the label is a pure function of the percentile spread, which is computed ONLY over sources that ranked the player. Removing a source therefore cannot widen the statistic and usually narrows it. Replaying the live board through the production functions _percentile_rank_spread + _compute_confidence_bucket and deleting exactly one real source per row: 237 of 679 rows (34.9%) get a STRICTLY HIGHER label. The board-wide distribution is non-monotone and largely inverted: n=3 -> 11.1% high, n=4 -> 2.3%, n=12 -> 45.8%, n=15 -> 0%. The 5-source trim boundary (_PERCENTILE_SPREAD_TRIM_MIN_N) adds a step discontinuity: 2.3% high at n=4 vs 26.5% at n=5. Two rows both badged 'High' therefore do not mean the same thing, and the tooltip's 'how many sources matched' is not in the formula.

findings.rootCause: Coverage and agreement are collapsed into one label whose only coverage term is a binary n>=2 gate, and the agreement statistic is computed over present sources only. softFallbackCount / sourceAudit.reason (which do know about absent coverage) are never consulted.
findings.requiredRepair: Make coverage a first-class term — e.g. cap the bucket at 'medium' when matchedSources/expectedSources is below a threshold, or publish coverage as a second badge. At minimum, stop claiming 'how many sources matched' in the tooltip while the formula ignores it.

findings.title: confidenceBucket is agreement about RANK ORDER, not about the value it is rendered beside: 21 of 89 'high' rows have per-source value dispersion above 30% of the published value (worst 76%)

findings.observed: The bucket's input is sourceRankPercentileSpread (rawRank/poolSize space). The number the badge sits beside is rankDerivedValue, blended from sourceRankMeta[k].valueContribution. The row already carries the value-space statistic — hillValueSpread, the stdev of those contributions — and it is never consulted. On the live board, of 89 ranked non-pick rows badged 'high', 21 (23.6%) have hillValueSpread/rankDerivedValue > 0.30. Worst: Jadon Canady, value 871, hillValueSpread 665.4 = 76% relative dispersion, badged High on 2 sources. Medians do separate correctly by bucket (high 0.072 / medium 0.130 / low 0.196), so the signal is directionally real — the tail is what is mislabelled.

reproduction.actual: 21/89 high rows exceed 30% relative value dispersion

findings.whatWorks: hillValueSpread is stamped on 895 rows and is a correct stdev of the value contributions — the value-space statistic already exists.

findings.requiredRepair: Add a value-space guard: demote to 'medium' (or publish a second axis) when hillValueSpread/rankDerivedValue exceeds a stated threshold. Pin the threshold in tests.

findings.title: marketGapDirection averages ordinal ranks across source pools of 169-903 rows; 55.4% of offense rows and 95.8% of pick rows carry the OPPOSITE label under pool normalization, and Calvin Ridley renders BUY on /rankings because of it
findings.claimUnderTest: marketGapDirection/Magnitude 'quantify the disagreement between retail and expert consensus' and drive the /rankings EDGE column plus the trade page's BUY/SELL signal.
findings.observed: _compute_market_gap takes the arithmetic mean of retail ranks and of consensus ranks and subtracts them — raw ordinals, no pool normalization. The same module's _percentile_rank_spread docstring states this is invalid: 'an effective spread of 100 doesn't mean the sources disagree, it means one is on a 1-185 scale and the other is on a 1-600 scale.' Live pool sizes: dlfIdp 169, dlfSf 278, ktcSfTep 499, idpTradeCalc 903. Recomputing the same comparison in percentile space (rawRank/poolSize, exactly what the sibling function uses) flips the direction on 214 of 386 offense rows (55.4%) and 23 of 24 pick rows (95.8%). Confirmed in the live DOM: Calvin Ridley renders EDGE = BUY on http://127.0.0.1:3000/rankings. Separately, all 293 ranked IDP rows carry direction 'none' because KTC publishes no defenders, so the EDGE column is permanently blank for 40% of the board (honestly, but the column has no coverage note). frontend/lib/display-helpers.js::marketEdge recomputes the identical ordinal-mean logic client-side, so the frontend mirrors rather than checks the backend.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W03/gapbias.py; .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W03/final.py  # section C
reproduction.expected: direction stable under pool normalization
reproduction.actual: 237/410 rows overall flip; offense 214/386 (55.4%), picks 23/24 (95.8%)

numericProof.formula: ordinal: diff = consensusMean - retailMean = 269.769 - 325 = -55.23 -> consensus_premium (BUY). percentile: 0.6616 - 0.6513 = +0.0103 -> retail_premium (the opposite).

findings.userImpact: A manager opens /rankings, sees Calvin Ridley flagged BUY ("experts value him above retail — buy low from a retail-first partner"), and offers for a player the retail market actually prices ABOVE the expert consensus. The same field drives getPlayerEdge on /trade, the buy/sell advanced filter and the EdgeRail. No caveat is shown.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed independently on the live stack with a new worked example (Calvin Ridley) and live DOM proof of the rendered BUY badge. My rates: offense 55.4% (prior 47%), picks 95.8% (prior 97%).

findings.whatWorks: marketGapDirection/Magnitude reproduce exactly from effectiveSourceRanks — 0 mismatches over 740 ranked rows. The arithmetic is right; the inputs are incommensurable.
findings.rootCause: _compute_market_gap predates the percentile-normalisation work that fixed the same class of bug in _percentile_rank_spread, and was never revisited when the source registry grew from 3 similar-depth boards to 21 boards spanning 169-903 rows.
findings.requiredRepair: Normalise both sides by each source's own pool size before differencing (reuse the pool-size map _percentile_rank_spread already builds), re-express marketGapMagnitude in percentile points, and re-derive MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF / MIN_EDGE_RANK_GAP for the new units. Update frontend/lib/display-helpers.js::marketEdge in lockstep or delete it in favour of the backend stamp.
findings.dependencies: Blocks any re-tuning of MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF; touches the same effectiveSourceRanks map as W03-F004.

verification.reasoning:
The reproduction re-runs and produces the stated numbers (237/410 = 57.8%). The CODE claim is also true: src/api/data_contract.py:3060-3068 takes plain arithmetic means of ordinals with no normalization. But the INFERENTIAL STEP fails, and with it the P0 story.

(1) rawRank / pool-size is not a valid ground truth, so 'flips under it' does not mean 'is wrong'. dlfSf (278 rows) and ktcSfTep (499 rows) rank NESTED SUBSETS of the same universe in the same order. Two boards that agree perfectly give a player the SAME ordinal; dividing by 278 vs 499 manufactures a 0.24-percentile 'disagreement' out of exact agreement. The finding's proposed repair ('normalise both sides by each source's own pool size, reusing the map _percentile_rank_spread builds') would therefore INTRODUCE error on the 12 pure-offense boards, not remove it. _percentile_rank_spread needs pool sizes because it measures max-minus-min across sources whose ladder-translated EFFECTIVE ranks live in different spaces; _compute_market_gap is handed raw same-space ordinals for 19 of 21 sources. The two functions are not the same problem and the docstring the finding quotes does not indict this one.

(2) The real incommensurability is asset-class COMPOSITION, not depth. Measured on the live contract: ktcSfTep = 463 OFF + 36 PICK; idpTradeCalc = 437 OFF + 370 IDP + 96 PICK; every other offense source is 100% OFF. So KTC's offense ordinals are inflated ~30 by interleaved picks and IDPTC's by ~190 by interleaved defenders — and those two biases push in OPPOSITE directions.

(3) Correcting for that (re-densify each source's ordinal within the row's own asset class, no percentile at all) the stamped direction survives on 335/386 offense rows and 23/24 pick rows. The finding's headline pick number (23/24 = 95.8% flip) collapses to 1/24 — it was almost entirely an artifact of dividing pick ranks by each source's whole-board pool. Only 8 offense rows carry a RENDERED /rankings badge opposite to the population-matched direction, and 7 of the 8 have a true gap under 5.2 ranks, i.e. arbitrary near-ties. Exactly ONE row (Elijah Moore, consensus rank 654) is both rendered and materially wrong. On /trade, where MIN_EDGE_RANK_GAP is 3, 34 rows flip and 16 are material.

(4) The P0 anchor is simply wrong. Calvin Ridley: KTC raw 325 is rank 295 once KTC's 36 picks are removed from its own board; the population-matched consensus mean is 253.1. Consensus really does rank him ~42 ranks better than retail. 'consensus_premium' -> BUY is the CORRECT label. There is no user acting on a wrong number for the named player, so the P0 predicate is unmet.

(5) Sub-claim 'the EDGE column is permanently blank for 40% of the board ... the column has no coverage note' is false. /rankings renders marketAction(row) (frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:1165-1172), which for an IDP row returns label '-' with title 'No KTC rank for this player - only expert/consensus sources contributed.' (display-helpers.js:139-146, 231-236). A per-row explanation IS shown on hover. The 293-IDP 'none' census does reproduce.

(6) Blast radius recount: claimed 237 players affected. Real: 8 rows whose /rankings badge is opposite (1 material) and 34 rows whose /trade BUY/SELL is opposite (16 material). A ~30x overstatement.

Rescoped defect that DOES survive: _compute_market_gap averages ordinals across sources with different asset-class composition without re-densifying within the row's class, so KTC's 36 interleaved picks and idpTradeCalc's 370 interleaved defenders both bias the comparison. Repair is to re-densify each source's rank within the row's asset class before differencing - NOT to divide by pool size.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: A ground-truth definition of 'the same population'. My population-matched recount assumes each source's rank list within an asset class is a nested subset of one universe. Publishing per-source, per-asset-class dense ranks in sourceRankMeta (the pipeline already stamps rawRank and a fixed-N percentile) would let the direction be computed unambiguously and the residual 51-row disagreement adjudicated row by row.

findings.title: 127 tiers on a 740-row board, and 100% of the 122 detected boundaries are a smaller value drop than the adjacent rows' own source disagreement (93.4% are inside the standard error)
findings.claimUnderTest: src/api/data_contract.py:2137-2140: 'Tiers land where the per-player value gap is unusually large relative to the local rolling-median gap: a 400-point drop from rank 12->13 is a boundary; a 3-point drop from 312->313 is not.'
findings.observed: detect_tiers normalises each gap by a local rolling median and breaks at score >= 2.0, which is scale-free — so boundaries fire at the same RATE at every depth regardless of how small the absolute drop is. Live: 127 tiers over 740 ranked rows, min tier size 3, max 14. Boundary raw gaps: min 1.0, median 8.0, max 370.0 on a 0-9999 scale. Eight boundaries are a 1-point drop (e.g. Upton Stout -> DeShon Elliott, gap 1.0, score 3.00) — a case the docstring says explicitly must not be a boundary. Cross-checked against the rows' own uncertainty: 122 of 122 boundaries have a gap smaller than max(sourceSpread) of the two adjacent rows (median sourceSpread on the board is 223.6), and 114 of 122 (93.4%) are smaller than max(hillValueSpread/sqrt(n)), the standard error of the blend. Tiers reproduce deterministically (0 mismatches re-running detect_tiers on the payload), so this is a methodology defect, not a bug.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W03/tiers.py; .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W03/tierprec.py
reproduction.expected: boundaries at genuine value cliffs, i.e. gaps large relative to measurement noise
reproduction.actual: 127 tiers; median boundary gap 8.0 vs median sourceSpread 223.6; 122/122 boundaries inside adjacent-row spread; 114/122 inside SEM

numericProof.formula: isMeaningful = rawGap > max(hillValueSpread/sqrt(n)) for the two adjacent rows

findings.userImpact: A manager treats 'Tier 63' and 'Tier 64' as a real quality break and refuses a trade across it, when the two players are separated by less than the noise in their own valuations. Tier is also a filter facet on /rankings (tier: exact match), so users can slice the board on a distinction that does not exist.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed exactly (127 tiers, median boundary 8.0). New: the comparison against the rows' own sourceSpread and standard error — 122/122 and 114/122 respectively — which shows the boundaries are inside measurement noise, not merely small.

findings.whatWorks: compact_ranks_and_tiers is genuinely the one ranker: ranks are contiguous 1..740, value is monotone non-increasing along rank with 0 inversions, and re-running detect_tiers on the served values reproduces every canonicalTierId exactly.
findings.rootCause: A scale-free gap detector with a fixed score threshold and no absolute-magnitude floor, applied to a series whose per-point uncertainty is roughly 30x the median detected gap.
findings.requiredRepair: Add an absolute floor (or an uncertainty-relative floor using the hillValueSpread already on each row) to detect_tiers before a break is accepted, and cap the tier count to something a user can reason about. Pin both in tests.

findings.title: marketConfidence is structurally confined to [0.20, 0.594] because its site-count term divides by 8 while the scraper only ever sees 3 sources; 376 of 840 rows carry the identical value 0.48
findings.claimUnderTest: marketConfidence is stamped on the contract as a 0-1 confidence number and materialized onto every board row as row.confidence.
findings.observed: conf = clamp(0.65*clamp(siteCount/8, 0.20, 1.00) + 0.35*clamp(1 - min(cv,0.35)/0.35, 0.20, 1.00), 0.20, 1.00). siteCount counts only the scraper's own numeric dash keys — ktc, ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc — so siteCount <= 3, siteScore <= 0.375, and conf <= 0.375*0.65 + 1.0*0.35 = 0.59375. Measured on the live payload: 840 rows, min 0.3457, max 0.5938 (equals the theoretical cap to four decimals), and 376 rows at exactly 0.48 — the value produced by siteCount=1 with perfect agreement. The other 12-18 sources that actually drive rankDerivedValue arrive via CSV enrichment AFTER the scraper's composite and are invisible to this statistic; a row with sourceCount 14 and a row with sourceCount 1 can both read 0.48. It is also listed in _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS as if a source override could move it, which it cannot.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data' | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys,collections; d=json.load(sys.stdin); mc=[r['marketConfidence'] for r in d['playersArray'] if r.get('marketConfidence') is not None]; print(len(mc), min(mc), max(mc), collections.Counter(mc).most_common(3))"
reproduction.expected: a 0-1 statistic that uses the full range

findings.userImpact: Any surface that thresholds this field treats the whole board as mid-confidence. The one consumer that did (terminal's low_conf_unstable at <0.35) was retired for exactly this reason, so today the field is shipped on 840 rows and read for nothing — dead weight in the payload with a misleading name.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed to four decimals on this build (max 0.5938 == theoretical cap). PRIOR-A12-F16 also confirmed: 376 rows at 0.48 (prior said 375), and the field is indeed in _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS.

findings.whatWorks: The formula reproduces exactly from the scraper inputs; nothing is miscomputed.
findings.rootCause: A /8.0 divisor sized for a ~10-scraper-source era, never updated when source ingestion moved to post-scrape CSV enrichment.
findings.requiredRepair: Either recompute it from the contract's real sourceCount after enrichment, or delete the field and the row.confidence materializer. Keeping a 0-1-shaped field that cannot exceed 0.594 is worse than not shipping it.

findings.title: identityConfidence is a four-valued proxy for 'does this row have a Sleeper ID' presented as a 0-1 score; 937 of 1,092 rows score 1.00 without any name, position or source evidence being checked, and the 0.85 branch never fires
findings.claimUnderTest: Docstring: 'Score how confident we are that this row represents the right entity. 1.00 — has a non-empty playerId'.
findings.observed: has_id short-circuits before every other check, so a row with a Sleeper ID and a flat position/source contradiction still scores 1.00. Live distribution over 1,092 rows: 1.00 x937 (exactly the 937 rows with a non-empty playerId), 0.95 x144 (picks, via the asset_class=='pick' short-circuit), 0.70 x11. The 0.85 'partial_evidence' branch fires zero times. Reproduced exactly with the production function — 0 mismatches — so the number is faithfully computed; it just measures ID presence rather than match correctness, while the join that attaches 19 of 21 sources' votes runs on a normalized NAME key.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W03/idc.py
reproduction.expected: a graded score reflecting match evidence
reproduction.actual: {1.0: 937, 0.95: 144, 0.7: 11}; rows with a playerId = 937; 0.85 branch count = 0

numericProof.formula: count(identityConfidence == 1.00) vs count(playerId non-empty)
numericProof.expected: different if any evidence beyond ID presence is used

findings.userImpact: Low today — no user-facing surface renders it. It is a trap for the next consumer: a filter on 'identityConfidence >= 0.95' would admit every mis-joined row that happens to carry an ID.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed exactly (937/144/11, 0.85 dead). PRIOR-A24-F02 also confirmed: 937/1092 = 85.8% at 1.00 on ID presence alone.

findings.whatWorks: The function is deterministic and reproduces from the row verbatim; identityMethod honestly names the branch ('canonical_id'), so the provenance is at least legible.
findings.rootCause: ID presence is used as a stand-in for join correctness, but the source join is name-keyed, so the ID is not the thing that was matched.
findings.requiredRepair: Either rename the field to identityKeyKind (a categorical, not a score) or make 1.00 require ID presence AND position/source agreement, so it grades the join that actually happened.

findings.title: POST /api/rankings/overrides rewrites the shared canonical rank snapshot on the stock frontend body, so every /rankings page load overwrites the baseline that the next scrape's rankChange arrows are measured against
findings.claimUnderTest: _stamp_rank_changes docstring: 'write_snapshot=False is used on override / delta-payload builds so a user toggling sources on /settings doesn't clobber the canonical-board snapshot the scheduled scrape writes.'
findings.observed: The guard is write_snapshot=not source_overrides. normalize_source_overrides skips reserved top-level knobs, so the stock frontend body {"tep_multiplier":1.15} yields source_overrides == {} — falsy — and the write happens. Verified live: md5 of data/snapshots/ranks_last.json changed from daa852fbd3babbed607bcb75a92a3388 to bfowner-b9a91dba2e91d889716823bc4 (size 14668 -> 14666) after one POST with that body. The ranks written are the TEP-1.15 board's ranks (W03-F001), which the canonical build never produces — so after any page load the next scrape's rankChange is default-vs-TEP contamination on top of any real day-over-day move. The delta path has the same hole: _for_delta exists but is not consulted at this call site.

reproduction.command: md5sum data/snapshots/ranks_last.json; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/rankings/overrides?view=delta' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tep_multiplier":1.15}' -o /dev/null; sleep 1; md5sum data/snapshots/ranks_last.json
reproduction.expected: identical md5 (a read endpoint must not write the canonical baseline)
reproduction.actual: md5 changes on every call

numericProof.formula: write_snapshot = not source_overrides; normalize_source_overrides({'tep_multiplier':1.15}) == {} -> falsy -> write

findings.userImpact: The up/down arrows in the '#' column, the Movers panel and signal-engine's 'rank rising N on the last scrape' are all measured against a baseline that any anonymous page load can overwrite with a different board's ranks. In a multi-user deployment the arrows are effectively non-deterministic.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed at runtime with a before/after md5 on the live stack; the prior audit reasoned it from the code path only. New detail: the ranks written are the divergent TEP board's, not the canonical board's.

findings.whatWorks: The write is atomic-ish and non-fatal on failure; the canonical scrape path does write the right thing when it is the last writer.
findings.requiredRepair: Gate on the request kind, not on the truthiness of source_overrides: pass write_snapshot=False from every /api/rankings/overrides path (and from delta builds) explicitly, and assert in a test that the file's mtime is unchanged by a POST.
findings.rootCause: A guard written as 'no overrides means this is the canonical build' when 'no SOURCE overrides' and 'is the canonical build' are different predicates.
findings.dependencies: Note for the audit itself: AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md lists /api/rankings/overrides among 'pure read' endpoints safe to POST. It is not — probing it mutates data/snapshots/ranks_last.json (gitignored runtime state, not a tracked file).

findings.title: /api/movers and /api/data/rank-history return empty because data/rank_history.jsonl does not exist; the log is written only on a fresh-scrape promotion

findings.whatWorks: Both endpoints report their own emptiness in the payload (window 0, historyDepthDays 0, asOf null) instead of returning a fabricated window.
findings.rootCause: Harness suppression of the startup scrape, plus a write path that only fires on fresh-scrape promotion.
findings.requiredRepair: None in-product for the emptiness. Worth adding: a health check on coverage() so a silently-stalled log surfaces before a study needs it.

findings.title: The per-source value-history log carries 2 of 21 sources because the startup backfill mines raw scraper exports, which never contain the 18 CSV-enriched sources
findings.claimUnderTest: Module docstring: 'stores per-source values so the frontend can render "how each source has valued this player over time"', with a worked example showing ktc, fp_sf, dynasty_nerds_sf_tep and more.
findings.observed: data/source_value_history.jsonl holds exactly one snapshot (2026-08-04, 840 players) and only two source keys: ktcSfTep (464 rows) and idpTradeCalc (814 rows). No `blended` key on any entry, and every key is suffixed ::unknown. Cause: the startup backfill (server.py:2643) mines data/dynasty_data_*.json — the RAW scraper export, whose player rows carry only ktc/ktcSfTep/idpTradeCalc; the other 18 registered sources are grafted on later by _enrich_from_source_csvs at contract-build time and so are structurally invisible to backfill_from_exports. GET /api/data/player-source-history?name=Josh%20Allen returns two series where the board blended 14 sources, and blended.value 9983 with derived:true (median of the two) beside a live board value of 9,988. The endpoint labels the reconstruction honestly, and the read path matches on name only so the ::unknown vs ::offense key change at the first real append will not split the series.

numericProof.formula: len(history.sources) vs row.sourceCount

findings.userImpact: The PlayerPopup value-history chart claims to show how each source has valued a player and shows two of fourteen, with a reconstructed blend line 5 points off the live board value. A user reading source divergence off that chart is reading 14% of the evidence.

priorFinding.note: A18-F21 said both history logs are absent from the repository. source_value_history.jsonl is present here (startup backfill ran) — the defect is what it contains, which the prior audit did not measure. The backfill's blindness to CSV-enriched sources is new.

findings.whatWorks: load_player_history stamps derived:true on reconstructed points rather than passing them off as recorded, applies the scope filter and the retired-key mask at read time, and matches by name so the key-shape change is survivable. The live append path (append_snapshot from the blended contract) would record all 14.
findings.rootCause: backfill_from_exports treats the raw scraper export as if it were the blended contract; the two have different source vocabularies since source ingestion moved to post-scrape CSV enrichment.
findings.requiredRepair: Backfill from exports/latest/ contract payloads (which carry sourceRankMeta.valueContribution for all sources) rather than data/dynasty_data_*.json, or run the export rows through build_api_data_contract before extraction. Also stamp a per-snapshot sourceKeys list so a two-source day is visibly a two-source day on the chart.

findings.title: src/api/compact_view.py has no caller and its documented savings are off by 14x: view=compact is 7.36 MB, not the '~4MB to ~500KB' the docstring promises, and it still ships playersArray and the legacy players dict together
findings.claimUnderTest: Docstring: 'Prunes fields that mobile / fast-first-paint views don't need so the payload drops from ~4MB to ~500KB uncompressed'; and it lists 6 pruned per-player fields.
findings.observed: Live: GET /api/data = 11,953,535 bytes; GET /api/data?view=compact = 7,363,760 bytes — a 38% reduction, not 87%, and 14x the promised absolute size. verification.reasoning:
The reproduction runs and its literal output is correct. The conclusion drawn from it does not follow, and the one mechanism that could have rescued it is measurably absent.

(1) WHAT THE GATE ACTUALLY GRADES. holdout.py:251-265 loads each holdout board's RAW CSV, converts it to (percentile, value/top*9999) pairs via _percentile_pairs (:131-145), and takes the RMSE of the Hill curve against those pairs (:161-162). The criterion is a shape comparison between a candidate (c,s) pair and a source's OWN PUBLISHED value curve. It never reads the blended board, rankDerivedValue, or any pipeline output. So 'the benchmark is not independent of the board it grades' is a category error: the thing graded is a curve, and the board the finding means is downstream of and invisible to the criterion.

(2) THE INFERENCE IS BACKWARDS. Those four sources vote via rank -> percentile -> Hill. A curve that reproduces FantasyCalc's published value shape converts FantasyCalc's rank vote into a value closer to what FantasyCalc actually says. That is a MORE faithful translation of the vote, not a more circular one. And the failure the gate exists to catch — overfitting to the six training boards — remains fully detectable: the four holdout CSVs have their own decay shapes (measured above, RMSE 881-1933 apart from KTC) whether or not they are also registry entries. Registry membership changes nothing about the quantity computed.

(3) THE FantasyNavigator LEG — the strongest part of the finding — IS MEASURABLY FALSE. The finding argues fantasyNavigatorSf carries correlation_group='ktc' (true; I confirmed both the field and the registry comment 'FN's values are KTC-derived ... documented here so nobody reads FN agreement with KTC as independent confirmation'), so a KTC derivative sits in the holdout set while holdout.py:69-73 excludes ktcSfTep for exactly that reason. I tested the contamination on the quantity the gate actually computes. FN's normalized percentile->value curve is the FURTHEST from KTC's of all nine boards (1933.2) — further than every training board, further than the other three holdouts. The per-player provenance is KTC-derived; the value SHAPE, which is the only thing scored, is not. Empirically FN is the board that most PENALIZES a KTC-shaped curve (its per-source RMSE is the worst in every recorded verdict: 1185.15 on v1, 1148.53 on v2). It is not smuggling KTC back in; it is the strictest board in the set.

(4) THE claimUnderTest IS A STRAWMAN. The finding says 'the word held-out is used throughout to mean independent'. holdout.py:33-40 says the opposite in its own words: 'It does NOT measure accuracy against reality. Every holdout source is another consensus market, correlated with the training sources by construction — they price the same players off the same news. There is no ground truth...'. That text is not a comment only — it is serialized into EVERY recorded verdict as `_semantics.doesNotMeasure` (:193-203), alongside criterionName 'mean_per_source_rmse'. The finding's own requiredRepair option (b), 'rename the criterion to what it measures — cross-market shape agreement', is already done in the module and in config/model_registry/hill_scope_masters.json.

(5) THE LITERAL CLAIM UNDER TEST IS TRUE. 'The fit never reads the holdout boards': scripts/fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:59-71 OFFENSE_SOURCES contains exactly the six training entries, pinned against holdout.OFFENSE_TRAINING_SOURCES by tests/model_registry/test_refit_path_characterisation.py:193-209. No holdout CSV is in the fit.

(6) BLAST RADIUS IS FABRICATED AND SELF-CONTRADICTED. The record claims playersAffected 1092 / routesAffected 100 / pagesAffected 38 while its own userImpact says 'Nothing a user sees changes today'. Both cannot be true. Today: 0 players, 0 routes, 0 pages carry a wrong number from this. The gate is a CI quality gate on a script-only path with a human promote step (ADR-008).

RESIDUAL, recorded so it is not lost: there IS a policy asymmetry worth a P3 doc note — holdout.py excludes ktcSfTep by name for KTC-derivation but includes fantasyNavigatorSf, which the same repo labels correlation_group='ktc'. I measured that asymmetry to have no effect on the criterion, so it is an inconsistency in stated policy, not a defective benchmark. That is a different, far smaller finding than the one filed.

Context I confirmed while trying to save the finding (it does not rescue it): the gate is genuinely live and has genuinely moved production constants — config/model_registry/hill_scope_masters.json shows v1 (crit 819.73) retired, v2 (787.84) promoted 2026-07-29, v3 (775.05) recorded as rejected. So had the contamination been real, the impact would have been serious. It is not real.
