verification.reasoning:
The reproduction runs verbatim and returns exactly the stated dict, so the OBSERVATION survives. The CONCLUSION and the root cause do not.

(1) The attribution is wrong. The finding frames this as a stale holdout SELECTION ('the holdout set was chosen when the four boards were value-direct and never revisited'). I ran the identical rank-signal test against OFFENSE_TRAINING_SOURCES and got the same answer: 4 of the 6 TRAINING boards (dynastyDaddySf, dynastyNerdsSfTep, yahooBoone, fantasyProsFitzmaurice) are also rank-signal in the live blend, and dynastyDaddySf/yahooBoone/fantasyProsFitzmaurice were demoted for the SAME Hampel reason quoted in the finding (61%->0%, 47%->~2%, 19%->~0%, data_contract.py:377-380). Only 2 of 8 boards on either side of the split feed a value the blend reads value-direct (_VALUE_BASED_SOURCES = {ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc}, neither of which is in either set — ktcSfTep is deliberately excluded, holdout.py:67-72). So this is not a train/holdout independence defect; it is a property of the entire Hill methodology, which by design learns the market's value-decay SHAPE from published value boards and then applies that shape to ordinal ranks. The shape has to be estimated from published values somewhere.

(2) The demotion rationale is over-read. The registry comments say FantasyCalc/OTCFFB values, normalized as raw/site_max*9999, landed OUTSIDE the Hampel window on a majority of rows relative to the consensus. That is a statement that the boards disagree with the consensus about decay, not that the codebase 'declared their decay systematically wrong' — holdout.py's own docstring (lines 33-40) says explicitly that no check here can establish which is correct. The finding converts a measured disagreement into a settled verdict.

(3) 'boards whose values it deletes' is false. data_contract.py:381-384 and 419-421: 'The value column is preserved via sourceNativeValues for audit / display / trade-finder use.' They are excluded from the blend, not deleted.

(4) The blast radius is fabricated. routesAffected 100 is the entire openapi census; pagesAffected 38 is the entire page census. holdout.py is imported only by scripts/model_registry.py, scripts/auto_refit_hill_curves.py, src/model_registry/* and tests. `grep -rn 'model_registry' server.py src/api/*.py` returns nothing — no request path reaches it. It touches production only through a human running promote+apply, which has happened exactly once (v1->v2).

What survives, narrowly: the promotion criterion is a mean of four per-source RMSEs, and it is dominated by the two boards whose decay is least like the consensus (FantasyNavigator 1149, OTCFFB 992, vs PFKDynasty 244 in the live v2 record). A promotion therefore optimizes partly toward decay shapes the blend rejects as votes. That is a legitimate criterion-design concern about a script-only, human-gated tool with no measured effect on any number served today.

'Every IDP value on /rankings moved by up to -34.6% (-23.9% at rank 200, -15.0% at rank 100)' — those three figures are the Hill function's own delta at fixed percentiles, and I reproduce them exactly. They are not what the board did. Rebuilding the live contract with the IDP pair reverted: 183 of 287 IDP rows changed, MEAN -2.69%, and only 25 rows moved more than 10%. The maximum was -33.5% on exactly one player. The observations re-run and are true. The conclusion built on them does not follow, and its sharpest specific claim is falsified by experiment.

WHAT SURVIVES (all re-verified): the four constant-tuning reports do all optimize mean absolute change in canonicalConsensusRank (backtest_blend_params.md:6, alpha_lambda:'Metric: value-weighted rank change', alpha_shrinkage, percentile_reference_n, soft_fallback). backtest_blend_params.md:8 really does say 'Lower = more stable = probably better-calibrated' — an unearned inference in a committed report. 1. 'Three of five constants do not even match the recommendation their own report produced, WITH NO NOTE ANYWHERE SAYING WHY.' False for all three. alpha: data_contract.py:5375-5395 is an 18-line comment naming the alpha=0 stability optimum, calling it 'product-bad' verbatim, citing docs/architecture/optimization-target.md, and stating the chosen cell (alpha=0.10, lambda=0.10, VW 0.299) as 'the cheapest non-degenerate joint point'. lambda: :5402-5429 documents the 2026-04-20 retirement and the reason (double-damping on the same signal). N: :5297-5303 gives the structural reason ('500 aligns with KTC's native pool'), echoed in CLAUDE.md. The finding read the standalone reports and not the constants.

2. 'N ships 500 against its own 400 recommendation' — I tested whether 400 is actually the better value under the repo's DECLARED target. tests/canonical/test_ktc_reconciliation.py imports _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N; with N=400 it fails 9 of 13, blowing the pinned tolerance bands (rank 200 at -20.4pp against a +/-10pp band, rank 400 value 996 -> 794). N=500 is not unexplained drift from a recommendation — it is the value that satisfies an enforced gate the churn metric does not measure. Adopting the finding's implied fix would break production calibration.

3. 'stability was adopted as a proxy and then read as if it were the target' — the opposite is documented. docs/architecture/optimization-target.md declares 'market consensus fit' with per-rank tolerance bands (+/-2pp ranks 1-50, +/-3pp 100-150, +/-10pp 200-400), pinned in the test above, and has a section 'What this target is NOT optimizing for' whose first bullet is 'Predictive accuracy on future trades — that would require a labeled trade corpus we don't have.' src/model_registry/holdout.py:26-41 says the same in its own docstring ('It does NOT measure accuracy against reality... Anyone citing these numbers must say which of those two claims they are making'). The alpha comment invokes that declared target BY NAME to reject the stability optimum. A repo that names its proxy, states its limits, and overrides the proxy when it conflicts with the declared target is not one that mistook the proxy for the target.

4. numericProof is invalid as constructed. expected=5 ('every shipped value equals its report's recommendation') is not a defensible expectation when the joint report — the later, authoritative one — explicitly instructs the reader NOT to take the standalone optima (alpha >= ~0.05, lambda >= ~0.05). Live alpha=0.10 SATISFIES that guidance, so the '1 of 5' count is wrong on its own terms.

5. Status and severity. No wrong number is demonstrated anywhere. blastRadius 1092 players / 100 routes / 38 pages is 'the whole board depends on the blend', which is trivially true of any constant and is not defect impact. Rescoping to P3 documentation/methodology hygiene, scoped to what actually survives: one overclaiming sentence in backtest_blend_params.md:8, three of four reports printing 'Promote X' without carrying the joint report's caveat, one genuinely untuned constant (MIN_FULL_COVERAGE_DEPTH=60), and the absence of a realized-outcome validation the repo already documents as unavailable. verification.reasoning:
The reproduction runs verbatim and every number in it is right, and I strengthened it: the finding asserts the 18 extra sources come from today's tree but never proved they are absent from the snapshot. They are - the archive's _canonicalSiteValues carries exactly three keys across all 1,074 players (idpTradeCalc 814, ktc 464, ktcSfTep 464), so the other 18 voters can only have come from CSVs/site_raw/ at the paths hardcoded at data_contract.py:279-470. pfkDynasty.csv and fantasyNavigatorSf.csv were first ADDED to the tree on 2026-08-03; they could not have contributed to any board served on 2026-07-14, yet they vote in its 'replay'. That is an airtight temporal leak, and all three cited backtest scripts do exactly this (backtest_alpha_shrinkage.py:71, backtest_soft_fallback.py:69, backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py:118-121 all call build_api_data_contract on a loaded snapshot). The reports and the player_valuation.py 'served board' comment exist as quoted (reports/*.md:3 'Snapshot count: 25'; src/canonical/player_valuation.py:71-76).

What I am rescoping is the SCOPE and SEVERITY, both of which are inflated to the point of being unusable.

(1) blastRadius {playersAffected 1092, routesAffected 100, pagesAffected 38} is a category error. It counts the entire site because the value model is unvalidated. No route serves a backtest; no page renders one; not one number a user sees changes if every report in reports/ is deleted. The artifacts actually affected are 7 files in reports/, 3 scripts in scripts/, 2 source comments, and the tuning PROVENANCE of alpha=0.10 / lambda / _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N. Severity without an honest blastRadius is rejected by the protocol's own rule 4, and this one would survive merge as '100 routes affected'.

(2) The strongest single instance the finding cites is the weakest one in impact. The player_valuation.py 'served board' comment sits directly under a header (lines 55-58) reading 'RECONSTRUCTION-ONLY. Nothing on the live valuation path evaluates these' - HILL_MIDPOINT/HILL_SLOPE are not live constants. And the primary fit that comment describes IS against a served board: backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py defaults to exports/latest and rebuilds it with today's CSVs on the same day, which reproduces what was served. Only the trailing '16 archived snapshots spanning 07-16 -> 07-30' STABILITY claim is a counterfactual. So 'the word served is false' is true of one clause, not of the sentence.

(3) Where the leak does bite is alpha-shrinkage / MAD-lambda / percentile-reference-N, which ARE live constants, and there the finding's real point is sharper than it states it: with 18 of 21 sources frozen at today's values across every 'snapshot', consecutive-day deltas are driven almost entirely by the 3 sources that ARE archived, so a stability result is close to guaranteed by construction. The conclusion that these reports cannot support a tuning decision follows. The conclusion that 'NO model in this repository may be described as validated' does not - the finding's own whatWorks concedes src/model_registry/board_holdout.py scores against realized 2025 points, and per CLAUDE.md that is the path the promotion gate actually runs on.

(4) Priority: P1 is not defensible for a defect with zero user-facing surface. Nobody acts on a wrong number; the served board may be entirely correct. This is a validation-integrity and documentation defect - real, worth fixing, and correctly scoped as P2. The requiredRepair (write playersArray into exports, archive all 21 CSVs per snapshot, give build_api_data_contract an optional site_raw root) is sound and I would keep it verbatim, including the last line - no backtest in reports/ should be cited as evidence until it lands.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: One export written with playersArray embedded, replayed through a build_api_data_contract given a site_raw root pointing at that snapshot's own CSVs: if the replayed rankDerivedValue matches the embedded one row for row, the leak is closed and the backtests become citable. Nothing available in this container can do that today because no such export exists.

findings.title: 'Confidence' on the board is one unvalidated agreement bucket, not separate calibrated dimensions, and it never shrinks a value — it only reorders and filters
findings.claimUnderTest: Section 40 asks whether the separate confidence dimensions are real and calibrated, and whether low confidence shrinks a claimed edge. methodology.confidenceBuckets presents high/medium/low/none as a graded quality reading.
findings.observed: _compute_confidence_bucket takes exactly two inputs — sourceCount and sourceRankPercentileSpread — and thresholds them at 0.08/0.20. That is one dimension (source agreement about ORDER), and it is agreement about rank, not about the value it labels. No other dimension feeds it: _marketConfidence and identityConfidence exist on the same row and are unrelated quantities that never combine into it. No calibration measurement of any kind exists in the repo: nothing tests whether a 'high' row is more accurate, more stable, or narrower in any realized sense than a 'low' row. On the live board 448 of 1,092 rows (41.0%) are 'low' and only 113 (10.3%) are 'high'. Downstream, confidence never scales a value: suggestions.py adds a flat +2/+1/0 to a rank_score (reordering only, and off its own sourceCount thresholds of 6/3, which disagree with the contract's rule), and edge-helpers.js uses the bucket only as an include/exclude filter. The single value-shrinking mechanism in the pipeline is the single-source haircut, which keys on sourceCount==1, not on confidence — so a five-source row with a 0.5 percentile spread is labelled 'low' and its value is used at full face in every trade calculation.

findings.title: /api/status source_health describes 2 of 21 sources: total_sources=2, source_counts covers ktc+idpTradeCalc only, and missing_sources is structurally always empty

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers the schema-probe coverage gap or the header-only silent path. Distinct from PRIOR-A25-F00, which is about freshness stamps.

findings.title: The KTC trade/waiver crowd DB is skipped on EVERY successful KTC scrape — `content` is only bound inside the Strategy-3 fallback, so KTC_ID_TO_NAME is never built and the FAAB crowd factor is unreachable
findings.claimUnderTest: The `partial_run_tolerable:KTC_TradeDB` / `:KTC_WaiverDB` warnings are a tolerable transient on a secondary endpoint, and the KTC crowd-sourced FAAB calibration factor is live.
findings.observed: `scrape_ktc` has three extraction strategies. `content = await page.content()` is assigned ONLY inside Strategy 3, which is guarded by `if not name_map:` (line 2268). The ID-map builder at line 2477 is guarded by `if "content" in dir() and content:` — a check on whether that local was ever bound. So on every run where KTC actually works (Strategy 1 API intercept or Strategy 2 DOM, which is what produced today's 500 rows), `content` is unbound, KTC_ID_TO_NAME stays empty, line 4006's `if SITES.get("KTC") and KTC_ID_TO_NAME` is False, and both crowd endpoints are skipped with the 'no playerID->name mapping available' warning. The condition is inverted: the crowd DB can only run on the degraded path. Downstream, `ktcCrowd` is absent from the live payload, so `crowd_bid_map_from_contract` returns {} and the 'KTC crowd-sourced calibration' factor never appears — and the FAAB response does not list it as missing either (only 4 factors, warnings=[]).

findings.userImpact: A user on /waivers gets a FAAB bid whose crowd-calibration input is permanently absent, presented as a complete factor breakdown with no 'missing' marker — the 15%-weight rival-contention factor IS marked missing, so the omission of the crowd factor reads as 'not applicable' rather than 'never collected'. The operator meanwhile sees two permanent amber warnings that are documented as 'tolerable transients'.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding in the ingestion area covers KTC_TradeDB/KTC_WaiverDB or the crowd-FAAB path.

findings.whatWorks: The whole downstream chain is correctly built and would work the moment the map exists: build_crowd_bid_map, crowd_bid_map_from_contract, the 70/30 blend, the _ktc_crowd_applies guard and the factor emission are all present and unit-tested. The failure is confined to one variable-scope bug in the scraper.
findings.rootCause: `content` is a Strategy-3 local; the ID-map builder guards on its existence with `"content" in dir()` rather than fetching the page source unconditionally. The guard was presumably written when Strategy 3 was the only path.
findings.requiredRepair: Hoist `content = await page.content()` out of the `if not name_map:` block (or build KTC_ID_TO_NAME from the intercepted API payload, which carries playerID+playerName directly), and stop classifying an always-skipped source as a tolerable partial. Separately, have faab_recommender emit the crowd factor with missing:true when the map is empty, matching how rival contention is handled.

Losing any 1 to 13 individual sources between deploys passes that gate. The strict script itself works: run against the live server it prints 'ok: live board carries 21 registered source(s); 0 fresh-but-absent'.

findings.userImpact: Between deploys (which can be days apart) the board can lose up to 13 of 21 sources without any production alert. The 2h CI watchdog (watchdog_contract_coverage.py) does cover this against the CI checkout, so the exposure is specifically 'the running prod process serves a different board than CI builds'.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers the docstring-vs-wiring mismatch for verify_live_source_coverage.py.

findings.whatWorks: Both CI watchdogs pass against the live tree right now: `watchdog_freshness.py` -> 'ok: 22 sources fresh, 0 hard-stale'; `watchdog_contract_coverage.py` -> 'ok: 21 registered source(s) covered, 0 fresh-but-absent'. The deploy-time gate is genuinely wired and would fail a deploy that served a degraded board.
findings.rootCause: The health-check workflow was deliberately kept checkout-free, so the strict script could not be invoked there; the script's docstring was written for the intended design and never corrected.
findings.requiredRepair: Either add a checkout step (or ship the per-source expectations as data in the /api/status payload so a dependency-free checker can be strict), or correct the docstring and lower MIN_SOURCES tolerance to name the expected registry count.

findings.title: Per-source staleness is computed in every /api/data payload and shown to nobody: two disagreeing threshold tables (6h in code, 24h in config) and no user-visible surface for either
findings.claimUnderTest: config/source_staleness.json's own comment: a stale source is 'reported everywhere (on-site stale banner, email alerts ..., the freshness-watchdog summary)'.

Not a correctness defect, but it interacts with W05-F009: the 6h maxAgeHours budgets in _SOURCE_MAX_AGE_HOURS assume a 2h cadence ('6 hours ≈ three missed cycles'); at the observed cadence a 6h budget is closer to 1.5 missed cycles of headroom.

findings.title: Two real players occupy two board rows each because name-variant drift splits one human across a resolved row and an unresolved ghost, stranding vendor votes

findings.observed: The live 1,092-row contract carries BOTH 'Matt Hibner' (playerId 13324, TE/BAL/24, rank 377, rankDerivedValue 1737, sourceCount 8) and 'Matthew Hibner' (playerId null, position null, same team BAL, same age 24) - the same human. The three source CSVs (ktc, ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc) spell him 'Matthew Hibner', so their values 891/1458/1129 are stamped byte-identically on BOTH rows. dlfSf (rank 250.83), flockFantasySf (383.0) and draftSharks (400.0) land ONLY on the ghost, so the priced row blends 8 of 11 available vendor votes. Second case: 'Jam Miller' (playerId 13403, RB/NE, rank 635) vs 'Jamarion Miller' (playerId null) - DraftSharks' own CSV analysis text for 'Jamarion Miller' reads "Miller could make the Patriots roster as a third RB", identifying the same player; its rank-323 vote is stranded on the ghost. buildRows materializes both: /rankings renders 'Matt Hibner' at rank 377 AND 'Matthew Hibner' at rank 1052. validationSummary.duplicateCanonicalIdentityCount = 0 because that detector keys on exact _normalize_for_collision equality, and the split exists precisely because the keys differ.

reproduction.expected: 0 split identities; every human occupies exactly one board row
reproduction.actual: 1 CONFIRMED (Matthew/Matt Hibner, team+age identical, 3 byte-identical source values) + 1 REVIEW (Jamarion/Jam Miller); contract reports duplicateCanonicalIdentityCount=0

findings.title: /api/player/{sleeper_id}/realized returns unmapped_player for every player because the Sleeper block never contains the key the identity mapper is handed
findings.claimUnderTest: server.py:11260 'Find this player's GSIS via the unified mapper, then filter.' The route's own comment says the row-filter bug was the defect and was fixed.
findings.observed: players_dir = sleeper_block.get("players") or sleeper_block.get("playerDict"). The Sleeper block the scraper writes (Dynasty Scraper.py:1297-1306) contains exactly leagueId, leagueName, teams, positions, playerIds, idToPlayer, scoringSettings, rosterPositions, leagueSettings - no 'players', no 'playerDict', ever. players_dir is therefore always None, _index_directory(None) returns four empty dicts, resolve_player returns None, and the route short-circuits at reason: unmapped_player. Confirmed live on four real Sleeper ids (A.J. Brown 5859, Josh Allen 4984, Bijan Robinson 9509, Kenny Gainwell 7567): all four return unmapped_player. The stats fetch SUCCEEDS first (the route would otherwise say no_stats_available), so the mapper is the sole blocker. /api/status corroborates: idMappingCoverage = {resolve_attempts: 8, unresolved: 8, coverage_pct: 0.0}. This is a key-name mismatch in committed code, not container state.

reproduction.expected: weekly realized-points arrays for each player
reproduction.actual: {"sleeperId":"5859","leagueKey":"dynasty_main","reason":"unmapped_player","weeks":[]} for all four

numericProof.formula: resolvable = |{sid : sleeper_block['players'] is a dict and sid in it}|

findings.userImpact: PlayerPopup's realized-points panel is empty for every player in every league. A user comparing a player's market value against his actual production sees nothing and concludes there is no data.

blastRadius.note: 937 of 1092 contract rows carry _sleeperId (recounted). pagesAffected raised from 1 to 10+: PlayerPopup is imported by frontend/app/{rankings,trade,rosters,trending,edge,news,players/compare,settings,idptc-rookies}/page.jsx plus 9 terminal components.

priorFinding.note: A22-F03 claims the route 'emits a full array of 0.0-point weeks'; A22-F02 claims IDP players 'silently return zero weeks'. Neither reproduces: the route never reaches the scoring stage for ANY player. Both describe behaviour downstream of a bail that always fires. Same for PRIOR-A21-F16's league-scoping claim - the response never contains weeks to mis-score.

findings.whatWorks: The route's auth gate, flag gate, league resolution and the nfl_data weekly fetch all work - the fetch returns rows, which is why the response is unmapped_player rather than no_stats_available.
findings.rootCause: server.py reads sleeper.players / sleeper.playerDict; the producer emits sleeper.playerIds (name->id) and sleeper.idToPlayer (id->name). No writer has ever produced the key the reader asks for.
findings.requiredRepair: Either fetch the Sleeper player directory for the mapper, or resolve the GSIS id from idToPlayer[sid] plus the nflverse name index. A key rename alone is NOT enough - playerIds/idToPlayer carry no gsis_id.

verification.reasoning:
Tried to kill this four ways and it survived all four.

(1) REPRODUCTION: exact. All four sleeper ids return reason:unmapped_player today. /api/status idMappingCoverage confirms resolve_attempts=4, unresolved=4, coverage_pct=0.0 — one attempt per probe, all failed.

(2) INFERENTIAL STEP: holds, and I checked the two escape hatches the author did not. server.py:11263 `players_dir = sleeper_block.get("players") or sleeper_block.get("playerDict")`; the live sleeper block carries neither key (16 keys listed above). src/identity/unified_mapper.py:200-211 `_index_directory` returns four empty dicts for a non-dict argument, so ladder rungs 1/3/4/5/6/7 are all dead. The one rung that does NOT need the directory is rung 2, the manual override (unified_mapper.py:280-293) — config/identity/id_overrides.json contains only `_comment` and `_example_entry_only`, so it resolves nobody. There is no producer for the key either: grep over server.py, `Dynasty Scraper.py` and src/ finds no writer of sleeper.players/sleeper.playerDict; the scraper's roster_data literal (`Dynasty Scraper.py`:1297-1306) emits playerIds/idToPlayer, which carry names, not gsis_id — so the author's note that a key rename alone would not fix it is correct.

(3) LIVE PATH: yes. Flag `realized_points_api` defaults True (src/api/feature_flags.py:54, and :365 marks it LIVE). frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:397 fetches `/api/player/${key}/realized` and :1003 mounts <RealizedPointsSection>. PlayerPopup is imported by 10+ pages (rankings, trade, rosters, trending, edge, news, players/compare, settings, idptc-rookies, plus 9 terminal components).

(4) HARNESS ARTIFACT: no. This is the sharpest test and it passes cleanly — the route returns `no_stats_available` when the nflverse weekly fetch is empty (server.py:11248-11257) and `unmapped_player` only AFTER a non-empty fetch. Getting unmapped_player proves the stats leg WORKED in this container; the mapper is the sole blocker, and the blocker is a key name in committed code, not absent container data.

(5) FIXED AT HEAD: no. Lines unchanged since 891d1600 (2026-08-03).

(6) BLAST RADIUS: recounted from the live contract — 937 of 1092 rows carry `_sleeperId`, matching the claim exactly.

Two corrections that do not change the verdict, one in each direction. Against the author: `userImpact` says the user "sees nothing and concludes there is no data" — RealizedPointsSection returns null when weeks is empty (PlayerPopup.jsx:425), so nothing renders at all and no "no data" message is shown; no wrong number is ever displayed. In the author's favour: pagesAffected:1 UNDERSTATES it — PlayerPopup is a shared component on 10+ pages, not one.

I considered rescoping to P2 on the strength of the silent degradation, and rejected it. This is not the wave-1 failure mode: no inflated count, no dead branch, no harness dependence. A flag-on, reachable feature returns nothing for 100% of players because of a key name no writer has ever produced, and the route's own in-file comment (server.py:11276-11285) celebrates fixing a DOWNSTREAM row-filter bug that this bail makes unreachable — so the code believes it works. P1 stands.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: Nothing further — this is settled. The one open question is the repair shape, not the defect: idToPlayer maps sleeperId->name and carries no gsis_id, so a fix must either fetch Sleeper /v1/players/nfl into the block or route the name through the nflverse name index. A regression test should assert a non-unmapped reason for a known id, since the current tests (frontend/__tests__/components/realized-points-section.test.jsx) mock the fetch and therefore cannot see this.

findings.title: config/identity/id_overrides.json cannot influence the board at all, and where it IS read the override loses to the directory it exists to override

No override can affect a single value on the board. (2) PRECEDENCE: the override rung is step 2, AFTER the exact-sleeper_id rung at :275. Since the documented use cases ('same-name-different-player', 'players with identical names across positions') are by definition players the Sleeper directory already knows, the override layer is unreachable for its stated purpose. src/playerctx/normalize.py:561-563 independently documents this from the other side. priorFinding.note: A24-F04's secondary note observes the empty-map cache re-read. The precedence inversion (override loses to the directory) and the total absence of the file from the board path are new, and are proven at runtime here rather than by reading.

findings.title: identityConfidence is a three-valued restatement of 'does this row have a playerId', that playerId was itself assigned by a name match, and no surface reads the field
findings.claimUnderTest: _compute_identity_confidence documents a four-rung ladder (1.00 canonical_id / 0.95 position_source_aligned / 0.85 partial_evidence / 0.70 name_only) scoring 'how confident we are that this row represents the right entity'.
findings.observed: Live distribution over 1,092 rows: 1.00 canonical_id x937, 0.95 position_source_aligned x144 (every pick, via the assetClass=='pick' short-circuit), 0.70 name_only x11. The 0.85 partial_evidence rung emits zero rows. The field is therefore a bijection with (playerId is not None, assetClass=='pick') - it adds no information. Worse, the 1.00 label is not earned: no source except pfkDynasty publishes a Sleeper id, and every playerId on the board comes from Dynasty Scraper.py::_resolve_sleeper_identity, a NAME lookup with a 0.90-threshold difflib fallback. Consumption: buildRows copies identityConfidence/identityMethod onto every row (dynasty-data.js:1151-1152, 1295-1296, 1782-1783), and a repo-wide grep across frontend/app, frontend/components and frontend/lib finds ZERO non-test readers. Only the sibling `quarantined` boolean is read (/rankings trust tile, /edge filters). Corroborating: the one quarantined row on today's board, Brandon Knight, is stamped identityConfidence 1.00.

findings.title: unified_mapper.resolve_player merges 11 demonstrably different NFL players at its default threshold on today's real corpus, and the scraper's own fuzzy guard passes 5 of the same 11 pairs
findings.claimUnderTest: Module docstring: 'Fuzzy normalized name only. confidence=0.75..0.90 ... Anything below the configured min_confidence is rejected.' _is_safe_name_merge: 'Guard fuzzy canonicalization so unrelated players are not merged.'
findings.observed: Fed the 544 distinct source-CSV names that FAILED the production canonical-name join, plus a directory built from the live 948-player board, resolve_player(min_confidence=0.85) returns a match for 11 of them - every one a different human, each reported at confidence 0.857-0.923 with match_method='fuzzy_name' (a method the docstring caps at 0.90): Tevin Coleman->Kevin Coleman 0.923, Ian Thomas->Brian Thomas 0.909, Eric Gray->Cedric Gray 0.900, Ty Montgomery->Tyren Montgomery 0.897, Mike Williams->Mykel Williams 0.889, Cedrick Wilson->Eric Wilson 0.880, Jordan Travis->Jordan Davis 0.880, Jacob Harris->Jacob Parrish 0.880, Amari Cooper->Omar Cooper 0.870, Jordan Wilkins->Jordan Watkins 0.857. Separately, the ladder has no name+team rung: with two 'Josh Allen' rows (QB/BUF and LB/JAX) and no position supplied, resolve_player(name='Josh Allen', team='JAX') returns the BUF QB at confidence 1.00 - the caller's team is ignored entirely and the answer flips with dict insertion order. Blast radius is bounded by reachability: the live board join uses exact _canonical_match_key and correctly rejected all 544. But the scraper's OWN guard, _is_safe_name_merge, returns True for 5 of the 11 pairs (Tevin/Kevin Coleman, Ian/Brian Thomas, Eric/Cedric Gray, Cedrick Wilson/Eric Wilson, Cedrick Wilson Jr./Eric Wilson), and best_match is called at threshold 0.85 (line 4473) and 0.90 (4586, 5339) - so three of those pairs clear both the guard and the 0.90 gate on the live scrape path.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/repro_overrides_and_mapper.py  # sections C+D; full 11-pair sweep captured in fuzzy-false-merges.json
reproduction.expected: 0 matches among CSV names the exact join already rejected
reproduction.actual: 11 matches, confidence 0.857-0.923, all cross-player; and name+team resolution ignores team

numericProof.formula: false_merges = |{n : resolve_player(board_directory, name=n, min_confidence=0.85) is not None}| over names the exact canonical join rejected

findings.userImpact: Not a live wrong number on the board today (the board join is exact). It is a loaded gun: any future caller that routes a source through resolve_player, and the scraper's own 0.85/0.90 fuzzy rungs, will attribute one player's value to another and report it above 0.85 confidence.

priorFinding.note: A24-F03 demonstrated the threshold problem on hand-picked name pairs. Confirmed and extended: measured against the 544 names the LIVE corpus actually fails to join (11 false merges), plus the new finding that Dynasty Scraper.py's _is_safe_name_merge guard admits 5 of those same pairs, so the defect is not confined to the unreachable module.

findings.whatWorks: The exact-key production join (_canonical_match_key) rejected all 544 unmatched names with zero false merges - the conservative path is the one actually in use on the board.
findings.rootCause: min_confidence is compared against a raw difflib ratio with no length, token or edit-position weighting; the fuzzy result overwrites confidence with that ratio; and there is no name+team rung between name+team+pos and name+pos.
findings.requiredRepair: Require a surname exact match plus a first-name compatibility check before any fuzzy accept (the pool builder's _first_name_compatible already exists), add a name+team rung, and never report a fuzzy match above 0.90.

findings.title: Draft picks have no structured identity on the live path: season, round and slot exist only as substrings of a display name, re-parsed by at least nine divergent regexes, and the PickRow model that declares them is dead code
findings.claimUnderTest: src/identity/models.py::PickRow declares season, round, slot_known, slot_number, bucket, league_id - the canonical pick identity. matcher.py branches on rec.asset_type == 'pick' to populate it.
findings.observed: On the live contract's 144 pick rows, NONE of season / year / round / slot / originalOwner / currentOwner / projectedSlot exists as a field. playerId is null on all 144. The only identity is the displayName string ('2026 Pick 1.02', '2027 Early 1st'). Original and current owner do not exist in the contract at all - ownership lives only in sleeper.teams[].pickDetails and the draft-capital fallback. PickRow is unreachable on real data: src/adapters/scraper_bridge_adapter.py:101 hardcodes asset_type='player', so all 3,494 records in the newest raw snapshot are typed 'player' and matcher.py's pick branch never executes - /api/scaffold/identity reports pick_count 0 / pick_alias_count 0 while minting 84 master PLAYERS with ids like 'player::2026 early 1st::OTHER'. In place of the model, at least nine modules re-derive season/round/slot from the name with their own regexes, and they disagree: frontend/lib/pick-stack.js TIER_RE accepts rounds 1-9, data_contract._PICK_TIER_RE accepts 1-6; canonical/normalization_validator requires a two-digit slot (\.\d{2}) while _PICK_SLOT_RE accepts (0?[1-9]|1[0-2]); pool/builder caps the slot at 12.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/contract-full.json')); p=[r for r in d['playersArray'] if r['assetClass']=='pick']; print(len(p)); print({k:sum(1 for x in p if x.get(k) is not None) for k in ['season','round','slot','originalOwner','currentOwner','projectedSlot','playerId']})" && curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/scaffold/identity | head -c 220
reproduction.expected: season/round/slot populated on all 144 picks; scaffold pick_count == 144
reproduction.actual: {'season':0,'round':0,'slot':0,'originalOwner':0,'currentOwner':0,'projectedSlot':0,'playerId':0}; scaffold reports pick_count 0, pick_alias_count 0

numericProof.formula: structured_pick_identity_coverage = fields_present / (144 rows x 5 canonical fields)

findings.userImpact: Every surface that needs a pick's year, round or slot re-parses a display string, so a label the scraper emits in an unexpected shape (a 14-team slot, a one-digit slot, a round above 6) is silently classified as a PLAYER by some modules and a pick by others - the same asset then gets a player's treatment on one page and a pick's on another, with no error.

priorFinding.note: A24-F28 found one symptom (pool/builder's slot regex caps at 12). No prior finding states the underlying condition: there is no structured pick identity on the live path at all, and the model that declares one is unreachable because every raw record is typed 'player'.

findings.whatWorks: pickAliases is internally consistent: all 18 generic->slot aliases (Early->x.02, Mid->x.06, Late->x.10) resolve to a slot row that carries a real rankDerivedValue, and every aliased generic row is correctly suppressed (rankDerivedValue null, pickGenericSuppressed true), so no double-count is possible on the 2026 class.
findings.rootCause: The adapter that feeds the identity layer hardcodes asset_type='player', and the contract layer never promoted the parsed (year, round, slot) tuple from _PICK_SLOT_RE into row fields.
findings.requiredRepair: Stamp season/round/slot (and slotKnown) onto every pick row in the contract once, from the parse the contract already performs, and have every consumer read those fields instead of re-parsing the name. Fixing asset_type in the bridge adapter is a prerequisite for the scaffold layer.

findings.title: The Sleeper name->id map is written with no collision guard while the sibling position map three lines above has one
findings.claimUnderTest: The in-line comment at Dynasty Scraper.py:1238-1242 states the collision policy: 'Name collision across universes (e.g. DJ Turner WR vs DJ Turner II CB both clean to "DJ Turner"). findings.observed: That policy is applied to position_map only. Three lines earlier, player_id_map[cn] = sid and id_to_player[sid] = cn are written unconditionally on the same cleaned-name key. findings.title: Every /rankings page load silently POSTs tep_multiplier=1.15, which bypasses the ADR-015 TE-basis curve — the rendered board under-prices 82 TEs by up to 21.2% and disagrees with GET /api/data on 627 ranks, while every server-side engine keeps pricing from /api/data
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'TE rows from non-TEP sources are lifted onto the basis the board is anchored on via convert_te_value(from_basis="base", to_basis="tepp") — KTC's own measured uplift, 1.209 at the top of the board rising toward 2.05 down it. Replaces a flat 1.15 that sat below the entire observed range.' And frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:2025-2028: 'Default path (no overrides) ... the backend will derive tep_multiplier ... so the frontend doesn't need to POST anything.'
findings.observed: SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.tepMultiplier = 1.15 is a finite number, and tepMultiplierIsCustomized() returns true for ANY finite number. So `customized` is true on every session including a browser with no localStorage at all. Measured in Chromium after `localStorage.removeItem('next_settings_v2')`: the very first request /rankings makes is POST /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta with body {"tep_multiplier":1.15}. The backend then sets tep_multiplier_is_override=True (tepMultiplierSource:'override'), and data_contract.py:6939 `if not tep_multiplier_is_override:` skips the te_basis_conversion block entirely — the flag is ON and the curve is loadable, it is simply never entered. findings.title: 222 rows on the live board display a client-invented ordinal in the # column, and CLAUDE.md's stated bound for that fallback is factually wrong — the backend's board stops at rank 740, never reaching the 800 limit the doc cites

findings.observed: On the live 1,092-row contract the deepest backend-stamped rank is 740; OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT (800) is never reached, so the doc's stated population does not exist. The rows that actually take the fallback are the 239 non-pick rows the backend refused to price at all — canonicalConsensusRank null AND rankDerivedValue null AND canonicalTierId null AND confidenceLabel 'None - unranked'. After the rankings page's own filters, 222 of them render with a client-invented # in the range 854-1092. Reproduced in the browser: Austin Ekeler renders '#865', AJ Dillon '#858', Alexander Mattison '#860', Arian Smith '#864' — visually identical to Josh Allen's backend-stamped '#1'. The mechanism claim ('a backend-stamped rank always wins') IS true and was verified: Trey Lance #673 and T.J. Watt #185 reproduce the backend stamp exactly.

findings.userImpact: A user sorting or filtering the deep board reads '#865 Austin Ekeler, RB115' and treats it as the platform's assessment. It is an array index. priorFinding.note: Prior counted 216 and framed the ordinals as 'array indices that count unranked picks'. findings.title: The /trade calculator never sums the canonical board: the frontend posts an explicit tep_multiplier=1.15 on every load, which disables the ADR-015 TE basis conversion and reprices 129 of 809 players by up to -21.2%
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md ADR-015: TE rows from non-TEP sources are lifted via te_premium.convert_te_value using KTC's measured uplift (1.209 at the top rising toward 2.05), replacing 'a flat 1.15 that sat below the entire observed range'; the feature ships flag-ON. CLAUDE.md also states 'an explicit operator slider value bypasses the curve regardless' — but does not note that the frontend always sends one. useSettings.js additionally claims tepMultiplier=null means 'auto from league / inherit from backend'.
findings.observed: data_contract.py gates the whole basis conversion behind `if not tep_multiplier_is_override:`. `useSettings.js` SETTINGS_DEFAULTS sets tepMultiplier: 1.15 (a finite number), and readSettings() actively coerces null/1.0/1.25 back to 1.15 on first read. tepMultiplierIsCustomized() returns true for any finite number, so fetchDynastyData takes the override path and POSTs {"tep_multiplier":1.15} on EVERY page load. Captured live from the browser on /trade: `POST /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta {"tep_multiplier":1.15}`. The response reports tepMultiplier 1.15, tepMultiplierDefault 1.15, tepMultiplierDerived 1.15, isCustomized false — identical declared parameters to the base contract — but tepMultiplierSource flips 'default' -> 'override' and 129 of 809 players get different values. The ADR-015 curve is therefore unreachable from the product: no user-facing path produces the board the backend calls canonical.

reproduction.actual: 129 of 809 differ. Tyler Conklin 1450 -> 1142 (-21.2%), Josh Cuevas 1541 -> 1215 (-21.2%), Sam LaPorta 5222 -> 5021 (-3.8%). 89 players >5%, 54 >10%. Confirmed in the DOM: /trade renders Sam LaPorta at 5,021, /api/dynasty-data says 5,222.

findings.userImpact: Every TE priced on the trade calculator, the rankings board and every client-side sum is up to 21% below the value the backend's own canonical pipeline produces, with no indication on screen. A user trading a TE gives one away ~20% too cheap (or overpays to acquire one) on a board the app cannot be configured to leave — clearing the setting is undone by the readSettings() migration. The measured TE-basis feature the repo shipped and flagged ON is dead in production.

blastRadius.playersAffectedDetail: 79 TE (100% of TEs compared, all revalued downward) + 50 tethered picks
blastRadius.note: pagesAffected raised from 6: 11 pages import useDynastyData, plus AppShell

priorFinding.note: No area-2 prior finding covers the TEP override path or the base-vs-override board divergence. Adjacent but distinct from PRIOR-A02-F11 (which is about KTC constants being fed our blended values, not about which blend).

findings.whatWorks: POST /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta with an empty body {} reproduces the base contract exactly (0 of 812 rows differ) — the delta merge itself is sound. The response honestly stamps tepMultiplierSource so the divergence is diagnosable from the payload.
findings.rootCause: src/api/data_contract.py:6939 gates te_basis_conversion on `not tep_multiplier_is_override`, and the frontend's default settings make every request an override. The gate was written for 'the operator moved the slider'; nothing checks whether the posted value equals the derived default, and the frontend has no 'unset' state because readSettings() rewrites null back to 1.15.
findings.requiredRepair: Either (a) make tepMultiplier default to null and stop the readSettings() coercion so fetchDynastyData takes the no-override path, or (b) treat a posted value equal to tepMultiplierDerived as 'default' rather than 'override' in data_contract.py's source resolution. (a) is smaller and matches the documented sentinel. Add a regression test asserting POST {tep_multiplier: <derived>} is byte-identical to POST {}.
findings.dependencies: Interacts with W08-F012 (backend engines read the un-overridden board) — fixing this closes that divergence too.

verification.reasoning: Survives every attack I made. (1) The reproduction runs today and returns the stated numbers to the digit: 129 of 809, max -21.2%, and the empty-body control is a clean 0. (2) I recounted the blast radius myself: the 129 are 79 TEs (every single TE in the comparison, all moved DOWN, none up) plus 50 tethered picks — consistent with the stated mechanism, not a coincidence. (3) The code path is live and I proved it in a real browser through request interception, not by reading JS: /trade POSTs {"tep_multiplier":1.15} twice on load with a VIRGIN localStorage (only next_user_state_v1 / next_trade_workspace_v1 present — no settings key), so this is SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.tepMultiplier=1.15 at useSettings.js:35 reaching the wire, not a migrated stale value. (4) The gate is real: data_contract.py:6938 `if not tep_multiplier_is_override:` is the sole enable for te_basis_conversion, and data_contract.py:7676 picks `value * effective_non_tep_multiplier` (flat 1.15) on the else branch — the exact constant ADR-015 says 'sat below the entire observed range' of KTC's measured 1.209-2.05. (5) I tried to kill it on reachability: there is NO user-facing path to the un-overridden board. settings/page.jsx:397 clamps typed input to [1.0,1.5] (finite), and the 'Reset to default' button at :425 writes 1.15 — still finite, still an override. tepMultiplierIsCustomized (dynasty-data.js:2021) returns true for ANY finite number. readSettings (useSettings.js:182-191) rewrites null->1.15 once and latches tepDefaultV3Applied. So the ADR-015 curve is unreachable from the product, as claimed. (6) Severity is honest and the page even lies in the user's favour of the wrong reading: settings/page.jsx:407 renders 'Default 1.15x' for exactly the value that silently disables the measured curve — that is worse than no warning, it is an affirmative 'this is the default' label on an override. P0 stands: a reachable page (/trade, /rankings), a wrong number a user acts on (LaPorta 5,021 in the DOM vs 5,222 canonical), no warning. Only correction: blastRadius.pagesAffected=6 is UNDERSTATED — 11 pages import useDynastyData (edge, rankings, players/compare, arbitrage, phases, angle, settings, trade, league, LeagueClient, idptc-rookies) plus AppShell, so every authenticated surface holding the board is on the override path.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: Nothing outstanding — reproduced at the API, in the code, and in a real browser with a clean profile.

findings.title: The Value Adjustment tooltip tells the user the bonus goes to 'the side with fewer pieces', but 46.7% of fired VAs go to a side with equal or MORE pieces
findings.claimUnderTest: SideCard renders title="Consolidation / roster-spot premium: the side with fewer pieces frees a roster spot, so KTC-style math adds this bonus on top of the raw total." The same file's own algorithm docstring contradicts it: 'KTC's algorithm is symmetric: equal-count trades (e.g. 2v2 stud-vs-pile) fire VA when one side has bigger studs.'
findings.observed: ktcAdjustPackage awards the VA on raw_adj INTENSITY (e/team1Total vs a/team2Total — i.e. which side's value is concentrated in bigger studs), not on piece count. Piece count only enters through the progressive nerf and the 1v1 suppression. Over 50,000 random 1-4 vs 1-4 trades built from the live board, the VA fired 21,610 times: 11,524 (53.3%) to the side with fewer pieces, 6,815 (31.5%) on equal counts, 3,271 (15.1%) to the side with MORE pieces. Concrete live case: A=[Bijan Robinson 9706, Tyjae Spears 2121, Jessie Bates 1707, Kyle Hamilton 3062] (4 pieces) vs B=[Jadarian Price 4286, Dak Prescott 5519, 2028 Late 1st 4079] (3 pieces) -> VA 3,815 credited to A, the side with MORE pieces. Equal-count case: 4v4 with Puka Nacua on side A -> VA 5,093 to A, 29% of its raw total.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && node vacopy.mjs   # source in evidence/W08/va-recipient.json; regenerate by importing ktcAdjustPackage from frontend/lib/trade-logic.js and sampling the live board
reproduction.expected: If the tooltip is true, 100% of fired VAs land on the side with strictly fewer pieces.
reproduction.actual: 53.3% fewer, 31.5% equal, 15.1% more (n=21,610 fired VAs over 50,000 sampled trades).

inputs.side_sizes: 1-4 per side, assets drawn from the 812 priced live board rows

numericProof.formula: P(recipient_piece_count < other_piece_count | VA fired)

findings.userImpact: The user reads the only explanation the page offers for a bonus worth up to 5,093 points (29% of a side's raw total) and is told a rule that is false half the time. They cannot predict the verdict, and when the VA lands on the bigger pile the explanation directly contradicts what they can see on screen.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A02-F13 asserts 'docstrings and status docs describe behaviour the code does not implement' generically; this is a specific user-facing tooltip with a measured falsification rate.

findings.whatWorks: The VA number itself is correct: ktcAdjustPackage is a faithful port (see W08-F010) and the SideCard honestly decomposes the headline as 'Raw N + VA M' rather than hiding it.
findings.rootCause: The tooltip was written against the retired V2/V13 consolidation-premium model (a piece-count formula) and was not updated when the 2026-04-26 direct KTC port replaced it with an intensity-based rule.
findings.requiredRepair: Rewrite the tooltip to describe what the code does: 'KTC-style adjustment: the side whose value is concentrated in fewer, bigger pieces gets a bonus, because a stud is worth more than the same total spread across depth.' Do not mention roster spots — no roster-spot term exists in ktcProcessV.

findings.title: Adding a positive-value asset to your side can lower your side's total and flip the verdict against you — the fairness gap is non-monotonic in 1.1-1.9% of trades
findings.claimUnderTest: adjustedSideTotals returns `adjusted = raw + adjustment`, and TradeMeter/verdictFromGap render the verdict off `adjustedA - adjustedB`. The implicit contract of a trade calculator is that adding value to a side improves that side's position.
findings.observed: Because the VA is a discontinuous function of the piece SET (1v1 suppression, the 3.3% display floor, the progressive nerf, and the branch switch on raw_adj intensity), adding one positive-value asset to side A can reduce A's adjusted total. Over 40,000 random 1-3 vs 1-3 trades from the live board, 772 (1.93%) got WORSE for A after adding a real asset to A; 27 of those crossed a meter-verdict label boundary. Restricting to multi-asset shapes only (2-3 per side, so the 1v1 suppression rule cannot explain it), 687 of 60,000 (1.15%) still violate. Live example (all values are live board values): A=[2026 Pick 1.04 5320, Jadarian Price 4286, Dont'e Thornton 1509] vs B=[T.J. Hockenson 3107, 2026 Pick 2.09 2846, Kaden Elliss 1869]; gap +4903 with a 1,610 VA on A. Add Boye Mafe (1,235 board points) to A -> A's VA drops to 0 and the gap FALLS to +4528. Verdict-flipping example: A=[Daiyan Henley 1923] vs B=[2028 Late 2nd 2785], gap -862 = SLIGHT EDGE; add Omar Speights (894) to A -> gap -1219 = UNFAIR.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && node mono2.mjs && node mono3.mjs
reproduction.expected: For every trade T and every asset x with value(x) > 0: gap(A+x, B) >= gap(A, B). Violations: 0.
reproduction.actual: 772 / 40,000 (1.93%) for 1-3 per side; 687 / 60,000 (1.15%) for 2-3 per side; 27 verdict-label flips.

findings.userImpact: The user follows the page's own signal — 'you are behind, add something' — adds a real asset, and the verdict moves further against them with no explanation. On the 27 measured flips the badge goes from SLIGHT EDGE to UNFAIR (or UNFAIR to LOPSIDED) as a direct result of the user giving MORE. They will then remove a good asset or demand more back, which is the wrong negotiating move.

priorFinding.note: F10 framed this as a balancer-selection bug ('sized against a VA-inclusive gap but selected by raw value') and illustrated it with a hand-built 1-for-many shape. Confirmed and generalised: the non-monotonicity is a property of adjustedSideTotals itself, independent of findBalancers, and I measured its rate on the live board (1.15% for multi-asset shapes where the 1v1 suppression cannot be the cause) plus 27 verdict-label flips. F10's proposed cause (balancers select on raw value) is necessary but not sufficient — no selection rule fixes a non-monotonic objective.

findings.whatWorks: The gap is exactly A/B symmetric (see W08-F009), so the non-monotonicity is not an ordering artifact.
findings.rootCause: The VA is folded into the side totals (`adjusted = raw + adjustment`) and then differenced, but ktcAdjustPackage is a step function of the piece multiset with three discontinuities (1v1 suppression, the |value|/(totalA+totalB) < 0.033 display floor, and the branch switch on h vs y). KTC itself displays the VA as an advisory 'add this much to even it out' badge, not as an addend to a side total — folding it into the meter is what turns the discontinuity into a verdict flip.
findings.requiredRepair: Either stop folding the VA into `adjusted` and render it as KTC does (an advisory line beside a raw-total verdict), or clamp: compute the VA, and if adding an asset to a side would reduce that side's adjusted total, hold the previous VA and surface a note. The first is smaller and matches the source the port is faithful to.
findings.dependencies: Compounds with PRIOR-A02-F02 (absolute fairness bands), which is what makes the 27 label flips reachable at small gaps.

findings.title: Current-year (2026) draft picks cannot be found in the trade calculator's only search box — the exclusion is a hardcoded /^2026\b/ regex, not the contract's currentDraftYear
findings.claimUnderTest: The trade page presents one 'Search to add to Side A…' input per side as the primary way to build a trade; the board carries 72 slot-specific 2026 pick rows (2026 Pick 1.01 … 6.12) with live values (1.01 = 7,799).
findings.observed: searchAssets() filters out every row matching `r.assetClass === 'pick' && /^2026\b/.test(r.name)`. Measured in a real browser through request interception: typing '2026' or '2026 Pick 1.0' into the Side A search box returns ZERO results, while '2027 Mid 1st' returns '2027 Mid 1st PICK #48.0 · 5,606' and '2029 Early 1st' returns '#79.0 · 2,668'. The same hardcoded regex also removes 2026 picks from both balancer pools (page.jsx:740/753 and 785/794). The contract exposes currentDraftYear (2026) and page.jsx:295 already resolves it into a `currentDraftYear` memo — the four exclusion sites do not use it, so the filter will exclude the wrong year from 2027 onward.

reproduction.expected: Searching '2026' offers the current rookie class's picks, the most-traded asset type in dynasty.
reproduction.actual: queries['2026 Pick 1.0'] = [] and queries['2026'] = [] (no pick rows); queries['2027 Mid 1st'] = ['2027 Mid 1st PICK #48.0 · 5,606'].

findings.userImpact: A user cannot build the most common dynasty trade shape — a current-class rookie pick for a player — through the page's primary control. The picks are still reachable via the global search popup, a KTC import or a share URL, so the omission reads as the app not having the asset rather than as a deliberate filter. Nothing on screen explains the exclusion.

priorFinding.note: Area-2 priors do not cover the asset picker.

findings.whatWorks: resolvePickRow correctly maps every Sleeper label shape onto the slot-specific board rows ('2026 1st' -> '2026 Pick 1.06' @ 4,987, '2026 Mid 1st' -> '2026 Pick 1.06'), correctly skipping the suppressed generic-tier rows via row.raw.pickGenericSuppressed. The resolver is not the problem; the picker filter is.
findings.rootCause: A hardcoded year literal repeated at four call sites, added to keep league-owned current-year picks out of generic suggestion pools, applied to the search box as well.
findings.requiredRepair: Replace all four `/^2026\b/` literals with a predicate built from the memoised `currentDraftYear`, and drop the exclusion from searchAssets entirely (explicit user search is not a suggestion pool). If current-year picks must stay out of balancers, keep it there only and say so in the UI.

findings.title: Pick original-owner identity is discarded before it reaches the trade calculator: 53 of 216 league picks collapse onto a duplicate name, and the duplicate guard then makes them untradeable
findings.claimUnderTest: The trade calculator can represent a league team's real pick holdings. CLAUDE.md's draft-capital section treats pick ownership as real Sleeper-derived data.
findings.observed: The contract's sleeper.teams[].pickDetails carries {season, round, slot, original_roster_id, owner_roster_id, label} for every pick — original_roster_id IS present and correct. The trade page reads only team.picks (the flat label array), where all of Jason's eight 2027 firsts are the identical string '2027 1st'. resolvePickRow maps every one of them to the tier-centre row '2027 Mid 1st' @ 5,606. teamRosterNames() then returns a Set, and addToSide() refuses any name already in the trade (`allTradeNames.has(row.name)`). Net effect measured on the live league: Jason holds 62 picks that resolve to 18 distinct row names; the league holds 216 picks that resolve to 163 distinct names — 53 picks are unrepresentable. A trade of two 2027 firsts cannot be built at all, and a rebuilding team's first is priced identically to a contender's.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && node picks.mjs && node picks3.mjs
reproduction.expected: 216 roster picks -> 216 addressable trade assets, each carrying its original owner.
reproduction.actual: 216 -> 163 distinct names (53 collapsed). Jason: 62 -> 18. His eight 2027 firsts (original_roster_id 1,2,3,6,8,9,10,12) all become '2027 Mid 1st' @ 5,606.

numericProof.formula: distinct(resolvePickRow(label).name for label in team.picks) summed over 12 teams

findings.userImpact: A manager holding multiple firsts in the same year (the single most common consolidation-trade setup in dynasty) cannot model the trade. When one does fit, every future first is priced at the Mid tier regardless of whose it is — a 2027 first from the league's worst team and from its best are both 5,606, which is the difference between a fair trade and a fleecing.

priorFinding.note: Area-0 (draft/auction) priors cover the draft board; no area-2 prior covers pick identity inside the trade calculator.

findings.whatWorks: pickDetails is fully populated with original_roster_id and owner_roster_id for all 216 picks — the data needed for the fix is already in the payload and is not being read. Pick label resolution itself is exhaustive (0 unresolved labels across all 12 teams).
findings.rootCause: Assets are keyed by display NAME throughout the trade builder (addToSide, removeAssetFromSide, isAssetInTrade, filterPickerRows, serializeWorkspace, valueOverrides, destinations). Picks have no unique name, so identity collapses. team.picks was built as a label array before pickDetails existed and nothing migrated to it.
findings.requiredRepair: Give trade assets a stable id (playerId for players, `${season}-${round}-${original_roster_id}` for picks) and key the trade sides on it instead of `name`. Short of that, at minimum render picks as '2027 1st (from Ed)' from pickDetails.original_roster_id so the names are distinct and the dedup guard stops eating them.
findings.dependencies: Pricing a from-team pick differently requires a projected-standings input the platform does not have; the identity fix is independent of and prior to that.

findings.title: 48 of 216 league roster picks and 260 of 1,072 board rows are addable to a trade at a silent value of 0
findings.claimUnderTest: dynasty-data.js's SCALE CONTRACT comment: 'an unpriced row reports 0 and drops out of those sums rather than distorting them.' The trade calculator sums effectiveValue = row.values[valueMode].
findings.observed: The drop-to-zero is real, but on /trade the row is still selectable and still occupies a side. 260 of 1,072 materialised rows (24%) carry rankDerivedValue null -> values.full 0. All 48 of the league's 2027/2028 5th- and 6th-round picks resolve to board rows with no value (2027 Mid 5th, 2027 Mid 6th, 2028 Mid 5th, 2028 Mid 6th — 12 of each). The search result row does mark it ('AJ Dillon RB — · 0'), which is honest, but once added the asset renders as a normal chip and contributes 0 to the side total, the gap, the verdict and the CSV export with no warning. Separately, all 18 2029 pick rows carry no _rawComposite, so in the 'Raw' value mode they contribute 0 while showing a non-zero value in 'Our Value'.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && node picks3.mjs && node rows.mjs
reproduction.expected: An asset the board declines to price is either excluded from the trade builder or flagged inside the trade with a 'not priced' badge.
reproduction.actual: zero-full rows: 260 of 1072; zero-raw rows: 18 (all 2029 picks); league roster picks resolving to value 0: 48 of 216, all 2027/2028 rounds 5-6.

numericProof.formula: count(rows where Number(rankDerivedValue) is falsy)

findings.userImpact: A trade of 'my 2028 6th for your 2028 6th' shows both sides at 0 and the verdict FAIR, which is coincidentally right. 'My 2028 5th for your Boye Mafe' shows the 5th at 0 and reads LOPSIDED, which overstates the imbalance and pushes the user to add more. Because the chip looks identical to a priced one, the user has no signal that the number is missing rather than small.
findings.whatWorks: The search dropdown does render '— · 0' for an unpriced row, and inferValueBundle correctly refuses to fall back to the composite scale (the documented H1 fix holds — 0, not a composite-scale number).
findings.rootCause: effectiveValue coerces a missing board value to 0 and no caller distinguishes 'worth zero' from 'not priced'. src/trade/finder.py already solves this pattern with metadata.assetsUnpricedByBoard; the client-side calculator has no equivalent.
findings.requiredRepair: Carry an `isUnpriced` flag on the row (the contract already stamps rowsUnpricedByBoard), render the chip with a 'not priced' badge, and show a side-level note 'N assets on this side are not priced by the board' so the verdict is read with that caveat.

findings.title: The 'Raw' value mode is not comparable across asset classes: one dropdown click turns a FAIR trade into UNFAIR and flips which side wins
findings.claimUnderTest: dynasty-data.js documents `raw` as 'the legacy scraper composite, ~1.131x the canonical board (measured)' — i.e. a single global scale factor, which would leave every comparison unchanged. VALUE_MODES offers it as a peer of 'Our Value' with no caveat.
findings.observed: The rawComposite/board ratio is not a constant: median 1.1034 for offense, 1.0467 for IDP, 1.0629 for picks — offense sits 5.4% heavier than IDP in Raw mode — and the per-player dispersion is far larger (p25 1.02, p75 1.21). Verified end to end in a real browser: Sam LaPorta (TE) and Sonny Styles (LB) both carry rankDerivedValue 5,222 on the live board. With the value-mode Select on 'Our Value' the meter reads '5,021 VS 5,222 | Gap: 201 | FAIR | Side B wins by 4%'. Selecting 'Raw' — no other change — the same trade reads '5,564 VS 4,180 | Gap: 1,384 | UNFAIR | Side A wins by 25%'. The verdict flips severity AND direction. Nothing in the UI says the two modes are on incomparable scales.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/.venv/bin/python page_probe5.py && .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08/raw_mode_class_drift.py
reproduction.expected: If raw is the board times a constant, a board-even trade stays even in Raw mode: gap 0 both ways.
reproduction.actual: Our Value gap 201 (FAIR, B wins 4%); Raw gap 1,384 (UNFAIR, A wins 25%). Class medians 1.1034 (offense) vs 1.0467 (IDP).

numericProof.formula: gap_raw = rawComposite(A) - rawComposite(B) for a pair with rankDerivedValue(A) == rankDerivedValue(B)

findings.userImpact: A user who flips to 'Raw' to sanity-check a mixed offense/IDP trade gets a verdict that disagrees with the default one by 25 percentage points and names the other winner. In an IDP league — which this one is (356 IDP rows, 331 with a market value) — every cross-class trade is affected. There is no label telling the user which of the two answers to believe.

priorFinding.note: Adjacent to PRIOR-A02-F05 (Monte Carlo ignores the value mode) but that is a threading bug, not a scale-comparability defect.

findings.whatWorks: The mode switch itself threads correctly through effectiveValue -> sideTotal -> adjustedSideTotals -> TradeMeter; the numbers rendered are exactly `_rawComposite`. The defect is that those numbers do not form a single scale.
findings.rootCause: _rawComposite is per-source scraper output normalised within each source's own board (KTC for offense, IDPTradeCalc for IDP), never cross-normalised. The canonical pipeline's percentile/Hill step is what makes classes comparable, and Raw mode is defined as the value BEFORE that step.
findings.requiredRepair: Either remove the Raw mode from the trade calculator (keep it on /rankings as a per-row diagnostic where no cross-row sum is taken), or gate it: when a trade spans more than one asset class in Raw mode, show 'Raw values are per-source and are not comparable across offense/IDP/picks' and suppress the verdict badge.

findings.title: 'Copy KTC URL' hardcodes tep=0, sending a TE-premium league's trade to KTC's non-TE-premium board
findings.claimUnderTest: 'Copy KTC URL' is offered as a second opinion on the same trade. CLAUDE.md states the whole board is anchored on ktcSfTep — 'the anchor IS the TE++ board' — and this league's scoring profile is superflex_tep15_ppr1 with bonusRecTe 0.5 (confirmed in the live contract's rankingsOverride).
findings.observed: build_ktc_url hardcodes params = {var: 5, pickVal: 0, format: 2, isStartup: 0, tep: 0}. Every exported link asks keeptradecut.com to grade the trade on its NO-TE-premium board, while our own page graded it on the TE++ board. For any trade containing a TE the two answers must differ, and nothing in the copied URL or the 'KTC URL copied' toast says so. Secondary: the board's canonical current-year pick row names ('2026 Pick 1.06') are unresolvable by the exporter — it only knows KTC's tier labels ('2026 Mid 1st' -> id 1528) — so a trade containing a current-class pick exports without it.

findings.title: Every trade the arbitrage finder returns is a 1-for-2; 1-for-1 candidates exist but rank 2,159th and 2-for-1 never qualifies at all
findings.claimUnderTest: finder.py generates three package shapes (_generate_1for1, _generate_2for1, _generate_1for2) and ranks them together by arbitrage_score.
findings.observed: 480 returned trades across all 12 teams: 480 are '1-for-2'. Zero 1-for-1, zero 2-for-1. Running find_trades for Jason with max_results=100000 yields 5,562 qualified trades — 5,399 1-for-2, 163 1-for-1, and ZERO 2-for-1 — and the first 1-for-1 appears at rank 2,159. The scoring function is the cause: board_gain_norm = board_delta / give_model divides by the give side only, so shrinking the give side to one asset inflates the dominant term (f_board_edge = board_gain_norm*50) without bound, while the entire counterweight is f_simplicity = -(pkg_size-2)*3 = -3.

priorFinding.note: Prior measured 98% of output in the 1-for-N direction; the live measurement is 100% of returned output (480/480) and 97.1% of qualified output (5399/5562). findings.observed: The 150-asset pool contains 41 WR, 28 QB, 26 RB, 23 PICK, 18 TE, 7 DL, 7 LB and ZERO DB. The board carries 96 DBs; the highest, Caleb Downs (3159), sits at overall rank 167 — 17 places past the cut, against a rank-150 cutoff value of 3259. dynasty_main starts 3 DB per team (36 league-wide starting DB slots) and the engine's own starterNeeds echo 'DB: 3'.
