findings.title: Monte Carlo uncertainty is a hard-coded flat +/-15% band on zero live rows, and the 9999 clamp makes it understate an elite asset by 5.07%
findings.claimUnderTest: monte_carlo.py module docstring: 'Given side-A and side-B as lists of players, each with a valueBand from Phase 4 (p10, p50, p90)... Depends on: Phase 4 confidence intervals'. build_trade_player: 'Prefers the Phase 4 valueBand dict; falls back to +/-15% band'.
findings.observed: 0 of 1,092 playersArray rows carry a valueBand, so the fallback IS the production path for every asset — every player, pick and defender is drawn from an identical +/-15% triangle regardless of whether the board blended 1 source or 14 (effectiveSourceRanks ranges 0-14 across the contract). The frontend synthesizes the same +/-15% band client-side. Worse, _shifted() clamps to 9999 while the +15% leg is not, so for a top-of-board asset the upper half of the band is truncated and the sampled mean falls BELOW the board value: Brock Bowers (rankDerivedValue 9947) simulates at sideAMean 9441.9. No convergence diagnostic, standard error, confidence interval or seed echo is returned; ten identical calls give winProbA 0.0001-0.0003 and meanDelta -4455.2 to -4439.3.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w09-full.json'));print('rows with valueBand:',sum(1 for r in d['playersArray'] if r.get('valueBand')),'of',len(d['playersArray']))" ; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w09.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/trade/simulate-mc -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"sideA":[{"name":"Brock Bowers","rankDerivedValue":9947,"pos":"TE","team":"LV"}],"sideB":[{"name":"Jonathan Taylor","rankDerivedValue":6431,"pos":"RB","team":"IND"},{"name":"Patrick Mahomes","rankDerivedValue":7461,"pos":"QB","team":"KC"}]}' | python -c 'import json,sys;r=json.load(sys.stdin);print(r["sideAMean"], r["nSims"])'
reproduction.expected: sideAMean == 9947 (the board value the user is shown)
reproduction.actual: rows with valueBand: 0 of 1092; sideAMean 9441.9

numericProof.formula: E[draw] = sum over segments of ((lo+hi)/2)*weight, using the piecewise-linear _triangular_draw quantile map

findings.userImpact: On /trade the MC panel says 'Side B came out ahead in 100% of 20,000 simulations'. That number is produced from an invented, uniform uncertainty and a mean that is 5% low for exactly the elite assets a trade usually hinges on. A user rejects an even trade because the simulator's fabricated distribution says it is not close.

blastRadius.playersAffectedNote: 1092 for the fabricated-±15%-band claim (0 rows carry valueBand). Only 12 for the 9999-clamp bias the title leads with — the rows where rankDerivedValue*1.15 > 9999. Bias range -0.27% to -5.21%, not a flat 5.07%.
blastRadius.codePathNote: the live /trade path is MonteCarloButton.jsx:41-60 (client synthesizes the band) + monte_carlo.py:368-376 (valueBand branch) + the _shifted clamp at :365-366. monte_carlo.py:379-387 (the fallback) is reached only by direct API callers.

priorFinding.note: Also confirms PRIOR-A09-F03 and PRIOR-A10-F02, which state the same defect from the constants and documentation angles. New here is the 9999-clamp bias: the fabricated band is not merely uninformative, it is directionally WRONG at the top of the board, understating the board value by 504 points (5.07%) with an analytic derivation that matches the live sideAMean to 1.1 points.

findings.whatWorks: The direction-symmetrization is real and effective (symmetryCheck.drift 0.0001, enforced true), the labelHint/disclaimer contract fields ARE returned by the backend, and run-to-run variance is genuinely small (meanDelta sd 5.1 on a magnitude of 4,447 over 10 runs at 100k sims) — the estimator is stable, it is just estimating a fabricated quantity.
findings.rootCause: The band producer (src/canonical/confidence_intervals) never stamps valueBand onto contract rows, so the documented input does not exist on any live row; the fallback was written as a degradation path and became the only path.
findings.requiredRepair: Either stamp valueBand from the data the contract already carries (effectiveSourceRanks spread / sourceSpread / confidenceBucket are all present per row), or stop reporting a win probability and report the point delta only. At minimum, clamp p50 and p90 consistently so the sampled mean equals the displayed board value, and return a convergence statistic (MC standard error on winProbA) so the reader can tell a stable 0.50 from a noisy one.
findings.dependencies: src/canonical/confidence_intervals.py has no producer wired into the contract build.

verification.reasoning:
The arithmetic is right and I reproduced it three times. sideAMean 9437-9447 against a board value of 9947, and the finding's analytic derivation lands on 9442.98 — inside its own 25-point tolerance. I also ran the control the finding did not: with an unclamped value the sampled mean equals the board value to 0.008% (8000.6 vs 8000), which PROVES the extended-triangular quantile map (monte_carlo.py:104-131) is mean-preserving and that max(0, min(9999, v)) in _shifted (monte_carlo.py:365-366) is the sole cause. The 0-of-1092-valueBand count reproduces exactly. The flag is default-ON (feature_flags.py:112), so the route is live and /trade reaches it.

Two corrections, one of which is a wrong code path.

(1) THE CITED LIVE PATH IS WRONG. codeRefs point at monte_carlo.py:368-387 and the observed text says 'the fallback IS the production path for every asset'. It is not the production path for /trade. MonteCarloButton.jsx:41-60 ALWAYS attaches an explicit valueBand to every asset it posts — it synthesizes p10=v*0.85, p50=v, p90=v*1.15 itself and rounds them — so the backend takes the valueBand branch at monte_carlo.py:368-376, never the fallback at :379-387. The finding's substance is untouched (the client fabricates the numerically identical band, and _shifted clamps p90 in BOTH branches, so the 9999 bias bites on the real page too), but the fallback branch is reached only by direct API callers, and a repair aimed only at monte_carlo.py's fallback would not change what /trade does.

(2) BLAST RADIUS CONFLATES TWO CLAIMS. playersAffected:1092 is honest for the fabricated-±15%-band half (0 of 1092 rows carry a valueBand — verified). It is wrong for the 9999-clamp half, which is what the title leads with and what the numericProof measures. Exactly 12 of 1092 rows satisfy rankDerivedValue*1.15 > 9999, and the bias across them is not a flat 5.07% — it is bias = 0.35*min(9999, 1.15v) - 0.4025v, running from -5.21% (Josh Allen) down to -0.27% (Caleb Williams). Only 6 of the 12 exceed 2%. '5.07%' is the Bowers case, near the worst case, not a population figure.

One thing that STRENGTHENS the finding and the author missed: server.py:11358-11360 states 'The labelHint + disclaimer fields are PART OF THE CONTRACT — the frontend MUST render the disclaimer somewhere visible so users don't mis-read win probability as real-world odds.' grep for 'disclaimer' in MonteCarloButton.jsx returns nothing, and the component's own header docstring says the output is rewritten in plain English with no 'consensus-band samples' language. So the mandated warning is not rendered. That is the closest this comes to P0 territory.

Severity: P1 held. The self-assigned P1 is defensible and I am not escalating it: the fabricated band is uninformative rather than fabricated-in-a-direction for 1,080 of 1,092 rows, and the directional bias the title leads with touches 12 elite assets. The 'no warning shown' condition IS met, but the mispricing is 0.3-5% on a dozen players, not an order-of-magnitude error.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: Nothing outstanding — both halves are settled at runtime. For the repair: clamp p50 and p90 on the same rule (or stop clamping p90 at 9999) and re-run the Bowers call; sideAMean should return 9947 ± 25. Separately, whether the missing disclaimer render is its own finding needs a check of whether any parent of MonteCarloButton surfaces result.disclaimer — grep says no component does.

findings.title: The leagueAdjusted valuation lens is a silent no-op on every all-offense trade in /api/trade/simulate and /api/trade/finder, while the response still stamps valuationMode: leagueAdjusted
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'No engine knows the feature exists, because every engine reads exactly one value — rankDerivedValue' and 'Every response stamps valuationMode — including "market". "This is the market board" and "this field is missing" must not read the same.'
findings.observed: overlay.adjusted_rows multiplies ONLY row['rankDerivedValue'] by the position factor. But both trade_simulator._resolve_asset and finder._score_trade prefer offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue when the trade contains no IDP asset — a field the overlay never touches. A Bowers-for-(Taylor+Mahomes) simulate call returns equity 4004 and per-player values 9950/6472/7482 under BOTH valuationMode=market and valuationMode=leagueAdjusted, and stamps 'leagueAdjusted' on the second. Substituting an IDP asset makes the lens visible immediately (Bowers 9947->10062, Hutchinson 6362->6984), proving the plumbing works and only the offense-only field is missed.

reproduction.command: for M in market leagueAdjusted; do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w09.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/trade/simulate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"teamName\":\"Jason\",\"playersOut\":[\"Brock Bowers\"],\"playersIn\":[\"Jonathan Taylor\",\"Patrick Mahomes\"],\"valuationMode\":\"$M\"}" | python -c 'import json,sys;r=json.load(sys.stdin);print(r["valuationMode"], r["equity"], [(x["name"],x["value"]) for x in r["sending"]+r["receiving"]])'; done
reproduction.expected: equity differs between the two modes
reproduction.actual: market 4004 [...9950, 6472, 7482]; leagueAdjusted 4004 [...9950, 6472, 7482] — byte identical

numericProof.formula: equityAdjusted = taylor*f_RB + mahomes*f_QB - bowers*f_TE

findings.userImpact: A user who switches the board to 'league adjusted' and re-runs a player-for-player trade sees an unchanged verdict labelled as adjusted. They conclude the lens has no effect on trades — or, worse, act on a market-priced equity number believing it is scarcity-corrected. The 291-point gap on this one trade is 7.3% of the equity.

blastRadius.note: 606 rows carry offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue (594 differ from rankDerivedValue): WR 216, RB 139, PICK 96, TE 84, QB 71. A third route, /api/trade/suggestions (src/trade/suggestions.py:767), has the identical branch but returned 0 suggestions in both modes on this stack, so it is unproven and excluded from the count.

priorFinding.note: Prior stated the overlay scales only rankDerivedValue and named suggestions.py as the mixer. New here: route-level live proof on /api/trade/simulate and /api/trade/finder, the exact 291-point arithmetic gap, and the observation that the honest 'valuationMode' stamp CLAUDE.md is proud of is what turns a silent no-op into an active misstatement.

findings.whatWorks: valuation_mode threading itself is real and correct on all five engine routes I tested: each accepts both the snake_case body field and the camelCase form, each stamps valuationMode on the response, and the finder's top-10 result set genuinely changes between modes (driven by the IDP rows, which DO get repriced).
findings.rootCause: overlay.adjusted_rows repriced the field CLAUDE.md says every engine reads, but two engines read a second field (offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue) for all-offense trades — a case the 'every engine reads exactly one value' invariant does not cover.
findings.requiredRepair: Scale offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue by the same factor inside overlay.adjusted_rows (and audit values.* for the same omission), or have the engines stop preferring the offense-only field when a lens is active. Add a test that asserts an all-offense simulate differs between the two modes.

verification.reasoning: Reproduces byte-identically, including the control. Mechanism confirmed in source: src/league_intel/overlay.py:86-93 multiplies ONLY copy['rankDerivedValue']; src/api/trade_simulator.py:63-65 returns row['offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue'] when offense_only, and :209 sets offense_only = trade_has_resolved and not trade_has_idp - gated on TRADE CONTENTS, not on a league setting, so it is the default path for any all-offense trade; src/trade/finder.py:686-691 does the same via Asset.offense_only_model_value. The field is written by the IDP-disabled pre-pass at data_contract.py:9188-9192, which the overlay never sees. I attacked reachability and found it stronger than the finding states, not weaker. frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:1656 exposes the Market / 'My league' SegmentedControl; :1549 and frontend/components/useTradeSimulator.js:39 both send the mode via withValuationMode(). And page.jsx:1678-1694 renders a Banner - 'Valued on your league's board ... Values and ranks are adjusted for positional scarcity measured from this league's rosters' - gated on the CONTRACT overlay, which DOES apply. So the page affirmatively tells the user the numbers are scarcity-adjusted while the simulator panel beside it shows market equity. The response stamps valuationMode='leagueAdjusted' with valuationNote=None, so the documented degrade-and-say-so contract (CLAUDE.md, 'Degrade, never fail') is not triggered either. That is an active misstatement, exactly as the finding argues. Not a harness artifact: /api/valuation/league-adjusted returns 200 with real factors from real rosters. Not fixed at HEAD. Not dead code. One correction: blastRadius playersAffected 812 is not what the contract shows. 606 rows carry offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue and 594 of those differ from rankDerivedValue, so 606 is the set of assets whose lens can be silently dropped. One expansion the finding missed, which I could not confirm live: src/trade/suggestions.py:767 (_eff_val) and :1739-1740 (_serialize_player) take the same offense-only branch under _trade_is_idp_free, so /api/trade/suggestions is a third affected route. On this stack it returned 0 suggestions in both modes for Jason's 57-man roster, so I am not counting it as proven; I leave routesAffected at the 2 the author demonstrated and flag the third as needing its own repro. P1 is honest and, if anything, conservative - the protocol's P0 bar (user acts on a wrong number, page they can reach, no warning shown) is arguably met, since the banner is worse than no warning. I do not inflate an author's own severity, so P1 stands.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: Scale offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue by the same row_factor_key factor inside overlay.adjusted_rows, then re-run the Bowers-for-(Taylor+Mahomes) simulate in both modes: leagueAdjusted must return ~4295 rather than 4004. Separately, drive /api/trade/suggestions to a non-empty result set (the roster that produced 0 here needs diagnosing on its own) to settle whether it is a third route.

findings.title: The Next bridge route for /api/trade/suggestions is the only one of four trade/angle bridges that drops the session cookie, so the suggestions feed 401s from the browser
findings.claimUnderTest: The bridge routes exist so the page works without a reverse proxy in front (finder/route.js header comment).
findings.observed: finder/route.js, angle/find/route.js and angle/packages/route.js each read request.headers.get('cookie') and forward it as a Cookie header. suggestions/route.js sends only Content-Type. The identical request that returns HTTP 200 with a full payload against :8000 returns HTTP 401 {'error':'auth_required'} through :3000. Secondary: the suggestions bridge's abort timeout is 5s while the finder's is 30s, even though the backend suggestions call measures 0.04s and the finder 5.48s — the timeouts are on the wrong routes.

reproduction.command: BODY=$(python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w09-full.json'));print(json.dumps({'roster':d['sleeper']['teams'][0]['players'][:20]}))"); for O in http://127.0.0.1:8000 http://127.0.0.1:3000; do echo -n "$O "; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w09.txt -X POST $O/api/trade/suggestions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$BODY"; done
reproduction.expected: 200 from both origins

numericProof.formula: grep -c Cookie over the four bridge route files

findings.userImpact: Under `npm run dev` and under any deployment where Next serves /api/ directly (as this audit container does), the trade-suggestions panel is permanently signed out. In production nginx routes /api/ to the backend and the bridge is bypassed, so the failure is dev/staging-only — which is exactly why it survives.

priorFinding.note: Prior stated the class ('bridge routes are inconsistent about forwarding the session cookie'); this pins the specific route, the specific status codes, and the three siblings that get it right.

findings.whatWorks: finder, angle/find and angle/packages bridges all forward the cookie correctly and return the backend's status verbatim.
findings.rootCause: Omitted header in one hand-written proxy; no test covers bridge-route cookie forwarding.
findings.requiredRepair: Add `Cookie: request.headers.get('cookie') || ''` to suggestions/route.js. Swap the two abort timeouts. Add one test that asserts every file under frontend/app/api/**/route.js that POSTs to BACKEND_API_URL forwards the cookie header.

findings.title: The finder's 'high confidence' tier is structurally unreachable: it measures the scraper's 3-source site count against a 5-source baseline while the board blends up to 14
findings.claimUnderTest: finder.py: confidence = source_confidence * ktc_confidence with CONFIDENCE_SOURCE_BASELINE = 5 'Expected source count for full confidence'; _confidence_tier returns 'high' at >= 0.75.
findings.observed: source_count is read from the legacy players dict's _sites field. Across the whole live payload _sites takes only the values 1 (526 rows), 2 (110), 3 (438) and null (18) — the maximum is 3. source_confidence therefore maxes at min(1, 3/5) = 0.60, and with ktc_confidence = 1.0 the confidence score cannot exceed 0.60, one tier below the 0.75 'high' threshold. All 480 returned trades across 12 teams are 'moderate' (244) or 'low' (236); 'high' appears zero times. The board's real blend count is on the contract rows: Brock Bowers has 12 effective post-Hampel sources while his _sites reads 3, and the contract's effectiveSourceRanks distribution runs to 14.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;from collections import Counter;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w09-full.json'));print('_sites:',Counter(p.get('_sites') for p in d['players'].values()));r=[x for x in d['playersArray'] if x.get('canonicalName')=='Brock Bowers'][0];print('Bowers effectiveSourceRanks:',len(r['effectiveSourceRanks']),'vs _sites:',d['players'][r['legacyRef']]['_sites'])" ; python -c "import json,glob;from collections import Counter;print(Counter(t['confidenceTier'] for f in glob.glob('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W09/finder-*.json') for t in json.load(open(f))['trades']))"
reproduction.expected: some trades reach confidenceTier 'high'
reproduction.actual: _sites max is 3; Bowers effectiveSourceRanks 12 vs _sites 3; Counter({'moderate': 244, 'low': 236})

numericProof.formula: maxConfidence = min(1, maxSites/CONFIDENCE_SOURCE_BASELINE) * ktc_confidence

findings.userImpact: Every arbitrage recommendation on /arbitrage is labelled at most 'moderate confidence', including trades resting on a 12-source consensus. The label is uninformative in one direction and misleadingly pessimistic in the other, and the confidence multiplier (0.7 + 0.3*conf) applies a permanent 0.88 haircut to every score, so it also cannot reorder anything.

priorFinding.note: Prior called the tier 'a constant'. It is not constant — it varies between moderate and low across 480 live trades — but the prior's mechanism claim (it reads the scraper's site count instead of the board's blend count) is exactly right, and the sharper consequence is that the top tier is arithmetically unreachable and the multiplier is a fixed 0.88 for every full-coverage trade.

findings.whatWorks: ktc_confidence and the full/partial coverage distinction are computed correctly; the confidence field is honestly surfaced in the payload rather than hidden.
findings.rootCause: build_asset_pool populates source_count from pdata['_sites'] (the scraper's site count) even on the migrated board path, where the correct quantity is len(row['effectiveSourceRanks']) from the contract.
findings.requiredRepair: Read the blend count from the contract row alongside board_values and positions (a third `source_counts_from_contract` map in the same keying), or lower CONFIDENCE_SOURCE_BASELINE to match _sites' actual range. The first is correct; the second only hides it.

findings.title: The finder's 'arbitrage' score is 80% own-side gain and 20% opponent appeal, so it ranks lopsidedness rather than the market/board gap it is named for
findings.claimUnderTest: finder.py header: 'Arbitrage score: how much we gain on our board while the opponent sees a fair/favorable deal on KTC.'
findings.observed: Measured over all 480 returned trades: mean f_board_edge = 21.81, mean f_ktc_appeal = 4.95. |boardEdge| accounts for 80.2% of |boardEdge|+|ktcAppeal|. The weights are literal (board_gain_norm*50 vs opp_appeal*30) but the two inputs are not on comparable scales — board_gain_norm routinely exceeds 0.4 on 1-for-2 packages while opp_appeal is gated to be merely positive and averages 0.165. The opponent-appeal term is effectively a pass/fail gate (opp_appeal <= 0 returns None) with a small tiebreaker attached, not half of an arbitrage measure.

reproduction.command: python -c "import json,glob,statistics;c=[t['rankingFactors'] for f in glob.glob('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W09/finder-*.json') for t in json.load(open(f))['trades']];print('mean boardEdge',round(statistics.mean(x['boardEdge'] for x in c),2),'mean ktcAppeal',round(statistics.mean(x['ktcAppeal'] for x in c),2));print('boardEdge share',round(statistics.mean(abs(x['boardEdge'])/(abs(x['boardEdge'])+abs(x['ktcAppeal'])) for x in c)*100,1))"
reproduction.expected: roughly balanced contribution between the two named halves
reproduction.actual: mean boardEdge 21.81, mean ktcAppeal 4.95, boardEdge share 80.2%

numericProof.formula: boardEdgeShare = mean(|boardEdge| / (|boardEdge| + |ktcAppeal|))

findings.userImpact: The top of /arbitrage is ordered by how much the user gains, not by how likely the counterparty is to say yes. A user works the list top-down and gets refused, because the ordering optimises the wrong half of the pitch.

priorFinding.note: Prior claimed 93/7; the live measurement over 480 trades is 80/20. The direction and the mechanism are confirmed; the magnitude differs, which matters because the prior's number would have implied ktcAppeal is nearly inert and it is not.

findings.whatWorks: rankingFactors is a genuinely useful disclosure — every component of the score is stamped per trade, which is what made this measurable at all without instrumenting the engine.
findings.rootCause: Two multipliers (50 and 30) applied to inputs with very different natural ranges, one of which is additionally floor-gated at zero.
findings.requiredRepair: Standardise both terms (e.g. rank-percentile or z-score within the candidate set) before weighting, or state the intended ratio and assert it in a test against a live payload.
findings.dependencies: W09-F002 — the 1-for-2 monoculture is what inflates board_gain_norm in the first place.

findings.title: Finder metadata.myRosterSize reports the post-filter asset count, understating a 57-man roster as 34 and a 44-man roster as 12

findings.title: The finder performs no dominance pruning: 40 returned trades for Jason are built from only 4 distinct give-side assets, one of which appears in 20 of them
findings.claimUnderTest: _deduplicate 'Remove duplicate trade packages (same assets, different order)' followed by a score sort and a MAX_RESULTS=40 cap.

findings.userImpact: The user scrolls a 40-row list believing it surveys their trade options; it surveys four of their players. Genuinely different opportunities on the rest of the roster are below the cap and never rendered.

findings.title: Monte Carlo run-to-run variance is small but no convergence statistic is exposed, and the panel that calls it 404s through the Next origin
findings.claimUnderTest: Prompt section 15: run simulate-mc 10 times on the same input and measure variance; is convergence exposed; does simulate disagree with simulate-mc?
findings.observed: Variance is genuinely low — 10 identical calls give meanDelta in [-4455.2, -4439.3] (population sd 5.13 on a magnitude of 4,447, i.e. 0.12%), stdDelta in [1439.3, 1449.6], winProbA in [0.0001, 0.0003]. But no convergence statistic, standard error, confidence interval or seed echo is returned, so a caller cannot distinguish a stable 0.50 from a noisy one; the only diagnostic is symmetryCheck.drift, which measures ordering bias, not convergence. nSims is also reported as double the request (asked 50000, got 100000) because symmetrize sums the two directional passes (symmetrize.py:74) — the UI renders that as 'X% of 100,000 simulations'. simulate and simulate-mc do NOT disagree on value source: both prefer offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue for all-offense trades and agree at 4004 / -3945 respectively once the same inputs are used (the 59-point gap is entirely explained by the frontend sending effectiveValue while the backend simulate reads the row). Separately, POST /api/trade/simulate-mc and /api/trade/simulate return 404 through http://127.0.0.1:3000, which is the origin the page is served from — MonteCarloButton fetches the relative path, so the panel is dead outside a reverse-proxied deployment.

reproduction.command: for i in $(seq 10); do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w09.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/trade/simulate-mc -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"sideA":[{"name":"Brock Bowers","rankDerivedValue":9947,"pos":"TE","team":"LV"}],"sideB":[{"name":"Jonathan Taylor","rankDerivedValue":6431,"pos":"RB","team":"IND"},{"name":"Patrick Mahomes","rankDerivedValue":7461,"pos":"QB","team":"KC"}]}' | python -c 'import json,sys;r=json.load(sys.stdin);print(r["meanDelta"], r["winProbA"], r["nSims"])'; done ; curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'next-origin simulate-mc=%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/trade/simulate-mc -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
reproduction.expected: a convergence/SE field, nSims matching the request, and a reachable route from the page origin
reproduction.actual: meanDelta spread 15.9 over 10 runs; no SE/CI/seed field; nSims 100000 for a 50000 request; next-origin simulate-mc=404

numericProof.formula: relativeRunToRunSd = sd(meanDelta) / |mean(meanDelta)|

findings.userImpact: A user cannot tell whether a 50/50 result is a genuine coin flip or sampling noise, and the sim count quoted in the plain-English summary is twice what was requested. In any deployment where Next serves /api/ (dev, and this audit container), the button errors out.

priorFinding.note: The missing-bridge-route half is exactly PRIOR-A14-F23, verified live (404 on both simulate and simulate-mc through :3000 while finder/angle bridges answer). The convergence-exposure and nSims-doubling observations are new. I could NOT reproduce PRIOR-A14-F06's claim that the frontend strips the disclaimer in a way that makes the result unreadable — the backend does return labelHint + disclaimer, and MonteCarloButton does substitute its own plain-English text; whether that violates the contract is a judgement call I am recording as partial rather than confirmed.

findings.whatWorks: The estimator is stable and the symmetrization is real and verified (drift 0.0001, enforced true). The 503 feature-disabled path is clean.
findings.rootCause: No SE computation in monte_carlo.py; nSims summed across the two symmetrization passes; no route.js under frontend/app/api/trade/simulate*.
findings.requiredRepair: Return mcStandardError = sqrt(p*(1-p)/nSims) on winProbA and echo the seed. Report nSims as requested (or rename to nDraws). Add the two bridge routes, forwarding the cookie.
findings.dependencies: W09-F005 — a convergence statistic on a fabricated distribution still describes the wrong quantity.

findings.title: Every bid recommendation on /draft ignores the user's remaining budget — with $4 left the board says "Win at $69 / Max bid $80 / Push up to $48"
findings.claimUnderTest: draft-logic.js's header documents Winning bid(p) = min(Theoretical Max, topCompetitorMax + 1) and describes effectiveBudgetFor as 'the maximum $ a team can actually bid on a single player right now'. The /draft modal advertises an overpay guard.
findings.observed: theoreticalMaxBid, myMaxBid, myWinningBid and enforceUpTo are computed from preDraft x aggression x tierInflation x phaseMultiplier and capped ONLY by topCompetitorMax + 1. Not one of them reads myRemaining or effectiveBudgetByIdx[myTeamIdx]. effectiveBudgetFor() is applied to RIVALS only (line 480-485 skips myTeamIdx). bidStatus() classifies against myWinningBid, so a bid 6x the user's cash reads 'Push up'. The only modal warning fires on amt > myWinningBid, never on amt > myRemaining, so entering an unaffordable amount below the ceiling shows nothing at all.

reproduction.command: node docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W10/probe-bid-vs-budget.mjs
reproduction.expected: a bid ceiling <= myRemaining ($4), or an affordability warning
reproduction.actual: myRemaining=4, Sonny Styles myMaxBid=$80, myWinningBid=$69, enforceUpTo=$48, bidStatus($24) = {level:'push', label:'Push up'}

numericProof.formula: theoreticalMaxBid = floor(preDraft * (1 + aggression*(BA-1)) * inflation*tierMult * phaseMultiplier); myWinningBid = min(theoreticalMaxBid, topCompetitorMax + 1); NO min(..., myRemaining) term exists

findings.userImpact: Mid-draft the user reads 'Win at $69' on a player they can only pay $4 for, bids, and either loses the auction after driving the price up or wins a bid they cannot fund. The bid-status chip actively says 'Push up' on an amount 6x their cash.

blastRadius.note: 72 is the default rookie pool (DEFAULT_ROOKIES) and is really 'every player in the user's workspace' — the omission is per-player-universal, not limited to 72. Manifests only while myRemaining < myWinningBid; at the pristine state ($417 vs $69) every emitted number is affordable and the defect is invisible.

priorFinding.note: Independently reproduced at runtime with concrete numbers and the bidStatus consequence, which the prior finding did not quantify. The slot half of the prior finding is split out as W10-F002.

findings.whatWorks: The rival-side ceiling (effectiveBudgetFor over other teams) is applied correctly and topCompetitorMax does cap the recommendation from above; the overpay banner fires correctly for the case it does cover (amount above the rival ceiling).
findings.rootCause: myWinningBid was designed as 'the price that beats the field', and no second clamp for 'the price I can actually pay' was ever added. effectiveBudgetFor exists and would answer it, but is deliberately skipped for myTeamIdx.
findings.requiredRepair: Clamp every emitted bid number by effectiveBudgetFor(myRemaining, mySlotsRemaining) and add an affordability state to bidStatus distinct from 'pass'. Add an amt > myRemaining branch to the modal warning.
findings.dependencies: Depends on W10-F002 — mySlotsRemaining is currently wrong, so the clamp must not be built on the capped slot count.

verification.reasoning:
The defect is real and I could not break the reproduction. The severity is not.

CONFIRMED: (a) the probe re-ran and produced the stated numbers exactly; it drives the real library API (createDefaultWorkspace -> recordPick -> computeDraftStats), not a hand-built fixture. (b) The code has no budget clamp: draft-logic.js:734-748 computes theoreticalMaxBid from preDraft x aggression x combinedInflation x phaseMultiplier and myWinningBid = min(theoreticalMaxBid, topCompetitorMax + 1); myRemaining appears nowhere in that block (grep: myRemaining is used at :426, :524-528, :866, :974, :1032, :1897 — never in bid derivation). (c) :479-481 skips myTeamIdx when reducing effectiveBudgetByIdx, so effectiveBudgetFor is rival-only as claimed. (d) bidStatus (:2517-2537) classifies only against myWinningBid/enforceUpTo — 'Push up' at $24 on $4 cash reproduced. (e) The columns are live and user-facing: a real /draft load through request interception renders ENFORCE / WIN AT / MAX BID headers with dollar values. (f) 72 = default pool size, confirmed. (g) Not fixed at HEAD. (h) The modal warning at page.jsx:794-814 fires only on amt > myCeiling, so an unaffordable bid below the ceiling shows nothing — confirmed by reading the branch.

WHERE IT OVERSTATES — 'with no warning shown', which is the P0 bar in the protocol:
- page.jsx:250-254 renders 'My remaining' as a permanent card in the stats strip ABOVE the same table that shows Win at, with tooltip 'Starting $X - spent $Y'. The user is looking at $4 and $69 simultaneously. That is not a warning attached to the recommendation, but it is not a hidden or fabricated number either — nothing on screen tells the user they have more money than they do.
- The bid modal's simulator (page.jsx:838-841) shows 'My remaining before -> after' for the entered amount.
- The Target Board / par sheet carries a real budget-aware buffer (draft-logic.js:866, :974) that goes red when myRemaining cannot cover committed targets, described in the page's own help text at :3257 ('Short (red): buffer < 0 - you can't afford'). Opt-in, and not per-player, but it exists.
- The emitted number is not wrong under its own definition. myWinningBid is documented as 'the price that beats the field' (:741-743) and it correctly is that. The defect is a missing second clamp, not a miscomputation. No server-side value, trade price or ranking is wrong.

The genuinely misleading surfaces are bidStatus returning 'Push up' on an amount 6x the user's cash and nextBestTargets recommending targets they cannot fund — both real, both advice defects rather than a wrong number acted on blind. Downgrading to P1: reachable, live, ships bad advice in a common late-auction state, but the contradicting fact is on screen and nothing downstream of /draft is corrupted. Keeping this at P0 alongside W03-F001 (where the page and the trade engine serve different prices for the same asset with no contradicting number anywhere) would flatten a real severity difference.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: Whether this is P0 or P1 turns on one UX question I cannot settle by code reading: does a mid-auction user read the 'Win at' cell or the 'My remaining' card first. A five-user session on /draft with a spent-down workspace would settle it. The code defect itself needs nothing further — there is no min(..., myRemaining) term anywhere in draft-logic.js.

findings.title: mergeDraftCapitalTeams hard-caps every team's slot count at 6, so the user's team — which owns 31 of the 72 live picks — renders as "0/6 slots" with a 5.2x-wrong $/slot
findings.claimUnderTest: The user's stated requirement is that the rookie auction optimizer has NO FIXED PLAYER SLOTS, no minimum and no maximum player count. draft-logic.js's own docstring says DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS 'only applies to a pristine workspace before the fetch completes' and that 'the actual per-team count is pulled from /api/draft-capital's picks array'.
findings.observed: buildTeam() computes initialSlots = Math.min(feedSlots, DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS) — DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS = 6 is a hard MAXIMUM applied to the live feed, not a pre-fetch default. Live /api/draft-capital reports Russini Panini owning 31 picks and CollinFoz 7; both are clamped to 6. Total board slots collapse from 72 to 46. Everything downstream is wrong: slotPressure saturates at 1.0 after 6 picks (true 6/31 = 0.19), phaseMultiplier locks at its 1.5x maximum for the remaining 25 picks, effectiveBudget reserves $5 instead of $30, and mdv ($/slot) reads $114 instead of $22. Confirmed in the rendered DOM: the Teams panel prints '0/6' and 'MDV $114' for a $685 / 31-pick team, and the header phase card prints '6 of 6 slots'.

reproduction.command: node docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W10/probe-slot-cap.mjs   # then: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W10/probe-draft-page.py
reproduction.expected: initialSlots 31 for Russini Panini, totalInitialSlots 72, mdv 685/31 = $22
reproduction.actual: initialSlots 6, totalInitialSlots 46, mdv $114, DOM shows '0/6' and '6 of 6 slots'

numericProof.formula: initialSlots = min(feedSlots, 6); mdv = remaining / slotsRemaining; slotPressure = 1 - slotsRemaining/initialSlots; phaseMultiplier = 1 + slotPressure*0.5

findings.userImpact: The user's own team is modelled as having 6 roster spots when it has 31. After 6 picks the app declares the draft over for them — slots 0, effective budget $0, phase multiplier pinned at 1.5x, and the 'Spend up — don't let $ go unused' recommendation fires — while $679 and 25 picks are still live. Every MaxBid for the remaining 25 picks is inflated by 1.5/1.097 = 1.37x by the saturated phase multiplier.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced against the live feed and the rendered DOM, and quantified the four downstream consequences (slotPressure, phaseMultiplier, effectiveBudget, mdv) the prior finding named but did not measure.

findings.whatWorks: slotsByTeamFromPicks() itself is correct — it returns the true 31/7/6/... counts from the live picks array. The corruption is introduced one function later.
findings.rootCause: A single Math.min against a constant named 'DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS' that is being used as a maximum. In a league with pick trading the number of picks a team owns is unbounded above.
findings.requiredRepair: Delete both Math.min(..., DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS) clamps in buildTeam(). Keep DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS strictly as the pre-fetch fallback its docstring describes.
findings.dependencies: W10-F001's proposed budget clamp must land after this, or it will clamp against the wrong slot count.

verification.reasoning:
Reproduced end to end today, on the running stack, through the sanctioned topology.

Code: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:1427-1431 is exactly `Math.min(feedSlots, DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS)` with DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS = 6 (line 53), applied to the LIVE feed branch (`picksArray ? ...`), which directly contradicts the constant's own docstring at lines 47-52 ('the actual per-team count is pulled from /api/draft-capital's picks array; this default only applies to a pristine workspace before the fetch completes').

Live path confirmed, not scaffolded: frontend/app/draft/page.jsx:3867 calls mergeDraftCapitalTeams with {picks: picksArray}, and :3909 fires fetchDraftCapital({quiet:true}) on mount - a silent auto-populate, no button press required. myTeamIdx defaults to 0 (draft-logic.js:324) and DEFAULT_TEAMS[0] is 'Russini Panini' (:162), so the clamped team IS the user's own team on the default path.

Input is genuine, not a harness artifact: the live /api/draft-capital for dynasty_main returns 72 picks with currentOwner attribution, 31 of them to Russini Panini, and teamTotals $685 - a real pick-hoarding state from the default league's Draft Data.xlsx path, not a fallback or a placeholder.

DOM confirmed in a real browser with request interception: 'Pick 0 of 46' (should be 72), 'PHASE 6 of 6 slots', and the user's own row printing '0/6' with MDV $114 against a true $685/31 = $22.10. Zero console errors, so this is not a degraded render. P0 predicate is met exactly: reachable page, auto-loaded, wrong number displayed, no warning anywhere in the rendered text, and the number is the one the user bids off.

Not already fixed at HEAD, and worse, deliberately pinned: frontend/__tests__/draft-logic.test.js:1291 is titled 'sets initialSlots from the picks array when supplied, CAPPED AT DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS' and asserts Russini (8 feed picks) -> 6. So the repo carries two contradictory declarations of intent (docstring vs test) and the repair must delete the test assertion too - worth adding to requiredRepair.

Two secondary consequence claims did NOT reproduce and should be corrected in the record, though neither touches the headline:
  (a) "the 'Spend up - don't let $ go unused' recommendation fires": it does not. playerRecommendation gates on stats.slotPressure >= SPEND_UP_PRESSURE_MIN (0.6) AND mdv > SPEND_UP_MDV_FLOOR (10) (draft-logic.js:1899-1903), and with slotsRemaining driven to 0 the local mdv is 0, so the gate fails. I drove the workspace to 1..5 clamped picks with the next player userTag='target' and got level 'neutral' at every pressure step including 0.667 and 0.833.
  (b) 'Every MaxBid for the remaining 25 picks is inflated by 1.5/1.097 = 1.37x': the phase-multiplier ratio is right but it is not the whole mechanism, because effectiveBudget simultaneously collapses to $0. Measured on the next live player after 6 picks: maxBid $4 clamped vs $2 true - a 2x distortion, not 1.37x, and the sign of the error is not uniform across the pool.

Blast radius recount: 72 picks / 1 route / 1 page stands. Two of eleven owning teams are clamped (Russini 31->6, CollinFoz 7->6); the other nine are unaffected, so the '46 vs 72' total-slot error is wholly attributable to those two rows. That does not narrow the user-facing harm, because one of the two is the user's own team and every stat on the header card (Pick x of 46, PHASE, MDV, EFF $) is derived from it.

findings.title: There is no perfect-draft optimizer: the only recommender is an unconstrained per-player sort whose 'EV' is zero for every contested player, so the panel is EMPTY whenever budget advantage >= 1
findings.claimUnderTest: Prompt section 26/27 asks whether the optimizer is a greedy value-per-dollar ranking or a real combinatorial optimizer. draft-logic.js documents nextBestTargets as an 'EV model' that ranks players 'by expected value'.
findings.observed: Neither. grep for perfect.?draft / optimiz / knapsack / combinator over all .py/.js/.jsx finds nothing but a 'Nomination optimizer' comment. nextBestTargets scores each player independently as ev = max(0, inflatedFair - myWinningBid) * tagWeight + scarcityBoost, sorts, and slices to a fixed limit=5. It never enumerates subsets, never checks budget feasibility, and never considers a second player. It is not even greedy value-per-dollar: myWinningBid collapses to the CONSTANT topCompetitorMax+1 for every player whose ceiling clears the field, so the 'price' is identical ($19) for a $60 asset and a $1 asset — there is no per-dollar quantity to rank by. Worse, the surplus term is structurally zero whenever budgetAdvantage >= 1 and the top rival can still cover fair value (theoreticalMax >= inflatedFair, and the min() then returns inflatedFair), and the ev <= 0 filter drops those rows: measured 0 rows returned at BA 1.0, 1.1, 1.5 and 3.0, versus 3 rows at BA 0.33. The panel populates only when the user is POORER than the field or the field is bankrupt.

reproduction.command: node docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W10/probe-nbt-emptiness.mjs && node docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W10/probe-greedy-suboptimal.mjs
reproduction.expected: a budget-feasible recommended SET, or at minimum a non-empty ranked list at ordinary budget advantage
reproduction.actual: BA 1.0/1.1/1.5/3.0 -> 0 rows returned; at BA 3.25 the returned order is byte-identical to a plain preDraft-descending sort, and every row carries the same Win-at price of $19

numericProof.formula: ev = max(0, inflatedFair - myWinningBid) * tagWeight + scarcityBoost, where myWinningBid = min(theoreticalMax, topCompetitorMax+1) = 19 for all four rows

findings.userImpact: There is no tool that answers 'given my $685 and my 31 picks, which set of rookies should I buy'. The one panel that looks like it answers that is blank for any user whose budget is at or above the league average — i.e. exactly the user this app was built for (live BA on /draft is 14.63x only because the slot cap of W10-F002 and the workbook budgets make it so). The requirement of no fixed player count is vacuously satisfied by there being no set-selection logic at all.

priorFinding.note: Prior said 'a preDraft sort wearing an EV model's clothes' — confirmed byte-for-byte on ordering. Extended with two facts the prior did not have: the price term is constant across players (so value-per-dollar is undefined), and the panel returns ZERO rows for BA >= 1.

findings.whatWorks: The sort is stable and deterministic, the AVOID tag exclusion works, and the tier-scarcity boost is applied as documented.
findings.rootCause: 'EV' was defined as surplus-against-my-own-winning-bid rather than value-per-dollar or a constrained subset objective. Because myWinningBid is derived from the same preDraft the surplus is measured against, the metric degenerates.
findings.requiredRepair: Build the actual optimizer: a bounded knapsack over (expected clearing price, board value) with the budget as the capacity, NO slot cardinality constraint (per the stated requirement), allowing the empty set and unspent budget as valid answers. Keep nextBestTargets as a separate 'cheapest relative to fair' screen and rename its 'ev' field, which is not an expected value.
findings.dependencies: Needs a per-player expected clearing price that is not a league-wide constant, and needs W10-F002 fixed so the budget capacity is real.

findings.title: Vendor 'Market' dollars are normalized to $1200 over a different row count per vendor, so KTC overrates 44 of the 45 rookies it covers and underrates none
findings.claimUnderTest: page.jsx documents the vendor dollars as making 'the vendorDollar - preDraft gap an honest "how many more dollars would a vendor-following leaguemate spend at this slot than my board does"'. nominationCandidates selects on vendorDollar > preDraft; bestValueOnBoard selects on preDraft > vendorDollar.
findings.observed: Every vendor column is _rookie_dollars_from_values(values, total=1200) — the SAME $1200 pool spread over a DIFFERENT number of rows: 72 for our board, 45 for KTC, 63 for IDPTC. Mean dollar is therefore 1200/45 = $26.67 for KTC against 1200/72 = $16.67 for us, a pure artefact of coverage. On the live payload KTC's dollar exceeds ours for 44 of 45 covered rookies and is below ours for 0. Downstream: nominationCandidates ('vendor overrates us') fires on 51 of 72 rookies including the board's own #1; bestValueOnBoard ('we rate them above the market') finds ZERO qualifying offense rows and fills 8 of its 10 slots with backfill.

reproduction.command: node docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W10/probe-vendor-rowcount.mjs
reproduction.expected: roughly balanced over/under counts between our board and a vendor board
reproduction.actual: KTC overrates 44, underrates 0; nominationCandidates returns 51/72; bestValueOnBoard offense qualifiers = 0

numericProof.formula: mean vendor dollar = 1200 / rows_covered; systematic lift = (1200/45) / 20.67 = 1.29x

findings.userImpact: The 'Nomination targets' panel tells the user to nominate their own #1 rookie (Jeremiyah Love) on the grounds that KTC overrates him by $3.50 — the $3.50 is a normalization artefact, not a market read. The 'Best value on the board' panel can never surface a genuine offense bargain because the comparison is biased against it by construction.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced exactly on the live payload and quantified the 1.29x lift plus both downstream panel effects.

findings.whatWorks: The Hill-curve dollar conversion itself is faithful — every column independently sums to exactly $1200, and the offense/IDP vendor routing picks the right vendor per row.
findings.rootCause: Each vendor's ranking is converted to dollars against the full $1200 league pool regardless of how many rookies that vendor actually publishes, so coverage differences become value differences.
findings.requiredRepair: Normalize each vendor over the pool value of the rows it covers (sum of OUR dollars for the same players), not over $1200. Or compare ranks rather than dollars.

findings.title: 'Best value on the board' renders backfill rows as green underrate signals with a double-negative percentage — 8 of 10 live rows say the vendor UNDERRATES a player the vendor actually rates higher
findings.claimUnderTest: bestValueOnBoard's docstring says the backfill exists so 'the panel always shows limit rows so the user can see what's still on the board even if we don't strictly outrate the market on every name' — i.e. backfill rows are explicitly NOT edge signals.
findings.observed: The renderer does not distinguish qualified rows from backfill rows. It emits a hardcoded minus sign in front of the already-signed percentage — `−{Math.round(gapPct * 100)}%` — and a tooltip reading '{vendorLabel} underrates by {gapPct*100}%'. On the live board 8 of the 10 rows are backfill with NEGATIVE gapPct, so they render as e.g. '−-18%' with the tooltip 'KTC underrates by -18% (+$-11 board edge)' for Jadarian Price, whom KTC rates $11.50 ABOVE our board.

reproduction.command: node docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W10/probe-vendor-rowcount.mjs   # inspect the bestValueOnBoard rows and their gapPct signs
reproduction.expected: backfill rows rendered neutrally, or excluded from the edge styling
reproduction.actual: rows with gapPct -0.18, -0.16, -0.12, -0.06, -0.04, -0.03, -0.03, -0.01 rendered through the '−{pct}%' underrate template

numericProof.formula: gap = ourDollar - vendorDollar = -11.5; gapPct = gap/vendorDollar = -0.1797; rendered as '−' + round(gapPct*100) + '%'

findings.userImpact: The panel headlined 'Best value on the board' presents the eight rookies the market most OVERRATES as the eight the market most underrates. A user shopping this panel buys exactly the players they should be selling.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced on the live board with the exact eight negative-gap rows.

findings.whatWorks: The two qualified rows (CJ Allen +29%, Dillon Thieneman +7%) are correct and correctly signed.
findings.rootCause: The backfill tier was added to guarantee a full panel, and the row template was reused verbatim without a qualified/backfill discriminator on the row objects.
findings.requiredRepair: Stamp `qualified: true|false` on each row in bestValueOnBoard and render backfill rows with neutral styling and no percentage. Remove the hardcoded '−' and use the sign already carried by gapPct.
findings.dependencies: Largely moot once W10-F004 is fixed — with an unbiased comparison the qualified tier will fill the panel — but the renderer bug should be fixed independently.

findings.title: The inflation multiplier is unbounded and its degradation flag has no UI consumer — at pick 71 on the live pool a $1 rookie shows a fair price of $112 and a max bid of $168 with no warning
findings.claimUnderTest: The in-file comment states: 'An absurd value substituted for an error is worse than no value, so degrade to "no global inflation" and say so; inflationDegraded lets the UI tell the user their PreDraft column is over-allocated instead of quietly showing four-figure fair prices.'
findings.observed: Two problems. (1) grep for inflationDegraded across frontend/ returns draft-logic.js and __tests__ only — NO page or component reads it, so when the guard fires the UI silently switches to inflation=1 and says nothing. (2) The guard fires only once expectedPoolRemaining <= 0, i.e. strictly AFTER the divergence has already happened: inflation = remainingLeague / (totalBudget - soldPreDraft) has a pole as soldPreDraft approaches totalBudget, and the run below (live 72-rookie pool that sums to exactly $1200, every pick paid at 0.9x preDraft) reaches inflation 11.45x at pick 61 and 116x at pick 71 with inflationDegraded still false the whole way.

reproduction.command: node docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W10/probe-inflation-livepool.mjs
reproduction.expected: a bounded multiplier, or a degradation notice before four-figure-ratio prices appear
reproduction.actual: picks=61 inflation=11.45 degraded=false; picks=71 inflation=116.00 degraded=false, next undrafted preDraft=$1 -> FAIR=$112 MAX=$168

numericProof.formula: inflation = remainingLeague / (totalBudget - soldPreDraft) = 116 / 1 = 116; inflatedFair = floor(preDraft * inflation * tierMult)

findings.userImpact: In the last dozen picks of a real draft the board tells the user a $1 rookie is worth $112 and that they may bid up to $168, with no warning banner. The arithmetic is not wholly fictional — money genuinely does chase a thin board late — but nothing caps it against the number of players left or against the user's cash (W10-F001), so the displayed number is unusable as guidance.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced with the real 72-row $1200 pool rather than the pristine board, which rules out the DEFAULT_ROOKIES $1211 mismatch (W10-F013) as the sole cause — the pole is in the formula itself.

findings.whatWorks: The degradation branch itself is correct and does prevent the ~800x case the comment describes; soldPreDraft correctly uses the preDraftAtPick snapshot so retroactive edits do not rewrite history.
findings.rootCause: An unbounded ratio with a guard placed at the far side of its own singularity, plus a status flag that was returned but never wired to a renderer.
findings.requiredRepair: Cap the multiplier (e.g. remainingLeague / max(expectedPoolRemaining, undraftedCount)) and render inflationDegraded — and a new 'inflation clamped' state — as a visible banner on /draft.

findings.title: /draft issues three /api/draft-capital fetches per load and two of them omit leagueKey, so the rookie pool and per-slot dollars always come from the default league
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Draft capital (per-team auction budgets, pick ownership)' follows leagueKey, and page.jsx line 3835 comments 'Scope the draft-capital fetch to the active league so per-team auction budgets come from the right Sleeper league.'
findings.observed: Only fetchDraftCapital (line 3840) is scoped. The rookie-pool auto-sync (3597) and the 'Sync from contract' path (4210) both call the bare '/api/draft-capital' with no leagueKey, so they resolve to the user's activeLeagueKey pref or the registry default rather than the league selected on the page. With dynasty_new selected the page merges dynasty_new's 10-team budgets and slot counts against dynasty_main's 12-team / 6-round / 72-pick rookie pool and its per-slot dollar curve. Compounding this, the non-default league's payload carries no rookieName / rookieKtcValue at all (Sleeper-derived fallback), and rescaleValuesToBudget is called with a hardcoded 1200 regardless of league.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/draft-capital?leagueKey=dynasty_new' | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['numTeams'], d['draftRounds'], len(d['picks']), any(p.get('rookieName') for p in d['picks']))"
reproduction.expected: the /draft rookie pool and slot dollars to match the selected league's shape
reproduction.actual: dynasty_new returns numTeams=10 draftRounds=4 picks=80 rookieName-present=False, while the unscoped fetches return dynasty_main's 12/6/72 board with a full rookie pool

numericProof.formula: pool budget per league should be teamCount * per-team auction dollars; the page uses 1200 unconditionally

findings.userImpact: A user on the second league sees the first league's rookie board and the first league's $1200/72-pick dollar curve stapled to their own team budgets. Nothing on the page says the two halves came from different leagues.

priorFinding.note: Prior flagged PickProjectorPanel mounting without a leagueKey. This is the same class of defect on two different call sites (the rookie-pool auto-sync and the contract sync), which the prior finding did not name.

findings.whatWorks: fetchDraftCapital is correctly scoped and the backend honours leagueKey properly — the dynasty_new response is genuinely that league's rosters and traded picks.
findings.rootCause: leagueKey scoping was retrofitted onto one of three fetch sites.
findings.requiredRepair: Thread selectedLeagueKey through all three fetches and derive the rescale total from the league's registry roster settings instead of the constant 1200.

findings.title: /api/draft-capital re-attempts a live keeptradecut.com scrape on every cache miss because only SUCCESS is memoized — the measured cold cost is 2.5s and the observed anonymous first hit was 13.2s
findings.claimUnderTest: server.py's cache comment says the endpoint 'used to run ~4s of synchronous work — an openpyxl parse plus up to six blocking Sleeper calls' and that the 300s result cache plus threadpool offload solved it. _KTC_CACHE_TTL is documented as 6 hours.
findings.observed: _get_ktc_rookies() writes _ktc_cache only when the live fetch SUCCEEDS. When KTC is unreachable or returns an unparseable page it returns None, falls through to the CSV, and caches nothing — so the next cache miss re-issues the same urllib.request.urlopen(timeout=15). Instrumented in-process against the live stack, _parse_draft_data logs 'KTC parse returned only 0 rookies, likely blocked' on every single invocation. Cost breakdown measured: openpyxl cold 1.27s / warm 0.64s, five Sleeper calls 1.20s total, _fetch_draft_capital end-to-end 2.5s per miss with everything warm and reachable. The route probe recorded 13.2s for the first anonymous request, and the backend log carries exactly one 'Sleeper API failed for draft capital team-name mapping: Connection reset by peer' at that timestamp. With six independent timeout=15 calls in the path the worst case is ~90s of a threadpool worker, and the 300s result TTL means the whole sequence repeats every 5 minutes for as long as the page is in use.

reproduction.command: ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV=1 .venv/bin/python -c "import time,server; [print(round((lambda t0: (server._fetch_draft_capital('dynasty_main'), time.time()-t0)[1])(time.time()),3)) for _ in range(2)]"
reproduction.expected: a memoized negative result and no repeated outbound KTC request per cache miss
reproduction.actual: 2.5s per call, 'KTC parse returned only 0 rookies, likely blocked' logged on every call

numericProof.formula: worst case blocking = outboundCallsPerMiss * perCallTimeoutSec = 6 * 15 = 90s

findings.userImpact: Every 5 minutes one /draft or /league visitor pays the full cold cost — 2.5s when the network is healthy, 13.2s as actually measured here, and up to ~90s if any of the six upstreams hangs rather than resetting. On the public /league page that visitor is anonymous.

priorFinding.note: Not present in the area-0 prior finding set.

findings.whatWorks: The result cache, the per-league asyncio single-flight and the run_in_threadpool offload all work correctly — the authenticated cache hit measured 6ms and 4ms, and the event loop is never blocked. The openpyxl workbook cache keyed on (path, mtime_ns, size) also works.
findings.rootCause: _get_ktc_rookies memoizes the positive result only; there is no negative cache and no circuit breaker around a best-effort scrape that sits on the critical path of a user-facing endpoint.
findings.requiredRepair: Memoize the failure with a short TTL (or a backoff), and move the KTC fetch off the request path entirely — it is a background-refresh concern, not a per-request one. Lower the per-call timeouts; 15s x 6 is far past any useful page budget.
findings.dependencies: Pre-declared non-finding: the Sleeper connection reset itself is container egress. This finding is about the code's handling — unbounded retry with no negative caching — not the failure.

findings.title: VERIFIED WORKING: the Sleeper-derived fallback's unpriced-pick exclusion behaves exactly as CLAUDE.md describes — 40 priced 2026 picks sum to exactly $1200 and 40 unpriced 2027 picks carry dollarValue null / isUnpriced true with no dilution
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: '_pick_value_from_contract returns None on a miss; build_sleeper_derived excludes unpriced picks from the dollar normalization (so they cannot dilute) and emits them with dollarValue: null + isUnpriced: true ... coveredPickYears is now derived from what was actually priced ... pricedPickCount / unpricedPickCount / unpricedPickYears make the omission visible.' The prior audit claimed the opposite — that 52% of the board is fabricated.
findings.observed: Every element of the claim reproduces on the live non-default league. The response carries pricedPickCount 40, unpricedPickCount 40, coveredPickYears [2026], unpricedPickYears [2027]. The 40 priced picks sum to exactly 1200.0 with zero rounding drift; all 40 unpriced picks carry dollarValue null, adjustedDollarValue null and isUnpriced true while retaining real Sleeper ownership (currentOwner / originalOwner / isTraded). teamTotals sums to exactly 1200. No hardcoded 7000/4000/2000/1200-by-round value appears anywhere in the payload. The fabrication the prior audit reported is gone.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/draft-capital?leagueKey=dynasty_new' | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); ps=d['picks']; print(len(ps), sum(1 for p in ps if p.get('isUnpriced')), round(sum(p['dollarValue'] for p in ps if p['dollarValue'] is not None),4), sum(t['auctionDollars'] for t in d['teamTotals']), d['coveredPickYears'], d['unpricedPickYears'])"

numericProof.formula: sum(dollarValue for priced picks) == totalBudget AND all unpriced picks have dollarValue is None

findings.userImpact: None — this is the correct behavior. Half the emitted board is honestly labelled unpriced rather than silently valued.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding's substance ('fabricates 52% of the board on live data') does NOT reproduce — the hardcoded round table is gone from the tree and the exclusion arithmetic is exact. The prior finding's secondary claim, that the 503 guard does not fire on a league mismatch, is TRUE but is a deliberate documented decision (Defect D-2 resolution in CLAUDE.md), not a defect.

findings.whatWorks: Everything named in the claim, verified numerically.
findings.requiredRepair: None. Note for the merge step: no frontend surface reads unpricedPickCount / unpricedPickYears / isUnpriced (only /trade reads coveredPickYears), so the backend's honesty is invisible to a /draft user — tracked separately, not blocking.

findings.title: /api/draft-capital serves the hand-maintained per-pick dollar curve to anonymous callers on the stated grounds that it is 'already viewable on Sleeper', which is false for that column
findings.claimUnderTest: The allowlist comment reads: 'Payload is public Sleeper data (team names, pick dollar values, owners) already viewable on Sleeper.'
findings.observed: The redaction itself works — the anonymous response is 17,400 bytes against 25,472 authenticated, rookieName / rookiePos / rookieKtcValue / rookieKtcDollar / rookieIdpDollar are all stripped, and rookieBoardRedacted:true is stamped. But of the three field groups the comment calls 'already viewable on Sleeper', only two are: team names and pick ownership. dollarValue / adjustedDollarValue / originalDollarValue come from column L of CSVs/Draft Data.xlsx, a hand-maintained Hill-curve valuation the operator wrote — Sleeper publishes no such figure. teamTotals.auctionDollars is derived from the same column, so an anonymous caller reads every team's draft-capital valuation on the operator's own curve.

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/draft-capital | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['rookieBoardRedacted'], d['picks'][0], d['teamTotals'][:2])"
reproduction.expected: either no proprietary valuation in the anonymous payload, or an allowlist comment that states accurately what is exposed
reproduction.actual: anonymous payload carries dollarValue 134.5 for pick 1.01 and auctionDollars 685 for the top team

numericProof.formula: anonymous payload retains dollarValue for all 72 picks, sourced from CSVs/Draft Data.xlsx L2:L73 which sums to 1200.0

findings.userImpact: None to the user; this is an operator disclosure decision. It is reported because the justification recorded next to the allowlist entry is factually wrong for one of the three things it authorizes, so the decision was made on a false premise.

priorFinding.note: Not in the area-0 prior set.

findings.whatWorks: _redact_draft_capital_for_public returns a copy and never mutates the shared cache, exactly as its docstring promises — verified by fetching anonymously then authenticated within the same 300s TTL window and confirming the authenticated response still carried all five private fields.
findings.rootCause: The allowlist comment was written for the ownership data and not revised when the pick-value column was added to the payload.
findings.requiredRepair: Operator decision. Either correct the comment to say the pick dollar curve is deliberately public, or add dollarValue/adjustedDollarValue/originalDollarValue/teamTotals to the redaction set and have the public /league tab render ownership only.
findings.dependencies: tests/api/test_draft_capital_public_redaction.py pins the current field set and would need updating if the redaction widens.

findings.title: hydrateWorkspace discards pos, assetClass, ktcDollar and idpTradeCalcDollar from every stored player on load, so the vendor panels are blank until a network refetch succeeds
findings.claimUnderTest: hydrateWorkspace is the localStorage rehydration path for DRAFT_STORAGE_KEY; the vendor panels (nominationCandidates, bestValueOnBoard) select on p.ktcDollar / p.idpTradeCalcDollar / p.assetClass.
findings.observed: Round-tripping a player through hydrateWorkspace reduces {id, rank, name, preDraft, pos, assetClass, ktcDollar, idpTradeCalcDollar} to {id, rank, name, preDraft}. Four of the eight fields — including both vendor dollars and the assetClass that the IDP/offense vendor routing was specifically written to depend on — are dropped. Both vendor panels therefore return zero rows on a cold load until the /api/draft-capital auto-sync lands, and stay empty for the whole session if that fetch fails (it is wrapped in a bare `if (!capitalRes.ok) return;`).

reproduction.command: node docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W10/probe-prior-verify.mjs   # 'before hydrate' vs 'after hydrate' lines
reproduction.expected: {"id":"test-guy","rank":1,"name":"Test Guy","preDraft":50,"pos":"LB","assetClass":"idp","ktcDollar":60,"idpTradeCalcDollar":55}
reproduction.actual: {"id":"test-guy","rank":1,"name":"Test Guy","preDraft":50}

numericProof.formula: fields retained / fields stored

findings.userImpact: On a page load where the draft-capital fetch is slow or fails — precisely a live-draft-night failure mode — the Nomination targets and Best value panels render empty with no explanation, and the IDP/offense vendor split silently falls back to the position string that assetClass exists to work around.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced by direct round-trip.

findings.whatWorks: Picks, tags, target board, par sheet and nominations all survive hydration correctly; the auto-sync does restore the missing fields on a successful fetch.
findings.rootCause: hydrateWorkspace rebuilds each player from an explicit whitelist that was not extended when pos/assetClass/vendor dollars were added to the player shape.
findings.requiredRepair: Extend the player whitelist in hydrateWorkspace to carry pos, assetClass, ktcDollar and idpTradeCalcDollar.

findings.title: Rookie pick values are point estimates everywhere on the live path — no mean/median/P10/P90/starter%/bust% distribution is served by any reachable route
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md describes a /draft 'Fundamental pick values (BDVM)' panel showing 'balanced-strategy pick EV / hit% / median / ceiling beside the market anchor, from buildBdvmPickRows', and config/bdvm/pick_outcomes_v1.json exists to supply pick outcome distributions.
findings.observed: Every pick field the live board emits is a scalar: dollarValue, adjustedDollarValue, originalDollarValue, rookieKtcValue, rookieKtcDollar, rookieIdpDollar. There is no distributional field anywhere in the /api/draft-capital payload, and none in the frontend workspace shape. The only distribution machinery in the repo is BDVM's, and GET /api/bdvm/values returns status 'no_projection_snapshot' because data/bdvm/ does not exist in this container — so the /draft BDVM pick panel and the 'Fund gap' column self-suppress and the user sees point estimates only. Separately, the only blanket multiplier over picks is config/weights/pick_year_discount.json's offsetDiscounts {0:1.00, 1:0.82, 2:0.66, 3:0.53}, which is applied per YEAR to every pick of that year regardless of round or slot — that lives on the /api/data board, not on the draft board, which applies no multiplier at all.

findings.title: DEFAULT_ROOKIES sums to $1211 against a comment claiming $1200, pulling the inflation singularity 11 dollars inside the draft on a pre-sync board
findings.claimUnderTest: The comment above DEFAULT_ROOKIES: 'Verbatim from the Inflation tab (columns A-C). Sums to $1200 to keep the league-wide accounting consistent with the sheet.'
findings.observed: The 72 preDraft values sum to 1211, not 1200. DEFAULT_TEAMS' budgets do sum to exactly 1200. Because inflation = remainingLeague / (totalBudget - soldPreDraft), the denominator crosses zero after 61 of 72 picks instead of at the last pick, and on a simulated draft paying 0.9x preDraft the multiplier reaches 111x at pick 60 while inflationDegraded is still false. On the live board this is moot — the auto-synced pool from /api/draft-capital sums to exactly 1200.0 (verified on all 72 rookieKtcValue entries) — so the impact is confined to a pristine or offline workspace.

reproduction.actual: DEFAULT_ROOKIES sum = 1211

numericProof.formula: sum(DEFAULT_ROOKIES[i].preDraft)

findings.userImpact: A user who opens /draft with the network down, or before the first sync lands, gets a board whose late-draft prices blow up 11 picks early. With the network up the live pool overwrites it.

priorFinding.note: The arithmetic is confirmed exactly. The prior's causal claim — that this mismatch 'is what breaks late-draft inflation' — is REFUTED: W10-F006 reproduces the same divergence on the live $1200 pool, so the pole is in the formula and the $11 only moves it earlier.

findings.title: Position FAAB calibration blends RAW dollar bids from three seasons with different budgets ($1000 / $200 / $100), inflating the RB anchor 5.0x and driving every bid too high
findings.claimUnderTest: faab_analytics.py docstring: 'calibrates the per-player FAAB recommendation against the league's actual historical winning bids for similar position+tier so the recommendation reflects how THIS league bids'. _league_budget() reads 'the current season's waiver_budget setting'.
findings.observed: _walk_waivers() flattens EVERY season's transactions into one bid list with no budget normalization, while _league_budget() returns only the CURRENT season's budget. The live snapshot covers 2026 (waiver_budget=100), 2025 (200) and 2024 (1000). positionBids['RB'].avg is therefore $43.00 -- a mean over bids denominated in three different currencies, with a max of $340 which is physically impossible in a $100 league. recommend_faab blends that number 50/50 into every RB bid on a $100 budget.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.public_league import snapshot_store;s=snapshot_store.load_snapshot();[print(x.season,(getattr(x,'league',{}) or {}).get('settings',{}).get('waiver_budget')) for x in s.seasons]" && curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-W11.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/faabAnalytics?leagueKey=dynasty_main' | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['positionBids'])"
reproduction.expected: Position averages expressed as a share of the season each bid was placed in, i.e. RB ~ $8.58 on a $100 budget
reproduction.actual: 2026 budget=100, 2025 budget=200, 2024 budget=1000; positionBids RB {'avg': 43.0, 'min': 1, 'max': 340, 'count': 53}; league max bid $340 on a $100 budget

numericProof.formula: normalized_bid = raw_bid / season_budget * 100 ; RB_anchor = mean(normalized_bids) ; recommended = 0.5*RB_anchor + 0.5*baseline

findings.userImpact: Every RB waiver bid on /waivers is anchored to a number 5x larger than the league's own budget-normalized history. A user is told to bid $22-$32 of a $100 budget on replacement-level running backs. This is the single largest contributor to the reported 'FAAB recommendations are too aggressive'.

blastRadius.note: 930 = contract rows in the 8 positions with >=3 historical bids (WR 217, DL 145, RB 140, DB 139, LB 114, TE 85, QB 71, K 19); PICK/None/T excluded. The finding's 283 appears to be the FA pool only. Also contaminated beyond positionBids: leagueAvgWinningBid, leagueMedianWinningBid, teamAggression, tierBids.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior area-4 set. PRIOR-A04-F08 noticed tierBids was unused but not that positionBids itself mixes budget regimes. Note the irony: src/adapters/ktc_crowd_faab.py::_parse_bid_pct DOES normalize by waiver_budget 'so multi-budget leagues normalize correctly' -- the league's own history is the one place it is skipped.

findings.whatWorks: The multi-add split at full precision (faab_analytics.py:240-246) and the tier breakpoints scaling with league_budget are both correct.
findings.rootCause: _league_budget() is scalar and current-season-only; _walk_waivers() is multi-season. The two are combined without a per-season divisor.
findings.requiredRepair: Carry the season's waiver_budget alongside each bid in _walk_waivers, express every bid as a share of its own season's budget, and re-multiply by the CURRENT budget before it reaches positionBids / leagueAvgWinningBid / leagueMedianWinningBid / teamAggression.
findings.dependencies: Fixing this alone drops RB recommendations from ~$32 to ~$15 and unpriced-RB recommendations from $22 to $4; W11-F002 must be fixed too or the unpriced case survives at a lower number.

verification.reasoning: Reproduced exactly, twice over. src/api/faab_analytics.py:143-172 (_walk_waivers) flattens all three seasons with no divisor; :102-121 (_league_budget) reads only snapshot.current_season. The live snapshot (data/public_league/snapshot.json, real league 1312006700437352448 'Risk It To Get The Brisket', seasons 2026/2025/2024 at budgets 100/200/1000) therefore yields positionBids RB avg 43.0 with max 340 on a $100 budget. My independent per-season normalization returns 8.58 — the finding's expected value to the cent (tolerance 0.05). The inferential step holds: src/trade/faab_recommender.py:69 _LEAGUE_CALIBRATION_BLEND = 0.5 and :172-192 blends positionBids[pos].avg 50/50 whenever count >= 3 (:93), which is true for all 8 positions. The path is live end to end: server.py:5179 builds the summary, :5295 passes it as league_faab_summary, frontend/components/waivers/ManualAddDrop.jsx:444 renders FaabRecommendation, which POSTs /api/waiver/faab-recommend (FaabRecommendation.jsx:418) from /waivers (page.jsx:617). Not a harness artifact: the snapshot is the operator's real Sleeper league history, not seeded test data, and the endpoint answers 200 today. Not fixed at HEAD (last touch of faab_analytics.py is dcf5ebef, which fixed the multi-add rounding and left the budget mixing). P0 criteria all met: reachable page (/waivers), wrong number a user acts on ($32 standard vs $15 under the intended calibration — a 2.1x overbid of a $100 budget), and no warning — 'warnings' is empty and the calibration factor is reported as PRESENT ('+$12'), i.e. the defect is presented to the user as evidence. Two small corrections, both in the finding's favour rather than against it: (a) the defect is not RB-only — every position's anchor is inflated (WR 20.84 vs 4.40, QB 37.74 vs 10.11), so the title understates scope; (b) blastRadius playersAffected 283 is low — every contract row in a position with >=3 historical bids is calibratable, which is 930 of the 1,092 rows (only PICK/None/T are exempt). 283 is defensible only if read as the current FA pool. leagueAvgWinningBid ($19.55) and leagueMedianWinningBid ($5.00, vs $2.00 normalized) are contaminated by the same mixing and feed _env_scale_factor, so the RB-specific framing understates the surface too.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: Nothing further — reproduced from three independent angles (snapshot budgets, endpoint payload, in-process recommend_faab ablation). If anyone wants to contest it, the only surviving question is whether a production snapshot ever carries a single budget across all seasons; the live one does not.

findings.title: Players the board declines to price (rankDerivedValue = 0) are recommended $22-$25 bids and described as a 'strong free-agent target'; 125 of 283 free agents are affected
findings.claimUnderTest: _compute_faab_bid: 'if candidate_value <= 0 or budget <= 0: return (0, 0, 0)'. faab_recommender module docstring: 'Missing data is never imputed into a normal-looking value'.
findings.observed: The zero guard fires correctly and the baseline factor row honestly reads 'Player value baseline: start at $0'. Step 4 then blends that $0 against the position's historical average -- 0.5*avg + 0.5*0 -- and resurrects a bid out of nothing. The explanation string is chosen only on the magnitude of the final number, so a player worth 0 gets 'strong free-agent target'. Rival contention can then raise it further: Zach Wilson (value 0) received '+$6 to clear top rival'.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-W11.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/waiver/faab-recommend -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"addPlayerName":"AJ Dillon","leagueKey":"dynasty_main","teamOwnerId":"owner-8b8a59adf44e"}'

reproduction.actual: {"conservative":15,"standard":22,"aggressive":31,"resolvedAddValue":0.0,"explanation":"Bid $22 - strong free-agent target.  Cap at $31 if you want the priority claim."}
