findings.userImpact: On /waivers a manager is told to spend 22% of the season budget on a player this product's own board refuses to value, with no warning and with copy calling it a strong target. The recommendation is a pure function of position, not of the player.

priorFinding.note: 125 of the 283 unrostered contract rows carry rankDerivedValue = 0 and 125 of those receive a non-zero bid; the observed bid set is {2,4,7,10,22,25} keyed entirely off position.

findings.whatWorks: The 15 zero-value rows whose contract row also carries no position (e.g. Foster Moreau) DO correctly return $0 -- the calibration is skipped when position is None.
findings.rootCause: _position_calibration is an unconditional blend on the running bid; nothing re-checks that the baseline was a real number rather than the zero-guard's sentinel.
findings.requiredRepair: Short-circuit recommend_faab when add_player_value <= 0 and return an explicit unpriced response (mirroring the BDVM 'unpriced with a reason' posture), or gate every post-baseline multiplier/blend on reasonable_base > 0.
findings.dependencies: Independent of W11-F001, but F001 sets the magnitude.

verification.reasoning: The API-level defect is real and reproduces verbatim: src/trade/waiver.py:120-121 returns (0,0,0) for a non-positive value, the honest baseline factor row says 'start at $0', and then src/trade/faab_recommender.py:457 blends that sentinel 50/50 with the position's historical average (_position_calibration, faab_recommender.py:172-192) with no re-check that the baseline was a real number; the explanation branch at faab_recommender.py:679-682 keys only on the final magnitude, so a null-valued player gets 'strong free-agent target'. All of that is confirmed. What does NOT follow is the userImpact and therefore the P0 grade. P0 requires a user acting on a wrong number 'on a page they can reach'. The ONLY caller of /api/waiver/faab-recommend is frontend/components/waivers/FaabRecommendation.jsx:418, and that panel renders only once an ADD player is selected from the pool built by frontend/lib/waiver-logic.js::buildTopWaiverPool, which drops every zero-value row at line 767 ('if (rowValue(row) <= 0) continue;') — and rowValue (waiver-logic.js:196-205) returns 0 for both rankDerivedValue null and values.full null. I confirmed this in a real browser under the protocol's request-interception topology: the ADD box populates normally (8 default candidates) but 'Dillon', 'Zach Wilson' and 'Moreau' all return 'No matches.', and zero faab-recommend calls fired. The /waivers 'FAAB hint' column uses the client port computeFaabHint (waiver-logic.js:884-897), which honestly returns $0 for these rows. So no user is told to bid $22 on AJ Dillon today; the wrong number exists only for a caller that reaches the endpoint directly with a name the UI will not offer. Blast-radius arithmetic checks out at the API layer (283 unrostered non-pick rows, 140 unpriced, 126 of them carrying a position and therefore eligible for the resurrection blend — the finding's 125/283 is within one row), but pagesAffected is 0, not 1. Latent defect, not a live one: any relaxation of the pool filter, or any non-UI consumer, exposes it immediately, which is why it should still be fixed.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: A UI path that puts an unpriced player into the ADD selector. Show one — e.g. a deep link, a URL param, or a pool-filter change that admits rankDerivedValue==null rows — and this returns to P0/P1 immediately. Conversely, adding a test that pins buildTopWaiverPool's zero-value exclusion together with an explicit 'unpriced' short-circuit in recommend_faab would close both halves.

findings.title: The bid saturates at the top of the FREE-AGENT pool, so 367 board rows (value >= 1908) price identically and no player anywhere justifies more than 40% of the budget -- there is no all-in threshold
findings.claimUnderTest: User's stated calibration intent: a ~9999 player justifies the whole budget, and the all-in threshold should sit far below the top of the dynasty market (near J.K. Dobbins / Jaylen Warren, not Josh Jacobs). frontend/lib/waiver-logic.js:858-860 documents 'a 9999-value player gets 30% of the budget'.
findings.observed: share = candidate_value / max(candidate_value, top_value_in_pool), so every player at or above the best available free agent has share = 1.0 and an identical baseline. On the live board the top free agent is Marlin Klein (1908, board rank 325), so Josh Allen (9988), Josh Jacobs (3859), Jaylen Warren (2937), J.K. Dobbins (2660) and Marlin Klein all take exactly the same $30/$21/$11 baseline. Sweeping the endpoint over all 283 free agents returns a maximum standard bid of $31; sweeping the top 200 of the whole board returns a maximum of $40. Nothing on the board triggers an all-in bid, and the number does not scale with the 1..9999 axis at all above rank 325.

findings.userImpact: The bid desk cannot express 'this is a league-winner, empty the budget' or 'this is roster filler, bid $1'. It compresses the entire dynasty market into a $12-$40 band, so the user cannot rank waiver targets by the recommendation and over-pays at the bottom while under-paying at the top.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed and extended. The prior finding measured _compute_faab_bid(1905,100,1905) = (30,21,10) in isolation; this reproduces the same saturation end-to-end through the live endpoint, counts the 367 affected board rows, and measures the actual ceiling ($40 over the top 200) against the user's stated intent. The lowball figure is 11 not 10 -- the rounding rule changed to explicit half-up since that measurement.

findings.whatWorks: The denominator is now correctly restricted to non-pick free agents (server.py:5130), which is what makes 1908 the anchor.
findings.rootCause: The formula answers 'what fraction of the best available free agent is this player' and prints a dollar sign on it. Its output range is structurally [5%, 30%] of budget regardless of the absolute quality of the pool.
findings.requiredRepair: Replace the pool-relative share with an absolute mapping from the 1..9999 board scale to a share of budget, with an explicitly calibrated all-in knee. The user's stated intent puts the knee near value ~2700-2950 (Dobbins/Warren), i.e. board rank ~180-210, not at Josh Jacobs (3859, rank 109).
findings.dependencies: Interacts with W11-F001 (the position blend currently dominates the baseline) and W11-F005 (the client hint uses the same formula with a different denominator).

findings.title: The recommendation is not monotonic in player value: 8,362 of 39,903 free-agent pairs invert, worst case a $21 swing in favour of the lower-valued player
findings.claimUnderTest: Implied by the product: a better player should not be assigned a lower recommended bid than a worse one.
findings.observed: Because the position blend (weight 0.5) and the trending kicker (up to x1.20) both sit downstream of the only value-sensitive term, position and Sleeper add-count routinely dominate value. Measured over all 283 free agents at a fixed budget/roster: 8,362 inverted pairs (21.0% of all pairs).

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;o=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W11/fa-pool-sweep.json'));v=sum(1 for i in range(len(o)) for j in range(i+1,len(o)) if o[i]['value']>o[j]['value'] and o[i]['standard']<o[j]['standard']);print(v,'of',len(o)*(len(o)-1)//2)"
reproduction.expected: 0 inversions
reproduction.actual: 8362 of 39903 pairs inverted. Worst: Zion Young (DL, value 1447) -> $10 vs Seth McGowan (RB, value 1383) -> $31. On the full board: Malik Willis (3684) -> $40 vs Josh Allen (9988) -> $38.

numericProof.formula: standard = 0.5*positionBids[pos].avg + 0.5*(baseline * value_gain * trending)

findings.userImpact: A manager comparing two waiver targets side by side is told to bid three times more on the worse one. The recommendation cannot be used to prioritise claims, which is its primary job.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding argued the formula is not a bid; this quantifies the consequence with a full pairwise sweep, which the prior set did not measure.

findings.whatWorks: Within a single position the ordering IS monotonic -- the inversions are entirely cross-position (plus the trending kicker).
findings.rootCause: A 0.5-weight additive blend on a position constant is applied after the value term, so it can exceed the value term's entire dynamic range.
findings.requiredRepair: Make the league calibration a MULTIPLIER on the value bid rather than a 50/50 blend with a position constant, so ordering within the value axis is preserved.
findings.dependencies: W11-F001 (the position constants are themselves inflated) and W11-F010 (they are means of a skewed distribution).

findings.title: The /waivers 'FAAB hint' column changes the recommended dollar bid for the same player when the user changes the position filter -- Charlie Kolar $19 under 'All positions', $21 under 'TE'
findings.claimUnderTest: Column header tooltip: 'Quick baseline share of a $100 budget - use the bid desk for a league-aware recommendation.'
findings.observed: topAddValue is the maximum add value among the CURRENTLY DISPLAYED bestMoves rows, and it is the denominator of computeFaabHint's share. Changing the position dropdown changes the visible set, which changes the denominator, which changes the printed dollar figure for players whose own value did not change. By construction the top row of the column always reads $21.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W11/repro_waivers_page.py   # Playwright with /api/* request interception per AUDIT_PROTOCOL; selects team 'Jason', reads the Best add/drop moves table under filters ALL / QB / RB / TE
reproduction.expected: identical hint for the same player under every filter
reproduction.actual: Charlie Kolar: $19 (All positions) -> $21 (TE). Mitchell Evans: $18 -> $20. Under every filter the #1 row prints $21 (Jonas Sanker, Joe Milton, George Holani, Charlie Kolar).

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A04-F02 is about the hint disagreeing with the bid desk (see W11-F007). This is the hint disagreeing with ITSELF across a display filter, which the prior set did not test. Measured in a real browser through request interception.

findings.whatWorks: computeFaabHint itself is a faithful port of the server formula (see W11-F020).
findings.rootCause: The denominator is computed from the filtered render list (page.jsx topAddValue memo) instead of from the whole addable pool.
findings.requiredRepair: Compute topAddValue once from the unfiltered addable pool (or, better, drop the pool-relative share entirely per W11-F003) and pass the league's real budget rather than a literal 100.
findings.dependencies: Shares the root formula with W11-F003.

findings.title: The value-gain modifier is inverted with respect to the drop side: adding a player for free is recommended at $32 while adding the same player and dropping a worthless one is recommended at $40
findings.claimUnderTest: _value_gain_modifier docstring: 'Bigger upgrade => higher modifier. Drop value of 0 (FA-only add, no drop required) returns 1.0 (no boost, no penalty).'
findings.observed: The modifier is 1 + (add-drop)/drop * 0.5 clamped to [0.5, 1.8], and drop_value appears in the DENOMINATOR. A no-drop add is hard-coded to 1.0, but dropping a near-worthless player produces a ratio near infinity and clamps to 1.8. So the transaction that costs the manager an extra asset is priced 80% HIGHER than the same transaction that costs nothing.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W11/faab_axis_probe.py  # read out['dropSideSweep']
reproduction.expected: bid(no drop) >= bid(same add, plus a drop)
reproduction.actual: drop_value 0 -> $32; drop_value 500 -> $40; drop_value 2000 -> $37; drop_value 3858 -> $32; drop_value 3859 -> $10; drop_value 5000 -> $0

findings.userImpact: Selecting a drop player -- something the UI encourages, since the calculator has a DROP side -- raises the recommended bid by up to 25% for the identical add. The manager pays more for a worse net transaction.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior area-4 set.

findings.whatWorks: The strictly-negative branch is right: add < drop returns $0 with 'Your drop is worth more than your add - don't bid.' Verified live at drop_value 5000 -> $0.
findings.rootCause: Using drop_value as the denominator makes the modifier a function of how BAD the drop is rather than of how much the roster improves.
findings.requiredRepair: Scale the modifier by net gain relative to the ADD's value (or to a replacement-level constant), not relative to the drop's value, and make the no-drop case the maximum rather than the neutral case.

findings.title: FAAB v2's budget-environment scaling stage cannot fire for any position that has bid history -- it is dead code on live data

findings.observed: The double-count guard suppresses env scaling whenever positionBids[pos].count >= 3. On the live league every position with any history has count >= 10 (QB 39, RB 53, WR 64, TE 26, DL 30, LB 39, DB 41, K 10), so _env_scale_factor returns None for all of them. It returns a non-None value only for positions with NO bid history (P, OL) or for a row with no position at all -- i.e. never for a real waiver add.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior area-4 set.

findings.whatWorks: The double-count guard itself is correct reasoning; it is the min-count threshold (3) that is set so low it swallows the whole feature.
findings.rootCause: The precedence gate reuses _POSITION_CALIBRATION_MIN_COUNT = 3, which any active league clears for every position.
findings.requiredRepair: Either delete the stage and the docstring claim, or change the precedence rule so env scaling applies to the residual after the position blend rather than being mutually exclusive with it.

findings.title: The league calibration anchors on the MEAN of a heavily right-skewed winning-bid distribution (league mean $19.55 vs median $5.00), systematically biasing every recommendation upward
findings.claimUnderTest: _position_calibration: 'Blend bid_estimate 50/50 with the league's historical average winning bid for position ... keeps the formula honest in leagues where users overpay'.
findings.observed: _stats_block emits only avg/min/max/count -- no median -- and the recommender blends against avg. The live distribution is extremely skewed: league mean $19.55 vs median $5.00 (3.9x), RB mean $43.00 vs median $18.00, QB mean $37.74 vs median $6.00. The recommender therefore calibrates to the tail, not to the typical claim, and it does this on top of the cross-budget contamination in W11-F001. summarize_league_faab already computes leagueMedianWinningBid at league level -- the per-position block simply never got one.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-W11.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/faabAnalytics?leagueKey=dynasty_main' | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin)['data'];print('leagueMean',d['leagueAvgWinningBid'],'leagueMedian',d['leagueMedianWinningBid']);print(d['positionBids'])"
reproduction.expected: a robust central estimate for the position
reproduction.actual: leagueAvgWinningBid 19.55, leagueMedianWinningBid 5.0; positionBids carries only 'avg' -- QB avg 37.74 (median 6.00), RB avg 43.00 (median 18.00)

numericProof.formula: anchor = mean(position_bids) vs anchor = median(position_bids)

findings.userImpact: Every bid is pulled halfway toward the mean of a distribution whose typical value is a quarter of that mean. Combined with W11-F001 this is why an unpriced QB is recommended at $25.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A04-F08 observed that tierBids is unused while the docstring claims position+tier calibration. This is the adjacent defect the prior set did not name: even within positionBids the statistic chosen is the wrong one.

findings.whatWorks: leagueMedianWinningBid is computed correctly and IS used by the contention aggression factor.
findings.rootCause: _stats_block was written for display (avg/min/max/count) and then reused as a calibration input.
findings.requiredRepair: Add a 'median' (and ideally a trimmed mean) to _stats_block and calibrate against it.
findings.dependencies: W11-F001 must be fixed first or the median is still denominated in three currencies.

findings.claimUnderTest: faab_recommender docstring: 'plus a pacing warning whenever the standard bid exceeds 40% of the remaining budget ... so the user consciously accepts the season-long tradeoff'.
findings.observed: aggressive = round(standard * 1.40) is rendered as a peer pill the user can act on, but the _PACING_WARN_SHARE check runs only against standard. Any standard between 29% and 40% produces an aggressive figure of 40-56% with an empty warnings array.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-W11.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/waiver/faab-recommend -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"addPlayerName":"Josh Allen","leagueKey":"dynasty_main","teamOwnerId":"owner-8b8a59adf44e"}'

findings.title: No FAAB input is sensitive to time of season, roster need, contender-vs-rebuilder posture, or whether the add is a temporary injury fill-in -- the bid is priced entirely on long-run DYNASTY value
findings.claimUnderTest: The bid desk is presented as a league-aware FAAB recommendation.
findings.observed: Grepping the whole FAAB path (waiver.py, faab_recommender.py, faab_contention.py, ktc_crowd_faab.py) for week / season / playoff / contender / rebuild / injur returns zero functional references -- only docstring prose. The single value input is rankDerivedValue, the dynasty market board. Positional need exists, but ONLY for modelling RIVAL bids (faab_contention.need_level_for); the requesting user's own roster need is never consulted. Consequence on the live board: the top of the free-agent pool is Marlin Klein, Tanner Koziol, Jack Endries and Sam Roush -- four deep-bench rookie TEs with dynasty upside -- while startable veteran RB depth (AJ Dillon, Alexander Mattison) prices at 0. The desk therefore steers the whole budget at players who will never enter a lineup.

reproduction.command: grep -nciE 'week|playoff|contend|rebuild|injur' src/trade/waiver.py src/trade/faab_recommender.py src/trade/faab_contention.py ; .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W11/faab_axis_probe.py
reproduction.expected: at least one in-season / roster-context input
reproduction.actual: 0 functional references in all three modules. Axis probe: the ONLY inputs the output moves on are player value (saturating), position (via the historical blend), Sleeper trending count, drop-side value, rival clearing price and the team's remaining balance.

numericProof.formula: sensitivity = |bid(axis=hi) - bid(axis=lo)|

findings.userImpact: A week-3 injury replacement a manager needs for four weeks and a durable dynasty asset are priced the same, and a rebuilding team is told to spend like a contender. A FAAB claim is a rest-of-season decision priced on a rest-of-career number.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding asserted this from code reading. I confirm it by axis-sweeping the live function and additionally show WHICH axes do move the number, and that league-wide remaining FAAB is unread (only per-rival balances, and only as a cap).

findings.whatWorks: Rival-side positional need IS modelled (NEED_FACTORS 1.0/0.55/0.25) and does reach the clearing price.
findings.rootCause: There is no rest-of-season value feed for the waiver pool. /api/ros/player-values covers only the top 500 board players; none of the 283 free agents (checked: AJ Dillon, Alexander Mattison, Marlin Klein, Jonas Sanker) appear in it.
findings.requiredRepair: Two separable pieces: (a) thread current week + a contender/rebuilder posture into a budget-pacing multiplier, which needs no new data; (b) extend the ROS aggregation past the top 500 so free agents carry a rest-of-season value the bid can be priced on.

So the threshold and the raw gap are both disclosed on the row the user clicked. What is defective is that two independently-authored noise floors produce two verbs for one number with no shared constant — a real Duplicate-or-conflicting-implementation defect and a genuine UX contradiction, but P1, not P0.

Two corrections to the surface list. /league is wrong: AppShell.jsx routes the /league subtree to PublicAppShell, which deliberately does NOT call useDynastyData, and LeagueClient.jsx:24 documents that it imports nothing from lib/league-analysis — so /league carries neither signal. The honest surface is: marketAction (10) exists on /rankings ONLY; getPlayerEdge (3) reaches PlayerPopup (app-wide via AppShell), /trade (trade-sections.jsx:559,666), /trades and /rosters. Also numericProof.rowsWithAnyDirectionalVerb=371 measured 356 for me on GET /api/data — the finding presumably counted on the tep=1.15 delta board (see W07-F001); the load-bearing 83 is identical on both boards, since marketGapMagnitude is byte-identical in the delta (Brock Bowers 5.363636... in both).

CLAUDE.md documents (ADR-015) that base-vs-TE++ is a measured 1.209-2.05 multiplier and applies a conversion to VALUES; no equivalent correction is applied to the RANKS this label is computed from, and no caveat appears anywhere on /rankings or /edge.

(2) I checked the inferential step independently rather than trusting the finding's spot numbers, and computed the FULL per-source median rank delta matrix. Every one of the 15 non-retail sources ranks TEs 31 to 62 ordinal places worse relative to KTC than it ranks QB/RB/WR — with zero exceptions, across sources with wildly different pool depths and methodologies. A per-player opinion difference cannot be unanimous across 15 independent boards in one position; a basis offset is the only explanation that fits. The finding's cited spot values (yahooBoone 9, dynastyNerdsSfTep 14, pfkDynasty 15, fantasyProsFitzmaurice 17, dlfSf 33, flockFantasySf 38, idpTradeCalc 115; WR fantasyNavigatorSf -30, dlfSf -22, dynastyNerdsSfTep -19, fantasyCalc -13, idpTradeCalc 78) all reproduce to the unit. The retail side is is_retail on ktcSfTep only (data_contract.py:1030), an SF-TE++ board. (4) Not a harness artifact — no entry on the non-findings list touches this, and I confirmed the Edge column renders by default in a real browser through request interception. It will not — the offset is uniform across all 15 sources.

findings.title: There is no central Buy/Sell Tracker: 16 label emitters, 14 reachable, 5 competing threshold sets on one quantity, and the two modules built to unify them are one flag-off and one caller-less
findings.claimUnderTest: The product requirement is a central Buy/Sell Tracker that is the broad primary recommendation system and is NOT the same feature as Consensus Edge. src/consensus_edge/__init__.py already states the problem in the repo's own words: 'The platform accumulated six overlapping answers to "is this player a buy?" ... "Buy" means a different thing on each screen. This package is the single answer.'
findings.observed: No module, route, page, table or state key is a central tracker. I enumerated 16 independent directional emitters (docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W12/label-families.json); 14 are reachable today. FIVE of them apply different cutoffs to the SAME retail-vs-consensus quantity: >0 (backend stamp), >=3 (getPlayerEdge, powers PlayerPopup and the /league Edge Map), >=10 (marketAction, powers the /rankings Edge column), sourceRankSpread>=20 AND rank<=250 (/edge panels and the /rankings rail), and >=10 on a different source set (idpMarketAction, /edge IDP tab). None of the 14 shares state, imports another, or reads another's output. The two candidates for an arbiter both fail: src/consensus_edge/* returns 503 on every route because the flag defaults off, and src/news/unified_signal_engine.py — 352 lines whose docstring calls it 'Unified signal engine — single entry point for every BUY/SELL/HOLD decision emitted to users' — is imported by nothing outside tests and one audit script.

Prior did not record that consensus_edge was designed as the arbiter or that unified_signal_engine has no caller.

findings.whatWorks: src/consensus_edge is the correct shape for the missing arbiter: it consumes other engines as components, renormalises weights over PRESENT components, refuses to score without a core component, forces Conflicted when strong evidence opposes, and separates direction from confidence. It is switched off for an honest reason (its top-20 buy list did not beat a random draw) rather than hidden.
findings.rootCause: Every new surface added its own label rather than consuming an existing one, and no module was ever made authoritative. The two attempts to consolidate were both left unreachable.
findings.requiredRepair: Pick one emitter as the tracker. The cheapest honest version: promote the retail-vs-consensus family to a single backend-stamped verb (one threshold, computed once in _compute_market_gap) that every surface renders verbatim, and demote the other emitters to explicitly-labelled secondary lenses. Then decide whether consensus_edge or unified_signal_engine is the long-term arbiter and delete the other.
findings.dependencies: W12-F001, W12-F002, W12-F004, W12-F008 are all instances of this.

verification.reasoning:
The core is real and I strengthened it with evidence the finding did not have. Three of its stated numbers are wrong, and its status label is wrong by the protocol's own vocabulary. Rescoped, not upheld as written.

WHAT SURVIVES (verified independently):
- src/news/unified_signal_engine.py has ZERO production importers. Every hit is a comment or docstring. Confirmed exactly as stated.
- /api/consensus-edge/top -> 503 feature_disabled; /board and /summary are 404 (only one route exists). The arbiter is unreachable. Per AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md the 503 itself is a non-finding but 'reachability is the claim to test' — that is what this claims, so it is admissible.
- Multiple unreconciled emitters, and the disagreement is LIVE and user-visible. I measured it rather than asserting it: on the running contract, 90 players — including Brock Bowers (rank 2) and Bijan Robinson (rank 3) — get a BUY/SELL verb in PlayerPopup (getPlayerEdge, >=3, trade-logic.js:949, rendered at PlayerPopup.jsx:666 which appears on every page, plus trade-sections.jsx:559/666 and the /league Edge Map via league-analysis.js:933) while the /rankings Edge column for the same player is blank (marketAction, >=10, rankings/page.jsx:1166). A further 50 carry a backend direction stamp no UI ever surfaces. That is a concrete contradiction on reachable pages with no warning.

WHAT IS WRONG:
(a) 'FIVE competing threshold sets on the SAME retail-vs-consensus quantity' — it is THREE. Verified in source: >0 (data_contract.py:3051), >=3 (trade-logic.js:949), >=10 (thresholds.js:46). The 4th entry gates on `sourceRankSpread` — cross-source DISPERSION, a different quantity — which the finding's own family record #4 concedes ('marketGapDirection for DIRECTION, sourceRankSpread for GATE and SORT'). The 5th, idpMarketAction, is not a competing threshold at all: display-helpers.js:370 imports the SAME MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF constant and applies it to the IDP market. It is the one pair in the whole set that IS consistent, and per-market separation of the retail anchor is documented policy (CLAUDE.md, finder.py per-market gate). Counting the one consistent case as evidence of inconsistency is the opposite of what it shows.
(b) status 'Missing' is wrong by AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md's own vocabulary ('Missing — no code exists'), which the protocol explicitly flags as the distinction most often botched at scale. Both candidate arbiters exist. unified_signal_engine is textbook 'Scaffolded only' (code exists, never called by anything reachable); consensus_edge is a deliberate flag-off. The composite is 'Duplicate or conflicting implementation'.
(c) numericProof 'expected: 1' is not derived from anything in the repo — it is the audit prompt's product preference restated as a measurement. The falsifiable core is the 3-way threshold split, which I confirmed and quantified.
(d) blastRadius playersAffected 1072 is not measured. The population that actually experiences the split is 421 rows carrying a direction stamp, of which 140 (90 + 50) are surfaced inconsistently.
(e) 'reachable today' = 14 is a production claim, not a container one. In this container /api/bdvm/values returns no_projection_snapshot, /api/sharp/market and /api/sharp/roster-percentage return cohort_building, and /api/movers returns empty risers/fallers (historyDepthDays 0) — all pre-declared blocked-by-data. Today, here, roughly 9 emitters actually emit a verb. 14 is right for production; the record should say so.

PRIORITY: keep P1 for the rescoped core. Not P0 — both renderings are honest applications of different cutoffs to the same magnitude, so no single number is wrong; the defect is that two screens contradict each other on 90 top-of-board players with nothing saying which is authoritative. The architecture half (16 emitters, no arbiter, two dead consolidation attempts) is real but is a P2 design finding, not P1.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: The rescoped core is settled — reproduced in source and measured on the live contract. What would settle the emitter COUNT (16/14) is a run on a production instance with data/bdvm/, data/intel/ and the platform ledger present, so the BDVM, sharp-tracker and movers emitters actually emit rather than returning no_projection_snapshot / cohort_building / empty.

findings.title: The 12-hour signal-alert cooldown is keyed on the rule TAG, so it never engages when the reason changes — which is exactly what changes when a signal flips — and the email then renders the flip as a first-ever signal
findings.claimUnderTest: signal_alerts.py: '_MIN_NOTIFY_INTERVAL_HOURS: Minimum hours between alerts for the same (user, signalKey). Stops a rapid-fire RISK -> SELL -> RISK flicker from spamming.'
findings.observed: state_key is aliasSignalKey or signalKey, and BOTH embed the rule tag (`sid:<sleeperId>::<tag>` / `<name>::<tag>`, built by terminal.py::_signal_key / _signal_alias_key). A different firing rule is therefore a different state row with prev_signal='' and prev_notified_at=0, so the cooldown branch is skipped entirely and the alert fires immediately. Executed against a scratch user_kv: RISK/alert_with_drop then RISK/high_vol_drop fired twice with zero elapsed time, and BUY/uptrend_controlled then SELL/sustained_downtrend fired twice with zero elapsed time. Because prev_signal is empty on the new key, priorSignal is None and format_alert_email prints '— -> SELL', so the digest presents a reversal as a brand-new signal. The digest also counts one player twice ('2 of your players had a signal change').

findings.userImpact: A user is emailed 'Josh Allen — -> SELL' hours after being emailed 'Josh Allen — -> BUY', with nothing in either message saying the other happened. The guard that was written to prevent exactly this is bypassed by the thing it was meant to catch.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior index. PRIOR-A23-F09 is a different alert defect (marked delivered before delivery is attempted); PRIOR-A05-F13 / PRIOR-A22-F05 / PRIOR-A23-F06 are about custom_alerts value_crosses being a level test.

findings.whatWorks: bdvm_signal_alerts.py keys its state on `bdvm:<playerId>` with no tag, so its 12h guard does work; and its baseline-seeding pass genuinely prevents a flag-on flood. That module is the correct pattern.
findings.rootCause: The tag is in the key for a legitimate reason — dismissals are meant to follow the reason, so a new reason re-surfaces a dismissed player — but the same key was reused for the notification cooldown, where the tag must NOT participate.
findings.requiredRepair: Split the two keys: keep `<name|sid>::<tag>` for dismissal lifecycle, and cool down on `sid:<sleeperId>` alone. Carry prev_signal across tags so priorSignal is truthful, and de-duplicate players in format_alert_email's count.

findings.title: Three independent email-sending detectors can alert on the same player on the same day, to the same address, with three separate cooldown namespaces and no cross-check
findings.claimUnderTest: bdvm_signal_alerts.py states it is 'Deliberately a SEPARATE detector from signal_alerts.py' with a different state namespace 'so terminal keys can never collide'. The stated benefit is isolation.
findings.observed: Isolation of STATE is achieved; isolation of the USER is not. All three read the same user_kv field notificationsEmail and all three call _deliver_email_smtp. signal_alerts and bdvm_signal_alerts run inside the SAME sweep, back to back, over the same roster (server.py:11695 then :11712), so one player in one sweep can produce two emails. custom_alerts runs from its own route over the same playersArray and can add a third. Their vocabularies are disjoint and opposite-capable: {RISK, SELL, BUY, MONITOR} from rank-history movement versus {STRONG_BUY, BUY, SELL, STRONG_SELL} from fundamental-minus-market alpha. Nothing compares them, and no message mentions the other detector.

reproduction.expected: one per-player decision reaches the user's inbox
reproduction.actual: three detectors, one address, three cooldown namespaces (signalAlertStateByLeague / bdvmSignalAlertStateByLeague / customAlertsState), zero cross-references

findings.userImpact: Two emails about the same player can arrive minutes apart telling him to buy and to sell, each looking authoritative and neither acknowledging the other. Because the label sets differ, he cannot even tell they are about the same question.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior index.

findings.whatWorks: bdvm_signal_alerts' baseline-seeding (first sweep per user+league records silently) is a genuinely good mechanism and is test-pinned; and both detectors degrade to an error field in the sweep summary rather than failing the sweep.
findings.rootCause: Each detector was added as an independent feature with its own state, and the delivery step was never centralised.
findings.requiredRepair: Introduce one per-(user, league, sweep) digest that collects candidate alerts from all detectors, resolves same-player conflicts explicitly (show both with their reasons, or suppress on disagreement), and sends once.

findings.title: Direction is never gated on confidence: 253 of the 356 directional verbs on /rankings sit on rows the same page badges as low or no confidence, and 102 rest on a 'consensus' of two sources or fewer
findings.claimUnderTest: edge-helpers.js header: 'Nothing is predicted or editorialized. Every label traces to a measurable property of the source data.' The /edge page states 'Every signal here is derived from measurable properties of the data — how many sources cover a player, how closely they agree'.
findings.observed: marketAction, idpMarketAction and getPlayerEdge read no confidence field at all — not confidenceBucket, not sourceCount, not isSingleSource, not anomalyFlags. On the live contract 356 rows carry BUY or SELL from marketAction; 173 of them are confidenceBucket 'low', 80 are 'none', and 5 carry anomaly flags. 102 of the 356 have at most two sources on the entire consensus side. Every future draft pick gets SELL from a two-row comparison (ktcSfTep vs idpTradeCalc) — two crowd trade calculators framed as 'retail versus expert consensus'. The rule engines are worse in a different way: signal-engine.js and terminal._evaluate_signal emit no confidence field whatsoever, and the one rule that read confidence was retired in 2026-07-30 because the metric is structurally capped at 0.59375.

findings.whatWorks: The registry already knows the truth — correlation_group 'ktc' exists and is documented, and is_cross_market marks idpTradeCalc as a market source. The facts needed for the fix are already stamped; only _retail_source_keys() ignores them.

findings.title: The terminal home page prescribes opposite actions from the same rank-history input: the Movers panel calls a riser a sell-high candidate while the Signals panel directly below calls the same rise a BUY

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A05-F12 and PRIOR-A23-F08 both claim 'MoversPanel labels risers as buy-low candidates and fallers as sell-high — both inverted'. That is NOT true at HEAD e96c06ef. The source at MoversPanel.jsx:196-215 reads 'Risers — sell-high candidates' / 'Fallers — buy-low candidates', carries a comment recording the correction as 'audit finding S-8', and the rendered DOM confirms it. findings.rootCause: Two panels were written from two different trading theses and neither was ever chosen as the product's position.

verification.reasoning:
The CODE READING is correct and I re-verified every leg of it independently: value-history.js:100 returns `baseline.rank - latest.rank`, so a positive trend7 IS a rise; server.py:3354 movers docstring 'Risers = rank improved (number got smaller)'; MoversPanel.jsx:198 heads risers 'sell-high candidates'; signal-engine.js:151-160 and its Python mirror src/api/terminal.py:970-976 both emit BUY for trend7 >= +3 with non-high volatility. Two opposite verbs off the same rank-history sign. That part survives.

What does not survive is the finding's framing of the evidence and its blast radius.

(1) NOT OBSERVED AT RUNTIME. `data/rank_history.jsonl` does not exist in this container. /api/movers returns historyDepthDays:0, risers:[], fallers:[]; /api/terminal returns signals:[]; the page renders 'No qualifying movers in this window' under BOTH headings and 'Buy 0'. Every trend7 is null, so `(c.trend7 ?? 0) >= 3` is false and buy.uptrend_controlled cannot fire. The reproduction command proves only that two HEADINGS co-exist on one page — it does not, and in this container cannot, exhibit one player carrying both labels. numericProof is therefore a code reading dressed as a measurement. In production (where the scrape appends rank history) the collision would be reachable, so this is not overturned — but the finding's confidence:high is not earned by what was actually run.

(2) pagesAffected 2 is wrong. '/trending' does not render MoversPanel and contains no sell-high framing — it computes its own movers from contract rows via lib computeMovers. MoversPanel.jsx:198 is the only 'sell-high candidates' string in the tree and TerminalLayout.jsx:76 is its only mount. pagesAffected = 1 (/).

(3) playersAffected 1072 is wrong by two orders of magnitude. /api/movers caps at limit=10 per side (server.py, `limit = max(1, min(50, limit))`, default 10) and the Signals panel is roster-scoped ('per roster player'). The observable collision set is bounded by 10 risers intersected with a ~30-player roster, not the 1,072-row board.

(4) The collision is narrower than 'any rise'. STRONG_HOLD (priority 50, signal-engine.js:131-147 / terminal.py:963-969) outranks BUY (priority 40). A riser with value >= 7000 and trend30 >= 0 returns STRONG_HOLD, not BUY. The BUY-vs-sell-high contradiction is confined to sub-7000 risers, or elite risers whose 30d trend is negative.

(5) The finding UNDERCOUNTS the theses. A third momentum consumer on the same page uses the reversal thesis: frontend/lib/portfolio-insights.js:556 feeds ScoutingIntel on / with 'Down N ranks in 7d ... potential buy-low if league treats it the same.' So it is 2 reversal panels vs 1 following panel, and signal-engine is the outlier — which sharpens 'which one should change' but does not add a fourth interpretation.

Severity: P1 overstates it. This is not a wrong number a user acts on — it is inconsistent prescriptive framing between two unvalidated heuristics measured over DIFFERENT windows and thresholds (movers: 14d default, threshold 15; signal: 7d, threshold 3), and it renders nowhere today. Real, worth fixing, P2.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: A populated data/rank_history.jsonl (>= 7 days deep) plus a selected team, then one query listing players that appear in /api/movers risers AND carry signal==BUY with tag uptrend_controlled in /api/terminal signals for the same roster. A non-empty intersection settles it as a live user-facing contradiction; an empty one after several scrapes would mean the 14d/threshold-15 and 7d/threshold-3 windows never actually overlap in practice and the finding collapses to a copy inconsistency.

findings.title: Both live rule engines return HOLD 'Stable — no movement, volatility, or news triggers' for 665 of 665 rostered players because the rank-history log does not exist, and no surface says the evidence is missing
findings.claimUnderTest: signal-engine.js: 'HOLD never fires as a rule — it's the fallback when nothing else does', with the user-facing reason 'Stable — no movement, volatility, or news triggers.'
findings.observed: data/rank_history.jsonl (the path in rank_history.py:74) is absent from this container, so GET /api/data/rank-history returns {"days":30,"history":{}}. Every context therefore has trend7=null, trend30=null and volatility=null, no rule can fire, and every player falls to HOLD. Queried all 12 teams: 665 of 665 rostered players return HOLD with the tag default_hold and that exact reason string. The reason asserts stability as a positive finding when the truth is that nothing was measured — 'we looked and it is quiet' and 'we have no data' render identically. /api/movers does better on the same missing input: it returns historyDepthDays:0 alongside the empty lists.

reproduction.command: for t in $(curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/terminal | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(" ".join(x["ownerId"] for x in json.load(sys.stdin)["availableTeams"]))'); do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/terminal?ownerId=$t"; done | python3 -c 'import sys,json,collections;c=collections.Counter();[c.update(s["signal"] for s in json.loads(l)["signals"]) for l in sys.stdin]; print(c)'

findings.userImpact: The Signals panel reports a calm, healthy roster when in fact it has measured nothing. Its default filter shows RISK/SELL/MONITOR/BUY, so the panel renders empty and reads as 'no issues' rather than 'no data'.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed exactly, and quantified across all 12 rosters. Also confirms PRIOR-A18-F21 (rank_history.jsonl absent from the repository) as the cause. Note the protocol's data-absence caveat applies to the emptiness; the finding is the WORDING, which is a code property and would mislead in production during any scrape lapse.

findings.whatWorks: The null-guards themselves are correct and deliberate: sell.sustained_downtrend and strong.elite_stable both test `trend30 != null` rather than coalescing to 0, with an in-code note that a `?? 0` once made unmeasured history satisfy `<= 0` and emit SELL. The engine fails safe. Both engines are also pinned to one shared fixture (tests/fixtures/signal_parity_cases.json).
findings.rootCause: HOLD is overloaded: it is both 'measured, nothing happening' and 'not measured'. The reason string only describes the first.
findings.requiredRepair: Return a distinct verdict (e.g. NO_DATA, tag 'no_history') when trend7, trend30 and volatility are all null, and have BuySellHold / TopSignalsRail render it as an evidence gap rather than folding it into HOLD.
findings.dependencies: data/rank_history.jsonl must exist for the engines to do anything at all.

findings.title: Every movement threshold is an absolute ordinal-rank count applied uniformly across a 1,092-row board, so a 3-rank move is a SELL at rank 900 and not a signal at rank 1
findings.claimUnderTest: signal-engine.js: 'No random labels: every signal is produced by a named rule whose boolean test evaluates known inputs.' The rules are stated as universal thresholds (trend7 <= -3, trend7 <= -5, MAD <= 1 / <= 4, value >= 7000).
findings.observed: _window_trend returns baseline_rank - latest_rank, a raw ordinal difference, and _volatility takes the MAD of raw ordinal deltas. Both are compared against fixed integers across a board whose ranks span 1 to 1,092. Moving from rank 5 to rank 8 and from rank 905 to rank 908 both produce trend7 = -3 and both fire sell.sustained_downtrend, which is in ACTIONABLE_SIGNALS and therefore emails. Conversely the #1 overall player dropping two spots — a far larger real repricing — fires nothing. The 'high volatility' label needs MAD > 4 ranks, which is near-certain deep on the board and near-impossible at the top, so RISK and MONITOR are structurally concentrated in the tail. /api/movers uses a fourth constant on the same scale (15 ranks). None of the four thresholds is depth-scaled, and the pipeline already stamps a percentile per source per row.

reproduction.command: sed -n '338,371p;897,983p' src/api/terminal.py   # _window_trend / _volatility / _evaluate_signal;  curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/movers | python3 -m json.tool | head -5   # "threshold": 15
reproduction.expected: a movement threshold that scales with board depth, or a percentile/value-based trigger
reproduction.actual: trend7 <= -3, trend7 <= -5, MAD 1 and 4, movers 15 — all raw ordinal ranks, all constant across 1,092 rows

numericProof.formula: a fixed ordinal threshold implies a value threshold that varies with the local slope of the Hill curve; the slope near rank 1 is roughly an order of magnitude steeper than near rank 900

findings.userImpact: The alerting is loudest about the players who matter least. A user who acts on the emails spends attention on tail moves and is never told when a top-10 asset repriced.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A12-F00 makes the same class of argument about marketGapDirection averaging ordinal ranks across pools of different depth — confirmed separately in W12-F002/F008. This is the time-series analogue: the same ordinal-ranks-are-not-commensurable error applied to movement over time rather than across sources. Recorded as partial because the prior finding does not cover the rule engines or /api/movers. Confidence is medium because with rank_history.jsonl absent I could not measure the realized firing distribution by depth, only derive it from the thresholds and the curve.

findings.whatWorks: The thresholds are at least identical on both sides of the Python/JS parity boundary and are pinned by tests/fixtures/signal_parity_cases.json, so a change on one side fails both suites.
findings.rootCause: The rules were written against ordinal ranks because that is what rank_history.jsonl stores, and no depth normalisation was added.
findings.requiredRepair: Express movement in value space (rank_history already stores rankDerivedValue alongside rank) or as a percentile delta, and re-derive the constants against the realized distribution once history exists.
findings.dependencies: Needs data/rank_history.jsonl to re-derive the constants empirically.

findings.title: Verified working: the only two label families with a documented, calibrated-or-honestly-uncalibrated score both refuse to show a number rather than fake one — /consensus-edge and /bdvm degrade to specific, truthful empty states
findings.claimUnderTest: The prompt asks whether a summary score in [-100,+100] has a documented meaning and is calibrated, and whether the system ever emits HOLD / NO SIGNAL on thin evidence.
findings.observed: consensus_edge's composite is 100*tanh(sum of renormalised weights times clamped component scores), with bands +-30/+-60 and confidence gates 35/50/70 — all in config/consensus_edge/params_v1.json, each carrying an explicit _status ('prior') and a _rationale saying the bands are NOT calibrated ('with a single validated component there is no basis for asserting that +60 means anything different in kind from +55'). COMPONENT_VALIDATION records mispricing as measured-null (rho +0.031 over 6 folds, beaten by a plain buy-cheap benchmark in 5 of 6), sharpFlow as unmeasurABLE, opportunity as measured-and-rejected at weight 0.0 — and score.py::composite excludes zero-weight components from componentsPresent so a rejected signal cannot inflate confidence. classify() is the only function in the platform that separates direction from confidence, returns INSUFFICIENT below a floor, downgrades Strong to plain when confidence is short, and forces CONFLICTED rather than averaging opposing evidence to Neutral. The whole package is behind a flag that defaults off with the reason stated in the 503 body and on the page. /bdvm likewise renders 'No projection snapshot yet ... this season's hasn't been built yet' rather than a board.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/consensus-edge/top?limit=5 ; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/bdvm/values | head -c 200 ; .venv/bin/python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/w12_page.py
reproduction.expected: an honest disabled/no-data state, not a fabricated board

numericProof.formula: score = 100 * tanh( sum_i (w_i / sum w) * clamp(v_i, -1, 1) ) over PRESENT components only

findings.userImpact: None — this is the behaviour the rest of the label layer should copy.

priorFinding.note: Recorded as a verified positive per the protocol's instruction that proving something works is as valuable as finding a defect.

findings.rootCause: n/a

findings.title: BDVM's "exact league scoring" drops all six reception yardage-band rules; WR fundamentals understated 19.7% and TE 22.0% on real 2025 data
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'No positional multipliers anywhere: Superflex/TEP/IDP format effects flow from exact scoring'; scripts/bdvm_build_baseline.py: 'scores them under the league's exact Sleeper scoring settings'.
findings.observed: The live league scoring block carries base rec=0.08 and six per-reception YARDAGE-BAND bonuses (rec_0_4 0.17, rec_5_9 0.42, rec_10_19 0.67, rec_20_29 0.92, rec_30_39 1.17, rec_40p 1.92). src/nfl_data/realized_points.py — the only scorer BDVM's baseline uses — references none of those six keys and emits no diagnostic for unread scoring rules. Because base rec is only 0.08, essentially the entire per-catch economy of this league is dropped. 52 of 85 non-zero scoring keys are not literally referenced (most are DEF/K, legitimately out of scope; the six reception bands are not).

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;s=json.load(open('/tmp/w13-contract-full.json'))['sleeper']['scoringSettings'];src=open('src/nfl_data/realized_points.py').read();print({k:s[k] for k in ('rec','rec_0_4','rec_5_9','rec_10_19','rec_20_29','rec_30_39','rec_40p')});print([k for k in ('rec_0_4','rec_5_9','rec_10_19','rec_20_29','rec_30_39','rec_40p') if f'\"{k}\"' in src])"  # then see the artifact for the per-position measurement
reproduction.expected: Every non-zero scoring rule the league pays is either applied or explicitly reported as unmodelled.
reproduction.actual: Six reception-band rules are silently dropped; the omitted points are position-correlated (pass-catchers only), so the fundamental board is biased BY POSITION, not merely rescaled.

numericProof.formula: omitted_ppg = 0.600 * receptions / games ; understatement% = omitted_ppg / (scored_ppg + omitted_ppg)

findings.userImpact: Every WR and TE on the /bdvm board, and their 'Fund gap' cell on /rankings and /draft, is understated by roughly a fifth relative to QB and RB. A user reads that as 'the market overprices pass-catchers' and sells them.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed and re-measured against real 2025 nflverse data under the live scoring block. Prior said WR ~15% / RB ~9% / QB 0%; measured WR 19.7% / RB 8.1% / QB 0.0% and additionally TE 22.0%, which the prior did not report.

findings.whatWorks: The 141-key scoring block IS read, and QB scoring is exact (0.0% understatement measured).
findings.rootCause: compute_weekly_points is a fixed key->column table with no band arithmetic and no unread-key accounting. nflverse weekly rows are game aggregates and carry no per-reception yardage, so the bands cannot be computed exactly from this feed — but the code neither approximates them nor declares them unmodelled.
findings.requiredRepair: Either estimate band bonuses from a per-player air-yards/aDOT distribution, or (minimum) emit the set of non-zero scoring keys the scorer did not consume into the BDVM payload meta so the board's own coverage is visible.
findings.dependencies: Shared with any other workstream auditing src/nfl_data/realized_points.py (ROS, playerctx).

findings.claimUnderTest: src/bdvm/roster.py module docstring: 'produces, per roster: strategy capitals ..., now/future ratio, quick starter FPG, positional surplus vs. replacement, value-weighted age, pick capital, and a contend/retool/rebuild direction.' CLAUDE.md: 'GET /api/bdvm/roster (strategy capitals + league-relative direction per roster)'.
findings.observed: analyze_rosters builds `assets` exclusively from roster['playerIds'] (roster.py:154-155). roster['picks'] is consumed only by len() for `pickCount` (roster.py:199). `capitals`, `nowFutureRatio`, `valueWeightedAge` and every asset the trade scan can propose are therefore player-only. No 'pick capital' field exists anywhere in the payload. The /bdvm Rosters table renders pickCount next to capitals computed as if those picks were worth zero.

findings.title: BDVM signal layer saturates at 81.5% STRONG_SELL: calibration anchors only the board maximum while the signal thresholds are absolute point values
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: the /bdvm board exposes 'fundamental-vs-market gap + signals' and the /rankings Fund-gap column is 'tinted by BDVM signal', with a tooltip asserting positive gap means the market underprices the player.
findings.observed: DynastyEngine.calibrate anchors each strategy so only the TOP asset reaches target_top_value (9800). Nothing reconciles the SHAPE of the two boards below the top. On a real run over the live contract the fundamental board's median balanced value is 511.6 against a market median of 1914.5, so 92.6% of the 676 market-anchored assets carry a negative gap. Because signal_thresholds are absolute (strong_sell_alpha = -900.0), 570 of 699 priced players (81.5%) read STRONG_SELL, versus 10 STRONG_BUY and 69 HOLD.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json,collections;d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W13/engine-live-run.json'));print(collections.Counter(p['signal']['signal'] for p in d['players']))"
reproduction.expected: An actionable signal distribution — a buy/sell board where the sell call means something.
reproduction.actual: Counter({'STRONG_SELL': 570, 'HOLD': 69, 'NO_MARKET': 23, 'BUY': 14, 'SELL': 13, 'STRONG_BUY': 10})

numericProof.formula: signal = f(alpha), alpha = gap x liquidity, gap = tradeValue.balanced - marketValue ; thresholds fixed at +/-400 and +/-900

findings.userImpact: The Fund-gap column on /rankings and the signal pills on /bdvm tell the user to sell four players in five. A signal that fires on 81.5% of the board carries no information, and the tooltip's stated interpretation ('positive means the market underprices') implies a calibrated comparison that has not been performed.

priorFinding.note: Measured with a reconstructed-baseline (proxy) snapshot built from ONE season back (2023/2024 nflverse pulls are not cached in this container). Production's 3-season baseline plus real Clay/IDP-Show sources will shift the magnitude. The STRUCTURAL cause — top-anchor-only calibration against absolute thresholds — is snapshot-independent, and the /bdvm page's own copy warns that proxy fundamentals are backward-looking, which is exactly the regime that produces this.

findings.whatWorks: The two boards do agree where calibration touches them: fundamental max 9800 vs market max 9999. Signals are correctly suppressed to NO_MARKET (23 rows) where no anchor exists.
findings.rootCause: calibrate() solves an anchor from the single maximum DV; the distribution below the max is whatever the surplus/discount stack produces, and it decays far faster than crowd market values. Absolute alpha thresholds then convert a distributional mismatch into a universal sell call.
findings.requiredRepair: Either calibrate on a rank-matched quantile map between the fundamental and market boards before differencing, or make signal_thresholds percentile-based within the board. Whichever is chosen, the /bdvm page should surface the board-level gap distribution so saturation is visible.
findings.dependencies: W13-F001 — the reception-band omission pushes pass-catcher fundamentals down and contributes to the negative skew.

findings.title: Tier-form rookie picks in rounds 5-6 cannot be priced: the regex covers 1st-4th only, and the 24 affected rows are labelled with the factually wrong reason "unparseable_pick_name"
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: the /draft 'Fundamental pick values (BDVM)' panel shows 'balanced-strategy pick EV / hit% / median / ceiling beside the market anchor'; unpriced assets are 'unpriced with a reason'.
findings.observed: _PICK_TIER_RE hardcodes (?P<round>1st|2nd|3rd|4th) and _ROUND_WORD has only four entries, so every 'YYYY {Early|Mid|Late} {5th|6th}' row falls through to distribution=None with reason='unparseable_pick_name'. This is a 6-round rookie draft: 24 of 144 pick rows (all of rounds 5-6 across 2026-2029) are affected. The slot-form parser accepts rounds 1-9, so '2026 Pick 5.03' prices fine while '2026 Early 5th' does not — the same asset class, two answers. The outcome model itself is not the limit: pick_values_all_strategies extrapolates past the last table anchor and returns 123.2 (round-5 Early) and 60.0 (round-6 Early) balanced EV for exactly these slots.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.bdvm.service import _parse_pick_slot;from src.bdvm.picks import pick_values_all_strategies;from src.bdvm.params import load_param_set;P=load_param_set();print([(n,_parse_pick_slot(n,12)) for n in ['2026 Early 4th','2026 Early 5th','2026 Mid 6th','2026 Pick 5.03']]);print({r:round(pick_values_all_strategies((r-1)*12+3,P,years_out=0)['balanced']['ev'],1) for r in (4,5,6)})"

numericProof.formula: unpriced_share = 24/144

findings.userImpact: A trade containing a future 5th or 6th is reported as 'Not priced by the fundamental board' on the /trade BDVM panel even though the model can price it, and the /draft fundamental-pick panel is missing a third of the draft. The stated reason misdirects a maintainer toward the pick NAME rather than the round coverage.

priorFinding.note: Not present in the 21 prior BDVM findings. Adjacent to PRIOR-A15-F18 (pick outcome tail) but a different mechanism: that one is the outcome table, this one is name parsing.

findings.whatWorks: The failure is HONEST — the pick is emitted with distribution: null and a reason, it appears in trade-eval's `unresolved` list rather than being priced at zero, and the /trade panel renders 'Not priced by the fundamental board: 2027 Mid 5th'. Verified by direct call.
findings.rootCause: _PICK_TIER_RE and _ROUND_WORD were written against a 4-round assumption; the slot-form regex was later widened to \d and the tier form was not.
findings.requiredRepair: Extend _ROUND_WORD/_PICK_TIER_RE to at least the league's configured rookie-draft round count, and rename the fallback reason to distinguish 'name did not parse' from 'round outside the model's coverage'.
findings.dependencies: Feeds W13-F002 — a pick-capital fix would still omit these 24.

findings.title: data/bdvm/ does not exist in this container, so all four BDVM routes answer 200 with status=no_projection_snapshot and every UI surface degrades correctly rather than fabricating a value
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: the engine 'answers status: "ok" with 726 players priced and 222 honestly unpriced'; the /rankings Fund-gap column 'gates on status == "ok" so it self-suppresses without a snapshot'; the /draft panel has the 'same silent-vanish posture'.

findings.observed: Two small honesty/robustness items in the same layer. (1) service.py:297 writes 'marketReadAfterFundamental': True as a literal into every meta block. findings.title: 28 of the board's 73 buy-side rows are labelled Buy directly above their own text saying the fair value is BELOW the market

findings.observed: The component score is a cohort-relative z-score, `tanh((logGap - cohortMedian) / cohortSigma / 3)`, so its sign tracks the gap RELATIVE TO the cohort median, not the gap itself. On the live board the anchor-free cohort medians are strongly negative — RB_WR_TE|mid median logGap -0.1688 (the anchor-free board prices the median mid-value skill player 15.5% below KTC), RB_WR_TE|high -0.0755, QB|mid -0.0545 — because removing ktcSfTep + fantasyNavigatorSf shifts the blend's level, not because the market is wrong. Each such row's `explanation[0]`, rendered verbatim at page.jsx:306, reads e.g. 'Our anchor-free fair value is 6% below the market (1594 vs 1702).' immediately under the word 'Buy'. findings.title: The weekly re-validation cron's output is read by nobody and nothing but a GitHub job-failure exit code, and its comparison ignores the effect size entirely
findings.claimUnderTest: The workflow exists to 'fail when the committed measurement stops describing the code'.
findings.observed: It does exactly one thing with its output: compare `decision.recommendation` (a string) between the fresh run and every committed docs/measurements/consensus-edge-board-validation-*.json, and sys.exit(1) if they differ. `pooled.topBuys.medianExcess` is printed and then discarded — the gate would stay green while the measured excess moved from -0.006 to -0.30, or from -0.006 to +0.20, as long as both sides still round to the same categorical recommendation. There is no notification wiring, no issue creation, and no repo-side consumer: the artifact is uploaded with 30-day retention and the job summary is written, both readable only by someone who opens the run. Neither is read by any code. The fresh measurement is deliberately not committed (a stated design choice, and the right one). The key names in the compare step do match the script's output shape (verified against both committed files), so the gate is not a silent no-op — it just measures the coarsest possible thing. The re-run could not be exercised here: scripts/validate_consensus_edge_board.py correctly refuses on a shallow clone (this container has .git/shallow and 409 commits) and prints 'shallow clone: run git fetch --unshallow first' rather than measuring a truncated panel and calling it history.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && timeout 120 .venv/bin/python scripts/validate_consensus_edge_board.py --horizon-days 7 --out /tmp/w14-rerun.json; echo "exit=$?"; git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository; grep -n 'medianExcess\|old_call != fresh_call' .github/workflows/consensus-edge-revalidate.yml
reproduction.expected: the gate compares the measured effect, not only its categorical summary; the re-run is exercisable
reproduction.actual: '[ce-validate] shallow clone: run `git fetch --unshallow` first.' (exit 2); the workflow's only drift condition is `old_call != fresh_call`, with medianExcess printed and unused

numericProof.formula: drift = (committed decision.recommendation != fresh decision.recommendation); medianExcess is not compared

findings.userImpact: Indirect. The flag default is supposed to move only when this gate says so; a gate blind to effect size can let the underlying measurement decay a long way before it reports anything, and the report itself reaches a human only if someone notices a red scheduled run.

priorFinding.note: no prior finding covers consensus_edge. Confidence is medium because the workflow's own execution could not be reproduced in this container (shallow clone); the compare-step logic was read and its key names verified against both committed measurement files.

findings.whatWorks: The workflow self-tests the gate (pytest tests/consensus_edge/test_board_validation.py + test_outcomes.py) before trusting it, uses fetch-depth 0 because the panel reconstructs boards with git show, deliberately does not commit the re-run (so the committed file can disagree with the code, which is the whole signal), and pr-validation.yml enforces the cheap half — the flag default must equal the committed verdict — on every PR.
findings.rootCause: The comparison was written against the categorical decision field only.
findings.requiredRepair: Compare pooled.topBuys.medianExcess against the committed value with a declared tolerance in addition to the recommendation string, and route the failure somewhere a human sees without opening Actions.
findings.dependencies: Requires an unshallow clone to exercise, which CI has and this container does not.

findings.title: rosterQuality is 22% of the Sharp Score and is structurally 0.0 for every manager because platform_records never populates any of its four inputs, and the weight is not renormalized
findings.claimUnderTest: config/sharp/scoring_v2.json declares weights performance 0.36 / rosterQuality 0.22 / multiLeagueConsistency 0.22 / longevity 0.12 / activity 0.08 and says they 'must sum to 1.0 across the positive components'. src/sharp/score.py documents rosterQuality as measuring value vs league average, age-adjusted value, depth and pick capital.
findings.observed: src/sharp/platform_records.py::build_manager_records constructs every ManagerRecord without roster_value_ratios, age_adjusted_value_ratio, depth_adjusted_value_ratio or draft_pick_capital_ratio, so all four stay at their dataclass defaults ([] and None). _roster_quality_component therefore finds `parts` empty and returns 0.0 on its `if not parts` branch for every manager, in every population. The 0.22 weight is multiplied by 0.0 and is NOT redistributed: the reachable score ceiling is 0.36+0.22+0.12+0.08 = 0.78 (plus at most +0.12 championship bonus, minus the uncertainty penalty), on a value the payload publishes as `score` on an implied 0-100 scale. Ranking order is unaffected (every manager loses the same 22 points), so qualification membership is not changed; what is wrong is the published number and the fact that a fifth of the documented model is dead code.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W15/reconcile_probe.py
reproduction.expected: rosterQuality component > 0 for a manager with a strong roster
reproduction.actual: F00_rosterQuality_component_value = 0.0; roster_value_ratios = [], age/depth/pick ratios all null for every record

numericProof.formula: score = 100 * clamp(0.36*perf + 0.22*rosterQuality + 0.22*consistency + 0.12*longevity + 0.08*activity + titleBonus - penalty, 0, 1); ceiling with rosterQuality==0 is 100*(0.36+0.22+0.12+0.08) = 78.0

findings.userImpact: A manager displayed with 'Sharp Score 68' on /market/sharp-tracker is at 68 out of a structural maximum of 78, not out of 100, and the roster-quality dimension the methodology advertises contributed nothing to their selection.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced with an exact decomposition: manual reconstruction 68.1 equals the engine's 68.1, and the 0.22 weight is verifiably multiplied by 0.0 with no renormalization.

findings.whatWorks: The component function itself is correct and would work the moment the inputs are supplied; the percentile machinery around it is sound.
findings.rootCause: platform_records.build_manager_records has no roster-value source. The ledger stores season results, not roster valuations.
findings.requiredRepair: Either populate the four ratios from stored rosters (sharp_roster_assets now exists and could be joined to the board), or drop rosterQuality from the weight table and renormalize the remaining four to 1.0. Shipping a weight that is always multiplied by zero is the one option that should not survive.
findings.dependencies: src/sharp/roster_store.py holds the roster data that would feed this.

findings.title: score_percentile compares a ROUNDED score against an UNROUNDED population, so the top manager's percentile flips between 1.0 and (N-1)/N on a float-rounding coin flip and a two-manager pool qualifies nobody
findings.claimUnderTest: percentile_rank's docstring: 'Midpoint handling for ties, so a population of identical values scores 0.5 rather than 1.0 - an all-identical population carries no information and must not read as universally elite.' Qualification is minScorePercentile 0.75 = top quartile of the evaluable population.
findings.observed: score_managers stores `entry.score = round(total, 1)` (line 596) but appends the UNROUNDED `total` to `raw_scores` (line 622), then calls `percentile_rank(entry.score, raw_scores)` (line 633). A manager's own value is therefore never found in its own `equal` bucket, and whether it lands in `below` depends on which direction round() moved it in the second decimal. Measured on controlled populations with strictly distinct scores: N=2 top percentile 0.5, N=3 1.0, N=4 1.0, N=5 0.8, N=8 1.0, N=20 1.0 - a value that should monotonically approach 1 as N grows instead oscillates. The intended midpoint value is ((N-1)+0.5)/N. Concretely at N=2 the single best manager in the whole evaluable pool scores percentile 0.5, fails the 0.75 bar and does not qualify, while at N=3 the best manager scores 1.0 and does. The percentile is also published to the client as `scorePercentile`.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W15/percentile_probe.py
reproduction.expected: top-of-population percentile = ((N-1)+0.5)/N, i.e. 0.75 at N=2, 0.833 at N=3, 0.875 at N=4, 0.9 at N=5, 0.975 at N=20 - monotonic in N and never 1.0
reproduction.actual: 0.5 at N=2, 1.0 at N=3, 1.0 at N=4, 0.8 at N=5, 1.0 at N=8, 1.0 at N=20 - non-monotonic, and 1.0 for a value the docstring says must never read as 1.0

numericProof.formula: percentile_rank(r, pop) = (|{v in pop : v < r}| + 0.5*|{v in pop : v == r}|) / |pop|; with r = round(t_max,1) != t_max the self term is 0, giving (N-1)/N when round() rounds down and N/N when it rounds up, instead of the intended ((N-1)+0.5)/N

findings.userImpact: Membership of the sharp cohort - which drives every number on both sharp boards - depends on a float rounding artifact whenever the evaluable population is small, which is exactly the state a growing cohort is in. A manager can be excluded from the cohort while being the highest-scoring manager observed.

priorFinding.note: The prior claim was that a small evaluable set can label up to half its members top-quartile. That is NOT reproduced: measured qualified shares were 0.0 (N=2), 0.333 (N=3), 0.25 (N=4), 0.4 (N=5), 0.25 (N=8), 0.3 (N=20) - never half. The real small-population defect is the rounded-vs-unrounded comparison documented here, which the prior audit did not identify.

findings.whatWorks: percentile_rank itself is correct when given a population containing the value being ranked; the bug is entirely in the caller passing a rounded value against an unrounded population.
findings.rootCause: Line 596 rounds for display, line 622 appends the raw value, and line 633 mixes the two.
findings.requiredRepair: Append `entry.score` (the rounded value) to raw_scores, or rank `total` rather than `entry.score`. One line either way. Add a regression test asserting the top-of-population percentile equals ((N-1)+0.5)/N for N in 2..10.

findings.title: multiLeagueConsistency - the anti-luck term - counts SEASON ROWS as independent leagues, and the user-facing contributor string says '6 independent leagues' for a manager with 3
findings.claimUnderTest: score.py: 'Repeated success across INDEPENDENT leagues - the anti-luck term. Deliberately a SHARE, not a count: adding mediocre leagues cannot raise it, so "plays in many leagues" can never masquerade as skill.' config: minLeaguesForFullCredit 4.
findings.observed: _consistency_component reads rec.finish_percentiles, which platform_records builds with ONE ENTRY PER SEASON ROW, not per league (line 152-156 iterates `seasons`, and `leagues` is computed separately as a distinct set at line 148 but never reaches this component). len(finishes) is therefore the season-row count. Measured on a synthetic manager with 6 completed seasons spread across 3 distinct dynasty leagues: finish_percentiles has 6 entries, observed_leagues is 3, and the breadth scale-down `if len(finishes) < minLeaguesForFullCredit` is bypassed because 6 >= 4 when the true league breadth is 3. The contributor string published in the payload literally reads 'Above median in 100% of 6 independent leagues'. The failure mode this is meant to prevent - one league's results reading as multi-league evidence - is reachable: a manager with two dynasty leagues and three seasons each gets 6 'independent leagues' of credit.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W15/reconcile_probe.py
reproduction.expected: consistency computed over 3 independent leagues; contributor text naming 3
reproduction.actual: F03_consistency_population: elite1_finish_percentiles_n = 6, elite1_observed_leagues = 3, contributor_notes = ['Above median in 100% of 6 independent leagues']

numericProof.formula: breadth scale = min(1, len(finish_percentiles)/minLeaguesForFullCredit); correct scale = min(1, distinct_leagues/minLeaguesForFullCredit) = 3/4 = 0.75

findings.userImpact: A manager with too few independent leagues to prove anything can receive full multi-league-consistency credit (22% of the score) and a payload string asserting a breadth they do not have.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced exactly, including the misleading user-facing contributor string.

findings.whatWorks: The share-not-count design is right; only the population it is computed over is wrong.
findings.rootCause: platform_records emits one finish percentile per season row and score.py treats the list length as a league count.
findings.requiredRepair: Either aggregate finish_percentiles per league before the consistency term, or pass rec.dynasty_leagues into _consistency_component for the breadth scale and reword the contributor string to say 'season' where it means season.

findings.title: Championship success is counted twice in the Sharp Score - once as a shrunk rate inside the performance component and again as a standalone bonus on top
findings.claimUnderTest: config/sharp/scoring_v2.json describes the championship bonus as the implementation of 'preferably they have won the league before', 'implemented as a bounded BONUS rather than a hard gate', and separately lists championshipRate at subweight 0.26 inside performance. Neither block says the two stack.
findings.observed: _performance_component computes a beta-binomial-shrunk championship rate, percentile-ranks it, and applies it at subweight 0.26 of the 0.36 performance weight (9.4% of the total score). _championship_bonus then ADDS up to +0.12 (12 points) to the same total for the same titles. Both fire for the same manager in the same pass. Measured: a 6-season manager with 2 championships gets championshipRate inside performance AND championshipBonus = 0.08 on top. Titles therefore carry up to ~21% of the reachable score, against a documented intent of 9.4% plus a marginal nudge.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W15/reconcile_probe.py
reproduction.expected: one championship pathway
reproduction.actual: F15_championship_double_count: in_performance_subweight 0.26, separate_bonus_applied 0.08, both_nonzero true

numericProof.formula: title contribution = 0.36*0.26*percentile(shrunkRate) + min(0.12, 0.06 + 0.02*(titles-1)); at percentile 1.0 and 2 titles = 0.0936 + 0.08 = 0.1736 of a 0.78 reachable ceiling

findings.userImpact: A lucky title carries roughly double the weight the published methodology describes, and at the margin decides cohort membership for a manager whose other evidence is ordinary.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced with both terms measured firing on the same record.

findings.whatWorks: The shrinkage on the rate term is genuinely correct and is the right treatment for a rare event.
findings.rootCause: The bonus was added as a product requirement ('preferably they have won the league') without removing or discounting the existing championshipRate subweight.
findings.requiredRepair: Pick one. Either drop championshipRate from performance subWeights and renormalize, or reduce the bonus to compensate, and say in the config comment that the two are additive if they are kept.
findings.dependencies: Interacts with W15-F002: with rosterQuality dead, the title terms are an even larger share of what actually moves.

findings.title: The maxAbandonedRosterRate eligibility gate can never fire because abandoned_rosters is never populated, and the recency gate is vacuous for any manager not already in the cohort
findings.claimUnderTest: config/sharp/scoring_v2.json documents seven hard eligibility gates: minCompletedSeasons, minDynastyLeagues, minLeagueAgeSeasons, minCompletedGames, minWinPct, maxAbandonedRosterRate 0.34, requireRecentActivityDays 400.
findings.observed: maxAbandonedRosterRate: platform_records.build_manager_records never sets abandoned_rosters, so it stays at its dataclass default 0, abandoned_rate is 0.0/observed_leagues = 0.0 for every record ever built, and `rec.abandoned_rate > 0.34` is unreachable. Measured across 10 synthetic records: abandoned_rate_all_zero true, abandoned_rosters_ever_set false. requireRecentActivityDays: days_since_last_activity is derived from asset_movements rows, and scripts/crawl_sharp_activity.py crawls movements only for `qualification="automated"` members - i.e. only for managers who already qualified. A manager who has not yet qualified therefore has no movements, days_since_last_activity is None, and the gate is skipped by its own `is not None` guard. The gate can only ever be applied to managers it cannot exclude for the first time.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W15/reconcile_probe.py
reproduction.expected: at least one record with a nonzero abandoned_rosters, or a documented note that the gate is inert
reproduction.actual: F09_dead_gates: abandoned_rate_all_zero true, abandoned_rosters_ever_set false over n_records 10
