findings.title: Two ManagerRecord builders with different gates coexist; the live boards use the strict one and the operator's own scoring report uses the loose one, so they can disagree about who is qualified
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Qualification is decided in src/sharp/score.py + config/sharp/scoring_v2.json over evidence from src/sharp/platform_records.py.' src/sharp/cohort.py: 'Do not reimplement the selection.'
findings.observed: src/sharp/records.py::build_manager_records is a second, independent evidence builder, and scripts/crawl_sharp_records.py --score calls it. The two apply different gates for the same question. platform_records requires source_identity_type == 'global_verified', is_complete, sharp_eligible, and every one of the seven _REQUIRED_RESULT_FIELDS to be non-null, keys records by manager_key, and drops FFPC rows with no recent activity. records.py requires only `is_complete = 1 AND sharp_eligible = 1`, keys by user_id, and coerces null wins/losses/ties to 0 via `or 0`, so a season row with unknown results contributes a 0-0-0 record rather than being excluded. The operator report is therefore built from a strictly larger and dirtier population than the one the boards serve, and a manager can appear qualified in the crawl's own --score output while being invisible on both boards.

reproduction.command: grep -n 'def build_manager_records' src/sharp/records.py src/sharp/platform_records.py; grep -n 'records.build_manager_records' scripts/crawl_sharp_records.py; sed -n '365,378p' src/sharp/records.py; sed -n '44,70p' src/sharp/platform_records.py
reproduction.expected: one builder, or the operator tooling calling the same one the boards call
reproduction.actual: src/sharp/records.py:354 and src/sharp/platform_records.py:72 both define build_manager_records; scripts/crawl_sharp_records.py:77 calls records.build_manager_records() while every board calls platform_records.build_manager_records()

numericProof.formula: |gates(platform_records)| - |gates(records.py)|

findings.userImpact: An operator running the documented `--score` pass sees a cohort that the product does not serve, and will debug the wrong population.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed including the direction: the looser builder is the one in the operator/bootstrap tooling.

findings.whatWorks: scripts/crawl_sharp_activity.py was already migrated onto cohort_members and documents why (its docstring names the exact hazard). crawl_sharp_records.py was not.
findings.rootCause: platform_records was added as the platform-neutral successor to records.py and the older builder was left in place with a live caller.
findings.requiredRepair: Point scripts/crawl_sharp_records.py --score at platform_records.build_manager_records and delete records.build_manager_records, or make it a thin alias.

findings.title: cohort_status re-derives curated FFPC membership with a WEAKER gate than cohort_members, so /api/sharp/cohort can report curated managers - and flip its status to ok - for a cohort both boards treat as empty
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'src/sharp/cohort.py::cohort_members is THE definition of who is a sharp. Every sharp-powered surface resolves its manager pool through it, and none of them may keep a second list or add a qualification rule.' src/sharp/cohort.py docstring: 'there is no second list to keep in sync.'
findings.observed: src/sharp/service.py::cohort_status does not use cohort_members. It recomputes curated membership inline as `curated_members(config) if config.get('allowCuratedInCombinedSignals') else []`, dropping the `ffpc_enabled` conjunct that cohort.py line 221 applies (`curated_enabled = bool(ffpc_enabled and config.get('allowCuratedInCombinedSignals'))`). With enabled=false, allowCuratedInCombinedSignals=true and one verified curated entry, cohort_members returns 0 curated members and coverage.curatedManagers 0, while cohort_status reports cohort.curatedManagers 1, ffpc.curatedContributionEnabled true, and - because `status = STATUS_OK if qualifiedManagers > 0 or curated or provisional` - flips the endpoint's status from cohort_building to ok. /api/sharp/cohort and /api/sharp/market then publish different values under the identical field name cohort.curatedManagers. This is dormant with the shipped config (enabled true, allowCurated false, curatedManagers []) but it is a second membership rule living outside the single definition.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W15/curated_probe.py
reproduction.expected: cohort_members curated count == cohort_status curated count for the same config
reproduction.actual: cohort_coverage_curatedManagers 0 and curatedContributionEnabled false, vs service_cohort_status_curated_count 1 and service_status_would_be 'ok'

numericProof.formula: cohort.py: curated = curated_members(cfg) if (enabled AND allowCurated) else []; service.py: curated = curated_members(cfg) if allowCurated else []

findings.userImpact: With FFPC ingestion switched off for an incident, the cohort endpoint would report the tracker as healthy and name curated managers that contribute to nothing, while both boards stay empty - the exact state an operator would use this endpoint to rule out.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior registry. The prior audit's F14 covers FFPC default-enabled config drift, which is a different claim.

findings.whatWorks: provisional_members carries its own enabled check internally, so the provisional half of the same expression is consistent between the two call sites.
findings.rootCause: cohort_status predates the extraction of cohort.py and was never migrated onto the coverage dict cohort_members already returns.
findings.requiredRepair: Have cohort_status call cohort_members(qualification='all') once and read curatedManagers / provisionalManagers / curatedContributionEnabled straight off the returned coverage dict. That also removes one of the two full population rebuilds per request (W15-F014).

findings.title: Sharp Roster Percentage publishes no per-player manager concentration, so one manager's five teams render as an 83% sharp roster percentage with nothing on the row or the page saying it is one human
findings.claimUnderTest: docs/sharp-roster-percentage/METHODOLOGY.md: 'A sharp with five legitimate dynasty teams contributes five roster observations... Both numbers ship. transparency.eligibleRosters counts rosters; transparency.uniqueSharpManagers collapses linked accounts to humans.' Roster-weighted is stated as the product definition.
findings.observed: Roster-weighted IS stated, and manager collapse IS published - but only at BOARD level. Every row in `players[]` carries sharpRosters, eligibleRosters, sharpRosterPct, slots, buySell, trend and sampleWarning, and NOT a unique-manager count. There is no field on the row, no query parameter and no page column from which a manager-weighted percentage can be derived. Proven on a synthetic cohort of 2 managers / 6 rosters where one manager holds 5 of them: the API returned sharpRosterPct 0.833333 with sharpRosters 5 and eligibleRosters 6 for a player rostered by exactly ONE HUMAN. The row's sampleWarning did not fire (6 >= MIN_PLAYER_DENOMINATOR 5). The board-level tiles do disclose the shape (uniqueSharpManagers 2, eligibleRosters 6, rostersPerManager 3.0), but the number a user reads and acts on is the per-row 83.3%, and nothing ties the two together. The sibling board built from the SAME cohort does not have this gap: src/sharp/market.py publishes uniqueManagers PER ASSET (canonical-manager-collapsed) and feeds manager breadth into signalStrength, i.e. the concentration hazard is guarded on one board and unguarded on the other.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W15/synthetic_ledger_probe.py
reproduction.expected: a per-row unique-manager count, or a manager-weighted percentage available, for a row whose 5 holding rosters belong to 1 manager
reproduction.actual: {"assetId": "4046", "displayName": "Offense Guy", "sharpRosters": 5, "eligibleRosters": 6, "sharpRosterPct": 0.833333} with no uniqueManagers field anywhere in the row

numericProof.formula: roster-weighted = |holding rosters| / |eligible rosters| = 5/6 = 0.8333; manager-weighted = |holding managers| / |eligible managers| = 1/2 = 0.5000

findings.userImpact: On /market/sharp-roster-percentage a user reads '83.3% of sharp rosters hold this player' as broad sharp consensus and buys or holds accordingly, when it can be one manager's portfolio conviction. The page's own footnote warns about league depth, format, cost, age and scarcity but says nothing about manager concentration, and the * small-denominator marker does not fire on this case.

priorFinding.note: The prior registry's sharp findings cover the score and the tracker; none addresses per-player roster concentration on the roster board.

findings.whatWorks: Deduplication is genuinely structural and was proven: a roster handed the same asset twice stored exactly one row per (roster_key, canonical_asset_id) - 5 rosters x 2 duplicate assets produced 5 stored rows. GET /api/sharp/roster-percentage/audit?assetId=... DOES list managerKey for every holding roster, so the information exists behind one extra API call per player; it is simply not on the board or the page.
findings.rootCause: The denominator design correctly focused on which rosters COULD hold a player and never revisited who OWNS those rosters at row level.
findings.requiredRepair: Add uniqueManagers (via cohort.canonical_manager_ids over the holding rosters' manager keys) and eligibleManagers per row, exactly as market.py already does per asset; render it as a column or fold it into sampleWarning when uniqueManagers is small relative to sharpRosters. Optionally expose a manager-weighted sort. Blast radius is zero today only because the cohort is empty; it is a P1 the moment a crawl runs.
findings.dependencies: src/sharp/cohort.py::canonical_manager_ids already exists and is already called at board level in _transparency.

findings.title: /market/sharp-roster-percentage calls its pool 'verified sharp managers' and labels its headline tile SHARP MANAGERS, while the shipped config admits unverified provisional FFPC observers into that pool at weight 0.55 with no breakdown on the page
findings.claimUnderTest: The page header reads 'Which players our verified sharp managers actually roster'. src/sharp/cohort.py documents provisional_members as selecting 'public FFPC observations WITHOUT claiming sharp-v2 qualification', with source rationale 'has not passed Sharp Score v2 history gates'.
findings.observed: config/sharp/ffpc_sources.json ships enabled: true, allowProvisionalPublicInCombinedSignals: true, provisionalPublicWeight: 0.55, and ten enabled seed leagues with allowProvisionalContribution: true. cohort_members therefore admits, by default, any FFPC manager merely OBSERVED in a trade on a configured public page - zero skill evidence - into the pool that both boards read. The live payload confirms the flag is on: /api/sharp/roster-percentage returns cohort.provisionalContributionEnabled true. The tracker page handles this correctly: it shows separate AUTOMATED / CURATED / PROVISIONAL tiles, a qualification filter with four options, a qualificationLabel that changes to 'Provisional public FFPC activity', and a 'Qualification guardrail' note. The roster page renders NONE of it: buildTransparencyTiles emits managers / rosters / sleeper / ffpc / other / coverage / refresh and no qualification breakdown, there is no qualification dropdown among its seven filters so the request is always qualification=all, and the one manager count on screen is labelled 'SHARP MANAGERS'. The payload already carries cohort.automatedQualifiedManagers, curatedManagers and provisionalManagers - the page just does not read them. Blast radius today is 0 rosters because FFPC contributes no rosters at all (METHODOLOGY.md limitation 2), so this is latent until a roster-bearing FFPC URL is configured.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/sharp/roster-percentage' | python3 -m json.tool | grep -E 'provisional|automated|curated'; grep -n 'verified sharp managers' frontend/app/market/sharp-roster-percentage/page.jsx; grep -n 'qualification' frontend/app/market/sharp-roster-percentage/page.jsx
reproduction.expected: the page discloses qualification method, as its sibling does
reproduction.actual: payload has provisionalContributionEnabled true / provisionalManagers; page.jsx line 338 says 'our verified sharp managers' and contains zero occurrences of 'qualification'

numericProof.formula: count of qualification-method disclosures rendered per page

findings.userImpact: Once FFPC rosters are ingested, a user on /market/sharp-roster-percentage reads a percentage described as coming from verified sharps that includes managers the system itself refuses to call qualified, with no way to filter them out from that page.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding says provisional managers sit in the default board under a column labelled 'Sharp managers'. That is REFUTED for /market/sharp-tracker, which discloses the three methods thoroughly and offers a qualification filter, and CONFIRMED for /market/sharp-roster-percentage, which the prior audit's scope did not include.

findings.whatWorks: The backend never conflates the methods: CohortMember.qualification_method is carried through, _QUALIFICATION_PRIORITY resolves a manager arriving by two routes to the strongest claim, and the /api/sharp/cohort note states that curated and provisional members are never represented as sharp-v2 qualifiers.
findings.rootCause: The roster board was built after the tracker and reused the cohort but not the tracker's disclosure surface.
findings.requiredRepair: Add the three qualification tiles and a qualification filter to the roster page (the payload fields already exist), and change the header to 'sharp managers' or 'qualified and observed sharp managers' unless the pool really is automated-only.
findings.dependencies: Latent until METHODOLOGY.md limitation 2 (no roster-bearing FFPC URL) is resolved.

findings.title: Four sharp operations workflows git add a gitignored path, which exits 1 and fails the step; verify-sharp-production.yml therefore fails BEFORE the health check it exists to run
findings.claimUnderTest: Each of these workflows ends by committing a JSON diagnostic under data/ops/ so the sharp production state is recorded in the repo.
findings.observed: .gitignore line 45 ignores `data/`, `git ls-files data/ops/` returns 0 tracked files, and `git add` on a path matching an active ignore rule exits 1 (verified: git 2.43.0, add_exit=1). GitHub Actions runs `run:` steps under `bash -e` by default, and force-sharp-production-now.yml additionally sets `set -Eeuo pipefail` immediately above its add. So the commit step fails in all four. In force-sharp-production-now.yml, trigger-sharp-no-environment.yml and trigger-sharp-now-via-merge.yml the damage is confined to a failed final step. In verify-sharp-production.yml it is worse: the 'Commit production smoke result' step has no `|| true` and sits IMMEDIATELY BEFORE 'Enforce healthy population', which is the only step that reads sharp-production-smoke.json and raises SystemExit when status != healthy. The workflow can therefore never reach its own assertion - it fails on bookkeeping and reports red whether production is healthy or not.

reproduction.command: git ls-files data/ops/ | wc -l; git check-ignore -v data/ops/sharp-production-smoke.json; cd /tmp && rm -rf gitaddtest && mkdir gitaddtest && cd gitaddtest && git init -q . && printf 'data/\n' > .gitignore && mkdir -p data/ops && echo '{}' > data/ops/x.json && git add .gitignore && git add data/ops/x.json; echo "add_exit=$?"
reproduction.expected: 0 (git add succeeds and stages the diagnostic)
reproduction.actual: add_exit=1, with 'The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files: data'; and git ls-files data/ops/ == 0

numericProof.formula: exit code of `git add <ignored path>` without -f

findings.userImpact: An operator using verify-sharp-production.yml to answer 'is the sharp cohort healthy in production' gets a red workflow that never evaluated health, and learns to ignore it.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed, and sharpened: the exit code is 1 (not merely a warning), and the ordering consequence in verify-sharp-production.yml - health enforcement placed after the failing commit - is the part that matters.

findings.whatWorks: The smoke-check python in verify-sharp-production.yml is correct and would work if it were reached; moving the enforcement step above the commit step is a one-line fix.
findings.rootCause: data/ was added to .gitignore; the refresh workflows that write into data/ use `git add -f`, and these four were never updated.
findings.requiredRepair: Use `git add -f`, or drop the commit steps entirely and publish the diagnostics as workflow artifacts. Independently, move 'Enforce healthy population' ABOVE 'Commit production smoke result' so a bookkeeping failure can never mask or preempt the assertion.

findings.title: The five 'kick sharp in prod' workflows are dead operational scaffolding: none is scheduled, four are self-triggering on their own file path, and the real cadence lives entirely in systemd timers
findings.claimUnderTest: Six sharp workflows exist in .github/workflows/; the brief asks whether the five 'kick sharp in prod' ones are dead operational scaffolding.
findings.observed: They are. Not one of the six has a `schedule:` trigger. check-sharp-production-now.yml is workflow_dispatch only. force-sharp-production-now.yml, trigger-sharp-no-environment.yml and trigger-sharp-now-via-merge.yml trigger on `push: branches: [main]` with `paths:` restricted to THEIR OWN yml file - i.e. they only run when somebody edits the workflow that runs them, which is a manual kick dressed as automation. verify-sharp-production.yml triggers on push to main with paths-ignore, so it fires on unrelated commits and then always fails at its git add (W15-F011). sharp-records-bootstrap.yml is workflow_run-chained plus dispatch. Three of the five names encode their own history ('force', 'now', 'no environment gate', 'via merge'). The actual recurring cadence is deploy/systemd: dynasty-sharp-discovery.timer 04:20 UTC, dynasty-sharp-records.timer, dynasty-sharp-rosters.timer, dynasty-sharp-activity.timer 06:30 UTC, dynasty-ffpc-sharp.timer 05:20 UTC - all daily, all installed by deploy/bootstrap-sharp-records.sh and deploy/install-systemd-service.sh, none referenced by any workflow.

reproduction.command: for f in .github/workflows/*sharp*.yml; do echo "== $f"; sed -n '1,12p' "$f"; done | grep -E '^(==|name:|on:|  schedule|  workflow_dispatch|  push|  workflow_run)'; ls deploy/systemd/ | grep sharp
reproduction.expected: at least one scheduled sharp workflow if GitHub Actions is the cadence
reproduction.actual: zero `schedule:` blocks across all six; five daily systemd timer templates under deploy/systemd/

numericProof.formula: count of sharp workflows with a `schedule:` key

findings.userImpact: None directly. The cost is diagnostic: an engineer reading .github/workflows/ concludes the sharp pipeline is CI-driven and looks in the wrong place when it stops producing data.

priorFinding.note: Related to but distinct from the git-add failure: this is about the workflows' trigger design, not their final step.

findings.whatWorks: The systemd timers are well designed and their rationale is documented in-file - dynasty-sharp-discovery.timer.template explains both the cadence and the 04:20 slot choice, and deliberately omits a [Unit] Requires= so a service failure cannot kill the schedule.
findings.rootCause: Incident-response workflows written to force a production restart were committed and never removed.
findings.requiredRepair: Delete the four one-shot kickers, keep verify-sharp-production.yml (fixed per W15-F011), and add a comment in .github/workflows/ pointing at deploy/systemd/ as the real cadence.

findings.title: Waiver and free-agent movements are ingested and stored with their tx_type but no sharp route can reach them: query_movements hardcodes tx_type='trade' with no parameter, so sharp adds/drops exist as data and are Missing as a surface
findings.claimUnderTest: The brief asks whether sharp adds/drops/trades/roster exposure are stored separately, or whether only completed-trade data exists (making the others Missing rather than empty).
findings.observed: Storage is separate and complete: src/intel/ledger.py defines INGESTED_TX_TYPES = (trade, waiver, free_agent), stores all three with tx_type on both `transactions` and `asset_movements`, indexes idx_mv_type_ts on (tx_type, ts), and exposes TRADE_TX_TYPES / WAIVER_TX_TYPES plus a tx_types parameter on its query helpers. The in-file comment states the rule explicitly and names the historical defect it fixes ('the previous aggregator bucketed purely on add/drop and never read txType, so every waiver claim and free-agent pickup was reported to users as a buy'). But the ONLY movement reader any sharp surface uses - src/intel/platform_ledger.py::query_movements - hardcodes "m.tx_type='trade'" as an unconditional clause with no parameter to vary it, and grep shows the sole consumer of WAIVER_TX_TYPES is src/intel/service.py:616, which is the league-scoped Insider Trading product, not Sharp. So: sharp TRADES are implemented; sharp ROSTER EXPOSURE is implemented (the roster-percentage board); sharp ADDS/DROPS as a distinct signal are Missing from every sharp route and page. The buy/sell columns on the tracker are trade-side add/drop, which is correct and not the waiver signal.

reproduction.command: grep -n "tx_type='trade'" src/intel/platform_ledger.py; grep -rn 'WAIVER_TX_TYPES' --include=*.py src/ scripts/ server.py; sed -n '101,121p' src/intel/ledger.py
reproduction.expected: a tx_types parameter on query_movements, or a sharp route exposing waiver activity
reproduction.actual: platform_ledger.py:1630 `"m.tx_type='trade'",` is an unconditional clause; WAIVER_TX_TYPES has exactly one consumer, src/intel/service.py:616, in a different product

numericProof.formula: |tx types reachable through query_movements| / |tx types ingested|

findings.userImpact: A user cannot see what the sharp cohort is claiming off waivers - arguably the higher-signal action, since a waiver claim is unilateral conviction rather than a negotiated trade. The data to answer it is already in the ledger.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior registry.

findings.whatWorks: Excluding waivers from BUY/SELL is correct and deliberately documented; the design decision is sound, only the read path is one-way. The board also never silently mixes them, which is the failure the comment records.
findings.rootCause: query_movements was written for the buy/sell board and the trade filter was pushed down into the query rather than left to the caller.
findings.requiredRepair: Add `tx_types: Sequence[str] = TRADE_TX_TYPES` to query_movements (mirroring the signature ledger.py already uses) and, if the product wants it, an explicitly labelled sharp waiver surface. Do not fold waivers into buy/sell.

findings.title: Both imperatively registered sharp market routes ARE present in the live app, and the described fragility is real but now triple-guarded - the residual risk is a stale OpenAPI schema, not a 404
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'server.py calls _sharp_service.register_http_routes() explicitly after importing the module. The import-time side effect alone is not enough: anything that imports src.sharp.service before the app exists makes it a no-op... /api/sharp/market then 404s with no other symptom.' The shared openapi.json is annotated as the authoritative census because 'grep misses the 2 imperatively-registered sharp routes'.
findings.observed: All five sharp paths are present in the live OpenAPI document, including both imperatively registered ones, and all five 401 anonymously and 200 authenticated. The described failure mode is real but is now guarded three ways: the module-level call at service.py:284, the explicit server.py:12743 call, and a self-heal inside cohort_status (service.py:57) that re-runs the idempotent registrar on every /api/sharp/cohort request. _server_app() also resolves the app under both 'server' and '__main__', which is the production start mode. The two roster-percentage routes were deliberately moved to plain @app.get decorators in server.py precisely because of this ordering hazard, and the docstring at server.py:12772 names the test that exposed it. Residual fragility worth recording: (1) the market handlers are registered without the response models or dependencies a decorated route would carry, and their handlers pass query params positionally into market_payload with no shared validation layer; (2) FastAPI memoizes app.openapi_schema after the first /openapi.json request, so if the cohort self-heal ever DID have to attach the routes at request time, they would work but stay invisible in the schema - a monitoring blind spot; (3) the self-heal only fires on /api/sharp/cohort, and /market/sharp-tracker fetches market and cohort concurrently, so a first market request would still 404 (the page's fetchFreshJson does list 404 as retryable, which is why this is not user-visible).

reproduction.command: python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/openapi.json'));print([p for p in sorted(d['paths']) if 'sharp' in p])"; for r in cohort market market/audit roster-percentage roster-percentage/audit; do printf '%-28s anon=' "$r"; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} auth=' "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/sharp/$r"; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/sharp/$r?assetId=4046"; done
reproduction.expected: all five paths in openapi.json; 401 anon / 200 authenticated on each
reproduction.actual: ['/api/sharp/cohort','/api/sharp/market','/api/sharp/market/audit','/api/sharp/roster-percentage','/api/sharp/roster-percentage/audit']; anon 401 on all five; authenticated 200 on all five

numericProof.formula: |sharp paths in live openapi| == |sharp paths declared in code|

findings.userImpact: None observed. The mitigation is effective.

priorFinding.note: The mechanism the prior audit flagged is confirmed present in the source, but its consequence is REFUTED at runtime: both routes are registered, in the OpenAPI schema, and serving. The prior finding predates the explicit server.py registration and the decorator migration of the roster-percentage routes.

findings.whatWorks: Registration is idempotent (early-returns when /api/sharp/market is already in app.routes), _server_app() handles both import modes, and auth is enforced by middleware so the imperatively added routes are covered identically to decorated ones - verified by the 401s.
findings.rootCause: Historical: routes were added from a module to avoid a second router, which coupled them to import order.
findings.requiredRepair: Optional. Migrating the two market routes to plain @app.get in server.py, exactly as the roster-percentage pair already was, would remove the last of the ordering machinery and the self-heal.

findings.title: cohort_members is genuinely the single membership definition, the five documented qualification gates that CAN fire were each proven firing, and an FFPC name collision cannot mint a false qualification
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: cohort_members is THE definition, no second list anywhere; qualification is documented in config/sharp/scoring_v2.json and enforced in src/sharp/score.py; platform identities are scoped per platform so an FFPC name collision cannot mint a false qualification.
findings.observed: All three verified. (1) SINGLE DEFINITION: every membership consumer resolves through cohort_members - market.py (x3), roster_percentage.py (x2), roster_collect.py, crawl_sharp_activity.py, crawl_ffpc_sharp.py, validate_sharp_roster_percentage.py. Greps for a hardcoded roster of sharps (SHARP_MANAGERS, KNOWN_SHARPS, sharp_list) return nothing; the only configured list is curatedManagers in config/sharp/ffpc_sources.json, which is empty and gated. The one exception found is a COVERAGE recount, not a second member list - see W15-F008. (2) GATES ENFORCED, and they match the config: against a 11-manager synthetic ledger, minWinPct 0.52 rejected a 42.9% manager with the exact message 'win rate 42.9% below the 52.0% floor'; minDynastyLeagues 2 rejected a single-league manager; minCompletedSeasons 2 and minCompletedGames 24 both fired on a one-season manager; and rows with sharp_eligible=0 produced NO ManagerRecord at all. minScorePercentile 0.75 + minConfidence 0.55 then admitted 2 of 7 evaluable (28.6%), consistent with a top-quartile bar. Config and code agree on every threshold I could exercise; the two that cannot fire are W15-F006. (3) IDENTITY COLLISION: FFPC name-only identities are keyed ffpc:league:{league_id}:name:sha256(league_id\0normalized_name)[:16], so 'John Smith' in league L1 and 'John Smith' in league L2 produce DIFFERENT manager_keys (3ebe26c17572a8e9 vs f96f6a4edc691721) while 'John Smith' and 'john  smith' in the same league correctly collapse to one. And a name-only identity cannot reach automated qualification at all: platform_records._row_reasons rejects any row whose source_identity_type != global_verified with reason 'league_scoped_identity'. Injecting a 6-season, 6-championship, 12-2-per-season FFPC name-only manager - a record that would trivially clear every numeric gate - produced ffpc_name_only_automated_qualified: false with reasons ['league_scoped_identity','missing_recent_activity'].

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W15/synthetic_ledger_probe.py; grep -rn 'cohort_members' --include=*.py src/ scripts/ server.py | grep -v 'src/sharp/cohort.py'; grep -rniE 'SHARP_MANAGERS|sharp_list|KNOWN_SHARPS' --include=*.py --include=*.json src/ config/ scripts/
reproduction.expected: all consumers via cohort_members; gates firing with config-matching messages; a name-only FFPC identity denied automated qualification
reproduction.actual: cohort_members resolved at 7 non-definition call sites and no hardcoded list matched; qualification map shows each gate firing with its configured threshold in the message; ffpc_name_only_automated_qualified false

numericProof.formula: win_pct = (wins + 0.5*ties)/(wins+losses+ties) = 18/42 = 0.428571; gate fires iff win_pct < 0.52

findings.userImpact: None - this is the positive result.

priorFinding.note: A verified negative for the 'second list' and 'FFPC collision' hypotheses the brief asked me to test. Also independently confirms the design PRIOR-A16-F14 worries about is at least enforced in code.

findings.whatWorks: Documented above. Two further verified positives on the roster board: the per-player denominator is genuinely per position family and is never the cohort size (an IDP measured 1/1 against IDP-capable rosters while 5 offense-only rosters were correctly excluded from his denominator, and an offense player measured 5/6), and deduplication is enforced by primary key rather than caller discipline (5 rosters each handed the same asset twice stored exactly 5 rows in sharp_roster_assets). The full sharp suite passes: 194 tests, tests/sharp/, python 3.11.15.
findings.rootCause: n/a
findings.requiredRepair: None. Keep the identity-type gate in _row_reasons - it is the load-bearing guard against the collision path.

findings.title: The roster board's empty state tells the user 'the sharp cohort is known' on the same screen as a SHARP MANAGERS tile reading 0, because status cohort_building is emitted for both an empty cohort and an empty roster store
findings.claimUnderTest: frontend/lib/sharp-roster-percentage.js::classifyEmptyState is documented as distinguishing 'the three real states so "we have not collected this yet" never renders as a failure'.
findings.observed: build_board collapses two different states onto one status: `status = 'ok' if filtered else ('cohort_building' if not stored else 'no_eligible_rosters')`. It branches on the ROSTER STORE only, never on the cohort size, so a 0-member cohort and a full cohort with no rosters both emit cohort_building. classifyEmptyState then renders 'Collecting sharp rosters - The sharp cohort is known, but its rosters have not been collected yet. Run the sharp roster crawl to populate this board.' Captured in a real browser today, that sentence sits directly beneath a tile reading SHARP MANAGERS 0 and 'Cohort represented - 0 of 0'. The instruction it gives ('run the sharp roster crawl') is also the wrong remediation: with no cohort, the roster crawl has nobody to crawl, and the correct first step is the discovery + records passes.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W15/page_probe.py
reproduction.expected: an empty state that distinguishes 'no cohort yet' from 'cohort exists, rosters not collected'
reproduction.actual: page renders 'SHARP MANAGERS 0 ... COHORT REPRESENTED - 0 of 0' and 'Collecting sharp rosters / The sharp cohort is known, but its rosters have not been collected yet' simultaneously

numericProof.formula: status = ok if filtered else (cohort_building if not stored else no_eligible_rosters) - has no term for len(members)

findings.userImpact: An operator following the on-screen instruction runs the roster crawl, which does nothing, instead of the discovery and records crawls that actually need to run first.

findings.title: Every GET on a sharp route rebuilds and re-scores the entire manager population from SQL, twice per /api/sharp/market and twice per /api/sharp/cohort, with no memoization anywhere in src/sharp

findings.observed: Instrumented counts of platform_records.build_manager_records (a full SELECT * FROM manager_seasons plus two GROUP BY aggregates, followed by score_managers over the whole population) per request: /api/sharp/market = 2 (market_payload calls cohort_members at line 269 and again at line 362 to build the per-platform coverage breakdown); /api/sharp/cohort = 2 (load_manager_records, then platform_records.coverage() which rebuilds); /api/sharp/roster-percentage = 1. The only lru_cache in src/sharp is on the two small JSON config loaders. The routes set Cache-Control private max-age 120-300 so a repeat browser hit is free, but every cold request and every filter change on either page (each of the roster page's seven dropdowns and the tracker's four re-fetch) pays the full cost, and the 300s auto-refresh timer on the roster page fires unconditionally. findings.title: completed_seasons is a league-season ROW count, so multi-league play inflates longevity and confidence while deflating the activity rate - the exact 'availability is not skill' failure the module says it prevents
findings.claimUnderTest: src/sharp/score.py design rule 1: 'No single weak signal can qualify anyone. Being in many leagues is not skill - it is availability.' config: longevity seasonsForFullCredit 5, activity tradesPerSeasonForFullCredit 6, confidence seasonsHalfCredit 3.0.
findings.observed: platform_records sets completed_seasons = len(seasons) where `seasons` is the list of eligible manager_season ROWS - one per (league, season) pair, not per calendar season. A manager in 3 dynasty leagues across 2 calendar years therefore reports completed_seasons = 6. Three consumers read it as a calendar-season count and all three are distorted in the same direction as league count: _longevity_component (saturating in completed_seasons) is INFLATED, compute_confidence (0.6 * seasons/(seasons+3)) is INFLATED and feeds the hard minConfidence 0.55 bar, _uncertainty_penalty is REDUCED, and _activity_component (trades / completed_seasons) is DEFLATED because trades are counted once per human while the denominator is counted per league. Measured for 3 leagues x 2 calendar seasons vs the same human's true record: longevity 0.7059 vs 0.4444 (+59%), activity 0.3333 vs 1.0 (-67%). The eligibility gate minCompletedSeasons 2 is also satisfiable by ONE calendar season played in two leagues, which is precisely the startup-draft-fallout case config/sharp/scoring_v2.json's minLeagueAgeSeasons comment exists to exclude.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.sharp.score import ManagerRecord,_longevity_component,_activity_component,load_config as L;c=L();k=dict(user_id='x',observed_leagues=3,dynasty_leagues=3,completed_games=84,wins=50,losses=34,trades_completed=12,finish_percentiles=[0.8]*6,days_since_last_activity=10);a=ManagerRecord(completed_seasons=6,**k);b=ManagerRecord(completed_seasons=2,**k);print('longevity',round(_longevity_component(a,c),4),round(_longevity_component(b,c),4));print('activity',round(_activity_component(a,c),4),round(_activity_component(b,c),4))"
reproduction.expected: longevity and activity identical for the same human regardless of how many leagues the seasons are spread over
reproduction.actual: longevity 0.7059 (6 rows) vs 0.4444 (2 calendar seasons); activity 0.3333 vs 1.0

numericProof.formula: longevity = s/(s+2.5); activity = clamp((trades/s)/6, 0, 1). With s=6: 6/8.5=0.7059 and (12/6)/6=0.3333. With the true s=2: 2/4.5=0.4444 and (12/2)/6=1.0

findings.userImpact: A manager who plays many leagues for a short time out-scores a manager with the same results over more years on the longevity and confidence terms, and is simultaneously penalised on activity for the same reason - the score moves on league count in two directions at once.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced with a measured two-way distortion; the prior finding named the mechanism but not the opposing signs or the knock-on to compute_confidence and the minConfidence gate.

findings.whatWorks: playoff_rate and win_pct are internally consistent (both numerator and denominator are per-row), so the performance component is not affected.
findings.rootCause: One SQL result set serves two different questions - how many league-seasons of evidence exist, and how many calendar seasons this human has played.
findings.requiredRepair: Add a distinct calendar-season count (COUNT(DISTINCT season)) to ManagerRecord and use it for longevity, activity and confidence, keeping the row count only where evidence volume is genuinely what is meant. Shares a root cause with W15-F004.

findings.title: Sharp Tracker and Insider Trading are genuinely separate products — separate routes, cohorts, services, pages and nav entries, with no silent cohort reuse in either direction
findings.claimUnderTest: PR #626 split one feature that shipped under two product names into two products: Insider Trading (league-scoped, cohort = your league-mates, no skill filter) and Sharp Tracker (global, cohort = qualified managers).
findings.observed: The split held. `src/intel/` imports NOTHING from `src/sharp/` (grep: zero import lines). The dependency runs one way only — `src/sharp/{cohort,discovery,market,records,record_queue,roster_collect,roster_store,service,platform_records,roster_percentage}.py` import `src.intel.{ledger,platform_ledger,signals,league_filter}`, i.e. the shared ingestion/metric layer named in the docstring, never a product module. The pools are computed by different functions over different evidence: intel's pool is `service._pool_member_ids(state)` = the keys of the snapshot's `members` dict (this league's managers, no filter); sharp's pool is `cohort.cohort_members()` over `platform_records.build_manager_records` + `score.score_managers`. `market.market_payload` filters every query by `manager_keys` from that cohort. Live: `/api/sharp/market` and `/api/sharp/roster-percentage` return 200 `status:"cohort_building"` with a populated `cohort`/`transparency` block; `/api/intel/summary` returns 503 `data_not_ready`. Nav has two distinct entries (`/market/sharp-tracker` under Market, `/league/insider-trading` under League) and the old `/intel` path is a redirect stub. The Insider Trading page subtitle states the cohort explicitly: 'These are the managers in this league, not a skill-filtered cohort.'

findings.title: The ledger's counting rules are correct: multi-team trades, refetches, failed transactions, window overlap and waiver-vs-trade separation all behave as documented under a live numeric probe
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md/src docstrings claim: eventId dedup makes re-ingest a no-op; windows are overlapping lenses never summed; only status=='complete' transactions count; buy/sell counts are TRADES ONLY and waiver/free-agent movements are never inside them.
findings.observed: All four hold when the real `crawler._events_from_tx` + `ledger.ingest_events` + `ledger.asset_signals` are driven with a synthetic transaction set. A 3-team trade (3 players rotating + 2 same-season-same-round picks) produced 10 distinct events with no asset double-counted (each player: buys 1 / sells 1); the two 2027 1sts were kept distinct by the `o<original_roster>` discriminator instead of collapsing. Re-extracting the same transaction with the same seen-set emitted 0 events, and re-ingesting the identical 14-event list inserted 0 movements and 0 transactions. A `status:'failed'` waiver emitted 0 events. FAAB was captured (42) on the waiver ADD only and null on the drop. Trade and waiver queries over the same rows are disjoint: `p1` shows trade buys 1 in the 7d/30d lenses and waiver adds 1 separately, never merged. The 45-day-old trade appears in the 90d lens (p1 buys 2) and not in the 30d lens (p1 buys 1) — the 90d count is a superset, not a sum.

findings.title: GET /api/intel/member/{ownerId} reports tradeCount as the sum of per-asset trade counts, so a single 3-player trade is reported as 3 trades

Each asset row's own tradeCount is a correct COUNT(DISTINCT tx_id) for that asset, but summing across assets counts one transaction once per asset it touched. Runtime: one trade in which uA sends p1+p2 and receives p3 is reported as `tradeCount: 3`.

findings.title: POST /api/intel/refresh is authenticated (session or constant-time bearer) with a per-user cooldown, but any signed-in user can trigger a crawl of EVERY active league
findings.claimUnderTest: 'The refresh + status routes accept EITHER a session cookie or a bearer token ... They are added to the self-authed allowlist so the session-cookie middleware defers to the endpoints' own auth check.'
findings.observed: Verified without POSTing (read-only protocol): anonymous `GET /api/intel/refresh/status` returns 401 auth_required, and a bogus `Authorization: Bearer nope` also returns 401 — so the allowlist entry does not create an anonymous hole. The bearer comparison is `hmac.compare_digest` over UTF-8/surrogateescape bytes (constant-time, and non-ASCII input cannot raise into a 500), rejection logging is rate-limited to one line per 60s and leaks only a length-EQUALITY boolean. Manual triggers carry a 600s per-user cooldown (429 + Retry-After) stamped only after a crawl actually starts; the cron bearer path is exempt by design. The workflow refuses to send the token to a guessed host when PROD_PUBLIC_URL is unset. Residual: authorization is 'any authenticated user', not admin — and `?leagueKey=all` lets any such user start a sequential crawl across every active registry league, i.e. hundreds of budgeted Sleeper calls, once per 10 minutes per account.

findings.title: ROS playoff/championship sims run on the OLDEST loaded season (2024), not the newest — sorted(snapshot.seasons, key=luck._season_sort_key) passes objects to a function typed for strings, so every season sorts equal
findings.claimUnderTest: playoff_sim.py:467 `current_season = seasons_sorted[-1]` and the module docstring ('every unplayed regular-season matchup in the current season') claim the sim operates on the newest season. The prior audit attributed the degenerate odds to 'the last loaded season is complete (offseason)'.
findings.observed: `_season_sort_key(season: str) -> int` does `int(season)` inside try/except (TypeError, ValueError). All four ROS call sites hand it a SeasonSnapshot OBJECT, not `s.season`, so int() raises TypeError and the key is 0 for EVERY season. sorted() is then a stable no-op and `[-1]` returns the LAST element of a newest-first list — the OLDEST season. On the live league (seasons 2026, 2025, 2024) the sims resolve current_season = 2024, status 'complete', 8 owners. The whole 2025 season is loaded and ignored. Every other module in the repo (luck.py:193, power.py:79, weekly_recap.py:613) passes `s.season` correctly; only src/ros/ does not.

findings.title: Weekly DISTRIBUTIONS are modelled (per-player Gaussian draws with the exact lineup re-solved on each draw), but the season sim then collapses each team to a symmetric Gaussian, discarding the right skew best ball creates
findings.claimUnderTest: Workstream question: are weekly distributions modelled, or only mean totals? Best ball is a max-of-distribution product; using means understates it.
findings.observed: Distributions ARE modelled at the player level. The best-ball presim (BEST_BALL_PRESIM_MIN_WEEKS 120 to MAX 1200, adaptive to a 1% relative SE on the mean) draws each player's weekly score from Gaussian(rosValue-derived mean, mean x per-position CV), solves the EXACT optimal lineup on every draw, and takes the empirical (mean, sd) of the resulting team total. That correctly captures the max-of-distribution lift in the FIRST TWO MOMENTS. It is then thrown away: `_simulate_matchup` (championship.py:150-152) and the regular-season loop both draw `rng.gauss(dist.mean, dist.sd)`, a SYMMETRIC distribution. A best-ball team total is right-skewed by construction (it is a maximum over an eligibility structure); modelling it as Gaussian understates the upper tail, which is exactly the region that decides single-elimination brackets. The payload's `bestBallVarianceBump: 1.1` plus a depth-proportional lift is a scalar patch on sd, not a shape correction.

reproduction.actual: {'bestBallVarianceBump': 1.1, 'bestBallVarianceMode': 'depth_aware', 'pointsModelSource': 'fallback-constants'} — sd scaling only; sampling is rng.gauss

numericProof.formula: team weekly score ~ N(mu, sigma) vs the true max-over-eligible-assignments distribution, which has positive skew

findings.title: The 72/18/5/5 team-strength formula is still live, hardcoded, never validated — and its labelled weights are not its actual contributions: coverage and health are stamped 5% each and move the composite by 0.46 and 0.24 points on a 298-point spread
findings.claimUnderTest: The /league ROS Strength tab renders the sentence '72% starting lineup + 18% best-ball depth + 5% positional coverage + 5% health' directly to the user.
findings.observed: The constants are unchanged and hardcoded (the 'can be overridden per-league via settings later' comment is still a TODO). They are coefficients on incommensurable quantities: startingLineupScore is an unbounded sum over 21 slots (live range 446-829), benchDepthScore an unbounded sum over 8 (67-211), while coverage and health are bounded 0-100. Measured on the 12 live teams: starting contributes 93.64% of the mean composite with sd 75.2, depth 4.24% with sd 7.05, coverage 1.04% with sd 0.129, health 1.07% with sd 0.066. Against a composite spread of 298.54 points, coverage moves 0.46 and health 0.24. The two terms the UI advertises as 10% of the answer jointly account for 0.23% of the discrimination between teams. Note this is a scale problem, not a weight problem — power_v2.py does the same kind of blend correctly by converting every input to a percentile first.

findings.title: Not one ROS source supplies a point projection — all 1,285 rows across the five live CSVs have an empty projection column, yet draftSharksRosSf is registered is_projection_source: True
findings.claimUnderTest: src/ros/sources/__init__.py:24 — 'is_projection_source bool — true if source provides per-player point projections', set True for draftSharksRosSf (the highest-weighted source, 1.25).
findings.observed: Every one of the five live source CSVs carries a `projection` column and every row of it is empty: draftSharksRosSf 0/939, fantasyProsRosOverall 0/389, fantasyProsRosSf 0/538, ffc2qbAdp 0/200, fantasyProsRosIdp 0/219. The entire ROS board is therefore a rank blend converted to a 0-100 index by rank_to_score, with no forward-looking point estimate anywhere. That is consistent with src/api/gameplan.py:36-52, which warns downstream consumers that rosValue 'is not points, despite the arithmetic downstream of it' — but the registry flag says the opposite, and it is the flag a reader checks. Two of the five sources are additionally registered source_type 'dynasty_proxy' with is_ros: False (fantasyProsRosSf w0.85, fantasyProsRosIdp w1.05), i.e. multi-year dynasty rankings feeding a rest-of-season product.

reproduction.command: for f in data/ros/sources/*.csv; do .venv/bin/python -c "import csv,sys;r=list(csv.DictReader(open(sys.argv[1])));print(sys.argv[1], len(r), sum(1 for x in r if (x.get('projection') or '').strip()))" $f; done
reproduction.expected: draftSharksRosSf: 939 rows, 939 with projections
reproduction.actual: draftSharksRosSf: 939 rows, 0 with projections (same for all five)

numericProof.formula: sum(rows with non-empty projection) across all registered sources

findings.userImpact: Anyone reading the registry or /api/ros/sources believes the board is projection-backed. It is a rank consensus, and 2 of 5 inputs are dynasty (multi-year) rankings rather than rest-of-season ones. The 'rest-of-season' label on every ROS surface overstates the horizon fidelity of the data.

priorFinding.note: F11 says the board is 23-41% multi-year dynasty rankings with no horizon disclosure — confirmed (2 of 5 sources are source_type dynasty_proxy, is_ros False). This adds the separate, sharper fact that the projection column is empty in 100% of rows across ALL five sources while one of them advertises is_projection_source: True.

findings.whatWorks: The rank-to-score path itself runs and produces a coherent 0-100 index; the honesty problem is in the metadata, not the arithmetic.
findings.rootCause: The flag was declared for a fetcher capability that was never delivered; the CSV schema reserves the column and nothing fills it.
findings.requiredRepair: Set is_projection_source False until a projection feed exists, and surface the dynasty-proxy share on /tools/ros-data-health.

findings.title: scoringProfile is a hand-typed label, not a fact about scoring: dynasty_main and dynasty_new carry the same string while their host scoring differs on 35 of 48 shared keys, so /api/data serves dynasty_main's board verbatim for dynasty_new
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Two leagues that use identical scoring share ONE ranking pipeline and ONE output... 503 data_not_ready only fires when the scoring profiles genuinely differ.' src/api/league_registry.py:480 calls scoringProfile 'the identifier for which set of rules produces this league's player values'.
findings.observed: scoringProfile is an opaque free-text field parsed at league_registry.py:144 and never validated against any scoring_settings. Both registry entries carry "superflex_tep15_ppr1". The live host says the two leagues share only 48 scoring keys and DISAGREE on 35 of them (rec 0.08 vs 1.0, pass_td 6.0 vs 4.0, pass_yd 1/30 vs 1/25, pass_int -4.0 vs -1.0, fum_lost -4.0 vs -2.0, bonus_rec_te 0.0 vs 0.5), plus 48 nonzero keys exist only in dynasty_main (the entire IDP card, first-down bonuses, completion/incompletion scoring, reception-distance bonuses). server.py:3076 compares the two label strings, they match, the 503 never fires, and GET /api/data?leagueKey=dynasty_new returns the dynasty_main board with rankDerivedValue identical on 1092 of 1092 rows. The only test that touches the field (tests/api/test_config_parity.py:199) asserts the string is non-empty and not literally "default".

reproduction.command: bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W18/repro.sh   # section R3
reproduction.expected: either a 503 data_not_ready for dynasty_new, or a board computed under dynasty_new's own 48-key full-PPR non-IDP scoring
reproduction.actual: HTTP 200, identical rankDerivedValue on 1092/1092 rows, meta.scoringProfile "superflex_tep15_ppr1"

numericProof.formula: count(k in shared : main[k] != new[k]) ; count(rows : rankDerivedValue_main == rankDerivedValue_new)

findings.userImpact: A user who switches to 'Blood, Sweat, and Beers' in the LeagueSwitcher sees a full-PPR, no-IDP, 4-pt-passing-TD league priced with a 0.08-PPR IDP superflex board. Every trade value, every rank, every tier on /rankings and /trade is computed under the wrong league's rules, and nothing on the page says so.

blastRadius.note: routesAffected 2 -> 3: add every consumer of the served sleeper block, which carries dynasty_main's scoringSettings/num_teams under dynasty_new's leagueId with sleeperDataReady:true. playersAffected 1092 and pagesAffected 8 confirmed. Partial mitigation not in the original: /rankings hides IDP rows for a non-IDP league (rankings/page.jsx:463-466); /trade does not.

priorFinding.note: Adjacent to PRIOR-A20-F04 (TE++ basis wrong for dynasty_new) but that finding assumes the shared-profile premise; this one refutes the premise itself.

findings.whatWorks: The 503 gate and the leagues_share_scoring helper are correctly wired and would fire if the labels differed; the mechanism is sound and only its input is unverified.
findings.rootCause: scoringProfile is authored by hand in registry.json with no derivation from, or check against, the league's actual scoring_settings. src/league_comparison/sleeper_scoring.py already computes a content hash of a scoring dict (_scoring_hash, sha1[:12]) — the registry does not use it.
findings.requiredRepair: Derive the profile identity from a content hash of the league's live scoring_settings (the mechanism already exists in sleeper_scoring._scoring_hash), or add a startup/CI check that every pair of leagues sharing a scoringProfile has byte-identical scoring_settings. Until then dynasty_new must get its own profile string.
findings.dependencies: Requires one read-only GET per league to api.sleeper.app, which config.py::fetch_live_league already does.

verification.reasoning:
I attacked this from four directions and it survived all four.

(1) The reproduction runs and every number is exact against a live api.sleeper.app fetch today, not a cached snapshot: 141 vs 48 scoring keys, 48 shared, 35 disagreeing, 48 nonzero keys existing only in dynasty_main, and each named example checks out (rec 0.08 vs 1.0, pass_td 6 vs 4, pass_yd 1/30 vs 1/25, pass_int -4 vs -1, fum_lost -4 vs -2, bonus_rec_te 0.0 vs 0.5). GET /api/data?view=app&leagueKey=dynasty_new returns 200 with 1092/1092 identical rankDerivedValue.

(2) The inferential step holds. server.py:3076 compares two label STRINGS (`if loaded_profile and loaded_profile != league_cfg.scoring_profile`), the labels match, the 503 is skipped, and the loaded contract is returned verbatim. src/api/league_registry.py:144 is a bare `str(entry.get("scoringProfile") or "default").strip()` — I grepped src/, scripts/ and tests/ for any validation, hash or cross-check of scoringProfile against scoring_settings and found none. The only test on the field (tests/api/test_config_parity.py:200 test_every_league_has_non_empty_scoring_profile) asserts non-empty, exactly as stated.

(3) The path is live and user-reachable: /api/leagues returns both leagues, dynasty_new is active:true with idpEnabled:false, and LeagueSwitcher.jsx renders it.

(4) Not a harness artifact: nothing here depends on absent data/, the suppressed scrape, or an unreachable host — I fetched the host successfully.

My own probing makes the finding WORSE, not narrower, which is why I am upholding rather than rescoping downward. Two additions worth carrying into the writeup. First, the `sleeper` block served for dynasty_new is a chimera: sleeper.leagueId is correctly 1320092771247222784, but sleeper.scoringSettings.rec is 0.08 and idp_sack 2.92 and leagueSettings.num_teams is 12 — all dynasty_MAIN's values — while meta.sleeperDataReady is stamped TRUE. Per CLAUDE.md that flag means 'the sleeper block is valid for the REQUESTED league', so it is affirmatively lying here; the honest stamp for this state is sleeperDataReady:false. Second, 770 of 1092 rows carry an idpRank and defenders sit high on the board served to a league whose 27 roster slots contain zero IDP positions (Aidan Hutchinson at consensus rank 36, Myles Garrett 82). /rankings does filter assetClass==="idp" at display (frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:463-466), so that one surface is partially mitigated — but the ranks it shows are backend stamps from a pool that included IDP (so the ladder has holes) and the values were percentile-normalized against that pool, and /trade applies no such filter.

One irony that sharpens the root cause rather than weakening it: the label 'superflex_tep15_ppr1' is factually wrong for dynasty_main itself — main is rec 0.08 with bonus_rec_te 0.0, i.e. neither ppr1 nor TE-premium — and factually right for dynasty_new (rec 1.0, bonus_rec_te 0.5). The string describes neither league correctly, which is the finding's thesis stated as strongly as it can be.

P1 is honest and I am not escalating. The board is a blend of externally published market rankings, not a board scored from league settings, so 'computed under the wrong league's rules' is true of the format axes (IDP inclusion, TE basis) and of nothing that is literally arithmetic on scoring keys. That distinction is what keeps it off P0.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: Settled. If anyone wants to press further, the remaining open question is whether the chimeric sleeper block (main's scoringSettings under new's leagueId, stamped sleeperDataReady:true) should be split out as its own finding — it is a distinct defect from the scoringProfile label and has its own repair.

findings.title: The cross-league Sleeper overlay stamps sleeperDataReady:true on a chimeric block — dynasty_new's real teams welded to dynasty_main's scoringSettings, rosterPositions and num_teams — which un-gates every team-dependent page
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md contract annotations: 'meta.sleeperDataReady — true iff sleeper block is valid for the *requested* league; false when the server served the shared rankings but doesn't have the requested league's rosters loaded' and 'meta.sleeperLoadedLeagueKey — which league the sleeper block *would* be for, when sleeperDataReady: false (diagnostic only)'.
findings.observed: On the sleeper_matches=False branch, server.py:3244-3256 carries positions / playerIds / idToPlayer / scoringSettings / rosterPositions / leagueSettings forward from the LOADED league and lays the requested league's overlay (teams, trades, waivers) on top, then unconditionally sets meta.sleeperDataReady = True at :3259. GET /api/data?view=app&leagueKey=dynasty_new returns sleeperDataReady:true AND sleeperLoadedLeagueKey:"dynasty_main" simultaneously — a combination the documented contract says cannot occur. The block reports leagueId 1320092771247222784 and 10 real teams (correct) alongside num_teams 12, 58 roster slots and dynasty_main's 141-key IDP scoring card (all wrong; the real league is 10 teams, 27 slots, 48 keys, no IDP). useTeam.js:84-94 reads the flag: true -> leagueMismatch false -> the data-not-ready state that exists precisely for this case never renders.

reproduction.command: bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W18/repro.sh   # section R3
reproduction.expected: sleeperDataReady:false (per the documented contract) OR a sleeper block whose scoringSettings/rosterPositions/leagueSettings belong to dynasty_new
reproduction.actual: sleeperDataReady:true with num_teams 12, 58 roster slots, rec 0.08 and idp_sack 2.92 — dynasty_main's values under dynasty_new's leagueId and leagueName

numericProof.formula: count(setting : value_served_for_dynasty_new != value_on_host)

findings.userImpact: On /trade, /waivers and /rosters under dynasty_new the starter/bench split comes from sleeper.rosterPositions (frontend/lib/portfolio-insights.js:105), so the user is shown a 21-slot IDP lineup with 3 DL / 3 LB / 3 DB / 1 K starting slots for a league that has none of those positions, plus 37 bench slots for a 17-bench league — and the 'no roster data yet' banner that would have prevented all of it is suppressed.

blastRadius.playersAffectedDetail: no player value is affected; the shared board is correct by scoringProfile design. The wrong artifact is league config: 144 of 164 compared settings, of which only rosterPositions (21 served starter slots vs 10 real) has a live consumer
blastRadius.note: pages cut from 5 to 2 — /trade and /waivers read only sleeper.teams, which the overlay supplies correctly; routes raised from 2 to 4 — three more handlers rebuild the same hybrid

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A19-F20 and PRIOR-A21-F05 report the same class (hardcoded league context leaking across leagues) in ROS/public-league; this is the contract-level source those inherit from.

findings.whatWorks: The no-overlay fallback path directly below (server.py:3288-3298) does it correctly: it nulls the sleeper block and sets sleeperDataReady:false. The defect is only on the overlay-succeeded branch.
findings.rootCause: The overlay merge treats 'we fetched the requested league's rosters' as equivalent to 'the sleeper block is valid for the requested league', but the overlay only supplies teams/trades/waivers — scoringSettings, rosterPositions and leagueSettings are never overlaid and silently retain the loaded league's values.
findings.requiredRepair: On the sleeper_matches=False branch, either drop scoringSettings/rosterPositions/leagueSettings from the carried-forward key list (leaving them absent rather than wrong) and keep sleeperDataReady:false, or fetch the requested league's own config in the overlay so the block is genuinely that league's. Do not stamp sleeperDataReady:true unless every field in the block belongs to the requested league.
findings.dependencies: W18-F001 — with a correct scoringProfile this path would 503 before reaching the overlay.

verification.reasoning: The core observation is exactly right and reproduces; the impact story around it does not. WHAT SURVIVES: server.py:3241-3253 carries positions/playerIds/idToPlayer/scoringSettings/rosterPositions/leagueSettings forward from the LOADED league and then unconditionally stamps meta['sleeperDataReady']=True at :3259, so /api/data?leagueKey=dynasty_new returns sleeperDataReady:true AND sleeperLoadedLeagueKey:'dynasty_main' together — the combination CLAUDE.md's contract annotations say cannot occur. The chimera is real and I verified it against the live Sleeper host, not the repo snapshot: dynasty_new is genuinely 10 teams / 27 slots / 48 scoring keys / rec 1.0 / no idp_sack, and the served block is 12 / 58 / 141 / 0.08 / 2.92. dynasty_new is active:true and idpEnabled:false in config/leagues/registry.json, so it is user-selectable. lineupSlots() on the served array yields 21 starter slots including 3 DL / 3 LB / 3 DB / 1 K for a league with none of those positions, versus 10 real — the finding's number, confirmed. WHAT DIES: (a) 'un-gates every team-dependent page' is the wrong frame. On /trade (page.jsx:182) and /waivers (page.jsx:620) the ONLY sleeper field read is `teams`, which the overlay supplies correctly for dynasty_new. On those two pages sleeperDataReady:true is the CORRECT answer — the whole point of the cross-league overlay is to make them work — and forcing false there would delete working multi-league functionality to satisfy a doc table. The defect is not the flag being true; it is that the flag certifies fields that were never overlaid. (b) The cited userImpact chain is misattributed: portfolio-insights.js:105 is imported by terminal/PortfolioSummary.jsx and terminal/ScoutingIntel.jsx and by nothing else. /trade and /waivers never touch it. The wrong 21-slot IDP lineup lands on /rosters (page.jsx:61 feeds buildRosterAnalysis + scoreTeamTiers) and /terminal. (c) blastRadius.playersAffected:1092 is not defensible — not one player value is wrong here. The board is shared across leagues on the same scoringProfile BY DESIGN, and the finding itself does not dispute the values. Zero players are mispriced; what is wrong is league CONFIG. (d) scoringSettings and leagueSettings have NO frontend consumer at all (verified by grep across frontend/ for scoringSettings/num_teams/numTeams — zero hits on the sleeper block), so 128 of the 144 mismatched settings are inert on the /api/data path. WHAT I FOUND THAT BROADENS IT: the identical carry-forward-then-stamp-true pattern is duplicated in three more handlers — /api/terminal (server.py:10577-10586), /api/trade/simulate (:10798-10804) and /api/signal-alerts/run (:11653-11659) — so routesAffected is 4, not 2, and the trade-simulate one runs server-side where the frontend grep cannot see it. src/bdvm/league_config.py:194-196 also reads all three fields, but from latest_contract_data rather than the per-request hybrid, so it is a separate leak, not this one. P1 is correct and I am leaving it there: a reachable page (/rosters, /terminal) shows a materially wrong starter/bench split for dynasty_new, but no traded value is misquoted and the wrong lineup is visibly absurd (K and IDP slots in a league with neither) rather than plausibly wrong.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: Settled. The remaining judgement call is the repair: the finding's option 'keep sleeperDataReady:false' would regress /trade and /waivers under dynasty_new, which work correctly today off the overlay's teams. The correct repair is the finding's other option — drop scoringSettings/rosterPositions/leagueSettings from the carried-forward key list at server.py:3243-3253 (and the three duplicates) so they are ABSENT rather than wrong, letting portfolio-insights fall to rung two of its own truth ladder, the registry's rosterSettings.starters, which is already correct for dynasty_new.

findings.title: src/nfl_data/realized_points.py disagrees with the league host on 36% of player-weeks: it never reads the six reception-distance rules, maps pass_int/pass_sack/fum_lost to nflverse columns that no longer exist, and has no kicker scoring at all
findings.claimUnderTest: src/league_comparison/scoring_engine.py:6 — 'compute_weekly_points ... is already the single source of truth for Sleeper-format fantasy scoring'. CLAUDE.md — BDVM's baseline is 'realized nflverse PPG under the league's exact scoring'.
findings.observed: Scored 636 real 2025 player-weeks (nflverse rows) against the same 636 Sleeper host stat lines under the SAME live dynasty_main scoring_settings. Only 406 (63.8%) agree within 0.011. Three independent causes, each confirmed by decomposing individual players: (1) rec_0_4/rec_5_9/rec_10_19/rec_20_29/rec_30_39/rec_40p appear in neither _SIMPLE_KEYS nor the threshold-bonus list, costing 157.03 points across 197 rows — Stefon Diggs 2025 wk5 exact 30.100 vs realized 23.400, delta -6.700 = 0.34+4.02+2.34 exactly. (2) _SIMPLE_KEYS maps pass_int->'interceptions', pass_sack->'sacks', fum_lost->'fumbles_lost'; the 2025 unified nflverse release names them passing_interceptions, sacks_suffered and fumbles_lost_total, so stat_row.get returns None -> _num -> 0.0 and the key is skipped. Patrick Mahomes wk14 exact 0.823 vs realized 14.823, delta exactly +14.000 = 3 INT x 4.00 + 2 sacks x 1.00. Across the sample these three penalties are worth 208 points that are never charged. (3) No kicker key is read at all (fgm_yds 0.07, xpm 2.31, xpmiss -3.15, six fgmiss_* bands) although K is a starting slot; every kicker scores 0.000 (33/33 rows wrong, mean -9.251). Per-group agreement: IDP 312/350 (89.1%, mean -0.034 — this path is essentially correct), other 66/71, WR 11/64, TE 10/48, RB 4/32, QB 3/38 (mean +6.533), K 0/33 (mean -9.251).

reproduction.command: bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W18/repro.sh   # section R5
reproduction.expected: 636/636 agree within 0.011 (the tolerance src/league_intel/scorer.py's own docstring sets)
reproduction.actual: 406/636 agree; QB mean +6.533, K mean -9.251, WR mean -1.558

inputs.reference: src/league_intel/scorer.score_stat_line, itself validated 1339/1339 vs Sleeper players_points

numericProof.formula: delta = compute_weekly_points(nflverse_row) - score_stat_line(sleeper_stat_line); agreement = count(|delta| <= 0.011)

findings.userImpact: The direction is systematic, not random: QBs are over-scored by ~6.5 pts/week and pass-catchers under-scored by 0.8-1.6 pts/week, so any fundamental value built on this engine tilts the board toward QBs and away from WR/TE/RB. On /rankings the 'Fund gap' column and on /bdvm the entire value board are derived from it; on /league-comparison the positional-balance verdict a user reads to decide whether their league over-pays QBs is computed from the engine that over-pays QBs.

blastRadius.playersAffected: every player-week scored by compute_weekly_points; 636 is the measured sample, 230 of which disagreed
blastRadius.note: Verified live in this container: GET /api/league-comparison (all four seasons 2022-2025) and GET /api/player/{sleeper_id}/realized. /api/bdvm/values|roster|trades return status 'no_projection_snapshot' (data/bdvm absent — pre-declared Blocked by data); the engine defect would reach them in production, where the weekly dynasty-bdvm-refresh timer writes the snapshot. Per-cause scope: dead column mappings -> /api/league-comparison + BDVM(prod) + /api/player/*/realized, ALL seasons, no warning anywhere; reception bands -> same routes but /api/league-comparison DISCLOSES them in .warnings; missing kicker family -> /api/player/*/realized only (K is excluded by league_comparison/scoring_engine.py::_canonical_position and by bdvm/service.py:61).

priorFinding.note: Confirms the reception-band half exactly (6 rules, WR most affected) and extends it with two causes that audit did not report: three dead nflverse column mappings worth +208 pts of uncharged QB penalties, and the complete absence of kicker scoring in a league that starts a K. Also partially confirms PRIOR-A24-F19 and refutes the implication in PRIOR-A22-F02 that IDP is the broken half — measured, IDP is the ONE group this engine gets right.

findings.whatWorks: The IDP path is correct and well-defended: the _SCORING_KEY_ALIASES derivation from sleeper_ingest.KEY_ALIASES resolves idp_pass_def->idp_pd and idp_qb_hit->idp_hit, _tackle_view reconstructs gamebook solo from the post-2025 columns, and the group agrees with the host at 89.1% with mean signed error -0.034.
findings.rootCause: realized_points is an allow-list engine keyed on nflverse column names, in a codebase that also contains a scoring-key-agnostic dot-product engine (src/league_intel/scorer.py) that is provably exact. The allow-list silently degrades in two ways — a live scoring rule with no entry, and an entry whose column was renamed — and _num(None) -> 0.0 makes both indistinguishable from 'the player did nothing'.
findings.requiredRepair: Add rec_0_4..rec_40p (nflverse publishes no reception-depth split, so they must come from src/nfl_data/reception_depth.py or be reported as uncovered, not silently zero); repoint pass_int/pass_sack/fum_lost at passing_interceptions/sacks_suffered/fumbles_lost_total via the existing candidate-tuple mechanism; add the kicker family. Structurally: make the engine assert that every NONZERO key in the league's scoring_settings is either mapped or explicitly declared uncoverable, and surface the uncovered set on the payload (src/nfl_data/scoring_coverage.py already exists for this and is not consulted at scoring time).
findings.dependencies: None. src/nfl_data/scoring_coverage.py already enumerates the gap.

verification.reasoning:
The reproduction is exact to the digit — 406/636 (63.8%), QB +6.533, K -9.251, WR -1.558, IDP 89.1%/-0.034. All three causes verified independently. But the three causes do NOT share a scope, and the finding presents them as one blast radius. Rescoped, with one half strengthened and one half cut.

STRENGTHENED — cause 2 (dead column mappings). realized_points.py:85-88 maps pass_int->'interceptions', pass_sack->'sacks', fum_lost->'fumbles_lost'; none of those three names exists in the nflverse column list, the real names are passing_interceptions / sacks_suffered / fumbles_lost_total, and all three rules are live and nonzero (-4.0 / -1.0 / -4.0). My ablation proves the attribution: repointing just those three columns cuts the QB signed error from +6.533 to +1.269, 81% of the bias. Two things the finding did not report make this WORSE than stated. (a) It is not a 2025 regression — I checked a 2022 row and it also carries passing_interceptions/sacks_suffered/fumbles_lost_total, so every season /api/league-comparison serves (2022-2025, meta.seasonsSources all 'nflverse') has inflated QB totals, not just the current one. (b) src/nfl_data/scoring_coverage.py — the module the finding proposes as the structural fix — classifies all three keys as 'scored'. The coverage auditor is fooled by the same dead mapping, so no warning is emitted for them anywhere. That is the genuinely silent, genuinely dangerous half, and it poisons exactly the number /league-comparison exists to produce: the QB positional baseline a user reads to decide whether their league over-pays QBs.

RESCOPED DOWN — cause 1 (reception bands). The arithmetic is right (six live rules 0.17-1.92/event, absent from realized_points.py entirely), but 'no warning shown' is false on the one demonstrably-live route. GET /api/league-comparison returns a `warnings` array that names rec_0_4, rec_5_9, rec_10_19, rec_20_29, rec_30_39 and rec_40p explicitly and says 'realized points for affected players are understated'. scoring_coverage IS consulted at payload time on this route, contrary to the finding's requiredRepair note; what it is not consulted at is scoring time.

CUT — cause 3 (no kicker scoring). It reaches none of the four non-realized routes the finding lists. src/league_comparison/scoring_engine.py::_canonical_position returns None for K (the module comment at :26 says 'Positions we report on (offense + IDP). Anything else (kickers...)'), and the live payload's positions are exactly ['QB','RB','TE','WR']. src/bdvm/service.py:61 _UNSUPPORTED_POSITIONS = {'K','PK','DEF','DST'} and :439-442 emits kickers as unpriced 'unsupported_position'. So no kicker row ever reaches either consumer. scoring_coverage additionally classifies xpm/xpmiss/fgm_yds as 'not_applicable' rather than uncovered — a deliberate scope decision, not an oversight. The residual defect is narrow but real: compute_weekly_points returns 0.000 for a kicker instead of declining, so the ONE route that would surface it (/api/player/{id}/realized) would show a normal-looking zero.

BLAST RADIUS. playersAffected 636 is the verifier's SAMPLE (3 weeks x matched players), not a population — recount it as 'every player-week this engine scores'. routesAffected 5 overstates what is testable here: /api/league-comparison is confirmed live and returns real 2022-2025 baselines; /api/bdvm/* x3 return status 'no_projection_snapshot' in this container (pre-declared Blocked by data — the engine defect is real in production but unverifiable here); /api/player/{id}/realized answers 200 with reason 'unmapped_player'.

Priority P1 upheld. The QB half is a wrong number, on a page a user can reach today, with no warning covering its cause, feeding the exact verdict the page sells. It is not P0 only because the page does render a prominent warnings block — about different keys — which a user will read as the coverage disclosure.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: For the BDVM leg, which is the largest claimed consumer and is unverifiable here: place a projection snapshot under data/bdvm/projections/ and diff /api/bdvm/values with the three column mappings repointed vs not, to measure how far the QB tilt propagates into fundamental value after replacement-level normalization — the +6.5/wk raw bias may compress substantially once every QB is over-scored together and the QB replacement level rises with it. For /api/league-comparison the question is already settled: recompute the 2022-2025 QB baselines with the repointed columns and the published 325.02/328.33 figures will fall.

findings.title: ADR-006's 'pure dot product, no stacking rules' claim independently reproduced against 1,339 host-scored player-weeks (max |delta| 0.005), and stacking answered on real host stat lines: pick-six charges -6.00, distance bonuses stack on the base reception, and one sack pays eight IDP categories
findings.claimUnderTest: src/league_intel/scorer.py:3-25 — 'a pure dot product over the keys shared between a player's weekly stat line and the league's scoring_settings ... No exclusions, no de-duplication, no special-casing ... reproduced Sleeper's own players_points exactly (|delta| <= 0.011) for 1,415 of 1,415 rostered player-weeks.'
findings.observed: Reproduced independently, not inherited. Fetched the 2025 predecessor league (owner-28c60701dbd5) with its own scoring_settings plus GET /v1/league/.../matchups/{5,9,14} for host-awarded players_points and GET /v1/stats/nfl/regular/2025/{5,9,14} for the raw stat lines. score_stat_line reproduces the host on 1,339 of 1,339 player-weeks with max |delta| = 0.005, inside the module's own 0.011 tolerance. Stacking, answered from host stat lines rather than from docs: (1) PICK-SIX STACKS — the host emits pass_int and pass_int_td on the same line (3 real cases, e.g. player 4046 wk5: pass_int 1.0, pass_int_td 1.0), so under 2026 rates a pick-six costs -4.00 AND -2.00 = -6.00. (2) RECEPTION-DISTANCE BONUSES STACK ON THE BASE RECEPTION — the buckets partition the receptions (rec_0_4 + rec_5_9 + rec_10_19 + rec_20_29 + rec_30_39 + rec_40p == rec) and are paid in addition to rec x 0.08; an 8-catch line at 1/3/3/0/1/0 scores 0.64 + 4.61 = 5.25 before yardage. (3) ONE SACK PAYS EVERYTHING APPLICABLE — 194 host lines carry idp_sack together with idp_sack_yd, idp_tkl_solo, idp_tkl_ast, idp_tkl_loss, idp_qb_hit and often idp_ff / idp_fum_rec. Worked case (player 4967, wk5, 2026 rates): ff 4.25 + fum_rec 3.19 + qb_hit 2.13 + sack 2.92 + sack_yd 1.111 + tkl_ast 0.80 + tkl_loss 4.25 + tkl_solo 1.33 = 19.981. The host also emits idp_tkl (combined), which carries no rate in this league, so solo+assist are not double-counted — a league that DID set idp_tkl would triple-count, and that would be Sleeper's behaviour too.

reproduction.actual: 1,339 player-weeks, max |delta| = 0.0050
