findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md 'Non-Negotiable Rules' #6 — 'Call out anything mocked, bypassed, stale, duplicated, half-wired, dead, or missing'. A verdict is an assertion about a trade; with no trade there is nothing to assert.
findings.observed: On a freshly-loaded /trade with 'No assets yet.' under both sides, Side A = 0 and Side B = 0, the sticky verdict bar renders 'Near even' with 'Gap 0' and a green-to-red gradient meter positioned at centre. verdictFromGap(gap) has no empty-trade guard: `if (Math.abs(gap) < VERDICT_NEAR_EVEN) return "Near even"` matches gap === 0 exactly as it matches a genuinely balanced trade. The two states — 'these two packages are close in value' and 'you have not built a trade' — render identically.

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/w26_shots.py docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26   # inspect trade-mobile.png
reproduction.expected: an empty trade shows no verdict
reproduction.actual: 'Side A 0 / No assets yet.' above a sticky bar reading 'SIDE A 0 — Near even — Gap 0 — SIDE B 0'

numericProof.formula: verdictFromGap(0) = 'Near even' because Math.abs(0) < VERDICT_NEAR_EVEN, with no guard on sideA.length + sideB.length === 0

findings.userImpact: Low in isolation — nobody acts on an empty trade. It matters as a pattern: the same unguarded verdict function is what renders during the ~1 s window while the contract is still loading, so a shared trade link can flash 'Near even' before either side has been priced.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A02-F00 concerns the DIRECTION of the trade verdict (which side the meter calls the winner). This is the degenerate-input case and is independent.

findings.whatWorks: The empty-list copy itself is good — 'No assets yet.' and 'Search to add to Side A…' are clear. The problem is only that the verdict bar does not respect them.
findings.rootCause: verdictFromGap is a pure function of the gap and has no notion of an empty package; its caller renders unconditionally.
findings.requiredRepair: Return null from verdictFromGap (or gate the sticky bar) when both sides are empty, and render a neutral 'Add assets to both sides' state.

findings.title: DESIGN/A11Y — /rosters position-breakdown bars fail WCAG contrast at 2.19:1 in 53 places, and colour is the ONLY encoding for every segment too narrow to hold its label

codeRefs.lines: n/a — measured from the rendered DOM

findings.claimUnderTest: design-taste-director SKILL.md product fit — 'data-dense but readable', 'mobile-friendly', 'credible for power users'. WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 (contrast 4.5:1 for text under 18.66px bold / 24px) and SC 1.4.1 (colour is not the only visual means of conveying information).
findings.observed: Computed from the live DOM at both 1366px and 390px: 53 text nodes on /rosters fall below their required contrast ratio, of 332 sampled. The worst and most numerous are the stacked-bar segment labels — white (#ffffff) on the PICKS orange rgb(243,156,18) at 2.19:1 against a required 4.5:1, rendered at 8.96px. The same treatment covers 'PICKS 158k', 'PICKS 38k', 'PICKS 28k' and so on across all 12 team rows, plus the 'PICKS' filter chip at 12.16px. Separately: a segment only receives an inline label when it is wide enough; narrower segments (RB/TE/DL/LB/DB on most rows) render as bare coloured blocks whose ONLY identification is hue, against a 7-colour legend in which DL and LB are both purple-family and DB is teal. A user who cannot distinguish those hues cannot read those values at all — there is no tooltip, no pattern and no text alternative on the narrow segments.

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/w26_probe.py /tmp/o.json && python3 -c "import json;[print(r['route'],r['viewport'],r['dom']['contrastFailCount'],r['dom']['contrastWorst'][:3]) for r in json.load(open('/tmp/o.json')) if r['dom'].get('contrastFailCount')]"
reproduction.expected: contrastFailCount 0
reproduction.actual: /rosters desktop 53/332 and /rosters mobile 53/329, worst ratio 2.19 (white on rgb(243,156,18), 8.96px)

numericProof.formula: ratio = (L_light + 0.05)/(L_dark + 0.05) with relative luminance per WCAG 2.1; required 4.5 for text below 18.66px

findings.userImpact: A power user scanning twelve rosters for positional imbalance — the page's entire purpose — cannot reliably read the segment values in bright light or on a phone, and cannot read the narrow segments at all without colour vision.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A03-F09 concerns the /rosters age-curve METHOD. No prior finding covers contrast or colour-only encoding anywhere in the product.

findings.whatWorks: Contrast across the rest of the app is genuinely good — 12 of the 14 pages probed returned zero contrast failures at both widths. The dark palette is well constructed. (My probe also flagged one node on /league-comparison at 1.02:1, the 'Recalculate' button; the screenshot shows it rendering as a legible light chip, so I treat that single hit as a false positive of my background-walk heuristic and exclude it from the count above.)
findings.rootCause: The bar palette was chosen for hue separation, not for contrast against white label text, and the label-visibility rule is width-driven with no fallback.
findings.requiredRepair: Darken the orange to ~#a8620a (white on it reaches 4.9:1) or switch those labels to near-black — the amber family is the only one in the palette that white fails against. For the narrow segments, add a per-segment title/aria-label carrying 'POS value', and add a hover/tap readout so hue is never load-bearing. Reducing the seven-hue palette to four plus texture would also address the DL/LB/DB confusion the design-taste rubric warns about.

findings.title: DESIGN — the 1-9,999 value scale is disclosed ONLY through hover tooltips (1,933 title attributes on /rankings) and appears in no visible text, so it is unreachable on every touch device
findings.claimUnderTest: design-taste-director SKILL.md — outcomes should be 'mobile-friendly' and 'credible for power users'. CLAUDE.md's Live Value Pipeline defines a 'Common 0-9999 internal value scale', so the number 9,988 on screen is meaningless without it.
findings.observed: The /rankings board renders VALUE as '9,988', '9,876', '9,706' with no unit and no scale on screen. The only statement of the scale is `title={`Hill-curve value ${val} (scale 1–9,999) — click for the per-source breakdown`}` on the value cell, and a second in the per-source column header info. A DOM scan of the rendered page for the string '9,999' / '9999' in visible body text returns FALSE at both 1366px and 390px. The page carries 1,933 title attributes — the disclosure layer for essentially every number on the board is hover-only. `title` never fires on touch, so on the 390px layout the scale, the meaning of the 'S+' badge beside each value, and the '14/15' sources ratio are all undiscoverable. Comparable hover-only counts elsewhere: /draft 838, /rosters 185.

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/w26_shots.py docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26 ; python3 -c "import json;[print(r['route'],r['viewport'],r['hoverOnly']['titleCount'],r['hoverOnly']['scaleStatedInVisibleText']) for r in json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/focus-hover-report.json'))]"
reproduction.expected: the scale appears in visible text on any page that prints a value
reproduction.actual: /rankings desktop titleTooltips=1933 scaleVisible=False ; /rankings mobile titleTooltips=1933 scaleVisible=False ; /draft 838 False ; /rosters 185 False

numericProof.formula: discoverability on touch = (visible-text disclosures) / (total disclosures); here 0/1933 for the value scale

findings.userImpact: On a phone, a user reads '9,988' next to Josh Allen and '8,383' next to Joe Burrow and has no way to learn whether the gap is large or small, whether the ceiling is 9,999 or unbounded, or what unit either number is in. On /rosters the same scale is summed into a team total of '328,504' with no unit anywhere. This is the single largest comprehension gap in the product and it is invisible to desktop testing.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A01-F06 concerns the methodology panel publishing a formula that is not the live curve — a correctness problem in the explainer. This is the separate problem that the explainer is unreachable on touch at all.

findings.whatWorks: The DESKTOP disclosure is genuinely thorough — the tooltip text is precise ('Hill-curve value N (scale 1–9,999)'), the per-source header distinguishes value-signal from rank-signal sources, and the board carries a 'How rankings work' link, a 'Methodology charts' link and an honest 'Derived from source agreement data — not predictions' caption. The rankings table also has a full <caption> and scope on all 10 <th> — the best table semantics in the app.
findings.rootCause: Disclosure was implemented as `title` attributes, which are a desktop-only affordance, and no equivalent was added for the mobile layout.
findings.requiredRepair: Put the scale in visible text once per board — a column subhead ('VALUE / 1–9,999') costs nothing and removes the ambiguity permanently. Replace load-bearing `title` attributes with a tap-and-hold or info-chip pattern on mobile, and give the 'S+' badge and the sources ratio a visible legend. Also note the DOM weight: 1,933 title attributes on one page is itself a parse and memory cost.

findings.title: A11Y FUNCTIONAL — /draft has 102 unlabelled form inputs and /settings has 4 (including two range sliders that change the board), and three of the app's four data tables have no th[scope], caption or aria-label

codeRefs.lines: n/a — .draft-inline-input / .draft-money-input, measured from the rendered DOM
n/a — measured from the rendered DOM

findings.claimUnderTest: WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2 (name, role, value) and SC 1.3.1 (info and relationships). The rankings board proves the codebase already knows how to do both — it ships a <caption> and scope on all 10 <th>.
findings.observed: Measured from the live DOM at both widths.  UNLABELLED CONTROLS (no text content, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby, no title, no <label for>, not wrapped in a <label>): /draft = 102, all of them `input.draft-inline-input` and `input.draft-money-input` — the per-pick team-name and dollar fields inside a 73-row auction table. A screen-reader user hears 'edit text' 102 times with nothing identifying which pick or team each belongs to. /settings = 4: two `input[type=number]` and two `input[type=range]`. The two sliders are the source-weight / TEP controls, i.e. unlabelled controls that change every value on the board.  TABLE SEMANTICS: /draft (73 rows, 14 <th>) has thScope 0, no caption, no aria-label. /settings' three tables (16/7/6 rows, 6/6/5 <th>) all have thScope 0, no caption, no aria-label. /rosters (13 rows, 4 <th>) same. Only /rankings and /finder (231 rows, 10 <th>) have scope on every header plus a caption.

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/w26_probe.py /tmp/o.json && python3 -c "import json;[print(r['viewport'],r['route'],'unlabelled',r['dom']['unlabelledCount'],'tables',r['dom']['tables']) for r in json.load(open('/tmp/o.json')) if r['dom'].get('unlabelledCount') or r['dom'].get('tables')]"
reproduction.expected: unlabelledCount 0; every data table has scoped headers and an accessible name
reproduction.actual: /draft unlabelled 102, table thScope 0/14, caption false ; /settings unlabelled 4, three tables all thScope 0 ; /rosters thScope 0/4 ; /rankings thScope 10/10 caption true

numericProof.formula: tablesFailing = tablesTotal - tablesWithScopedHeaders

findings.userImpact: A screen-reader user cannot operate the live auction board at all — 102 identical unnamed text fields inside an unlabelled 73-row grid gives no way to know which pick is being edited. On /settings the same user can move two sliders with no idea what they control, and those sliders re-rank the entire board.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding in the 531-item index addresses form labelling or table semantics.

findings.whatWorks: The app-wide accessibility baseline is better than most: every one of the 14 pages probed has lang="en", exactly one <h1>, a <main> landmark, a working skip-link, and zero images missing alt (188 player headshots on /rankings, all with alt). PlayerImage.jsx additionally sets loading="lazy" and decoding="async" with a three-stage graceful fallback. /rankings and /finder are a model for the other tables. Zero horizontal page overflow at 390px on all 14 pages, with every wide table correctly wrapped in an overflow-x:auto container.
findings.rootCause: The rankings table was built with semantics in mind; the later tables and the draft board's inline editors were not, and there is no lint rule or test asserting the invariant.
findings.requiredRepair: Add aria-label to each draft inline input naming its pick and field ('Pick 1.05 team', 'Pick 1.05 dollars'), add scope="col" to every <th> and a <caption> (or aria-label) to the /draft, /settings and /rosters tables, and add visible <label> elements to the two /settings sliders and two number inputs. Then add an eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y rule so the invariant is enforced rather than re-audited.

findings.title: DESIGN/MOBILE — at 390px the trade calculator's sticky verdict bar is clipped by a floating action button, /draft's teams panel refuses to stack, and /rankings' edge-summary chips truncate to unusable stubs

codeRefs.lines: n/a — sticky verdict bar, measured from a 390x844 render
n/a — 'Teams & budgets' panel, measured from a 390x844 render
n/a — Edge summary chips, measured from a 390x844 render

findings.claimUnderTest: design-taste-director SKILL.md — 'strengthen thumb-zone controls and persistent actions on mobile', 'data-dense but readable'. CLAUDE.md Performance Rules — 'Prioritize page-load speed and perceived responsiveness'.
findings.observed: Three distinct 390px defects, each captured in a screenshot.  (1) /trade: the sticky bottom verdict bar renders 'SIDE A / 0 / [meter] / Near even / Gap 0 / SID' — Side B's label is cut to 'SID' and its number is overlapped by a floating circular action button anchored bottom-right. The bar is the calculator's primary readout and half of it is unreadable.  (2) /draft: the 'Teams & budgets' panel lays out a heading column beside a full-width 'Load from Draft Capital' button and does not stack; the description wraps one or two words per line ('Budgets pre-' / 'fill from' / 'the live' / 'Draft' / 'Capital'), producing a five-line ragged column ~90px wide.  (3) /rankings: the Edge summary cards clip their content to '#244 E…' / 'Sell +…' / '#202 De…' / 'Sell…' — the player is unidentifiable and the magnitude is gone, so the panel conveys only that a signal exists. The 'FLAGGED — NEEDS CAUTION' heading is itself cut mid-word by the same floating button.  None of these produces page-level horizontal overflow (documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth on all 14 pages, which is why a scroll-based check misses them entirely).

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/w26_shots.py docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26   # inspect trade-mobile.png, draft-mobile.png, rankings-mobile.png
reproduction.expected: no clipped labels or single-word wrap columns at 390px
reproduction.actual: trade-mobile.png shows 'SID' + occluded Side B total; draft-mobile.png shows a 5-line single-word column; rankings-mobile.png shows '#244 E…' / 'Sell +…'

numericProof.formula: page-level scrollWidth > clientWidth detects 0 of these 3 defects, because each clips WITHIN a fixed-position or flex container rather than overflowing the document

findings.userImpact: On /trade the user cannot read what the other side of their own trade is worth — on the surface most likely to be used on a phone, mid-negotiation. On /rankings the edge summary, which exists to name buy and sell candidates, names none of them.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding addresses mobile layout.

findings.whatWorks: The mobile shell is otherwise strong and clearly deliberate: a five-item bottom tab bar (Home/Ranks/Trade/News/Menu) in the thumb zone, zero horizontal page overflow on all 14 pages at 390px, every wide table wrapped in its own overflow-x:auto container so the page body never scrolls sideways, and the /rankings board correctly reflows from a 1,278px table to a 578px one. The stat-tile grid reflows cleanly to two columns.
findings.rootCause: The floating action button is positioned over the sticky bar's right edge with no reserved gutter; the /draft panel uses a row flex with no stacking breakpoint; the edge chips use fixed-width truncation rather than reflowing to two lines.
findings.requiredRepair: Reserve right padding on the sticky trade bar equal to the FAB's footprint (or move the FAB above the bar); add a flex-direction:column breakpoint below ~520px to the /draft teams panel; let the edge-summary chips wrap to two lines on narrow viewports so the player name and the magnitude both survive.

findings.title: A11Y — 8 of the first 22 keyboard tab stops on /draft have no visible focus indicator (no outline, no box-shadow); /trade has 3 and /rosters 2

codeRefs.lines: n/a — no :focus-visible rule reaches these controls

findings.claimUnderTest: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.7 (focus visible). The rest of the app passes, so this is a gap rather than an absent system.
findings.observed: Walking Tab 22 times from document start and reading getComputedStyle on document.activeElement at each stop: /draft at 390px has 8 stops where outlineStyle begins 'none' AND boxShadow is empty or 'none'; /trade at 390px has 3; /rosters at 1366px has 2. The same walk on /rankings (both widths), /draft at 1366px, /league-comparison and / returns 0 — so the default focus treatment does exist and works, and these are controls that override it. Focus ORDER itself was sane on every page walked: no stop landed on a zero-size or off-screen element.

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/w26_shots.py docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26 ; python3 -c "import json;[print(r['route'],r['viewport'],r['noFocusRing'],'/22') for r in json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/focus-hover-report.json'))]"
reproduction.expected: 0 /22 on every page
reproduction.actual: /draft mobile 8/22 ; /trade mobile 3/22 ; /rosters desktop 2/22 ; every other combination 0/22

numericProof.formula: a stop fails when getComputedStyle(el).outlineStyle starts with 'none' and boxShadow is empty or 'none'

findings.userImpact: A keyboard-only user tabbing through the live draft board loses track of where they are 8 times in the first 22 stops — on the page where a mistaken keystroke costs a draft pick.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers keyboard focus. Rated medium because my detector only reads outline and box-shadow; a control indicating focus purely via a background-colour change would be a false positive here.

findings.whatWorks: Focus order is correct everywhere walked, the skip-link is present and first on all 14 pages, and 5 of the 8 page/viewport combinations walked have a visible ring on all 22 stops.
findings.rootCause: Specific controls (draft inline inputs, trade chips) reset outline without substituting an equivalent indicator.
findings.requiredRepair: Add a global `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }` that these components do not override, and remove the local outline:none resets.

findings.title: A11Y/MOBILE — 873 of 900 interactive targets on /rankings at 390px are under 44px, and type as small as 9.0px ships on three pages

codeRefs.lines: n/a — row-level interactive cells, measured from a 390x844 render

findings.claimUnderTest: design-taste-director SKILL.md — 'strengthen thumb-zone controls and persistent actions on mobile'. WCAG 2.1 SC 2.5.5 (Target Size, AAA) sets 44x44 CSS px; SC 2.5.8 (AA, 2.2) sets 24x24 as the floor.
findings.observed: Measured on visible, non-zero-size interactive elements (a[href], button, input, select, textarea, role=button/tab/link, tabindex>=0) at 390x844: /rankings 873 small of 900 total, /finder 873 of 900, /draft 373 of 475, /settings 39 of 126, /rosters 31 of 63. At 1366px the counts are similar (/rankings 891 of 900), so this is a row-density decision rather than a responsive-layout failure. The bulk on /rankings and /finder is the per-row player/value/source cells, which are clickable (they open the popup and the per-source breakdown) but sized for information density. Separately, computed font sizes below 11px appear on /rankings (9.0, 9.2, 9.3, 9.9, 10.6, 10.9), /finder (same set), /rosters (9.0, 9.3, 9.6, 9.9), /settings (9.3, 10.2, 10.6, 10.9) and /league (9.9, 10.2, 10.4, 10.6, 10.9) — 9.0px on a 390px phone.

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W26/w26_probe.py /tmp/o.json && python3 -c "import json;[print(r['viewport'],r['route'],r['dom']['smallTargetCount'],'/',r['dom']['interactiveCount'],r['dom']['tinyFontSizes']) for r in json.load(open('/tmp/o.json')) if r['viewport']=='mobile']"
reproduction.expected: interactive targets >= 44px in at least one dimension; no type below 11px
reproduction.actual: /rankings mobile 873/900 small, tinyFonts [10.6, 10.9, 9, 9.2, 9.3, 9.9]

numericProof.formula: smallTargetFraction = smallTargets / interactiveTotal

findings.userImpact: Tapping a specific player row on a phone is error-prone, and the 9px metadata (team, age, spread) is at the edge of legibility on a 390px screen for anyone without perfect near vision.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers touch targets or type scale.

findings.whatWorks: The pages that are NOT dense tables get this right: /terminal 4 small of 26, /bdvm 7 of 29, /waivers 9 of 31, /market/sharp-roster-percentage 11 of 33. The bottom tab bar targets are correctly sized. So the small-target problem is confined to the board rows and is a deliberate density trade, not an oversight everywhere.
findings.rootCause: The rankings row is a desktop-density table reflowed to mobile without a distinct mobile row treatment, so every cell keeps its desktop height.
findings.requiredRepair: This is the one finding here where the fix is a design decision, not a bug fix. Recommendation, per the design-taste rubric: give /rankings a distinct mobile row — a two-line card at ~56px with rank+name+position on line one and value+confidence+edge on line two, one tap target per row instead of eight, and raise the metadata type floor to 11px. That is a deliberate density reduction, so it should be a stated decision rather than a silent change; keep the current dense table available behind the existing 'Columns' control for power users.

findings.title: _LEAGUE_CONTEXT_CACHE is a single global slot with no league key, so every league's rookie-anchor roster count and TE bonus come from the default league
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md 'Rule for new code' — 'Need rosters / teams / matchups? -> resolve via leagueKey. One pipeline per league. Never collapse.' roster_count is a per-league property (team count) and bonus_rec_te is a per-league scoring property.
findings.observed: `_LEAGUE_CONTEXT_CACHE = {"context": None, "fetched_at": 0.0}` is a single-slot dict with a 1-hour TTL and NO league dimension. `_resolve_league_context()` takes no league argument at all — it resolves the id via `league_registry.get_sleeper_league_id()`, which returns the DEFAULT league, then caches the result globally. Any second league on the same scoring profile with a different team count or TE bonus reads the default league's numbers from this cache. The cache is also read-before-write with the fetch outside any lock, so concurrent cold misses each hit Sleeper.

reproduction.command: grep -n '_LEAGUE_CONTEXT_CACHE' -A6 src/api/data_contract.py | sed -n '1,12p' ; grep -n 'def _resolve_league_context' -A3 src/api/data_contract.py
reproduction.expected: cache keyed by league (or by scoring profile, with the league-specific parts excluded)
reproduction.actual: _LEAGUE_CONTEXT_CACHE = {'context': None, 'fetched_at': 0.0} ; def _resolve_league_context(default_roster_count=...) — no league parameter

numericProof.formula: distinct values servable = cacheSlots = 1, while distinct correct values required = leaguesInRegistry

findings.userImpact: Only realised on a multi-league deployment where the two leagues differ in team count or TE premium; today both live leagues share scoring_profile superflex_tep15_ppr1, so the observable impact is latent. Reported because the audit brief asks explicitly whether each cache key includes the league key, and this one does not.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A20-F03 found a related shape in gameplan — 'scoringFit and receptionFit are measured against a Sleeper league that is not in the registry, then cached per league key as if they were'. Same family (a league-scoped quantity cached without the right key), different module. Rated medium because the impact is latent on the current single-scoring-profile registry.

findings.whatWorks: The function's degradation path is correct and well documented — a fallback dict with fetched_from_sleeper: False is returned on any failure rather than raising, so the pipeline produces output offline, and the flag makes the fallback visible to callers. By contrast, the caches that DO get keying right are numerous: _OVERRIDES_RESPONSE_CACHE keys on (body hash, view, leagueKey, sleeper_matches) and deliberately refuses to cache the leagueAdjusted path at all; _OVERLAY_RESPONSE_CACHE keys on (kind, leagueKey, loadedLeague, view, sleeper_matches) with the freshness stamp inside the value; gameplan's _BUNDLE_CACHE keys on league_key plus a source stamp rather than a clock; _DRAFT_CAPITAL_CACHE keys on league key.
findings.rootCause: The function predates multi-league support and was never given a league parameter when the registry landed.
findings.requiredRepair: Give _resolve_league_context a league_key parameter and key the cache dict on it, defaulting to the registry default so existing callers are unaffected.

findings.title: Three documented payload/page claims are measurably wrong: '~4 MB uncompressed' (is 11.95 MB), '~90% byte reduction' (is 38%), and 'frontend/app/ ... terminal/' (the directory does not exist and /terminal is a 404)
findings.claimUnderTest: (1) CLAUDE.md: 'view=full (default, backward-compat): returns the full canonical contract (~4 MB uncompressed...)'. (2) server.py:3126-3128 and frontend/app/api/dynasty-data/route.js:45: compact is a '~90% byte reduction' / '~90% smaller'. (3) CLAUDE.md directory listing: 'frontend/ ... app/ # rankings/, trade/, draft/, bdvm/, waivers/, terminal/, news/, settings/, login/'.
findings.observed: (1) The full contract measures 11,953,535 bytes uncompressed — 2.99x the documented ~4 MB. (2) compact measures 7,363,760 bytes against full's 11,953,535, a 38.4% reduction, not 90%; and it is 13.0% LARGER than the view desktop requests (see W26-F001). (3) `ls frontend/app/terminal` returns 'No such file or directory'; the directory listing shows no terminal entry; grep finds no link to '/terminal' anywhere in frontend source. Loading http://127.0.0.1:3000/terminal in a browser renders the app shell around Next's 'This page could not be found.' — and still downloads 12,481,320 decoded bytes of player contract to do it (see W26-F002). The /api/terminal ENDPOINT is live and is correctly consumed by the home page, so only the page claim is false.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -o /dev/null -w 'full=%{size_download}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data ; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -o /dev/null -w 'compact=%{size_download}\n' 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data?view=compact' ; ls frontend/app/terminal
reproduction.expected: full ~4000000 ; compact ~1195000 (90% reduction) ; frontend/app/terminal exists
reproduction.actual: full=11953535 ; compact=7363760 ; ls: cannot access 'frontend/app/terminal': No such file or directory

numericProof.formula: reductionPct = 100 * (1 - measuredCompactBytes / measuredFullBytes) ; fullRatio = measuredFullBytes / (documentedFullMB * 1e6)

findings.userImpact: None directly on a user. It matters because the '~90%' figure is the stated justification for routing mobile devices to that view, and it is what makes W26-F001 look like a non-problem to a reader of the code.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A10-F09 established the pattern ('CLAUDE.md declares defect D-2 resolved while the code it cites says the opposite'). These are three further instances. The '~4 MB' figure and the compact-vs-app inversion were both pre-noted in evidence/perf/api-data-payload-sizes.txt; this finding supplies the mechanism and the third instance.

findings.whatWorks: The vast majority of CLAUDE.md's technical claims that I tested held up, including the scoring-profile vs leagueKey split, the ETag/304 behaviour, the single-flight design of the overlay and overrides caches, the /league public-data exemption in AppShell, and the fact that view=array carries no legacy players dict.
findings.rootCause: The figures were written before the contract grew and were never re-measured; the terminal page was removed or renamed without updating the directory listing.
findings.requiredRepair: Re-measure and correct the three figures. If /terminal is meant to exist, note that /api/terminal is live and consumed by the home page, so only the page is missing; otherwise remove it from the directory listing.

findings.title: The /rankings Edge column and its buy/sell filter carry no signal for any of the 398 IDP rows, while /edge labels the same players BUY/SELL from a second, parallel detector
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md presents IDP as a first-class asset class on the blended board, and /edge advertises a market-gap BUY/SELL system. edge-helpers.js/marketAction is documented as 'Always rendered with an explicit state — never an ambiguous dash' (frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:1164).
findings.observed: _retail_source_keys() returns exactly {'ktcSfTep'}, and KTC publishes no IDP. _compute_market_gap therefore short-circuits to ('none', None) whenever retail_ranks is empty, which is every IDP row: the whole-board census is DL 145/145, LB 114/114, DB 139/139 = 398/398 marketGapDirection=='none'. In the browser (request-interception topology per AUDIT_PROTOCOL) all 43 IDP rows on /rankings page 1 render EDGE '—' while offense rows render BUY/SELL/HOLD. The advanced filter edge=buy|sell tests the same field, so it returns zero IDP rows by construction. Meanwhile /edge runs a SECOND detector, idpMarketAction(), anchored on idpTradeCalc, and renders 10 IDP SELL rows + 4 IDP BUY rows for players that /rankings shows as '—'. Abdul Carter (board #82), Micah Parsons (#80), Jared Verse (#84), Myles Garrett (#81), Caleb Downs (#145) are SELL on /edge and blank on /rankings; Nick Bolton (#112), Edgerrin Cooper (#102), Jordyn Brooks (#135), Fred Warner (#141) are BUY on /edge and blank on /rankings.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data -o /tmp/w27.json && python3 -c "import json,collections;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w27.json'));c=collections.Counter((r['position'],r.get('marketGapDirection')) for r in d['playersArray']);print({k:v for k,v in c.items() if k[0] in ('DL','LB','DB')})"
reproduction.expected: IDP rows carry retail_premium/consensus_premium like offense rows, or the UI states the exclusion per position
reproduction.actual: {('DL','none'):145, ('LB','none'):114, ('DB','none'):139} — 398/398. Browser DOM: 43/43 IDP rows show EDGE '—'.

numericProof.formula: marketGapDirection = 'none' iff retail_ranks == [] ; retail_ranks = [r for k,r in effectiveSourceRanks if k in {'ktcSfTep'}]

findings.userImpact: A manager scanning /rankings for buy-low / sell-high candidates sees a blank Edge cell on every defender and concludes no IDP edge exists, in a league that starts 9 IDP of 21 slots. Filtering /rankings by 'Buy edge' silently drops 36% of the board. The same manager on /edge is told Micah Parsons is a SELL. Two pages, one concept, opposite answers, no reconciliation shown.

priorFinding.note: A05-F17 criticises the SCALE of the /edge IDP comparison (ladder-translated ranks averaged against an untranslated anchor). This finding is about a different half: that the /rankings Edge column and edge filter have no IDP path at all, and disagree with /edge about whether an IDP signal exists. Not a paraphrase — A05-F17 assumes the IDP detector is the only one; the contradiction between the two detectors is unrecorded.

findings.whatWorks: /edge's IDP panels do compute and render an IDP buy/sell using idpTradeCalc as the anchor, and marketEdge()'s tooltip on /rankings honestly says 'No KTC rank for this player'. The refusal is honest at the field level; it is the two-surface contradiction that is not.
findings.rootCause: 'Retail market' is defined as a single registry flag (is_retail) held by exactly one offense-only source. The gap detector was written for that one board and never generalised to a per-market anchor the way finder.py's gate was (src/trade/finder.py:538 IDP_MARKET_KEYS). /edge worked around it with a private duplicate instead of fixing the contract field.
findings.requiredRepair: Make _compute_market_gap per-market — anchor IDP rows on idpTradeCalc the way src/trade/finder.py already anchors IDP assets — and stamp which market produced the direction (marketGapMarket). Then delete idpMarketAction/idpMarketEdge and let /edge read the contract stamp, so one definition serves both pages.
findings.dependencies: Interacts with W27-F005: the same rank-space comparison is basis-blind for TE. Fixing the anchor without fixing the basis leaves the TE monoculture intact.

findings.title: Trade suggestions cannot propose a defensive back to anyone — the top-150 board gate contains zero DBs — yet /trade tells all 12 teams to 'target DB' while every team already rosters 5-9 of them against a 3-DB requirement
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md and src/trade/suggestions.py:230-238 both assert the BOARD_TOP_N_FILTER gate ranks against 'our own blended board, which answers asset quality directly and for every asset class, including IDP and picks that no single retail board covers', and that sharing finder.py's gate 'would reintroduce the offense-only blind spot F-3 just removed'.
findings.observed: build_asset_pool_from_contract(contract) returns exactly 150 assets: WR 41, QB 28, RB 26, PICK 23, TE 18, DL 7, LB 7, DB 0. The first DB in the full 812-row pool is Caleb Downs at board rank 167 (display_value 3159 against a board maximum of 9988). A single global top-N on a board where offense tops out at 9999 and the best defender sits near 6400 is exactly the failure mode finder.py:578-583 documents and fixes with a per-market cut — suggestions.py never got that fix. Consequence measured across all 12 rosters: 51 suggestion assets total, of which DL 5 and LB 11 and DB 0, and rosterAnalysis.needPositions contains 'DB' for 12 of 12 teams. Actual DB depth per team from sleeper.positions: Jason 8, Ed 5, Ty 7, Collin 7, MaKayla 7, Eric 8, Roy 6, Joey 8, Brent 9, Kich 7, jstuedle 5, Blaine 8 — against 3 mandatory DB starters. The engine reports a shortage at the one position no team has a shortage at, because starterCounts only counts pool members and no DB is ever in the pool.

reproduction.command: python3 -c "import json,sys,collections;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.trade.suggestions import build_asset_pool_from_contract as B;c=json.load(open('/tmp/w27.json'));print(collections.Counter(a.position for a in B(c)));full=B(c,board_top_n=0);print([(i,a.name,a.display_value) for i,a in enumerate(full,1) if a.position=='DB'][:1])"
reproduction.expected: The pool contains DBs proportionate to a lineup that starts 3 of them (per-market cut, as finder.py does)
reproduction.actual: Counter({'WR':41,'QB':28,'RB':26,'PICK':23,'TE':18,'DL':7,'LB':7}) — DB absent; first DB at pool rank 167

numericProof.formula: idp_share_of_pool = (DL+LB+DB)/150 = 14/150 = 9.33% vs idp_share_of_starting_lineup = 9/21 = 42.86%

findings.userImpact: On /trade, the Trade Suggestions panel renders a red 'Should target DB' badge (trade-sections.jsx:1099-1103) to every manager in the league. Acting on it means spending real trade capital acquiring a defensive back at a position where the manager already has 167%-300% of the starters needed — and the engine can never actually offer one, so the advice is unfollowable as well as wrong. No warning is shown that the candidate pool has no DBs in it.

blastRadius.playersAffectedNote: 96 DBs, 100% excluded from the suggestion pool; 279 IDP rows excluded in total (DL 108 + LB 75 + DB 96) out of an 812-row pool

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A14-F00/F01 describe the identical failure class in finder.py (offense-only pool) and are refuted at HEAD — see W27-F010. The twin defect in suggestions.py is unrecorded, and the code comment at suggestions.py:230-238 explicitly asserts the opposite.

findings.whatWorks: DL and LB do reach the pool (7 each) and do appear in suggestions (16 of 51 assets across 12 teams). starter_needs_for_league correctly derives {DL:3, LB:3, DB:3} from the league's roster_positions. The failure is confined to the quality gate, not to IDP awareness in general.
findings.rootCause: BOARD_TOP_N_FILTER is a single global cut over a value scale that is not comparable across asset classes: offense peaks at 9999, IDP at ~6400 and DB at 3159. finder.py identified this and ranks each market's own population from 1; suggestions.py kept the global cut and documented it as safe on the untested premise that 'our own blended board covers every asset class'.
findings.requiredRepair: Apply the top-N cut per position family (or per asset class) in _apply_board_top_n_filter, mirroring finder.py's market_groups. Separately, rosterAnalysis.starterCounts must count the manager's WHOLE roster, not only pool members, or needPositions must be suppressed for any family with zero pool coverage and say so.
findings.dependencies: Requires no data change; purely an engine-side gate change. Interacts with W27-F007 (hybrid eligibility) for how DL/LB counts are attributed.

verification.reasoning:
The reproduction re-runs exactly (one correction: it needs GET /api/data, not ?view=app, which carries no playersArray and returns an empty pool). The defect is real and unfixed at HEAD: src/trade/suggestions.py:698 `_apply_board_top_n_filter` is a single global cut on `board_rank` with no per-family handling, so 0 of 96 DBs survive while src/trade/finder.py:579-583 documents this exact failure mode ('a single global top-150 removes every IDP player (WS-J F-3)') and fixes it per-market. The in-code comment at suggestions.py:229-238 asserting the blended board 'answers directly and for every asset class, including IDP' is contradicted by its own output. needPositions contains 'DB' for 12/12 teams; the badge markup at frontend/app/trade/trade-sections.jsx:1097-1103 renders it as a negative Badge. All confirmed.

P0 fails three of the protocol's own tests, so this is rescoped to P1, not overturned:
(1) 'no warning shown' is false. The SAME panel, 20 lines above the badge (trade-sections.jsx:1074-1081), renders `{totalSuggestions} suggestions · {rosterMatched}/{rosterCount} matched` — '6 suggestions · 16/57 matched' for Jason, '3/44' for jstuedle. That is a rendered disclosure that the analysis covers a minority of the roster. It does not name the DB blind spot, which is why the finding survives at all, but it defeats the P0 'no warning' clause.
(2) 'a user acts on a wrong number' is not met. Every number a trade is actually priced on is correct — the sellHigh/buyLow cards read `rankDerivedValue` and their arithmetic is untouched. The wrong output is an advisory label. Furthermore src/trade/suggestions.py:281 documents `starter_counts` as `# above-replacement count`, not a raw roster count. Under the engine's own definition 'you have zero above-replacement DBs' is literally TRUE for all 12 teams. The finding's inferential step — from 'no DB in pool' to 'the engine reports a shortage that does not exist' — silently substitutes raw-count semantics the code never claimed. What is genuinely defective is narrower and still worth fixing: because 'above replacement' is operationalised as 'top-150 OVERALL on a scale where DB peaks at 3159 against a board max of 9988', the DB need is structurally permanent, identical for every team, and unsatisfiable by the engine that raised it — a signal that can never turn off carries no information. Note the same is largely true of DL (need for 10/12) and LB (11/12), which the finding treats as working.
(3) blastRadius playersAffected:139 is not derivable from anything I could recount. The pool holds 96 DBs and excludes all 96; total IDP excluded is 279 (DL 115-7=108, LB 82-7=75, DB 96-0=96). 139 matches neither.
Minor: numericProof.startingSlots=21 is wrong — live metadata.starterNeeds sums to 20, so the IDP lineup share is 9/20 = 45.0%, not 42.86%. Direction and conclusion unchanged.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: Change _apply_board_top_n_filter to cut per position family (mirroring finder.py's market_groups at finder.py:583-599) and re-run the 12-roster sweep: DB should enter the pool and needPositions should stop containing 'DB' for teams that roster startable DBs. Separately, decide the semantics question the finding papers over — if starter_counts is meant to stay an above-replacement count, the fix is to suppress or footnote needPositions for any family with zero pool coverage, not to switch it to a raw roster count.

findings.title: The /angle page can never return an IDP player in a counter-package: the engine defaults include_idp=False and the page never sends the flag
findings.claimUnderTest: server.py's /api/angle/packages docstring says 'Market value is per-position: IDPTradeCalc for IDP (DL/LB/DB), KTC for everyone else', and the /angle page's own hint reads 'KTC for offense, IDPTC for IDP' — presenting the page as IDP-aware.
findings.observed: src/trade/angle.py:711 and :1216 both drop every IDP row from the candidate pool unless include_idp is true, justified in-code by 'most leaguemates don't gravitate toward them'. server.py:6526 defaults includeIdp to False. `grep -rn includeIdp frontend/` returns zero hits — frontend/app/angle/page.jsx:318-334 builds its body from mode/ownerId/playerNames/minMyGainPct/maxMarketGainPct/targetTeamOwnerIds/leagueKey only, and there is no UI control anywhere. Live A/B on the same request: includeIdp=false returns 10 candidates whose 18 assets are QB 10, WR 5, TE 2, RB 1 (zero IDP); includeIdp=true returns 13 candidates including 3 LB. The selected/offer side accepts IDP fine (an all-LB offer prices correctly on idpTradeCalc), so the exclusion is one-directional: you may give defenders, you may never be offered one.

reproduction.command: for v in false true; do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/angle/packages -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"ownerId\":\"owner-8b8a59adf44e\",\"playerNames\":[\"Justin Jefferson\"],\"limit\":50,\"includeIdp\":$v}" | python3 -c "import json,sys,collections;d=json.load(sys.stdin);c=collections.Counter(p['position'] for x in d['candidates'] for p in x['players']);print(len(d['candidates']),dict(c))"; done
reproduction.expected: Both runs return IDP counter-assets in a 9-IDP-starter league, or the page exposes the toggle

numericProof.formula: idp_assets_returned_on_the_live_UI_path = 0 because include_idp = bool(body.get('includeIdp', False)) and the page never sets it

findings.userImpact: A manager using the Package Builder to shop an offense piece is shown a return market that contains no defenders, in a league where 9 of 21 starting slots are defensive. Thirty percent of the plausible counter-packages (3 of 13 here) are withheld with no indication they were filtered, so the manager concludes no defensive return exists and either accepts a worse offense package or walks away from a fair trade.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers the include_idp default or its absence from the frontend body.

findings.whatWorks: The offer side handles IDP correctly: an all-LB offer is priced on idpTradeCalc, carries market_uncertainty_band 1859 (16.8% of the total) and two explicit market_warnings naming the assumed offense<->IDP exchange rate. The exclusion is a candidate-pool filter, not a valuation failure.
findings.rootCause: A deliberate default ('most leaguemates don't gravitate toward IDP') encoded as an engine-side hard filter rather than a user-visible preference, in a codebase where the only two live leagues on this scoring profile include one that starts 9 IDP. The parameter exists and works; nothing reachable sets it.
findings.requiredRepair: Derive the default from the league's roster_positions (idpEnabled / IDP starter count) rather than a constant, and add an 'Include IDP' toggle to /angle that sends includeIdp. Cheapest correct fix: default include_idp to True whenever league_cfg's roster settings contain any DL/LB/DB/IDP_FLEX slot.
findings.dependencies: None; the flag already threads server.py:6561/6603 into both angle entry points.

findings.title: /api/angle/find applies a +/-5% cross-market plausibility gate that is narrower than the two boards' own measured p10-p90 disagreement, and stamps no uncertainty band
findings.claimUnderTest: src/trade/angle.py:68-69 excuses find_angles from the cross-market machinery: 'find_angles (the 1-for-1 pivot) is untouched: it compares two single assets, so there is no cross-market sum to constrain.'
findings.observed: There is no SUM, but there is still a cross-market SUBTRACTION, and the visibility gate is applied to it. Selecting an IDP player returns a candidate list that is 37 of 38 cross-market: the selected player's market_value comes from idpTradeCalc and the candidates' from ktcSfTep. With the default maxMarketGainPct=5 the endpoint returned exactly 2 candidates — Bo Nix at market_gain_pct 4.54 and Brock Purdy at 2.51 — both entirely premised on differencing an IDPTC number against a KTC number. Re-measured on this contract the paired IDPTC/KTC ratio spans p10 0.886 to p90 1.083 over 475 shared players, i.e. routine per-player disagreement of roughly +/-10%, twice the width of the gate. The response carries no uncertainty_band, no marketsUsed and no mixedMarket stamp — unlike /api/trade/finder (which stamps mixedMarket per trade) and /api/angle/packages (which returns market_uncertainty_band, market_gain_low_pct/high_pct and withheld_uncertain=311 on the same data).

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/angle/find -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"ownerId":"owner-8b8a59adf44e","playerName":"Carson Schwesinger"}' | python3 -m json.tool | head -30
reproduction.expected: Cross-market candidates are either suppressed near the gate or stamped with the measured band, as /api/angle/packages does
reproduction.actual: 2 candidates at market_gain_pct 4.54 and 2.51, both cross-market, with no band, no marketsUsed and no warning

numericProof.formula: gate_width = 5.0% ; measured cross-board noise = (p90 - p10)/2 = (1.0826-0.8864)/2 = 9.81%

findings.userImpact: Anyone calling this endpoint (no shipped page does today — /angle uses /api/angle/packages only) is handed IDP-for-offense pivots whose entire 'the market says this is fair' claim is smaller than the two boards' routine disagreement. The verdict is a coin flip presented as a decision.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced end-to-end on the live endpoint rather than by code reading: 37/38 candidates cross-market, 2 admitted at 4.54% and 2.51%, and the p10/p90 re-measured independently at 0.886/1.083 on today's contract. Priority lowered from the prior's framing because /api/angle/find has no UI caller — grep for '/api/angle/find' in frontend/ finds only the bridge route.

findings.whatWorks: /api/angle/packages, which DOES go through src/league_intel/cross_market.value_package, gets this right: it prices single-market where it can, sizes a band from the same measured spread, withholds packages whose gap straddles the gate (311 withheld on a live run) and names the assumption in market_warnings.
findings.rootCause: The cross_market rewiring covered the package path and explicitly exempted the 1-for-1 path on the grounds that only sums are dangerous. A difference of two numbers from different publishers carries the same scale risk as a sum of them.
findings.requiredRepair: Route _make_candidate's market comparison through cross_market.compare_packages with single-asset packages, or at minimum stamp market_source per side plus a band and suppress candidates whose gain straddles the gate — the same posture /api/angle/packages already ships.
findings.dependencies: src/league_intel/cross_market.py is already imported by angle.py, so no new dependency.

findings.title: The market-gap direction is computed in RANK space where no TE-basis correction exists, so 33 of 33 edge-eligible tight ends are SELL and none is BUY
findings.claimUnderTest: ADR-015 / CLAUDE.md: TE rows from non-TEP sources are lifted onto the board's tepp basis using KTC's own measured uplift, so the board is basis-consistent for tight ends.
findings.observed: The basis conversion operates on VALUES inside the blend (data_contract.py:7674-7695). marketGapDirection is computed from ORDINAL RANKS (data_contract.py:3039-3056) and never sees it. ktcSfTep is the sole is_retail source and is a TE++ board; the consensus mean it is differenced against is dominated by base-TE boards. Measured on the live contract, mean(consensusRank) - mean(retailRank) by position: TE +41.60 (94.5% retail_premium), PICK +90.14, WR -6.83 (35.8%), RB -8.50 (25.8%), QB -24.69 (6.1%). Applying the /edge panel's own gate (canonicalConsensusRank <= 250, sourceRankSpread >= 20, not quarantined): TE 33 retail_premium / 0 consensus_premium, against QB 21 buy / 0 sell, RB 27 buy / 6 sell, WR 41 buy / 9 sell. Nine of the ten rows the Sell panel actually renders are tight ends (Eli Raridon, Mason Taylor, Greg Dulcich, Hunter Henry, Pat Freiermuth, Dalton Schultz, Max Klare, Travis Kelce, AJ Barner). On /rankings the same skew renders as TE 19 SELL / 0 BUY of the 23 tight ends on page 1.

reproduction.command: python3 -c "import json,collections;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w27.json'));e=[r for r in d['playersArray'] if (r.get('canonicalConsensusRank') or 9**9)<=250 and (r.get('sourceRankSpread') or 0)>=20 and not r.get('quarantined')];c=collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter);[c[r['position']].__setitem__(r['marketGapDirection'],c[r['position']][r['marketGapDirection']]+1) for r in e];print({k:dict(v) for k,v in sorted(c.items())})"
reproduction.expected: TE buy/sell split resembles the other offense positions (roughly 1:3 sell:buy)
reproduction.actual: TE {'retail_premium': 33} — 33 sell, 0 buy, 0 aligned

numericProof.formula: diff = mean(consensus ordinal ranks) - mean(retail ordinal ranks); diff > 0 => retail_premium => SELL. The tepp->base basis difference is a pure rank shift the value-space conversion never reaches.

findings.userImpact: On /edge the 'Sell signals' rail is a tight-end list, and on /rankings 19 of 23 visible tight ends carry a red SELL badge. A manager who sells tight ends on that signal is trading away the position their two-mandatory-TE league is structurally short of, on the strength of a format artifact rather than a mispricing.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced independently. Counts differ slightly from the prior (33 of 33 edge-eligible here vs the prior's 36 of 36; top-250 offense census TE 35 sell / 0 buy vs the prior's 36 sell) because I gate on canonicalConsensusRank and the prior appears to have used a marginally different rank column — the direction and the 0-buy result are identical, and 9 of 10 rendered Sell rows are TEs in both.

findings.whatWorks: The VALUE-space TE basis conversion is applied correctly and exactly once (see W27-F009), and the league-adjusted overlay's tePremium axis is deliberately ABSENT so it cannot double-count. The defect is confined to the rank-space gap label.
findings.rootCause: Two different quantities share the name 'market gap': the value-space blend (basis-corrected) and the rank-space retail-vs-consensus mean (not). The correction was inserted at the value stage only, and nothing raised an error when the rank stage kept comparing a TE++ ordinal against base-TE ordinals.
findings.requiredRepair: Either compute the gap in the basis-corrected value space (retail value vs blended value, both on the tepp basis), or rank-correct the retail side for TEs before differencing. A cheaper interim: suppress the direction for TE rows and say why, rather than emitting a signal that is 100% one-directional.
findings.dependencies: Shares the anchor definition with W27-F001; a per-market anchor rewrite should fix both at once.

findings.title: src/ros/ normalizes no position strings, so 6 IDP rows in /api/ros/player-values are bucketed as S/DT/DE and receive fabricated positional ranks like 'S1' and 'DE1'
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Position Normalization — Single source of truth: POSITION_ALIASES in src/utils/name_clean.py. All modules import from there.'
findings.observed: No module under src/ros/ imports POSITION_ALIASES or normalize_position (grep returns zero hits across src/ros/*.py). The live /api/ros/player-values payload contains 500 rows whose positions include S 3, DT 2, DE 1 alongside the canonical DB 74 / DL 55 / LB 45. Because aggregate.py:275 buckets positional ranks on the raw string, Gregory Rousseau is stamped rosRankPosition 1 ('DE1'), Kamren Curl rosRankPosition 1 ('S1') at rosValue 15.96, and Christian Wilkins rosRankPosition 1 ('DT1') at 12.52 — each the notional #1 of a bucket of one to three players, while the real DB bucket holds 74 and the DL bucket 55. All six rows come from fantasyProsRosIdp.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/ros/player-values' | python3 -c "import json,sys,collections;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(collections.Counter(p['position'] for p in d['players']));print([(p['canonicalName'],p['position'],p['rosRankPosition'],p['rosValue']) for p in d['players'] if p['position'] in ('S','DT','DE')])"
reproduction.expected: Every IDP row carries DL/LB/DB per POSITION_ALIASES
reproduction.actual: Counter includes {'S':3,'DT':2,'DE':1}; e.g. ('kamren curl','S',1,15.96)

numericProof.formula: unnormalized = count(position not in POSITION_ALIASES.values())

findings.userImpact: No shipped surface renders rosRankPosition today (frontend/lib/ros-index.js:119 indexes it and nothing reads it), so user impact is currently nil — but the payload publishes a positional rank of 1 for a replacement-level safety, and any future consumer that buckets by position drops these six players from their real family.

priorFinding.note: A18-F19 is about the CLIENT normalizePos omitting 7 IDP aliases. This is the server-side twin in src/ros/, which the prior does not name. Measured, not inferred.

findings.whatWorks: src/ros/lineup.py compensates downstream with its own eligibility map (_SLOT_ELIGIBLE includes DE/DT/EDGE/S/CB), which is why /api/ros/team-strength still fills all 36 DL / 36 LB / 36 DB slots. Only the aggregate's own positional bucketing is affected.
findings.rootCause: src/ros/ was written as a self-contained subsystem and never wired to the shared normalizer; lineup.py's private alias map hid the omission by making the visible surface work.
findings.requiredRepair: Call normalize_position() in src/ros/aggregate.py where the display position is carried (:223-224) and where positional ranks are bucketed (:275). Then delete lineup.py's private alias sets in favour of the shared table.

findings.title: DL/LB hybrid eligibility is implemented in exactly one subsystem (src/ros/); the /api/data contract carries no fantasyPositions, so 55 of 937 rostered players are single-eligible everywhere else and 32 of them disagree with Sleeper's own primary position
findings.claimUnderTest: src/ros/lineup.py:84-89 states the correct rule — 'Sleeper evaluates eligibility against fantasy_positions, so a DL/LB hybrid legally fills either an LB or a DL slot. Checking only position (as this module used to) silently benches the player.' The question is whether anything outside src/ros/ obeys it.
findings.observed: Intersecting the live Sleeper player file with contract.sleeper.idToPlayer: 55 of 937 rostered players carry more than one fantasy position — 50 DL/LB, 3 DB/LB, 1 DB/WR (Travis Hunter), 1 OL/OT. The /api/data contract exposes a single position per player: playersArray rows have a 'position' string and no 'fantasyPositions' key, and sleeper.positions is a flat name->string map. On 32 of the 55, the contract's position disagrees with Sleeper's own primary (Micah Parsons, T.J. Watt, Khalil Mack, Joey Bosa, Travon Walker and others are 'LB' to Sleeper and 'DL' on the board). grep for fantasy_positions/fantasyPositions across src/ finds it only in src/ros/{lineup,scrape,team_strength,playoff_sim}.py, src/league_intel/sim.py and src/public_league/snapshot.py — never in data_contract.py, suggestions.py, finder.py, angle.py or waiver.py. findings.title: CLAUDE.md's KTC-vs-IDPTradeCalc comparability claim reproduces on the live payload, ADR-025 is not in tension with it — but the summary hides a 10% TE-specific divergence that the code's own module docstring records
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md 'Cross-market note': 'of KTC's 500 rows, 475 also appear on the IDPTC board at a median value ratio of 1.000 (p10 0.888, p90 1.054, measured 2026-07-26). Both top out at 9999, so there is no rescaling to apply between them.' Set against ADR-025 in docs/consensus-edge/DECISIONS.md, 'idptradecalculator.com is the IDP market, and it cannot also be the IDP scale'.
findings.observed: Re-measured independently on the live contract: ktcSfTep prices 501 rows, idpTradeCalc 911, and 475 are shared (94.8% of KTC). Pooled ratio idpTradeCalc/ktcSfTep: median 0.9970, p10 0.8864, p90 1.0826. Both boards max at 9999. The claim reproduces to three decimal places on n and p10. The two documents are NOT in tension: CLAUDE.md asserts unit comparability between two retail boards; ADR-025 asserts that a board cannot serve as the fair-value anchor its own market price is measured against (circularity), which is a different proposition about the consensus-edge board and does not deny comparability. What CLAUDE.md's pooled median hides is a single large positional divergence: TE median ratio 0.9000 (p10 0.8385, p90 0.9434, n=72) against QB 1.0322, WR 1.0103, RB 0.9939, PICK 1.0000. IDPTC's tight ends sit 10% below KTC's because KTC's is a TE++ board and IDPTC's is not — the same basis difference that drives W27-F005 — and the value-blend happens to neutralise it only because idpTradeCalc is registered is_tep_premium and so takes the flat 1.10 native correction (0.900 x 1.10 = 0.990).

The if/elif in data_contract.py:7674-7695 makes both branches mutually exclusive, and convert_te_value's two-basis API is a no-op when from == to, so a second call cannot compound.

findings.title: The live board is blind to the league's IDP scoring: defensive backs are the cheapest family (best DB at board rank 167) even though this league pays 5.32 per pass defensed and 5.32 per interception against 1.33 per solo tackle
findings.claimUnderTest: The workstream question 'does LB tackle volume automatically outrank scarcer DB/DL production?', and CLAUDE.md's framing of IDP as a first-class asset class whose format effects 'flow from exact scoring'.
findings.observed: Measured on the live board, the answer to the tackle-volume question is NO in the direction expected and YES in a different one. Per family: DL n=145, max 6362 (Aidan Hutchinson, board pos 36), median 1376; LB n=114, max 5908 (board pos 44), median 1319; DB n=139, max 3159 (Caleb Downs, board pos 167), median 943. Edge rushers lead, linebackers follow, and defensive backs are compressed to roughly half the value at every quantile: the DL top-1-to-starter-depth ratio is 3.64x and LB 3.26x against DB 2.29x. That ordering is inherited wholesale from idpTradeCalc, a generic IDP calculator, and nothing in the live value path re-scores it under this league's actual settings — which pay idp_pass_def 5.32, idp_int 5.32, idp_tkl_loss 4.25, idp_ff 4.25, idp_sack 2.92, idp_qb_hit 2.13 and idp_tkl_solo 1.33. A 15-pass-defensed cornerback earns 79.8 points from that one category alone. The only league-aware IDP lever that reaches a value is the league-adjusted overlay's single per-family scarcity factor (DL 1.09776, LB 0.97971, DB 1.01183) — one constant per position, derived from roster structure, not from scoring; its tePremium and projectionCorroboration axes are ABSENT and there is no scoring axis at all. The subsystem that would close the gap, BDVM, answers status 'no_projection_snapshot' in this container.

reproduction.expected: IDP family ordering reflects the league's own scoring weights, or the payload discloses that it does not
reproduction.actual: DL max 6362 pos 36 / LB max 5908 pos 44 / DB max 3159 pos 167, with no scoring-derived adjustment anywhere and no disclosure

numericProof.formula: dbMax/dlMax = 3159/6362 = 0.497 — the best DB is worth half the best DL on a board that never reads a scoring setting

findings.userImpact: Every DB decision on the site inherits a generic-format price. Concretely it is what puts zero DBs in the trade-suggestion pool (W27-F002) and what makes 'need DB' unfixable, and it means a manager in a pass-defensed-heavy league is systematically told his most format-advantaged position is his least valuable one, with nothing on the page saying the valuation is format-generic.

priorFinding.note: A24-F19 notes 12 canonical IDP scoring keys have no RULE_META entry so their contributions apply to every position bucket — a defect inside the scoring-fit machinery. This finding is upstream of that: no scoring-derived quantity reaches rankDerivedValue for IDP at all on the live path. Confidence is medium because 'the market is wrong about DBs for this league' is not directly falsifiable without a projection feed, whereas 'nothing in the live path reads the scoring settings for IDP value' is.

findings.whatWorks: The IDP family ordering is internally coherent and on one scale with offense (idpTradeCalc's IDP maximum 6444 vs offense 9999 confirms a shared, non-renormalized scale). The lineup-structure half of league awareness is real: replacement.py measures starter thresholds from the exact optimizer over real rosters, and starter_needs_for_league reads roster_positions correctly.
findings.rootCause: Market-rank ingestion is the only live value concept, and every registered IDP source publishes a format-generic board. The fundamental, scoring-exact concept exists (src/bdvm/) but has no projection snapshot in this environment, so the market board is the whole answer.
findings.requiredRepair: Short term: disclose it — stamp on the contract (and note on /rankings) that IDP values are format-generic and not re-scored under the league's settings, the way ValueBasisNote already does for /draft. Medium term: land a projection feed so BDVM's exact-scoring path can supply the fundamental comparison the market board cannot.
findings.dependencies: Blocked on data/bdvm/projections/ (a pre-declared Blocked-by-data condition) for the medium-term half; the disclosure half is unblocked.

findings.title: The 12-team / 14-week schedule generator and its NFL-aware optimizer do not exist anywhere in the repository — not a route, not a script, not a config, not a doc
findings.claimUnderTest: Prompt section 28 specifies a full fantasy schedule generator: 12 teams, 3 named divisions, weeks 1-14, 6 matchups/week, every team exactly once per week, no fantasy byes, divisional opponents twice, non-divisional once, no back-to-back repeat opponents, Jason vs Michaela forced to week 4, optimized against real 2026 NFL weeks 1-14 (NFL head-to-head + NFL bye weeks prioritised over rivalry preferences, with 8 tier-1 rivalry owners weighted).

A whole-tree grep over all 10,409 tracked files for generate_schedule|build_schedule|schedule_generator|scheduleGenerator|makeSchedule|round.?robin|'no back-to-back'|'divisional opponent' returns 14 files, and every one is unrelated. The 100-operation live OpenAPI census contains no schedule route (only /api/public/league/matchups and /api/public/league/matchup/{...}, which READ posted Sleeper matchups). frontend/app has no schedule directory and no nav entry. The word 'division' appears nowhere as a data structure — the three division names (The Pit / Sweet Pepper Bacon / Barbacoa) exist only as inert strings inside Sleeper's league metadata blob in config/league_intel/sleeper_league_snapshot_2026-07-26.json; no module reads them. The two nearest-sounding artifacts are NOT this feature: src/public_league/playoff_odds.py::_round_robin_schedule is a synthetic pairing fallback used only to simulate UNPOSTED weeks for playoff odds (it copies observed Sleeper pair-sets by cycle residue and honours none of the stated constraints, has no division model, no week-4 pin and no NFL input), and src/bdvm/schedule.py fetches the nflverse NFL slate purely to mark per-player bye weeks for BDVM ROS weighting. Neither is user-reachable as a scheduler.

findings.title: The rookie draft-capital tier is structurally dead — Sleeper publishes no draft_round field on any of its 12,207 player records, so two of the six configured weights can never fire, yet the UI tells every user that rookie draft capital is part of the score
findings.claimUnderTest: src/api/team_assignment.py's module docstring says the model 'rewards ... rookie draft capital'; _score_player's T4 adds weights.rookieRound1 (+4) / rookieRound2 (+2) via _draft_round(meta) reading meta['draft_round'] or meta['draftRound']; config/team_assignment.json ships both weights as live knobs; and the /league tab's on-page explainer tells the user that additional NFL teams are derived from 'starting QBs, primary skill-position players, rookies with high draft capital, and (if IDP is enabled) starting defenders'. The same file's own docstring argues at length that 'a declared-but-unread knob is worse than no knob: editing it looks like it does something' — and then ships two.
findings.observed: Sleeper's /v1/players/nfl payload has no draft_round key whatsoever. Across all 12,207 player records in the unpruned data/public_league/nfl_players.json, the key 'draft_round' is present 0 times and 'draftRound' 0 times (the record vocabulary is: active, age, birth_*, college, competitions, depth_chart_order, depth_chart_position, espn_id, fantasy_data_id, fantasy_positions, first/last/full_name, gsis_id, hashtag, height, high_school, injury_*, kalshi_id, metadata, news_updated, number, oddsjam_id, opta_id, pandascore_id, player_id, player_shard, position, practice_*, roto*_id, search_*, sport, sportradar_id, stats_id, status, swish_id, team, team_abbr, team_changed_at, weight, yahoo_id, years_exp). _draft_round() therefore returns None for every player on every roster, and T4 contributes exactly 0 points to every score ever produced. The league currently rosters 102 players with years_exp == 0 — i.e. 102 genuine rookies that the tier was written for — and not one of them scores a rookie point. The live payload's contributor-reason histogram contains 13 distinct reasons and zero instances of '1st-round rookie' or '2nd-round rookie'. The snapshot is not pruned (src/public_league/sleeper_client.py::fetch_nfl_players stores the vendor dict verbatim), so this is an upstream-vocabulary gap, not a local data-loss bug.

reproduction.expected: if the tier were live: a nonzero count of records carrying draft_round, and '1st-round rookie'/'2nd-round rookie' appearing among the live contributor reasons
reproduction.actual: records 12208 draft_round 0 draftRound 0; live reasons = {'QB anchor':16,'IDP DB starter':13,'WR committee':13,'IDP LB starter':13,'RB committee':10,'RB starter':9,'TE starter':8,'WR starter':8,'IDP DE starter':4,'IDP DL starter':2,'TE committee':2,'IDP DT starter':2,'IDP CB starter':1} — no rookie reason at any count

findings.userImpact: Two failure modes, both live today. (1) The on-page explainer at /league?tab=teamAssignment states that 'rookies with high draft capital' contribute to the score. They do not, and never have — a manager whose roster is loaded with premium rookies gets no credit for it and will read the breakdown as evidence that the model rated those rookies at zero, when in fact the model never looked. (2) config/team_assignment.json is explicitly presented as operator-editable ('Edit favorites/aliases/weights here without redeploy'), and its own _doc block invites retuning assignmentMinPoints when 'too few NFL teams qualify' — an operator who instead raises rookieRound1 to try to lift qualification will observe absolutely no change and have no way to learn why. Because 5 of 12 managers currently return exactly one NFL team (their favorite only), that is a realistic operator action.

priorFinding.note: Same DEFECT CLASS as PRIOR-A03-F17 ('a config file presents eight tunable knobs of which six do nothing, so an operator tuning them will change JSON and see no movement'), and that finding's specific keys are confirmed FIXED. But the fix was incomplete and the prior audit missed why: it identified the inert knobs by reading the code (which weights _score_player never references) and therefore could not see rookieRound1/rookieRound2, which ARE referenced by _score_player and so passed its test. They are inert for a different reason only live data reveals — the field they depend on does not exist in Sleeper's payload. Two of six weights remain dead after the remediation that the prior finding prompted.

findings.whatWorks: The other four weights all fire and are correct: qbAnchor 16 times, skillStarter 25 (RB 9 / WR 8 / TE 8), skillCommittee 25 (RB 10 / WR 13 / TE 2), idpStarter 35 across DB/LB/DE/DL/DT/CB. _draft_round itself is defensively written and returns None cleanly rather than throwing; the defect is that its input never exists.
findings.rootCause: The tier was designed against a field Sleeper's player endpoint does not publish, and nothing ever asserted the field's presence. tests/api/test_team_assignment.py pins the weight-key SET (that every declared weight is read by _score_player) but constructs its own fixture metas with draft_round injected, so it proves the code path exists while proving nothing about whether real data ever reaches it — the exact blind spot that let a dead tier ship as a live knob.
findings.requiredRepair: Two acceptable repairs, and the module's own stated policy picks the second. (a) Source real draft capital: the rookie draft round is available from nflverse (the same release family src/bdvm/schedule.py already fetches) and the platform separately carries rookie draft-slot priors in scripts/bdvm_build_baseline.py — join on gsis_id, which IS on the Sleeper record. (b) Delete T4 and both weights outright, exactly as eliteProductionTop10/Top24 and idpElite were deleted on 2026-08-04 for being unread, and drop 'rookies with high draft capital' from the JSX explainer. Whichever is chosen, add a test that asserts against the REAL data/public_league/nfl_players.json vocabulary — a weight declared in config must be demonstrably reachable on live input, not just on a hand-built fixture.
findings.dependencies: An external draft-capital feed if repair (a) is taken; none if (b).

findings.title: The best-ball 'no fixed starting lineup' concern does not apply — starter/backup is read from Sleeper's NFL depth chart, not the fantasy lineup — but 35 of 666 rostered players carry no depth data and kickers are structurally unscorable in a league with a K slot
findings.claimUnderTest: Prompt section 32 asks whether 'starters' and 'backups' are identified correctly in a BEST BALL league, where there is no fixed starting lineup.
findings.observed: The concern is misplaced, and I could not reproduce it as a defect: _score_player never reads the fantasy lineup. 'Starter' means meta['depth_chart_order'] == 1 and 'committee' means depth_chart_order in (2,3) — Sleeper's NFL depth-chart position for that player on his NFL club. Best ball changes only how a fantasy lineup is set; it has no bearing on an NFL depth chart, and the feature's whole purpose is NFL-team correlation, so the NFL depth chart is the correct input. Confirmed in the live league: settings.best_ball == 1 and roster_positions carries a full explicit starting set (QB/2RB/3WR/2TE/2FLEX/SUPER_FLEX/K/3DL/3LB/3DB + 37 BN), and the scores reproduce exactly without any lineup input. Two real, smaller gaps do exist. (1) Coverage: 35 of 666 rostered players have depth_chart_order == null, so every skill and IDP tier silently skips them — they are indistinguishable in the output from players scored at zero. (2) Vocabulary: _SKILL_POSITIONS and _IDP_POSITIONS between them cover QB/RB/WR/TE/DL/DE/DT/LB/DB/CB/S, which leaves 20 rostered players permanently unscorable — 19 kickers and 1 'SS'. The kicker case is not hypothetical roster clog: roster_positions contains a K starting slot, so every one of the 12 teams is required to roster a kicker and no kicker can ever contribute a point toward his NFL team. 'S' is in the IDP set but Sleeper emits 'SS'/'FS', so the safety alias is the wrong string.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && .venv/bin/python -c "import json,collections;pl=json.load(open('data/public_league/nfl_players.json'));s=json.load(open('data/public_league/snapshot.json'));cur=[x for x in s['seasons'] if str(x['season'])=='2026'][0];print('best_ball',cur['league']['settings'].get('best_ball'));ap=[p for r in cur['rosters'] for p in (r.get('players') or [])];SK={'RB','WR','TE'};ID={'DL','DE','DT','LB','DB','CB','S'};print('rostered',len(ap));print('depth null',sum(1 for p in ap if (pl.get(str(p)) or {}).get('depth_chart_order') is None));print('unscorable pos',collections.Counter((pl.get(str(p)) or {}).get('position') for p in ap if (pl.get(str(p)) or {}).get('position') not in SK|ID|{'QB'}))"
reproduction.expected: if the best-ball concern were real, the scorer would have to consult starters/matchup lineups and would disagree with a depth-chart-only recomputation
reproduction.actual: best_ball 1; rostered 666; depth null 35; unscorable pos Counter({'K': 19, 'SS': 1}) — and the depth-chart-only recomputation in W28-F002 matches the live payload on all 12 managers with 0 mismatches

numericProof.formula: unscoredShare = (depthNull + permanentlyUnscorablePositions) / rostered = (35 + 20) / 666

findings.userImpact: A manager expanding 'Show breakdown' sees a player omitted with no explanation in two distinct cases that look identical: the player genuinely scored zero, or the model had no depth-chart data for him / has no rule for his position. A manager who rosters a starting kicker on, say, Baltimore gets zero Baltimore correlation from him even though the league forces him to roster a kicker. Low severity because the output is an entertainment/flavour mapping, not a trade or lineup decision.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers depth-chart sourcing or position-vocabulary coverage in this module (PRIOR-A03-F17, the only team_assignment prior, is about config knobs). Recorded partly as a verified NEGATIVE: the best-ball starter/backup suspicion raised in the prompt does not reproduce.

findings.whatWorks: 631 of 666 rostered players (94.7%) carry depth_chart_order and are scored. The best-ball-independence of the model is a correct design choice, and the IDP gate (_league_idp_enabled reading roster_positions for DL/LB/DB slots) correctly returns True for this league, which is why 35 IDP contributions appear on the live payload.
findings.rootCause: _IDP_POSITIONS was written against a guessed Sleeper position vocabulary ('S') rather than the observed one ('SS'/'FS'), and no tier was ever written for K. Missing depth_chart_order is treated as 'not a starter' rather than 'unknown', so absent data and a zero score are conflated.
findings.requiredRepair: Add 'SS' and 'FS' to _IDP_POSITIONS (one-line, matches the existing pattern of listing raw Sleeper codes). Decide explicitly about K — either a kickerStarter weight or a code comment stating kickers are deliberately excluded, so the omission is a decision rather than an oversight. Optionally surface depth-unknown players in the contributors list at 0 points with reason 'no depth chart data', which is the same honest-omission posture the codebase already uses for assetsUnpricedByBoard in src/trade/finder.py and unpricedPickCount in the draft-capital fallback.

findings.title: The 15-point qualification threshold leaves 5 of 12 managers with only their favorite team, so the 'up to 3 NFL teams' promise delivers a mean of 1.92 — and the config's own note flags this exact knob as untuned
findings.claimUnderTest: The section header promises 'Each manager is mapped to 1-3 NFL teams ... Teams scoring at least 15 pts qualify; max 3 NFL teams per manager.' config/team_assignment.json's thresholds._doc states outright that removing the double-counted elite-production tier 'lowered every roster score' and that assignmentMinPoints 'is the knob to retune if too few NFL teams qualify' — i.e. the repo already suspects this number is stale and never measured it.
findings.observed: Measured on the live payload: teams-per-manager distribution is {1: 5, 2: 3, 3: 4}, mean 1.92 against a cap of 3, and 5 of 12 managers (Collin, Jason, Roy, Ty, jstuedle) show only their favorite with no roster-based team at all. Their nearest misses are close to the line, not far from it — Collin's second-best NFL team is BUF at 14 (threshold 15), Jason's is WAS at 14, jstuedle's best team of any kind is TB at 12 while his own favorite KC scores only 6. Because the favorite bypasses the threshold, jstuedle's card displays 'Kansas City Chiefs FAVORITE' with the score suppressed entirely (the JSX prints 'N pts from roster' only when score > 0, so jstuedle's card reads 'FAVORITE · 6 pts from roster' while Brent's BUF at 0 renders as a bare 'FAVORITE' with no number at all). Separately, the output has no uniqueness constraint: 19 distinct NFL franchises are used across 12 managers, with HOU assigned to 4 different managers (Ty, Eric, Kitch and Joey all declare it as favorite) and KC to 2 (Joel's favorite and Brent's roster-based qualifier). That is defensible for a 'which NFL teams do you correlate with' readout but wrong for anything named 'assignment' that implies exclusivity, and nothing in the UI states which of the two it is.
