findings.userImpact: Five of twelve managers open the tab and see a single card entry that is just the favorite they declared by hand in a config file — the entire roster-correlation half of the feature produces nothing for them, and the explainer above it still promises 1-3 teams. Nobody trades or starts a player because of it, hence P3, but the feature reads as broken to 42% of the league.

priorFinding.note: New. PRIOR-A03-F17 explicitly notes that 'only assignmentMinPoints reaches the UI' and treats it as the one knob that works, but never measured what it produces. It is the removal of the weights that finding prompted which left the threshold mis-scaled.

findings.whatWorks: The cap and the sort are both correct: roster_based is ordered by (-score, abbr) and sliced to remaining_capacity, the favorite always occupies slot 0 and always counts toward the cap, and no manager exceeds 3. The threshold is read from config at request time, so retuning it needs no redeploy exactly as the config claims.
findings.rootCause: assignmentMinPoints 15 was set against the pre-2026-08-04 weight scale, where a primary QB scored 13 and a primary skill player 8. Removing the double-counting T3 tier dropped those to 10 and 5 — roughly a 38% cut to every roster score — but the threshold was left at 15. The config file documents the cause and explicitly defers the fix.
findings.requiredRepair: Scale the threshold with the weights: 15 * (10/13) ~ 11.5, so 11 or 12 restores the pre-change qualification rate. Verify by re-running the reproduction command and checking the distribution, not by reasoning about it. Separately, either state in the JSX explainer that NFL teams are not exclusive across managers, or add a uniqueness pass if exclusivity is actually what 'assignment' is meant to mean — that is a product decision, not a bug fix.
findings.dependencies: Interacts with W28-F003: repairing the dead rookie tier would itself raise scores and change the right threshold, so fix F003 first and tune the threshold once, afterwards.

findings.title: /api/trade/suggestions emits two different value concepts under one field name, showing Travis Hunter at 5,637 on /trade while /rankings shows 4,401
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'The whole trick is that every engine reads exactly one value - rankDerivedValue' (src/league_intel/overlay.py:17-21), and stage 11 two-way boost is 'A genuine post-blend OVERRIDE: rankDerivedValue becomes max(offense value, alt-position-family value)'.
findings.observed: suggestions.py READS rankDerivedValue at intake (:561) but RE-SERIALIZES it from offense_only_value whenever _trade_is_idp_free(give, receive) is true (_serialize_suggestion :1762 -> _serialize_player :1737-1741). Both concepts ship under the same key 'displayValue'. On the live payload 19 of 51 asset legs across all 12 teams disagree with the board in DEFAULT market mode. Worst case Travis Hunter: the offense-only board never saw the two-way boost, so /trade shows 5,637 while /rankings shows 4,401. The same player can carry two different displayValues inside ONE response - Brian Thomas appears at 4,436 in one suggestion leg and 4,466 in rosterAnalysis.byPosition.

reproduction.actual: market mode : 19/51 legs disagree with rankDerivedValue; worst: Travis Hunter shown=5637 board=4401 (+28.08%)

findings.userImpact: A user reading a sell-high suggestion on /trade sees Travis Hunter valued 28% above the board that /rankings, /rosters, the TradeMeter and every team total use. priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A20-F06 identified the overlay/offense-only scale mix as a leagueAdjusted problem. This finding shows the SAME mechanism is already wrong in DEFAULT market mode, independent of any lens, and that the two-way boost (stage 11) is silently reverted on a user-facing surface - which PRIOR-A08-F01/A11-F07 examined only as a math/test-coverage question.

findings.whatWorks: finder.py made this migration correctly: metadata.valueSource is stamped 'rankDerivedValue' on a live probe and unpriced assets are counted rather than dropped silently.
findings.rootCause: The offense-only board is a legitimate second value concept (an IDP-disabled re-run of the pipeline) but it is serialized into the field name the board value owns, so the response has no way to say which concept a number belongs to.
findings.requiredRepair: Either (a) drop the offense_only branch in _serialize_player and always emit rankDerivedValue, keeping offense-only for the internal _eff_val gap math only, or (b) emit it as a distinct key (offenseOnlyDisplayValue) plus a per-suggestion valueBasis stamp, and have trade-sections.jsx render the board value. Special-case the two-way players: max(offense, alt) must not be discardable by an offense-only re-read.

blastRadius.routesAffectedNote: /api/trade/suggestions (measured 21/51 legs), /api/trade/simulate (measured identical delta across modes), /api/trade/finder (same offense_only substitution at finder.py:248-249). NOT 6.

priorFinding.note: Prior identified the mechanism by code reading. Reproduced here at runtime across all 12 rosters with per-leg arithmetic: 21/51 legs, and 12/12 for one roster. Prior did not measure blast radius or note that the response stamps the mode it is not honouring.

findings.whatWorks: The lens itself is real and correct where it applies: 709/1092 rows carry a factor, monotonicityViolations is empty, and Jayden Daniels moves 8898 -> 9061 exactly as factor 1.018366 predicts. adjusted_rows correctly returns ALL rows rather than compact_ranks_and_tiers' ranked subset.
findings.rootCause: The overlay was written against the invariant 'every engine reads exactly one value'. That invariant is false for suggestions.py, and nothing enforces it - tests/api/test_valuation_mode_threading.py checks that handlers STAMP the mode, not that the served numbers moved.
findings.requiredRepair: Scale offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue by the same factor in overlay.adjusted_rows (and mirror _offenseOnlyFinalAdjusted), OR remove the offense-only serialization per W29-F001. Add an assertion to the threading test that at least one served value differs between modes for a roster with known non-unit factors.

verification.reasoning:
UPHELD ON SUBSTANCE, rescoped on mechanism and blast radius. The reproduction runs today and returns the stated number exactly — 21/51 legs (41.2%) at the unadjusted value under valuationMode:leagueAdjusted — and I reproduced the mechanism per-leg rather than trusting the aggregate. The numericProof checks out to the digit: Kenneth Walker rdv 5813, factor 1.041554, round(5813*1.041554)=6055, served 5831 = offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue. src/league_intel/overlay.py:86-93 scales exactly one key (copy['rankDerivedValue']) and offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue rides through untouched; the response stamps leagueAdjusted with valuationNote:null, so nothing on screen says otherwise. The client-side inconsistency is real too — dynasty-data.js:1943-1952 additionally scales values.overall/finalAdjusted/displayValue and :1978 _finalAdjusted, and neither side touches the offense-only key. The lens toggle is live and user-reachable (frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:1656).

RESCOPED BROADER on mechanism. The finding frames this as a SERIALIZATION defect (suggestions.py:1737-1741, displayValue). It is not — it is an ARITHMETIC defect. `_eff_val(p, offense_only)` (suggestions.py:760-768) is called at :1038, :1044-1045, :1049, :1052-1053, :1091, :1099, :1111-1112, :1177-1203, :1253, :1258 — it is what picks the trade targets, sets give_val/recv_val, and drives gap and fairness. So under the adjusted lens an IDP-free suggestion is CONSTRUCTED on the unadjusted board, not merely labelled with unadjusted numbers. Fixing the serializer alone would leave wrong trades with right-looking prices.

RESCOPED BROADER on routes. The finding names 2 routes and claims routesAffected:6 without recounting. I measured a third route failing the same way: /api/trade/simulate returns a byte-identical delta (totalValue 1754, KW at 5831) under market and leagueAdjusted for an IDP-free trade, via src/api/trade_simulator.py:63-64 reading offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue. The control case proves the route is otherwise wired correctly (5813 -> 6055 with an IDP leg present), so this is the same offense-only hole, not a separate defect. src/trade/finder.py:248-249 substitutes offense_only_model_value (mirrored from _offenseOnlyFinalAdjusted, finder.py:479) on the same condition and is affected identically. Three engine routes materially, not 2 and not 6.

RESCOPED NARROWER on players. 606 is the count of rows CARRYING an offense-only value. Only 416 of those also carry a league factor, so only 416 could have moved under the lens; for the other 190 the market and adjusted answers are identical anyway and there is nothing to be wrong about.

Severity stays P1, deliberately not P0. The served number is a real market value, not a fabricated one, and the factors measured here span roughly 1.01-1.10, so the error is low single-digit percent — on a lens the repo's own backtest (docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md) records as 'no difference detected'. A user is misled about WHICH board they are on, not handed a nonsense price.

findings.title: Every visible trade-history grade is today's board applied retroactively to trades up to a year old; the as-of path exists but only drives a secondary badge and is dead without rank_history.jsonl
findings.claimUnderTest: frontend/lib/trade-retro-value.js:1-8: 'The existing analyzeSleeperTradeHistory grades trades at *current* values. This helper layers in the at-trade snapshot so the UI can show a trade's age.' frontend/app/trades/page.jsx:392: 'Rank history lets each trade be valued at the date it happened.'
findings.observed: resolveTradeItemValue reads row.values.full - today's board - for players (:146) and for picks (:132). Everything a user reads is built from it: pctGap, the letter grade, the 'won by X%' headline (trades/page.jsx:264) and the teamScores won/lost/totalGain leaderboard (:552-573). gradeRetro IS wired with asOfMs but produces only an aged_well/aged_poorly/stable badge, never the headline. Its own at-trade leg has two holes: picks always take the current value by design (trade-retro-value.js:76-83, source 'current'), and trades predating coverage fall back to the earliest sample (pointAt :52-56). Live contract carries 110 trades spanning 2025-08-05 to 2026-07-31; 24% of the 1,002 traded assets are picks and 60% of trades contain at least one. In this container the badge is inert: data/rank_history.jsonl does not exist and GET /api/data/rank-history?days=365 returns {"days":365,"history":{}}, so every asset takes current_fallback and verdictDelta is identically 0.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w29.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data/rank-history?days=365'; ls data/rank_history.jsonl
reproduction.expected: populated per-player history so gradeRetro can value assets at the trade date
reproduction.actual: {"days":365,"history":{}} and 'ls: cannot access data/rank_history.jsonl: No such file or directory'

numericProof.formula: share = pickAssets/tradedAssets ; tradeShare = tradesContainingAPick/110

findings.userImpact: Every 'A+ / won by 38%' verdict and the whole manager win/loss leaderboard on /trades is hindsight. A manager who traded for a player who later broke out is scored as prescient; the counterparty is scored as fleeced, when at the time the deal may have been even. Nothing on the page discloses the as-of basis.

priorFinding.note: Prior identified the hindsight grade and the badge-not-grade structure by code reading. Added here: runtime proof the retro path is currently inert (rank_history.jsonl absent, endpoint returns an empty history object), and the pick share that the retro path can never fix even when populated - 24% of assets, 60% of trades.

findings.whatWorks: The as-of machinery is genuinely built and correctly shaped: pointAt picks the closest-before sample, valueFromPoint prefers the server-stamped canonical val over a local Hill approximation, and data/source_value_history.jsonl exists with a documented 180-snapshot retention.
findings.rootCause: gradeRetro was layered on as an enhancement rather than substituted into analyzeRawTrade, so the correct valuation never reaches the number the user reads.
findings.requiredRepair: Make the at-trade valuation the primary grade when history covers the trade date, and label the current-value number explicitly as 'today'. Stamp per-item source (rankHistory | current_fallback) on the rendered grade so a partially-covered trade says so. Ensure rank_history.jsonl is produced in production. Pick history is the real gap - either persist pick values per snapshot or exclude pick-bearing trades from the graded leaderboard.
findings.dependencies: Requires rank_history.jsonl to be written by the scrape/refresh path.

findings.claimUnderTest: src/api/gameplan.py:34-38: 'Two scales that must never be mixed - rosValue (0-100, rest-of-season STRENGTH INDEX) and canonicalSiteValues (0-9999, dynasty market) are different currencies with no validated conversion between them.'
findings.observed: The predicate is `dynastyValue < rosValue * 0.7` with `isStrong` requiring rosValue >= 60, and dynastyValue supplied as `row.values?.full ?? row.rankDerivedValue` (PlayerPopup.jsx:142) - the 0-9999 board. Live /api/ros/player-values gives max rosValue 86.79, so the right-hand side maxes at 60.8. The live board's minimum rankDerivedValue is 757. The two ranges do not overlap: 0 of 1,092 rows can satisfy it. The tag has never rendered. The same predicate is duplicated in three places (two JS, one Python).

reproduction.command: OUT=/tmp/w29 bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W29/repro.sh

reproduction.actual: max(rosValue*0.7)=60.8  min(rankDerivedValue)=757  rows able to fire: 0

findings.userImpact: A veteran with strong short-term value and a collapsed dynasty price - exactly the sell-now case the tag exists to surface - is never flagged, on the popup and on the /trade RosTradeFitPanel. Silent absence, not a wrong number.

findings.requiredRepair: Convert one side before comparing - e.g. compare dynasty percentile rank against ROS percentile rank - and collapse the three copies to one shared helper. Add a unit test asserting the tag fires on a constructed case, which would have caught this at zero cost.

findings.title: The league-adjusted board's scarcity is measured entirely in ROS log-rank units, so a 0-100 ordinal index sets the multiplier on every dynasty trade value under the adjusted lens
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: the valuation overlay is driven by 'positional scarcity from this league's 12 rosters'. It does not say the scarcity is measured in ROS units.
findings.observed: compute_scarcity reads value = float(p.get('rosValue')) for every rostered player (replacement.py:631) out of data/ros/team_strength/<league>.json, and measure_endogenous_starters solves the lineup over the same field. lineupScarcity is a RATIO of two rosValues, so it is dimensionless and no scale is mixed - but rosValue is 100*(ln(N+1)-ln(r))/ln(N+1), an ordinal log-rank index (ros/aggregate.py:171, gameplan.py:40-49). A ratio of two ordinal indices is not a cardinal 'drop from the top player to the last starter'. That ratio becomes factor = 1 + (lineupScarcity - 0.5)*0.20 (adjustment.py:247) and multiplies every dynasty value the engines serve. Live: WR lineupScarcity 0.634 -> factor 1.0268; DL 0.767 -> 1.0978; LB 0.598 -> 0.9797. replacement.py:20-52 documents the known bias honestly (projection path measures FLEX-TE share at 0.0% vs 10.4% on weekly actuals) but the docstring lives on the measurement function, not on the published board.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w29.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/valuation/league-adjusted | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print({k:round(v['lineupScarcity'],4) for k,v in d['scarcity'].items()}); print({k:d['factors'][k] for k in list(d['factors'])[:4]})"
reproduction.expected: scarcity documented as derived from a cardinal value scale
reproduction.actual: lineupScarcity values 0.436-0.767 are ratios of rosValue, a 0-100 ordinal log-rank index; factors 0.953-1.043 multiply the 0-9999 board

numericProof.formula: factor = 1 + (lineupScarcity - reference) * sensitivity

findings.userImpact: A user selecting the adjusted board gets every trade value multiplied by a number derived from rest-of-season ordinal ranks. The direction is plausible and bounded (MAX_TOTAL_ADJUSTMENT 0.25, observed +-4.5%), but the quantity is not the cardinal scarcity the name implies, and the /rankings toggle says nothing about ROS being its input.

priorFinding.note: Priors reference rosValue scale mixing at the tag call sites (A01-F14 / A02-F06 / A19-F13) but none trace rosValue through compute_scarcity into the adjusted board that the engines serve.

findings.whatWorks: The coupling is dimensionally SAFE - a ratio of rosValues cancels units, so this is not the 0-9999-vs-0-100 error of W29-F005. Guardrails are real: evidence tier is STRUCTURAL_ONLY, absent axes contribute exactly 0, MAX_TOTAL_ADJUSTMENT clamps to +-25%, monotonicityViolations is empty on the live board, and docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md records that the adjusted board is deliberately a toggle rather than the default because four backtest framings found no improvement.
findings.rootCause: ROS is the only per-player quantity the platform has that is defined over a full roster including bench, so it is the only thing an endogenous lineup solve can run on. That is a real constraint, not an oversight.
findings.requiredRepair: Two separable steps. (1) Cheap and correct now: state the input in the overlay payload (a scarcityBasis: 'rosValue-ordinal' stamp) and in the /rankings toggle copy, so the lens does not read as board-derived. (2) The real fix: measure lineup scarcity from realized weekly scoring under the league's rate card - the same source scripts/measure_te_demand_actuals.py already uses - rather than from projection point estimates, which replacement.py itself shows understate flex demand for high-variance positions.
findings.dependencies: Step 2 depends on weekly actuals coverage; src/bdvm/actuals.py already scores nflverse weekly rows under exact league settings.

findings.title: trade-logic.js::displayValue ignores the user's per-player value override and its docstring describes a pick-year discount effectiveValue does not apply
findings.claimUnderTest: trade-logic.js:192-201: 'Use this anywhere a row's "Our Value" number is shown (picker cells, sort comparators, headers). Don't use effectiveValue directly for display - it also applies the pick-year discount which is trade-math-only, not display.'
findings.observed: effectiveValue (:181-185) applies no pick-year discount at all - it returns row.customValue when set, else row.values[valueMode]. The stated reason for displayValue's existence is therefore stale; the pick-year discount is applied in the backend pipeline (stage 12, config/weights/pick_year_discount.json) and is already baked into the value both functions read. The two functions now differ in exactly one way the docstring does not mention: displayValue (:203-209) never consults customValue, so a user's typed override drives the trade math but not any surface that renders through displayValue. Today the only displayValue call site is the search-results dropdown (trade-sections.jsx:118), which shows candidates before they are added and therefore before an override can exist - so the divergence is latent, not live.

reproduction.command: sed -n '181,209p' frontend/lib/trade-logic.js
reproduction.expected: effectiveValue applies a pick-year discount, per its own docstring
reproduction.actual: effectiveValue body is `if (row.customValue != null && row.customValue > 0) return row.customValue; return Number(row.values?.[valueMode] || 0);` - no discount term

numericProof.formula: count of pick-year-discount operations in effectiveValue body

findings.userImpact: None today. The risk is the next call site: the docstring instructs developers to use displayValue for 'picker cells, sort comparators, headers', and any such use inside a side would render the pre-override number beside a total computed from the override.

priorFinding.note: No prior covers the effectiveValue/displayValue divergence or the stale discount rationale.

findings.whatWorks: The override plumbing itself is clean: sidesWithOverrides (trade/page.jsx:534-544) copies rows rather than mutating, and every total, flow and Monte Carlo payload routes through effectiveValue so the override is applied consistently in the math.
findings.rootCause: The pick-year discount moved into the backend pipeline and the client-side implementation was removed, but the docstring that justified the two-function split was not updated.
findings.requiredRepair: Correct the docstring to state the real difference (customValue awareness), and make displayValue honour customValue so the two cannot diverge on a row inside a side. If a genuine 'show the board number, not the override' surface is wanted, name it that.

findings.observed: The two sections do NOT describe the same league. v1 reports playoffSpots=7 over 12 owners; v2 reports playoffSeeds=6 + byeSeeds=2 over 8 owners. Four owners present in v1 (Brent, Kich, Blaine, jstuedle) are absent from v2 entirely. Of the eight owners both engines cover, two flip: Eric and MaKayla read playoffProbability 0.0 on v1 and playoffOdds 1.0 on v2. A user toggling one settings switch sees a manager go from 'will miss the playoffs' to 'certain to make them'.

reproduction.command: for s in playoffOdds rosPlayoffOdds; do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/$s" -o /tmp/$s.json; done; python -c "import json;v1=json.load(open('/tmp/playoffOdds.json'))['data'];v2=json.load(open('/tmp/rosPlayoffOdds.json'))['data'];print(v1['playoffSpots'],len(v1['owners']),v2['playoffSeeds'],len(v2['playoffOdds']))"
reproduction.expected: two engines describing one league: identical spot count and identical owner set

numericProof.formula: sum(playoffProbability) == playoffSpots

findings.userImpact: A manager reads the Playoff Odds tab, sees his team at 0% and starts selling; the other engine says he is a lock. Nothing on the page names which engine produced the number.

priorFinding.note: prior claimed a team missing from the sim is coerced to 0%; measured live, v2 omits FOUR of twelve owners. The spot-count disagreement (7 vs 6) is additional.

findings.whatWorks: Both engines run, cache and return well-formed payloads; v1's probabilities do sum to its own spot count and v2's to its own.
findings.rootCause: Two independently-parameterised simulators were allowed to coexist behind a boolean instead of one engine with a strategy input, so their league constants (playoff spots, owner set) were never forced to agree.
findings.requiredRepair: Derive playoff spots and the owner set from one place for both engines, and stamp the producing engine on the payload so the UI can name it.
findings.dependencies: F002 (both engines are degenerate in preseason regardless)

findings.title: Both playoff-odds engines publish 100%/0% certainty with zero games played and 14 weeks remaining, and the convergence check passes on it
findings.claimUnderTest: playoff_odds.py: 'Run N Monte Carlo simulations… sample each owner's score from their empirical distribution.' The v1 module documents collapse to 0/1 only for the season-over case ('remaining_weeks == 0').
findings.observed: Live payload: weeksPlayed=0, weeksRemaining=14, numSims=10000, scheduleCertainty='posted', every owner currentWins=0 and currentPointsFor=0.0 — and every playoffProbability is exactly 1.0 or exactly 0.0. v2 is the same shape at n_simulations=2000 and reports converged=true with worstPlayoffOddsSe=0.0: the standard error is zero because every simulation returns the identical answer, so the convergence gate certifies a degenerate result. rosChampionship inherits it — Roy shows playoffOdds 1.0, medianFinalSeed 3 and championshipOdds 0.0 simultaneously.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/playoffOdds' | python -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin)['data'];print(d['weeksPlayed'],d['weeksRemaining'],d['numSims']);print(sorted({r['playoffProbability'] for r in d['owners']}))"
reproduction.expected: a spread of probabilities strictly between 0 and 1 with 14 weeks unplayed

numericProof.formula: count(distinct playoffProbability) over 12 owners

findings.userImpact: A manager opens /league in August and is told his team has a 0% chance of making the playoffs before a single snap. Trade-deadline direction (src/ros/direction.py) reads these same odds, so the same input drives a 'Strong Seller' recommendation.

priorFinding.note: reproduced live with exact payload values; the additional observation is that v2's convergence gate (converged=true, worstPlayoffOddsSe=0.0) certifies the degenerate output.

findings.whatWorks: scheduleCertainty is reported honestly ('posted'), and both engines publish weeksPlayed/weeksRemaining so a caller COULD suppress the section.
findings.rootCause: With no scored weeks, every owner's empirical distribution is the same league-wide fallback, so every simulation produces the same standings and the tie-break (PF, all zero) resolves deterministically.
findings.requiredRepair: Refuse to publish odds when weeksPlayed == 0 (the same posture the codebase uses for unpriced BDVM players), or seed preseason means from a projection source rather than an empty history.

findings.title: Three Python ports of KTC's Value Adjustment ship simultaneously and one of them rounds differently; its own parity test's ±1 tolerance is exactly the size of the divergence
findings.claimUnderTest: All three modules claim to be verbatim/line-for-line ports of frontend/lib/trade-logic.js::ktcAdjustPackage. trade_grading.py:103-112 states explicitly that Python's builtin round() is round-half-to-even and gives the wrong answer where JS gives another, and defines _js_round = floor(x+0.5) to avoid it.
findings.observed: src/trade/ktc_va.py — the port used by trade suggestions, the angle finder and the Monte Carlo sim — still calls Python's round() at :116 (ktc_reverse_adjust) and :319 (the returned value). The other two ports use floor(x+0.5). Over 20,000 random packages the ktc_va result differs from market_value_adjustment on 38 of them (0.19%), always by exactly 1; side and displayed never differ. ktc_va's own parity test asserts agreement 'to ±1', so the test cannot fail on this.

numericProof.formula: ktc_adjust_package(A,B).value

findings.userImpact: A package graded on /trade (JS) and the same package graded by trade suggestions can differ by one point of value adjustment. The magnitude is tiny; the fact that one algorithm has three maintained copies is not.

priorFinding.note: prior said 'three independent ports with no test tying two of them together'. Measured: the untied pair diverges on 0.19% of packages, always by 1, and the rounding function is the cause.

findings.whatWorks: Side selection and the display gate agree across all three ports on all 20,000 trials — the divergence is confined to the final rounding.
findings.rootCause: Three ports were written at different times; only two adopted the JS-rounding shim, and the third's parity test tolerance hides the gap.
findings.requiredRepair: Collapse to one port. If that is deferred, at minimum change ktc_va.py's two round() calls to floor(x+0.5) and tighten its parity tolerance to 0.

findings.title: Three call sites in trade suggestions still read the hardcoded dynasty_main starter demand, so in the 10-team no-IDP league a surplus TE is detected and then excluded from every sell suggestion

findings.title: Hill curves are fitted on percentiles over a 400-row denominator and served on a 500-row one, so the same rank is worth up to 25% more at serve time than the fit ever saw
findings.claimUnderTest: holdout.py:81-83 — 'The fit truncates every source to its top 400 before computing percentiles. Matched exactly so train and holdout RMSE are the same quantity measured on different data.' The match is between train and holdout; nothing matches either to SERVING.
findings.observed: The fit maps native rank i to p = i/(n-1) with n capped at FIT_TOP_N = 400, i.e. a denominator of 399. Serving maps rank to p = (rank-1)/(_PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N - 1) = (rank-1)/499. The same rank therefore lands at a smaller percentile at serve time and, under the fitted Hill V(p) = 9999/(1+(p/c)^s), at a HIGHER value than any observation the fit was scored against. With the champion OFFENSE constants (c=0.11, s=1.11): rank 50 serves 13.2% high, rank 100 18.5% high, rank 400 25.4% high.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "from src.model_registry.holdout import hill, FIT_TOP_N;from src.canonical.player_valuation import HILL_PERCENTILE_C as C, HILL_PERCENTILE_S as S;from src.api.data_contract import _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N as R;f=lambda r: hill((r-1)/(FIT_TOP_N-1),C,S);g=lambda r: hill((r-1)/(R-1),C,S);print([(r, round(f(r),1), round(g(r),1), round(100*(g(r)-f(r))/f(r),2)) for r in (50,100,200,400)])"
reproduction.expected: identical percentile denominators, so 0% difference

findings.userImpact: Every value on /rankings past the top handful is produced by a curve evaluated outside the coordinate system it was scored in. The holdout RMSE that gates promotion (787.84 for the champion) is therefore not a measurement of the served board's error.

blastRadius.note: 709 of 1092 rows carry >=1 rank_hill source contribution; the other 383 are priced purely value_direct and are untouched by the Hill denominator. Pages: /rankings and /trade (equity sums rankDerivedValue).

priorFinding.note: the formula registry names 'TRAIN/SERVE SKEW, open' for percentile-reference without a magnitude. This attaches one. Confidence is medium rather than high because serving normalises POST-LADDER effective ranks, so the arithmetic is exact only for sources whose ladder is near identity — KTC, the very source _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N=500 was chosen to align with.

findings.whatWorks: Train and holdout ARE matched to each other, as the docstring claims, and the champion's params match the committed constants exactly.
findings.rootCause: FIT_TOP_N and _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N are two independent constants with no assertion tying them together.
findings.requiredRepair: Either fit at 500 or serve at 400; add a test that imports both constants and asserts they agree.

verification.reasoning: Reproduction re-runs and yields the stated numbers exactly. The two constants are real and independent: src/model_registry/holdout.py:83 FIT_TOP_N=400 and src/api/data_contract.py:5303 _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N=500, with no assertion tying them; scripts/fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:335 truncates each source with values[:400] and :207 divides by n-1. Serving divides by _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N-1=499 at data_contract.py:7590-7594 for every non-value-direct source. src/canonical/player_valuation.py:383-385 already concedes the split in prose ('offline fit tooling may still pass native-pool percentiles') without justifying it. I attacked the inferential step by refitting the master myself under the serve denominator. My native-pool reimplementation reproduces the committed constants to within rounding (c=0.1100 s=1.120 vs shipped 0.1100/1.110), which validates the reimplementation; the serve-denominator refit lands at c=0.0750 s=1.100, and the shipped curve therefore serves 24.7%-41.9% ABOVE a coordinate-consistent curve across ranks 50-400. The defect is LARGER than the finding claims, not smaller. Registry confirms the shipped constants came from this exact fit script via the champion promotion, so the fit is causally upstream of live values. Two corrections, neither fatal. (a) blastRadius playersAffected 1092 is wrong: 383 rows are priced purely from value_direct sources (ktcSfTep/idpTradeCalc bypass the Hill entirely per data_contract.py:7597-7620), so 709 rows carry any Hill-path contribution. (b) The numericProof's single fit denominator of 399 holds for only 3 of the 6 OFFENSE fit sources; DLF/DD/DN/Fitz have 281/367/294/299 positive rows, so the master is an average over curves fitted at denominators 280-399. The '13.2%/18.5%/25.4%' figures are therefore an illustrative lower bound, not a measured serve error - my refit supplies the measured one. Also correcting one piece of rhetoric: 'evaluated outside the coordinate system it was scored in' overstates it. Both fit and serve evaluate p in [0,1]; what differs is the rank->p mapping. No extrapolation occurs (offense rank_hill sources top out at effective rank 293-463, so p<=0.93). Not fixed at HEAD. Not a harness artifact - the CSVs, the registry and the live contract are all present and the path is the live /api/data pipeline. P1 stands: the affected quantity is rankDerivedValue, which /rankings displays and /trade sums into equity, and no warning is shown. The finding's own userImpact undersells this by framing it as a holdout-RMSE governance problem; the sharper impact is that the distortion is rank-dependent (bigger deeper), so multi-player packages of mid-board assets are systematically inflated against elite anchors.
verification.whatWouldSettleIt: Promote a challenger fitted with p=(i)/(_PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N-1) through scripts/model_registry.py and diff the resulting board against today's on the 709 affected rows, then re-score both against the four holdout sources under the SERVE coordinate rather than the native one. A cheap permanent guard: a test that imports FIT_TOP_N and _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N and asserts they agree, which is the finding's own requiredRepair and costs nothing.

findings.title: The running backend rewrites two TRACKED files under data/ on every Sleeper poll, so a deployed checkout's git tree is never clean
findings.claimUnderTest: .gitignore:45 is a bare `data/`, and CLAUDE.md describes data/ as "MOSTLY gitignored" runtime output — implying the running app's writes land on untracked paths.
findings.observed: `git ls-files` shows data/sleeper_last_good.json and data/scrape_state/sleeper_last_success are TRACKED, and `git check-ignore` matches neither (tracked files ignore .gitignore). The audit harness booted the backend read-only, with run_scraper monkeypatched to a no-op and no scrape ever executed, and both files still changed: sleeper_last_success moved 1785867508.5162156 -> 1785914134.965936 and sleeper_last_good.json's savedAt advanced with a full re-serialization of all 12 rosters (~340 KB of diff). The writes come from the ordinary Sleeper-overlay refresh on the request path, not from scraping. Observed three times across the session; restored by hand each time.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && git ls-files data/sleeper_last_good.json data/scrape_state/sleeper_last_success && git status --porcelain data/
reproduction.expected: Runtime state written by the app lands on gitignored paths; `git status` stays clean while the server runs.
reproduction.actual: Both paths are tracked; `git status --porcelain data/` reports both modified after the backend has been up long enough to refresh the Sleeper overlay.

numericProof.formula: count(tracked files modified by the running process with no scrape executed)

findings.userImpact: Not user-facing. It is deployment-facing: a production checkout's working tree is dirty within minutes of boot, so `git pull --ff-only` on the deploy host fails or silently stashes, and any deploy script gating on a clean tree either blocks or learns to ignore real drift. It also means every deploy can carry one league's cached roster snapshot into the repository as a committed diff.

priorFinding.note: Adjacent to W03-F010 (a READ path rewriting the shared canonical rank snapshot) — same class, different files. Neither W03-F010 nor the .gitignore findings (W05-F012, W15-F011) cover these two paths. Found by the orchestrator while restoring drift between repair waves, not by a workstream.

findings.whatWorks: The write itself is correct behaviour — caching the last-good Sleeper payload is what lets the app degrade honestly when Sleeper is unreachable, and W31 is not an argument against that cache.
findings.rootCause: These two files were committed before `data/` was gitignored. A tracked file ignores .gitignore, so the bare `data/` rule that was meant to keep runtime output out of the repo does not apply to them, and nothing since has noticed.
findings.requiredRepair: `git rm --cached` both paths so the runtime writes land on ignored files, and confirm nothing reads them from the repository rather than from the deployed filesystem (a fresh clone must still boot — `load_from_disk` already tolerates their absence, and tests/e2e/preflight.py seeds what the stack needs). Then check `git ls-files data/` for the same pattern elsewhere: 8,198 files under data/ are tracked, and any of them the app writes at runtime has this defect.

_sanitized.why: B8 — git is a distribution channel. Manager identifiers are deterministic non-reversible pseudonyms and per-manager intelligence values are nulled with their keys kept, so this capture still proves which fields the payload exposed, how many managers it covered and how deep it went. Public league-wide facts (rank, odds, percentile) and the strategy text the findings turn on are preserved.
